## CHG-293 Project Editor Content Authority And Shared Read-only Chat History Plan

### Status and Gate

- Gate 1: specification/source understanding and remaining authority exception
  discussed; no current-environment mutation or Provider test was performed.
- Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-09-10 with `OK`. This includes both Chat
  surfaces and explicit Editor denial even with ProjectArchive.execute.
- Gate 3: specification 10.50, this plan, changelog, test design and traceability
  prepared on 2026-09-10.
- Gate 4 implementation approval: APPROVED by Peter on 2026-09-10.
- Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-09-10 with
  `Peter approves CHG-293 Project Editor Content Authority And Shared Read-only Chat History`.
- Gate 5: repository implementation and focused verification recorded below;
  full E2E/coverage and delivery gates remain open.

### 1. Specification Understanding

The six requirements are PROJECT-013, PROJECT-014, CHAT-SHARE-001,
CHAT-OWNER-001, CHAT-AUTHOR-001 and CHAT-COMPAT-001. Project Editor grants
content management, not Project governance or ownership of other people's chat.
Shared history is an authorized read policy, not a relaxation of continuation,
feedback, deletion, CSV execution or export policy. User names come from actual
creator identity, never current-user copy or guessed historical provenance.

Observed code evidence:

- `backend/app/domain/project_access.py:project_capabilities` currently sets
  `can_manage_lifecycle=is_owner`, despite the existing Editor content baseline.
- `backend/app/api/routes/documents.py:update_document_lifecycle` requires
  PROJECT_OWNER_ROLES; other content paths already largely accept Editors.
- `backend/app/api/routes/projects.py:_require_project_archive_authority` and
  the Projects page use Owner OR execute grant without an Editor explicit deny.
- `backend/app/api/routes/serving.py` history list/get are actor-only; summaries
  omit creator identity and calculate can_continue from version readiness alone.
  `_ensure_conversation_can_continue` returns when no actor-filtered row exists,
  so it is not a safe global conversation ownership check.
- Document Chat loads only the first conversation and renders one non-selecting
  history card. Project Chat discards Backend can_continue in its local mapper.
  Both lack creator-name history metadata and need guarded write controls.

### 2. Discussion and Confirmation Items

Confirmed: Editors can CRUD permitted content regardless of its author, but
cannot manage Project settings/models, members/permissions, Project deletion/
archive, Owner publication or another actor's chat. Existing review locks,
version immutability, impact confirmation and soft-delete behavior remain.
Both internal Chat surfaces share authorized history; exact Project/surface/
document-version boundaries remain. Editor+execute must be denied archive,
impact and cleanup retry; other roles' established authority is unchanged.

Implementation defaults remain conservative: export is still creator-only;
existing approval evidence and public Integration API history are not shared;
CSV execution from another person's conversation is disabled until starting an
own conversation. No new UI filters, model changes or GraphRAG work are included.
If a schema/identity issue requires broader repair, return for scope review.

  the question whether Editor must be denied archive even with execute grant.

4. Use a transaction-scoped PostgreSQL advisory lock keyed to the global

   preventing ID reuse. Same-ID different-actor races cannot produce mixed authors.

   models; no SQL migration, V049 application or legacy backfill planned. Any

6. Client switching uses conversation identity and request generation/cancellation;
   late answers or history loads must update only their originating conversation.
   Opening others' history cannot turn it into an own draft. New drafts are not
   counted as persisted history before successful first response.
7. Archive policy is a separate helper from the active-only document capability
   path, so archived+failed cleanup retry is evaluated correctly. Server projection,
   API denial and Frontend badge/button must agree. Editor explicit deny does not
   clear the actor's execute grant or affect other Projects.

## CHG-292 Canonical Tag Graph Synchronization And Consistency Plan

### Status and Gate

- Gate 1: repository/source review and eight-part scope discussion documented
  in the current conversation; no live graph inventory was represented as done.
- Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-09-09 with
  `我接受你的建議，請往下做` after the scope/recommendations discussion.
- Gate 3: specification section 10.49, changelog, this plan, test design and
  traceability prepared for review.
- Gate 4 implementation approval: APPROVED by Peter on 2026-09-09.
- Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-09-09 with
  `Peter approves CHG-292 Canonical Tag Graph Synchronization And Consistency`.

This is a new bounded change, not continuation authority for CHG-291 migration
Stage B. Do not implement code, create executable feature tests, run behavioral
tests, build application images, apply schema/constraints, change Kubernetes,
or repair existing graph data before the appropriate approval. Current approval
allows repository implementation and isolated verification; current-environment
graph repair, application image builds, DDL and deployment remain separately gated.

### Confirmed understanding and design decisions

1. PostgreSQL remains canonical; Neo4j projects existing Tag UUIDs and genuine
   DocumentVersion/Chunk assignments. No new tag inference, tag merge, entity
   model, framework dependency or graph-enabled answer path is in scope.
2. Candidate previews remain PostgreSQL-derived. Candidate artifact rebuilds
   must not write formal Neo4j. Formal graph publication receives the complete
   approved version snapshot, not merely a Chunk list.
3. Published/previously published assignments are immutable in place. Enforce
   the existing re-review requirement on Backend mutations and compatible UI
   controls; do not auto-create/publish a replacement version.
4. All formal writers share a canonical builder, scoped safe writer and verified
   receipt; only source-owned tag edges are reconciled. Tag-only work must never
   delete Chunk nodes, global orphan Tags, history or unrelated relationships.
5. Formal graph reads use actual Neo4j assignments, while PostgreSQL hydration
   supplies authorized content only. Missing projection fails honestly with a
   safe operational error; unpublished document previews remain available.
6. Graph-only compare/apply is distinct from chunk reconciliation, Embedding,
   index build and publication. It does not mutate canonical source data or
   manifests. Current-environment inventory/backfill/deployment are separate
   exact-scope actions, not implicitly authorized by implementation approval.

No blocking product question remains from the accepted scope. Low-level schema
or compatibility needs that exceed these decisions must return for explicit
specification/plan review rather than being silently implemented.

### Current evidence and planned module boundaries

| Area | Observed behavior | Planned change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend/app/domain/review_publish.py` | Active sync omits tags; `_write_graph` deletes version chunks/tag links and returns formula counts. | Accept a shared canonical projection, upsert structure safely, reconcile only owned tag assignments, verify exact scoped result, preserve non-tag edges and historical identities. |
| `backend/app/domain/graph_sync_jobs.py` | Existing durable jobs/outbox/lease are available; resync calls the tag-free active writer. | Reuse jobs, validate project/version/revision/digest, serialize competing scope writes, reject obsolete work, record truthful success/failure/retry evidence. |
| New small domain modules such as `graph_projection.py` / `graph_reconciliation.py` | Tag loading is private to candidate artifacts and identity rules are duplicated. | Separate immutable projection building, safe graph IO, scoped difference verification and graph-only orchestration; names may follow local patterns without combining them with Embedding. |
| `backend/app/domain/chunk_artifacts.py`, `extraction_pipeline.py` | Candidate reconciliation calls Embedding/index then writes staging Neo4j; preview may use tag names as IDs. | Remove candidate formal graph side effects, keep content rebuild semantics, share UUID-based preview projection and revision validation; tag-only preview refresh never calls the expensive rebuild. |
| `backend/app/api/routes/documents.py` and publication/lifecycle entry points | Tag add/delete/auto commits PostgreSQL without consistent graph evidence refresh; published states are not all covered by review-only locking. | Refresh candidate evidence transactionally, guard immutable published assignments, preserve authorization/audit, ensure lifecycle and switch/resync cannot revive stale serving scope. |
| `backend/app/api/routes/serving.py` and existing graph operations routes | Formal reader fetches structure from Neo4j and appends PostgreSQL tag edges. | Read genuine scoped Tag nodes/edges for graph/neighbors/paths; distinguish unpublished preview, legitimately empty graph, truncation and incomplete formal projection; retain authorized content hydration. |
| `backend/app/api/schemas.py`, graph/tag clients and zh/en locales if necessary | Existing graph envelopes, safe errors and operational UI should remain stable. | Add only required non-breaking metadata/error mapping and readonly tag affordances. No new dashboard, graph layout redesign or changed Chat/API query behavior. |
| New `backend/scripts/chg292_graph_tag_reconcile.py` | No bounded tag-only compare/apply contract is established. | Build default-read-only operator tool with explicit environment/project/document/version scope and digest-bound opt-in apply; no automatic whole-database mode. |

### Data, concurrency and compatibility design

- Preserve `tags`, `chunk_tags`, `document_version_tags`, source strings and
  canonical IDs. Do not normalize historical tag text as a side effect.
- Reuse GraphSyncJob, Outbox payload and existing JSON metadata for source
  revision/digest/receipt where sufficient. Store only safe allowlisted
  provenance on graph edges; do not add User/Model/Job graph nodes.
- Bind work to project generation, version identity, canonical source digest
  and source revision/publication generation where applicable. Coordinate
  same-scope writers with existing PostgreSQL transactional locks plus durable
  ownership/revalidation; test both competing versions and same-version retries.
- Validate a consistent canonical snapshot, execute the bounded Neo4j mutation
  transaction, read back the expected relation identities/metadata, and commit
  a matching receipt. A crash between external commit and receipt is repaired
  idempotently; no distributed atomicity is claimed.
- Graph-only repair must not reuse `_delete_version_chunks`, whole-project
  archival, Embed/Indexer, publication or manifest-switch operations. Orphan
  Tags without relationships may be retained; unrelated cleanup is not needed
  to satisfy this change.
- Check existing Neo4j identity/constraint prerequisites before relying on
  uniqueness. Duplicates or uncertain ownership are fail-stop findings. If
  additional Neo4j DDL is needed, specify and test it in disposable services;
  current-environment installation is separately gated, never a read/startup
  side effect. Additional PostgreSQL columns/migrations require scope refinement
  before implementation; this plan does not silently authorize a V050 migration.
- Preserve existing routes/envelopes and source ID semantics. Add stable
  `published_tag_revision_required` (409) and `graph_projection_not_ready`
  (503) via the established error pattern, plus zh/en operational copy. Existing
  no-permission/not-found behavior remains non-disclosing.
- Existing incomplete formal graphs may become visibly not-ready. Deployment
  must include a separately approved inventory and compatible repair/cutover
  decision before enforcing the new read contract on existing users. Do not
  solve compatibility with silent PostgreSQL relationship fallback.

## 1. Specification Understanding

- Specification source: `SPECIFICATION.md`
- Specification sections read: all sections 1 through 13.
- Requirement IDs: see `TRACEABILITY.md`.
- Summary of intended behavior: NomoSmart v1.0 is a full rewrite of an
  enterprise knowledge management platform covering OIDC identity, RBAC,
  project membership, document import, per-document pipelines, two-stage
  approvals, extraction review, RAG, validation runs, a unified internal
  knowledge graph exposed only through permission-scoped Project/Document
  views, notifications, reports, Docker Compose deployment, and full i18n
  coverage.
- In-scope items: all v1.0 functionality described in `SPECIFICATION.md`.
- Out-of-scope items: compatibility with existing application behavior,
  existing API contracts, existing schema, existing frontend structure, and
  identity shortcuts based on arbitrary request headers.
- Assumptions found in the specification: PostgreSQL is the source of truth;
  OpenSearch, Neo4j, S3, Redis, and Celery are supporting systems; formal
  identity is Keycloak OIDC; all user-facing frontend text requires Traditional
  Chinese and English i18n keys.

## 4. Development Plan

- Plan owner: Codex
- Plan date: 2026-06-19
- Target requirement IDs: all v1.0 IDs listed in `TRACEABILITY.md`.
- Architecture/design approach: build a clean v1.0 application around explicit
  contracts. PostgreSQL is the system of record. FastAPI exposes API modules.
  Flyway creates schema. Celery workers execute background jobs through Redis.
  OpenSearch, Neo4j, S3-compatible storage, and Keycloak are integration
  adapters behind typed configuration. The frontend uses Next.js App Router,
  TypeScript, i18n, lucide-react, and API contract types.
- Data model changes: create the full v1.0 schema through Flyway, including
  users, roles, permissions, external groups, project members, project owners,
  documents, versions, references, pipeline runs/steps, approval requests/tasks,
  review records, notifications, graph sync jobs, chunks, tags, chat records,
  validation runs/items, and encrypted AI model settings.
- API changes: implement the v1.0 API modules listed in spec section 12, with
  OIDC auth, permission dependencies, project-scope filtering, approval
  optimistic locking, staging/production retrieval separation, and graph
  authorization enforced on the backend.
- Frontend/UI changes: rebuild app routes for login, dashboard, import,
  extraction, approval workspace/detail, reports, and system management. Use
  dense enterprise dashboard styling, Traditional Chinese default locale, and
  complete `zh`/`en` i18n keys.
- Scoped SYS-001 UI approach: refactor `/system` into a client-side accessible
  six-Tab workspace with compact summary/tool rows and operational tables. Use typed
  frontend fixtures for this UI milestone. The permissions Tab selects one
  NomoSmart role at a time and keeps matrices isolated; the identity-source Tab
  presents editable non-secret Keycloak OIDC metadata, masked secret status,
  connection validation and federated LDAP/AD health/sync summaries.
- The System Parameters Tab uses typed fixture fields for upload size, IANA
  timezone and staging retention TTL, with field validation, effective-value
  metadata, save/restore controls and explicit fixture-only feedback.
- Scoped SYS-001 backend boundary: this UI milestone does not create direct
  LDAP/AD connections. Future APIs persist role matrices, mappings, safe OIDC
  configuration metadata and audit events; deployment secrets remain external.
  Activation must validate the candidate and preserve the last-known-good OIDC
  configuration on failure.
- Configuration changes: introduce typed environment configuration for backend,
  frontend, Celery, Redis, PostgreSQL, Keycloak, OpenSearch, Neo4j, S3, CORS and
  encryption keys. AI providers, model endpoints and encrypted API keys remain
  System Management data in PostgreSQL rather than deployment environment
  parameters. No real secrets are committed.
- Deployment changes: create Docker Compose first, with env template,
  health checks, named volumes, and Redis/Celery wiring. Helm follows after
  Compose foundation is stable.
- Test plan updates: keep `TEST_PLAN.md` as the quality gate and add concrete
  test commands as tooling is introduced. Critical tests must cover auth,
  authorization, permission unions, project membership, approvals, import
  pipeline, config loading, secret handling, migrations, staging/production RAG,
  graph authorization, and rollback-sensitive deployment behavior.
- Traceability updates: replace placeholder traceability rows with requirement
  IDs mapped to spec sections, implementation areas, tests, harness commands,
  and status.
- Migration/rollback plan: Flyway versioned migrations are append-only. Initial
  schema starts with `V001__initial_schema.sql`. Rollback for early milestones
  is environment rebuild from migration history and seed/test data; production
  rollback procedures must be documented before deployable release.
- Risks and mitigations: external services can slow integration, so adapters
  should have deterministic tests and Compose-backed validation. Auth and graph
  authorization are high-risk and must be implemented backend-first. The full
  scope is large, so milestones must remain traceable and independently
  verifiable.

### Scoped Plan: PROMPT-001 System Prompt Management

- Scope: add System Prompt management beside AI Models in `/system`, with
  separate global Chat and Judge prompts plus per-model prompts for Chat/Judge
  AI models only.
- Backend approach: add `system_prompts` and `system_prompt_versions`, enforce
  RBAC with `System.AIModelSettings`, validate 8000 Unicode characters, keep
  enable/disable and version history, audit changes without prompt full text,
  and expose `/api/v1/system-prompts` plus model prompt endpoints.
- Runtime approach: resolve prompts as ordered layers rather than replacement:
  backend safety default, then enabled model-specific prompt, then enabled
  global prompt for the same Chat/Judge model type. Preserve blank enabled
  prompts as intentional layers and persist ordered source/version/hash
  metadata with chat and validation execution records.
- Frontend approach: add a System Prompt management surface adjacent to AI
  Models, with two fixed top sections for global Chat and global Judge prompts,
  where each global box is the direct edit/create entry point without separate
  top-right global-add buttons. Keep a separate model-specific prompt section
  below, clear scope/model badges and status summaries on the main page, and
  move full prompt editing into a popup modal with priority/layering guidance,
  version list, active state, character counter, validation errors,
  close/Escape/backdrop behavior, loading/empty/error states and zh/en i18n
  strings.
- Test strategy: backend schema/API/RBAC/version/audit tests, frontend System
  Management UI and i18n tests, and Chat/Judge prompt-layering tests using real
  configured runtime paths or blocked/unavailable reporting under `TEST-002`.
- Verification commands planned: `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace`,
  `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved`, `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:plan`,
  `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:backend`, `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:frontend`,
  `./HARNESS/harness.sh i18n:hardcoded`, `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:build`,
  `./HARNESS/harness.sh coverage:check`.
- Gate status: updated on 2026-06-30 for layered prompt behavior and UI/UX
  refinement; awaiting human approval of this updated scoped plan before
  implementation or feature test execution.

### Scoped Plan: CHUNK-001 / TAG-001 Manual Chunking and Tag Management

- Scope: implement persisted manual chunking from Original/Markdown text
  selection, plus chunk-level and document-level tag management on the
  Knowledge Detail page.
- Backend approach: add or extend chunk mutation APIs for creating a manual
  chunk from a source range. The API must validate project/document access,
  `manual_edit_enabled`, version editability and optimistic lock, then replace
  fully overlapping chunks, split partially overlapping chunks, preserve source
  anchors/offsets/lineage, recalculate source-order indexes and audit the
  mutation. Add tag APIs for chunk and document-version tags with `tag_text`,
  `source`, created metadata, model/prompt metadata when applicable, add/delete
  operations and audit.
- LLM tagging approach: implement auto-tagging endpoints that resolve the
  project Chat LLM model, apply existing `PROMPT-001` System Prompt layering,
  call the real configured provider path, parse conservative tag results, and
  persist them directly as `source = llm`. If the model, credential, provider,
  prompt resolver or network is unavailable, return a blocked/unavailable error
  and do not create deterministic fallback tags.
- Frontend approach: update `/project/[id]/knowledge/[knowledgeId]` so selecting
  text in Original or Markdown shows a compact floating Manual Chunk action.
  After save, refresh the live detail and keep the selection/chunk focus
  coherent. Add document tag controls beside the Original/Markdown switch and
  chunk tag controls on chunk cards, with source-aware chips, auto-tag actions,
  manual add inputs, delete controls, loading/error states and zh/en i18n.
- Data/schema impact: likely requires schema/model support for chunk
  active/superseded state, source offsets/ranges, lineage metadata, tag source
  and optional LLM execution metadata. Prefer additive fields/tables that keep
  existing chunk/tag records readable.
- Test strategy: backend tests for permission/lock validation, overlap
  replace/split, ordering, lineage, audit, tag source CRUD and LLM unavailable
  failure; frontend tests for selection toolbar, disabled manual editing,
  document/chunk tag controls, direct live API calls, i18n and no client-only
  success.
- Verification commands planned: `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace`,
  `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved`, `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:plan`,
  `./HARNESS/harness.sh backend:syntax`, focused backend tests for chunks/tags,
  `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:backend`, `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:frontend`,
  `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:lint`, `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:build`,
  `./HARNESS/harness.sh coverage:check`, and `git diff --check`.
- Risks: source-range mapping differs between structured Original pages and
  Markdown text; overlap splitting must be atomic to avoid duplicate retrieval
  ranges; real provider auto-tagging may be blocked by missing credentials, so
  blocked/unavailable must be reported honestly under `TEST-002`.
- Gate status: approved by Peter on 2026-07-01; implementation and focused
  verification may proceed.

### Scoped Plan: CHG-167 TAG-001 Document / Chunk Tag Relationships

- Scope: extend existing `TAG-001` tag management so document-version tags and
  chunk tags are relatable by a shared project-scoped canonical `tag_id`, rather
  than behaving as independent display-text lists.
- Backend approach: keep `tags` as the canonical project-scoped tag identity and
  enforce normalized tag reuse through `(project_id, normalized_name)` or an
  equivalent normalization contract. Preserve cross-project isolation. Extend
  tag response contracts so document-version tags can include related chunk
  summaries for the same `document_version_id` and `tag_id`, and chunk tag
  details can indicate whether they support a document-level tag.
- Data/schema impact: prefer additive migration support for `normalized_name`
  when current `tags.name` uniqueness is not sufficient for stable matching.
  Existing same-project tag records with equal normalized names should be
  consolidated or migrated without losing `chunk_tags` and
  `document_version_tags` relationships. Existing tag UUIDs remain the canonical
  runtime relationship identity after normalization.
- Frontend approach: update the Knowledge Detail `貼標` tab to show, for each
  document tag, the related chunk count and optionally a compact related-chunk
  list or affordance that can focus matching chunks. Chunk tag chips should keep
  their existing compact layout and may show a small indicator when the tag is
  also present at document level.
- Graph/review/query approach: graph preview and review-summary derivation must
  use `tag_id` to connect DocumentVersion / Chunk / Tag relationships. Search
  or filtering behavior that references document/chunk tags should use tag IDs
  or backend-derived relationships, not raw display text matching.
- Test strategy: backend tests for normalized tag reuse, duplicate prevention,
  cross-project isolation, document-tag-to-related-chunk derivation, chunk-tag
  document-level support indicators, graph/review summary relationship
  derivation, and migration compatibility. Frontend tests for document tag
  related-chunk counts, chunk focus affordance, and no text-only relationship
  assumptions.
- Verification commands planned: `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace`,
  `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved`, `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:plan`,
  `./HARNESS/harness.sh backend:syntax`, focused backend relationship tests,
  `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:backend`, `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:frontend`,
  `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:lint`, `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:build`,
  `./HARNESS/harness.sh coverage:check`, and `git diff --check`.
- Risks: normalizing existing tag text can merge records that previously looked
  distinct only by whitespace/case; migrations must keep audit/source metadata
  coherent. Graph and review summaries may currently derive unique tags by text,
  so implementation must update those consumers consistently.
- Gate status: approved by Peter on 2026-07-01; implementation and focused
  verification may proceed.

### 6.2 Scoped Change Approval: GRAPH-003

- Plan prepared: 2026-06-20
- Scope: add bounded mouse/pointer drag-to-pan to both document and project
  knowledge graph canvases.
- Frontend approach: keep pan offset and drag origin in each graph component,
  apply pan and zoom together on the scene transform, use pointer capture so a
  drag remains stable outside the initial target, and expose grab/grabbing cursor
  feedback. A movement threshold will distinguish dragging from clicking.
- Interaction rules: dragging the background or a node pans the scene; a real
  drag suppresses the following click so it cannot select/clear a node. Reset
  clears selection and returns the scene to center. Pan is bounded relative to
  the visible canvas and continues to coexist with wheel/button zoom.
- Test strategy: verify pointer down/move/up/cancel, movement threshold, pan
  bounds, pointer capture, node click without drag, click suppression after drag,
  reset-to-center, zoom coexistence, and desktop/mobile behavior for both graph
  components. Then run `frontend:lint`, `frontend:build`, `spec:doctor`,
  `spec:trace`, and `plan:approved`.
- Deployment/config impact: none.
- Approved by: Peter
- Approval date: 2026-06-20
- Approved scope: GRAPH-003 document and project graph drag-to-pan.
- Approval wording: `OK, GO`

Implementation and feature-test execution for GRAPH-003 may begin only after
this scoped approval is recorded.

### 6.3 Scoped Change Approval: GRAPH-004

- Plan prepared: 2026-06-20
- Scope: allow every visible node in document and project graphs to be dragged
  independently while its connected SVG edges follow in real time.
- Frontend approach: initialize local node-position maps from the existing
  layouts, start node dragging from the node pointer handler with propagation
  stopped before the canvas pan handler, convert pointer deltas into graph
  coordinate percentages accounting for current zoom, and clamp positions to
  visible canvas bounds.
- Interaction rules: node dragging and canvas panning are mutually exclusive;
  movement beyond the click threshold suppresses node selection, while a normal
  click retains first-degree highlighting. Reset restores every node position,
  canvas pan, and selection. Component unmount on modal close naturally discards
  temporary positions.
- Test strategy: verify every node type can move, connected edge endpoints update
  during drag, unrelated nodes remain fixed, canvas pan does not change, bounds
  are enforced, click/drag threshold is respected, zoomed dragging remains
  proportional, reset restores defaults, and reopen starts from defaults. Then
  run `frontend:lint`, `frontend:build`, `spec:doctor`, `spec:trace`, and
  `plan:approved`.
- Deployment/config impact: none; positions are not persisted.
- Approved by: Peter
- Approval date: 2026-06-20
- Approved scope: GRAPH-004 temporary per-node drag positioning in both graphs.
- Approval wording: `OK`

### 6.16 Scoped Change Approval: IMPORT-001 / IMPORT-002 / DSYNC-001 / CONFIG-002

Plan date: 2026-06-22

Scope:

- Add project-scoped file upload accepting PDF, DOC, DOCX, TXT, MD, and MARKDOWN with a backend-authoritative, globally configurable 100 MB default limit.
- Start extraction automatically only for a successful single-file upload. Add multi-file partial-result upload that creates ready documents without Pipelines and supports manual per-document extraction.
- Add one-file FTP, FTPS, SFTP/SSH, and S3-compatible data-service configuration, secure credential handling, connection tests, immediate initial background synchronization, one-time and standard five-field Cron scheduling, manual Sync Now, content-fingerprint version creation, and manual extraction after every successful sync.
- Update frontend, backend, persistence/migrations, workers/scheduler, audit/error contracts, Traditional Chinese and English localization, typed runtime configuration, safe Docker/Helm examples, automated tests, and requirement traceability required by CHG-064.

Implementation approach and task breakdown:

1. Add typed global upload-limit configuration and public non-secret configuration discovery; wire consistent safe examples into local, Docker Compose, and Helm configuration.
2. Define migration-backed document-source, encrypted credential-reference, schedule, and sync-run data contracts, indexes, uniqueness/locking constraints, and audit events. Keep PostgreSQL as the task state source of truth.
3. Build reusable server-side file validation and source snapshot storage. Implement single and multi upload APIs with per-item results, idempotency, permission checks, atomic single-upload Pipeline dispatch, and manual extraction dispatch guards.
4. Implement protocol adapters behind the existing service boundary for FTP, FTPS, SFTP/SSH, and S3. Enforce TLS/host-key checks, secret masking, one-file identity, timeouts, size/format validation, and sanitized failures.
5. Implement Celery sync jobs plus scheduler integration for initial, manual, and Cron triggers. Add five-field Cron/timezone validation, next-run calculation, sync locking, fingerprints, unchanged detection, transactional next-major allocation, working-version conflict handling, retries, and audit records.
6. Build the upload and data-service modal/wizard using existing operational UI patterns and lucide-react icons. Add protocol-specific fields, friendly/basic and advanced Cron controls, per-item upload outcomes, sync states, ready-for-extraction action, and Version Management Sync Now.
7. Add matching Traditional Chinese and English strings, accessibility states, keyboard behavior, responsive handling, and clear non-color-only status/error messages.
8. Implement the tests defined in `TEST_PLAN.md`, update traceability statuses, run narrow checks first and broader frontend/backend/E2E/coverage/deployment checks before handoff.

Test strategy:

- Unit tests cover validation, typed config, Cron/timezone parsing, fingerprints, version allocation, state transitions, and sanitized errors.
- API/job tests cover permissions, idempotency, single/multi branching, partial results, dispatch recovery, initial/manual/scheduled sync, locking, version conflicts, audit, and secret non-disclosure.
- Protocol integration tests use deterministic local fakes or disposable containers; no production services or credentials are required.
- Component/E2E tests cover the upload and service workflows, manual extraction/sync actions, status display, localization, accessibility, responsive behavior, and prior-Active continuity.
- Frontend and backend application logic must each retain at least 80% automated coverage; critical upload, authorization, secret, scheduling, and version flows require explicit tests regardless of aggregate coverage.

Deployment/configuration impact:

- Add a documented global upload-size setting with a 100 MB default to typed backend configuration, frontend config discovery, `deploy/docker/nomosmart.env.example`, Compose wiring, and Helm ConfigMap/values.
- Add only secret references/placeholders for service credentials; no real password, key, token, endpoint, or bucket is committed. Operators must provide runtime secrets through the established secret mechanism.
- Scheduler/worker deployments need queue and schedule configuration, readiness visibility, structured logs, and safe retry settings. Database schema changes require forward migration and documented rollback/compatibility notes.

Risks and mitigations:

- Legacy DOC parsing and remote protocol differences can vary by implementation; isolate adapters/parsers, validate fixtures for each type, and report unsupported/corrupt content explicitly.
- Remote sync may be slow or unavailable; create the list item first, use background jobs, visible states, bounded timeouts/retries, and preserve the prior successful version.
- Concurrent scheduled/manual syncs can duplicate versions; serialize per source and combine locks, fingerprints, unique constraints, and idempotency keys.
- Cron timezone/DST behavior can surprise operators; store IANA timezone, preview human-readable timing and next run, and test DST boundaries.
- Upload limits may diverge across proxy, frontend, and backend; make backend authoritative, expose its effective value, and validate deployment-layer limits in configuration checks.

### 6.26 Scoped Change Approval: AUTH-003 / AUTH-004 Authentication Setting Lock

Plan date: 2026-06-22

Scope:

- Extend the `/system` authentication-settings panel so Keycloak configuration
  and LDAP/AD people/group synchronization management appear on one page while
  LDAP/AD connection credentials remain exclusively in Keycloak Federation.
- Make a successfully validated and active configuration read-only by default.
  Require fresh Keycloak authentication plus current System Settings Edit
  permission for a user/session-bound, 10-minute editing window.
- Validate edits as a candidate, atomically activate only successful candidates,
  retain the last-known-good configuration and immediately relock after save,
  cancel, logout, expiry or permission loss.
- Provision a dedicated Keycloak-local break-glass administrator during system
  initialization from deployment Secret input. Keep it disabled by default and
  require OIDC, MFA, dedicated System Admin mapping, alerts, audit, post-use
  disablement and credential rotation. Do not add NomoSmart local authentication.

Implementation approach:

1. Add typed authentication-setting read, reauthentication, lock, validation
   and atomic update contracts with explicit draft, locked and temporary-unlock
   states; return only masked secret status.
2. Implement backend authorization and a server-side unlock grant bound to the
   reauthenticated user, OIDC session and identity-settings scope. Enforce the
   10-minute limit and revoke on save, explicit lock, logout, account disablement
   or permission loss; reject stale and concurrent candidate versions.
3. Implement Keycloak forced reauthentication and validate the returned issuer,
   subject, session, `auth_time`, account state and current NomoSmart permission
   before issuing the unlock grant.
4. Persist non-secret Keycloak metadata and LDAP/AD synchronization source,
   people/group scope, Cron schedule and IANA timezone through a typed settings
   service. Validate discovery/JWKS and sync fields before atomic activation and
   retain versioned last-known-good data.
5. Update the frontend to show a unified dense settings page with locked fields,
   status and history, an explicit Reauthenticate to Edit action, remaining-time
   feedback, candidate errors, cancel/lock behavior and matching zh/en text.
6. Add structured audit events for reauthentication, unlock, revoke/expiry,
   validation, activation and break-glass use without tokens or secrets.
7. Extend Keycloak/bootstrap and Docker/Helm configuration templates to accept
   break-glass identity and credential Secret references, provision the account
   disabled by default, map its dedicated role, and document enable/use/disable/
   rotate/recover operations without committing a default credential.

Test strategy:

- Frontend/component tests cover locked defaults, same-page Keycloak and LDAP/AD
  sync controls, no credential fields, reauthentication states, countdown,
  cancellation, expiry, save relock, errors, accessibility, responsive layout
  and Traditional Chinese/English coverage.
- Backend/API tests cover fresh `auth_time`, user/session/scope binding, latest
  permission checks, disabled users, permission removal, expiry/revocation,
  direct API denial, stale/concurrent candidates, atomic success and rollback.
- Security tests prove secrets/tokens/LDAP credentials never enter responses,
  DOM, logs or audit records and that frontend-only state cannot unlock APIs.
- Integration/E2E tests use controlled Keycloak and Federation fakes to cover
  reauthentication, candidate discovery/JWKS validation, synchronization setting
  updates, last-known-good recovery and post-save lock behavior.
- Deployment tests cover Secret-only break-glass initialization, disabled
  default state, dedicated role/MFA policy, activation/use alerts, audit,
  post-use disablement and credential rotation with no shared default password.

Deployment/configuration impact:

- Add safe example variables or Secret references for break-glass username,
  initial credential source, enabled-default=false and required Keycloak policy;
  never include a real or product-default password.
- Add server-side temporary-unlock storage and expiry configuration. Production
  deployments must support immediate revocation across backend replicas.
- Document last-known-good restore and break-glass runbooks for Docker Compose
  and Helm/Kubernetes, including enable, login, recovery, disable and rotation.

Risks and mitigations:

- A frontend-only lock is bypassable: every mutation is authorized and gated by
  the backend unlock grant and current permission check.
- Misconfiguration can block all users: validate candidates before atomic
  activation, retain last-known-good settings and document deployment recovery.
- Break-glass credentials increase attack surface: keep the Keycloak account
  disabled, Secret-provisioned, MFA-protected, alerted, audited and rotated.
- Concurrent administrators can overwrite changes: use configuration versions
  and optimistic concurrency, requiring reload and revalidation on conflict.
- Navigation revocation can be interrupted: attempt explicit client revocation
  while retaining the server-side 10-minute/session-bound hard limit.

### 6.29 Scoped Change Approval: Backend Foundation Milestone 1

- Plan prepared: 2026-06-23.
- Gate 2 confirmation: complete. Q-046 through Q-057 and CHG-073 through
  CHG-077 record Peter's Backend decisions.
- Target requirements: `BACKEND-001`, `API-001`, `DB-001`, `CONFIG-001`,
  `SEC-001`, `AUTH-001`, `AUTH-002`, `AUTH-003`, `AUTH-004`, `PERM-001`,
  `PROJECT-001`, `SYS-001`, `OCR-001`, `IMPORT-006`, `UPLOAD-SEC-001`,
  `SEARCH-001`, `VERSION-001`, `TEST-001`, and `OPS-001` foundations.
- Scope:
  - Create the Python 3.12 FastAPI Backend foundation with `pyproject.toml`, uv
    lock, application factory, `/api/v1`, typed configuration, request IDs,
    standard errors, structured logging, health/readiness and adapter boundaries.
  - Create the complete v1.0 `V001__initial_schema.sql` Flyway migration,
    matching SQLAlchemy models and safe seed data. This includes all section 8
    tables plus system parameters, identity settings/unlocks, audit logs,
    idempotency keys, outbox events, file scans, embedding profiles/builds and
    Active Version Manifests so later milestones do not rewrite the foundation.
  - Implement Keycloak JWT/JWKS validation, `/auth/oidc/config`, `/auth/me`,
    user/group synchronization records and the normally disabled break-glass
    status boundary. No identity-header fallback is permitted.
  - Implement role/permission union evaluation, project membership/owner scope,
    user/role/permission/external-group APIs, project foundations, system
    parameters, identity-setting lock state and append-only audit services.
  - Historical Milestone 1 foundation: implement versioned AES-256-GCM
    envelopes and AI/OCR model configuration contracts. CHG-247/`SECRET-001`
    now limits that encryption path to approved drafts, non-production and
    controlled legacy migration reads; production Vault-capable credentials
    store only `vault://` references.
  - Define storage-key, quarantine/scanner, embedding-profile and serving-manifest
    domain contracts with unit tests, but do not yet upload files or write search
    vectors.
- Explicitly out of scope for Milestone 1:
  - Document upload endpoints, Celery extraction jobs, protocol sync adapters,
    OCR execution, OpenSearch indexing/query, Neo4j writes, approval workflow,
    RAG/validation, reports and production deployment rollout.
  - Frontend fixture replacement, except contract changes strictly required for
    `/api/v1` types after the Backend endpoint exists.
- Implementation order:
  1. Scaffold Backend packaging, settings, logging, error and test foundations.
  2. Define Flyway V001, schema invariants, seed roles/system parameters and
     migration validation.
  3. Add SQLAlchemy models, repositories, transaction helpers, idempotency and
     outbox primitives.
  4. Add OIDC/JWKS validation and controlled test-token fixtures.
  5. Add users, external groups, sync-run persistence and Keycloak Admin adapter.
  6. Add RBAC union and project-scope dependencies, then user/role/project APIs.
  7. Add system parameter, AI/OCR model encryption, identity-setting lock and
     audit APIs.
  8. Add storage/search manifest domain contracts and adapter health checks.
  9. Run narrow unit/API/migration checks, then the complete Backend milestone
     suite and coverage gate.
- API/data conventions:
  - UUID primary keys, UTC `timestamptz`, ISO 8601 output and optimistic lock
    columns where concurrent governance actions will occur.
  - `/api/v1` only; errors use `code`, `message`, `details`, `request_id`.
  - Offset pagination for bounded administrative lists and cursor pagination for
    audit/sync/event histories.
  - Secrets never appear in responses, logs, audit rows or fixtures. This
    historical AES rule is superseded for production Vault-capable AI/OCR and
    integration credentials by CHG-247/`SECRET-001`; AES remains only for its
    explicitly bounded draft/non-production/legacy cases.
  - PostgreSQL is authoritative. Redis, S3, OpenSearch, Neo4j and Keycloak are
    adapters and must not become alternate business-state sources.
- Development configuration impact:
  - Backend runs locally on `127.0.0.1:8000`; frontend is
    `http://127.0.0.1:3000`; CORS also allows `http://localhost:3000`.
  - Existing local Docker services on `127.0.0.1` provide PostgreSQL 18.3,
    Redis 7.4, RustFS, OpenSearch 3.6, Neo4j 5.26 and Keycloak 26.
  - Real values live only in an ignored `backend/.env`; the repository receives
    a safe `.env.example`. AI provider/model/key values remain System Management
    data, not environment variables. No real secret may be committed.
  - The external Desktop Compose is a development dependency for this milestone;
    repository-owned root Compose remains the approved later deployment task.
- Test strategy:
  - Unit: configuration validation, error envelope, encryption/tamper/wrong-key,
    permission union/deny, project scope, UUID/time serialization, pagination,
    S3 salted-name calculation, canonical extension, scanner states, embedding
    profile compatibility and manifest fail-closed logic.
  - Migration/model: clean-database Flyway apply, constraints/indexes/seeds,
    ORM/schema agreement and migration idempotency expectations.
  - Auth/API: valid/expired/not-before/wrong-issuer/wrong-audience/rotated-key JWT,
    disabled/unsynced/no-role users, arbitrary identity-header rejection,
    masked settings, system-parameter atomic validation and RBAC/project scope.
  - Sync/security: Keycloak adapter fakes plus bounded local integration,
    failed-sync preservation, no secret leakage, audit append-only behavior,
    idempotent request replay/conflict and outbox recovery.
  - Coverage: Backend application logic must reach at least 80%; auth,
    authorization, configuration, encryption and migration critical flows require
    explicit tests regardless of aggregate coverage.
- Deployment/operations impact:
  - Add Backend health and readiness definitions; readiness reports dependency
    status without exposing credentials.
  - Use structured logs with request/correlation IDs and sanitized exceptions.
  - Production scanner, Docker Compose/Helm packaging, SBOM and container scans
    remain release tasks, but their config and adapter boundaries must not be
    blocked by Milestone 1 design.
- Risks and mitigations:
  - A complete V001 is large: validate table groups incrementally while applying
    one clean initial migration as required by the specification.
  - PostgreSQL 18 is newer than many deployed environments: use supported SQL,
    pin drivers and verify migration/ORM behavior against the available 18.3
    container without depending on version-specific conveniences unnecessarily.
  - Manually initialized Keycloak state is not reproducible: implement an
    idempotent, secret-safe realm/client/bootstrap representation in a later
    deployment scope; Milestone 1 tests use controlled OIDC fixtures and verify
    the existing Development realm only in bounded integration checks.
  - Published-manifest and upload contracts could be mistaken as implemented
    integrations: keep their traceability status as foundation-only until the
    upload and RAG milestones pass real adapter tests.

### 6.30 Proposed Milestone: Live OIDC, Identity Sync, Projects and Permissions

- Plan prepared: 2026-06-23.
- Gate 2 confirmation: complete. Q-058 through Q-063 and CHG-078 record
  Peter's approved behavior decisions.
- Target requirements: `AUTH-001`, `AUTH-002`, `AUTH-005`, `PERM-001`,
  `PROJECT-001`, `SYS-001`, `API-001`, `DB-001`, `TEST-001`, and `OPS-001`.
- Scope:
  - Replace the formal `/login` fixture path with a live Keycloak Authorization
    Code + PKCE S256 flow, safe callback and logout. Add a client-only auth
    provider and API client that keep tokens in memory, restore through Keycloak
    SSO after reload, coalesce refresh, retry a 401 at most once and never turn a
    403 into a refresh loop.
  - Package the existing two-step NomoSmart login visual as a Keycloak 26 Theme
    so account/password and OTP remain Keycloak-hosted. Keep a clearly isolated
    component-preview/test path only if needed for frontend regression tests.
  - Add externalized public OIDC settings for frontend origin, issuer, client,
    audience, callback and logout URI. Configure/verify the Development public
    client `nomosmart-frontend` without committing a secret.
  - Complete the Keycloak Admin adapter with pagination and per-user group
    retrieval, then implement Celery worker/beat and PostgreSQL outbox dispatch.
    Reconcile users, groups, manager links and external-derived role memberships
    atomically after a complete snapshot; preserve manual roles and the last
    successful state on any failure.
  - Complete users, roles, role-user assignments, permission matrices and
    external-group mapping APIs with validation, pagination, audit, soft
    deactivation and optimistic concurrency.
  - Complete project detail/update/archive/member APIs. Project creation becomes
    atomic across selected models and initial members; owner/editor/viewer are
    the only role values, Owner governance stays synchronized, and the final
    active Owner cannot be removed.
  - Add Flyway V002 and matching ORM changes for sync trigger/snapshot metadata,
    safe role-membership provenance, permission concurrency and any project
    membership constraints required by these contracts.
- Explicitly out of scope:
  - Direct LDAP/AD connection or credential storage in NomoSmart, SCIM, social
    login, local passwords, external notification delivery and production Secret
    Manager integration.
  - Document/import/extraction/OpenSearch/Neo4j business implementation beyond
    authorization regressions needed to prove project scope.
  - Docker Compose and Helm completion; this milestone documents new variables
    and worker commands while deployable packaging remains a later milestone.
- Implementation order:
  1. Apply CHG-078 contracts to schemas/types and create Flyway V002.
  2. Build the frontend OIDC configuration, in-memory session state, callback,
     route guard, API wrapper and logout behavior using controlled OIDC fakes.
  3. Package the NomoSmart Keycloak Theme and verify the Development public
     client/redirect/audience configuration.
  4. Extend the Keycloak Admin adapter, implement snapshot reconciliation and
     transaction-level rollback, then wire Celery worker/beat/outbox dispatch.
  5. Complete user, role, manual role assignment, permission and group-mapping
     APIs, including concurrency and audit.
  6. Complete project CRUD/member/Owner APIs and project-scope dependencies.
  7. Run unit/API/component tests, clean migration tests, controlled worker
     integration, bounded Development Keycloak smoke and the coverage gates.
- API/data decisions:
  - Administrative lists use bounded offset pagination; sync run history uses a
    stable cursor. Mutation errors retain the standard API envelope.
  - User-synchronized identity fields are read-only to normal admin APIs; only
    local supplemental fields and NomoSmart status may be edited directly.
  - Role memberships record `manual` or `external_sync`; reconciliation changes
    only external-derived rows. External groups never own permissions directly.
  - Permission replacement and project/member changes require the current
    `lock_version`; stale requests return 409 without partial writes.
  - Project deletion is archive/soft delete. All project data access requires
    both RBAC operation permission and visible project scope.
- Test strategy:
  - Frontend unit/component: redirect state/nonce/PKCE, safe return path,
    callback failures, memory-only storage, reload restoration, single-flight
    refresh, one retry, logout, route protection and zh/en states.
  - Theme: Keycloak 26 template/resource packaging, account/password and OTP
    screens, error/accessibility/responsive states and proof that NomoSmart
    runtime receives no credentials.
  - Backend auth/API: JWT variants, disabled/unsynced/no-permission identities,
    user/role/permission/project authorization combinations, union semantics,
    soft delete, last Owner, stale lock, audit and secret-safe errors.
  - Worker: pagination, attribute validation, manager second pass, group mapping,
    manual-role preservation, removed-user deactivation only after a complete
    snapshot, mutual exclusion, retry/idempotency, rollback and crash recovery.
  - Integration: clean V001+V002 migration, PostgreSQL reconciliation, Celery
    eager/fake broker tests, controlled Keycloak fake and bounded local Keycloak
    login/admin smoke without relying on production services.
- Configuration/operations impact:
  - Add safe frontend public OIDC examples and backend Celery beat/worker
    settings. No frontend client secret is introduced.
  - Default identity schedule is `0 2 * * *` in `Asia/Taipei`; one worker with
    concurrency 2 remains the Development default, while PostgreSQL prevents
    overlapping full syncs.
  - Structured logs and audit contain run IDs and safe counts only, never tokens,
    authorization codes, verifier values, passwords, OTP or LDAP attributes not
    required for operations.
- Risks and mitigations:
  - Memory-only tokens complicate reload: use Keycloak SSO restoration and an
    explicit loading state before protected content/API calls render.
  - Snapshot reads can fail mid-pagination: separate collection/validation from
    the final PostgreSQL transaction and never deactivate from a partial set.
  - Role and Owner changes can lock out administration: protect system roles,
    reject the final project Owner removal and cover stale-write conflicts.
  - Theme/API configuration drift can break login: keep realm/client/theme
    bootstrap idempotent and verify discovery, redirect and audience in a bounded
    Development smoke check.

### 6.31 Proposed Scoped Milestone: AUTH-006 Secure Logout

Status: approved by Peter on 2026-06-26 and implemented.

Scope:

- Target requirement: `AUTH-006`, with supporting `AUTH-001`, `AUTH-003`,
  `API-001`, `DB-001`, `I18N-001` and `SEC-001` constraints.
- Add an authenticated Header user-name button dropdown with a localized Logout
  action. The menu must be keyboard reachable, close on Escape/outside selection,
  and remain compact with the existing operational Header style.
- Extend the frontend auth provider so Logout calls Backend once, clears
  memory-only tokens and transient OIDC artifacts, prevents duplicate logout
  clicks, then redirects through Keycloak end-session to `/login`.
- Add Backend `POST /api/v1/auth/logout`. It must validate the Bearer JWT,
  revoke session-bound server grants such as authentication-settings unlock,
  write token-safe audit, and record the access-token identity in a denylist
  until its `exp`.
- Add a Flyway V004 migration and SQLAlchemy model for `revoked_auth_tokens`.
  Store only irreversible token identity/digest, issuer, subject, audience,
  issued/expiration timestamps, reason, actor and safe metadata; never store
  token material.
- Update the JWT authentication path so every protected API denies tokens that
  match the denylist before constructing the user context or effective
  permissions.

Implementation approach:

1. Backend schema and model:
   - Add `V004__revoked_auth_tokens.sql` with unique token identity/digest,
     expiration index and audit-friendly metadata.
   - Add model/schema contract updates and migration tests.
2. Backend auth service/API:
   - Extract a deterministic, irreversible token identity from `jti` when
     present; otherwise use issuer/subject/audience/iat/exp plus SHA-256 digest
     of the token.
   - Add idempotent logout service behavior so repeated logout does not create
     duplicate rows or leak whether a token was previously revoked.
   - Add denylist lookup to the OIDC/JWT dependency used by protected routes.
   - Revoke active `identity_unlock_grants` for the same user/session context
     when available, and create audit without token values.
3. Frontend auth/menu:
   - Decode display name from ID token claims when available, with a safe
     fallback.
   - Replace the static Header `Peter` pill with a dropdown button and Logout
     menu item using lucide-react icons and zh/en i18n.
   - Ensure logout cleanup is memory-first, storage-free and duplicate-safe.
4. Tests:
   - Backend tests for valid logout, missing/invalid token, denylist replay,
     duplicate logout, no-`jti` fallback, expired cleanup eligibility,
     identity unlock revocation and secret-safe audit/error responses.
   - Frontend tests for menu open/close, keyboard behavior, localized Logout,
     backend logout call, token cleanup, no persistent storage writes,
     Keycloak end-session redirect and duplicate-click suppression.
   - Schema contract tests for V004 and `revoked_auth_tokens`.

Verification commands:

- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:plan`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:backend`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:frontend`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:lint`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:build`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh coverage:check`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh`
- `git diff --check`

Risks and boundaries:

- This scoped milestone does not create or store NomoSmart passwords and does
  not change Keycloak credential/MFA ownership.
- Denylist lookup adds one database check to protected API authentication; the
  table must be indexed by irreversible token identity and expiration.
- Keycloak refresh-token revocation may require a public-client-compatible
  endpoint path. If Keycloak rejects revocation for the public client, Backend
  denylist plus Keycloak end-session remains the mandatory security boundary and
  the rejection must be logged without token material.
- Human Browser E2E with a real Keycloak credential/OTP may still require a test
  user provided by Peter or an approved temporary test account.

### 6.32 Proposed Milestone 3: Live Frontend API Integration and Permission-aware UI

Status: approved by Peter on 2026-06-26 and implemented.

Scope:

- Target requirement: `UI-002`, with supporting `AUTH-001`, `AUTH-006`,
  `PROJECT-001`, `SYS-001`, `PERM-001`, `CONFIG-001`, `I18N-001` and `TEST-001`.
- Replace authenticated-shell fixture assumptions with live `/api/v1/auth/me`
  state. Header, route access and action availability use Backend-synchronized
  identity and permission union, not ID-token claims or hard-coded fixture names.
- Introduce a typed frontend API layer over the existing memory-only OIDC
  `apiFetch`. It must normalize loading, empty, error, forbidden, conflict and
  validation states without persisting tokens.
- Make navigation and key actions permission-aware:
  - Hide unauthorized high-level routes such as `/system` and `/projects`.
  - Show an in-page forbidden state for direct unauthorized URLs.
  - Disable actions that require create/edit/delete while preserving readable
    pages when the user has `view`.
- Connect `/projects` to live APIs:
  - `GET /api/v1/projects` for visible project cards and status tabs.
  - `POST /api/v1/projects` for the create-project modal.
  - `GET /api/v1/users` for enabled member candidates.
  - `GET /api/v1/models` for Chat and Embedding model choices.
  - Keep project-internal document/Pipeline/Graph/Chat data as clearly labeled
    fixtures, but use the real project id/title context when entering
    `/project/[id]/import`.
- Connect `/system` to live API data:
  - Users, roles, manual role users, role permission matrix, external group role
    mappings, models/OCR, identity settings and system parameters load from the
    Backend foundation APIs.
  - Enable safe saves for permission matrices, manual role users, external group
    mappings, system parameters and supported model operations that already have
    backend contracts.
  - Keep high-risk actions such as destructive role deletion, user disablement,
    model deactivation or project archival disabled/deferred unless the current
    UI has confirmation, optimistic lock handling and error recovery.
- Maintain the fixture/live boundary:
  - Remove fixture banners from sections that truly use live APIs.
  - Keep explicit demonstration labels on document import lists, Pipeline, Graph,
    Chat, approvals and reports until those domains receive live integration.

Implementation approach:

1. API client and session state:
   - Add typed payload/result definitions for `/auth/me`, users, roles,
     permissions, role users, external group mappings, models, identity settings,
     system parameters and projects.
   - Extend `AuthProvider` or a companion hook with `currentUser`, effective
     permission helpers and API-state helpers while keeping tokens memory-only.
   - Ensure 401/403/409/422 handling matches the spec: refresh only on 401, no
     refresh for 403, no optimistic success on 409.
2. Permission helpers:
   - Implement reusable `can(module, function, action)` helpers from Backend
     permission grants.
   - Add route/page guards and action-state helpers used by `AppShell`,
     `/projects` and `/system`.

     members; refresh the list after success and preserve modal state on errors.

     document cards as fixture data with a visible boundary label.
4. System Management UI:
   - Replace static users, roles, mappings, model rows, identity-settings summary
     and system parameters with live data loaders.
   - Wire selected safe saves to live APIs with lock_version/conflict handling.
   - Keep disabled/deferred controls visible only where they help communicate

5. Tests and documentation:

   - Update traceability and final verification with exact commands and known
     live-browser gaps.

### 6.33 Proposed Milestone 4: Live Document Upload, S3 Storage, Version Foundation and OCR Selection

Status: approved by Peter and implemented as Milestone 4 foundation on
2026-06-27.

Scope:

- Target requirements: `IMPORT-001`, `IMPORT-002`, `IMPORT-006`,
  `UPLOAD-SEC-001`, `DOC-001`, `OCR-001`, with supporting `PROJECT-001`,
  `PERM-001`, `CONFIG-001`, `SEC-001`, `AUDIT-001`, `I18N-001` and `TEST-001`.
- Convert project document import from fixture-only behavior to live Backend
  document upload and list APIs.
- Persist uploaded source files to S3/RustFS with salted-hash object names,
  canonical extensions and sanitized original filenames stored only in
  PostgreSQL.
- Create document and `v1.0` version records for each accepted upload.
- Preserve the quarantine/scanner state machine. Development may use the
  explicit disabled scanner stub, but extraction cannot start before accepted
  scan state.
- Implement single-file and multi-file branching:
  - one valid file creates a document/version and dispatches one extraction
    Pipeline skeleton immediately;
  - multiple files return ordered per-item results, preserve successful items,
    and leave each valid item in `ready_for_extraction` until manually started.
- Add OCR selection to extraction creation:
  - System Management AI Models can hold multiple active OCR models and one
    system default;
  - projects may define an optional project default OCR;
  - document/version Pipeline creation may choose an OCR model, falling back to
    project default and then system default;
  - multi-file upload uses one shared OCR choice in this milestone;
  - reliable text-layer documents skip OCR unless the user explicitly confirms
    forced OCR;
  - Pipeline creation snapshots `ocr_model_id`, `ocr_config_version` and
    non-sensitive OCR execution settings;
  - inactive or missing OCR models are rejected at Pipeline creation;
  - OCR models referenced by any Pipeline, document version or processing record
    cannot be permanently deleted.
- Implement only the Pipeline state foundation needed for upload/extraction
  handoff. Real parse/OCR/chunk/embedding/OpenSearch/Neo4j execution remains a
  later milestone unless represented by deterministic stubs.

Explicitly out of scope:

- Data-service import/synchronization, FTP/FTPS/SFTP/S3 remote adapters and
  scheduled sync.
- Cross-project document reference creation and copy-extraction.
- Real OCR execution, parser execution, chunking, embedding, OpenSearch writes,
  Neo4j writes, approval workflow, production index publication and RAG query.
- Enterprise malware scanner integration beyond the existing configurable
  scanner adapter/stub boundary.

Implementation approach:

1. Schema and models:
   - Add/extend tables for documents, document versions, source object metadata,
     scan state, pipeline runs and pipeline steps where not already present in
     the foundation schema.
   - Add OCR usage references and project default OCR fields or settings records
     so model deletion can be guarded by database checks.
   - Preserve UUID, UTC, optimistic locking and append-only audit conventions.
2. Upload validation and storage:
   - Stream upload files, enforce configured size, validate allowed extension,
     MIME and magic bytes, compute unsalted `content_sha256`, generate at least
     16-byte random salt, compute salted `storage_name_hash` and write the
     canonical S3 key.
   - Normalize and sanitize `original_file_name` for display/download only.
   - Use idempotency/outbox or equivalent cleanup so failed database writes or
     dispatch failures do not leave unmanaged objects.
3. Scanner and Pipeline handoff:
   - Model `quarantine`, `scan`, `accepted` and `rejected`; Development
     disabled mode transitions through the same states with a controlled stub.
   - Single valid uploads create and dispatch exactly one Pipeline skeleton
     after accepted scan state.
   - Multi-file uploads never auto-dispatch; manual extraction creates exactly
     one Pipeline for the chosen document version.
4. OCR selection:
   - Expose active OCR candidates and resolved defaults to the frontend.
   - Let upload/extraction actions send an optional `ocr_model_id` plus
     `force_ocr` confirmation.
   - Validate active OCR and forced-OCR confirmation on the Backend. Store
     snapshots on Pipeline creation and keep later model edits isolated.
   - Add guarded delete behavior for OCR models with clear conflict responses.
5. Frontend live integration:
   - Replace `/project/[id]/import` document-card fixtures with live list data
     while retaining clear fixture boundaries for downstream extraction detail,
     graph and chat pages.
   - Wire the existing upload modal to live upload APIs, including batch OCR
     selection, force-OCR warning, ordered per-item results, loading/error states
     and i18n.
   - Show `ready_for_extraction` without fake progress or ETA; manual extraction
     opens OCR selection and starts one Pipeline.
6. Tests and traceability:
   - Add backend unit/API tests for validation, storage naming, metadata,
     scanner gating, upload branching, OCR default resolution, forced OCR,
     guarded delete, permission checks, audit and recovery.
   - Add frontend tests for OCR selection UI, force warning, upload states,
     batch results, manual extraction and no-token persistence.
   - Update traceability, test plan and verification results after
     implementation.

Test strategy:

- Backend:
  - allowed/denied extension, MIME and magic-byte combinations;
  - configured size limit and empty/corrupt file rejection;
  - salted-hash object key uniqueness and original filename exclusion from S3;
  - successful single upload creates document, `v1.0`, scan state and one
    Pipeline skeleton;
  - mixed multi-file upload preserves successful siblings and returns ordered
    per-item failures;
  - manual extraction creates one Pipeline and rejects duplicates/inactive OCR;
  - system/project/document OCR default resolution and snapshot immutability;
  - forced-OCR confirmation and text-layer skip behavior;
  - referenced OCR delete denial and unreferenced delete success;
  - permission, project scope, audit and sanitized error behavior.
- Frontend:
  - upload modal validation, selected-file rows, clear-all, submit/complete
    states and per-item summaries;
  - OCR dropdown/default display, batch-shared OCR selection and forced-OCR
    warning/confirmation;
  - live document list, ready-for-extraction cards without fake Pipeline
    metrics, manual extraction action and forbidden/loading/error states;
  - Traditional Chinese and English i18n coverage.
- Integration:
  - Development RustFS bucket upload and cleanup path;
  - Development PostgreSQL transaction consistency;
  - Backend readiness remains green after schema changes.

- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor`

### 6.35 Milestone 6: Live Knowledge Extraction Pipeline and Document Version Lifecycle

Status: approved by Peter on 2026-06-27 and implemented.

Gate 2 confirmation:

- Peter confirmed the Milestone 6 scope on 2026-06-27:
  `1. A, 2. A, 3.A+B, 4. A, 5.A且限制3次, 6. A, 7.A`.
- This means Milestone 6 ends at staging / submission-ready output; it uses
  deterministic adapter/stub contracts first, includes Development OpenSearch
  staging writes through an adapter, uses rule-based auto-tagging, supports
  step-level retry up to three attempts, excludes data-service synchronization,
  and allows development extraction results that match the production contract.

Scope:

- Target requirements: `PIPE-001`, `PIPE-002`, `PIPE-004`, `PIPE-005`,
  `PIPE-006`, `PIPE-007`, `DOC-001`, `DOC-002`, `DOC-003`, `DOC-005`,
  `IMPORT-001`, `IMPORT-002`, `OCR-001`, `KNOW-001`, `KNOW-002`,
  `GRAPH-001`, `SEC-001`, `CONFIG-001` and `TEST-001`.
- Complete the live file-upload document extraction path from accepted source
  file to staging artifacts and submission-ready state.
- Keep staging strictly isolated from production: no production OpenSearch
  publication, no formal Neo4j graph sync, no active-version switch and no RAG
  production retrieval in this milestone.
- Preserve the approved Active/Working model: a new processing or
  submission-ready version does not affect the prior active version until a
  later publication milestone completes.

Backend scope:

1. Pipeline persistence and state machine:
   - Add or complete `pipeline_runs`, `pipeline_steps`, artifacts and status
     fields needed for per-document-version progress.
   - Enforce one mutually exclusive active working pipeline per document/version
     and reject duplicate manual starts with clear 409 responses.
   - Represent canonical steps through upload, parse, OCR, split, chunk,
     Markdown, tag, embedding, staging index, graph preview and submission
     preparation, while keeping later approval/publish/production steps defined
     but not executed.
2. Document version lifecycle:
   - Complete backend allocation for same-source re-extraction revision bumps
     and source-content update major bumps where the current file-upload source
     contract can support it.
   - Preserve prior active versions during new working versions.
   - Return Active and Working version summaries to the project document list
     and version-management APIs.
3. Extraction adapter contracts:
   - Replace deterministic development adapters for parser, OCR, chunking,
     Markdown, rule-based tagging, embedding, staging index and graph preview
     with real configured development/test implementations under `TEST-002`.
   - If historical adapter code remains temporarily, isolate it from runtime and
     passing test paths.
   - Keep adapter interfaces bound to real engine contracts and blocked/
     unavailable behavior when required services are missing.
4. OCR execution:
   - Use the Pipeline snapshot of `ocr_model_id`, config version and non-secret
     execution settings.
   - Skip OCR for reliable text-layer files unless force OCR was confirmed.
   - Execute the OCR step when forced and fail closed on OCR adapter errors.
5. OpenSearch staging:
   - Implement staging-index adapter and Development OpenSearch write path.
   - Use project/document/version scoped staging index identity or aliasing that
     cannot collide with production indexes.
   - Store staging document IDs / index references in PostgreSQL artifacts for
     later cleanup and review.
6. Retry and recovery:
   - Support step-level retry from failed steps up to three attempts.
   - Preserve valid completed artifacts where safe; invalidate downstream
     artifacts when an upstream step is rerun.
   - Record retry counts, sanitized errors, timestamps, status transitions and
     audit events.
7. API surface:
   - Add or complete APIs for pipeline start, run detail, step detail, retry,
     document list with live pipeline summaries, version list and extraction
     artifacts.
   - Keep authorization on the backend for project edit/extraction operations.

Frontend scope:

- Replace remaining project import and knowledge-extraction fixture status with
  live document / version / pipeline reads for file-upload documents.
- Show ready-for-extraction without fake progress, running pipelines with real
  percent/step detail, failed runs with sanitized error and retry controls, and
  submission-ready output with links into the extraction review page.
- Display Active versus Working version summaries in document cards and version
  management.
- Keep OCR selection behavior from Milestone 4, but show the actual snapshot
  used by the pipeline.
- Provide dense operational progress UI consistent with the NomoSmart style:
  text+icon status, expandable steps, visible retry limits, clear staging labels
  and no production/active implication before publication.

Explicitly out of scope:

- FTP / FTPS / SFTP / SSH / S3 data-service synchronization.
- Two-stage manager / Owner approval decisions.
- Publish action, Active switch transaction, production OpenSearch index
  creation or production graph sync.
- Real external parser/OCR/embedding model integration beyond replaceable
  adapter contracts and the local Development OpenSearch staging write.
- Production RAG query over the new staging outputs.

Test strategy:

- Backend unit/API tests:
  - pipeline state transitions, duplicate-run denial, start permissions,
    document-version summaries and Active/Working preservation;
  - deterministic parser/OCR/chunk/Markdown/tag/embedding/graph-preview adapter
    output and contract compatibility;
  - OCR skip versus force-OCR execution and snapshot immutability;
  - staging OpenSearch adapter success/failure with sanitized errors;
  - step-level retry from failed steps, downstream invalidation and hard stop
    after three attempts;
  - audit and no-secret/no-sensitive-content log behavior.
- Frontend tests:
  - ready/running/failed/submission-ready document-card states;
  - expanded step detail, retry controls, disabled retry after limit, staging
    labels and Active/Working version display;
  - live API client usage and fixture-boundary regression.
- Integration-style tests where practical:
  - single uploaded file starts one pipeline and reaches submission-ready with
    staging artifacts;
  - multi-file manual extraction creates exactly one pipeline for the selected
    document and rejects duplicate starts;
  - Development OpenSearch staging adapter writes and records index references,
    or reports a clear skipped/unavailable result when the local service is not
    available in the test environment.

  real adapters.

Status: approved by Peter on 2026-06-27 and implemented.

Gate 2 confirmation:

- Peter confirmed the preferred options on 2026-06-27 as
  `1A, 1A, 3A, 4A, 5A`.
- The second `1A` is interpreted as question 2 option A:
  direct API-key entry encrypted by Backend and Secret Ref are both supported.
- Confirmed decisions:
  - keep `Custom / Generic HTTP`;
  - support direct API-key entry or Secret Ref;
  - allow Ollama and vLLM without API key;
  - store provider-specific settings in existing `AIModel.config` JSON;
  - validate required provider fields on both frontend and backend.

Scope:

- Target requirements: `MODEL-001`, `SYS-002`, `SEC-001`, `I18N-001` and
  `TEST-001`.
- Update System Management AI Models create/edit UI so provider selection drives
  the visible fields, validation, helper text and normalized config payload.
- Keep the database schema unchanged. Provider-specific options are stored in
  the existing `config` JSON and secrets continue to use encrypted direct entry
  or `api_key_secret_ref`.

Provider support:

- OpenAI:
  - API Key or Secret Ref required;
  - Base URL, Model name, Organization ID, Project ID;
  - Chat / Embedding / Judge supported; optional embedding dimension.
- Gemini:
  - API Key or Secret Ref required;
  - Model name and optional API version;
  - Chat / Judge supported; Embedding possible when explicitly configured.
- Claude / Anthropic:
  - API Key or Secret Ref required;
  - Model name, optional Base URL and Anthropic-Version;
  - Chat / Judge supported.
- Ollama:
  - Base URL and Model name required;
  - API Key optional / usually absent;
  - timeout and Chat / Embedding capability hints.
- vLLM:
  - OpenAI-compatible Base URL and Model name required;
  - API Key optional;
  - OpenAI-compatible mode, timeout and Chat / Embedding / Judge capability
    hints.
- Custom / Generic HTTP:
  - Endpoint required;
  - API Key or Secret Ref optional according to the target service;
  - Headers JSON, Config JSON and timeout.

Backend scope:

1. Add provider-specific validation for create/update without changing the
   `ai_models` schema.
2. Normalize recognized provider fields into `config` keys such as
   `model_name`, `base_url`, `api_version`, `organization_id`, `project_id`,
   `headers`, `timeout_seconds`, `openai_compatible` and
   `embedding_dimension`.
3. Preserve current secret rules:
   - `api_key` is encrypted and never returned;
   - `api_key_secret_ref` may be stored;
   - omitted `api_key` during edit keeps the existing key.
4. Keep existing model type constraints and default uniqueness behavior.

Frontend scope:

- Replace the free-text Provider input in the System Management model modal with
  a provider selector.
- Render provider-specific fields and helper notes for OpenAI, Gemini,
  Claude / Anthropic, Ollama, vLLM and Custom / Generic HTTP.
- Keep an advanced JSON section for additional config, but prevent accidental
  plaintext API key storage in config JSON.
- Preserve dense System Management styling, permission gating and edit/create
  behavior.

Explicitly out of scope:

- Real outbound provider connection tests beyond the existing model test
  placeholder behavior.
- Adding a new table or migration for provider-specific settings.
- Building full runtime adapters for every provider in this scoped UI change.

Test strategy:
