## CHG-169 Pipeline Chat LLM Auto-tagging and Chunk Text Spacing

Scope:

- Replace the formal extraction pipeline's historical rule-based tagging
  success path with Chat LLM automatic tagging for v1.0.
- Apply automatic tagging to both document-version / article-level tags and
  every chunk-level tag.
- Cover all formal extraction sources: single-file upload immediate extraction,
  multi-file manual extraction, data service / HTTP API manual extraction,
  cross-project reference extraction, copy extraction in the target project,
  source-update re-extraction and same-source re-extraction.
- Run tagging after Markdown/chunk generation and before embedding / staging
  index work.
- Increase vertical spacing inside Knowledge Detail Chunk card text so
  paragraphs, lists and tables are easier to distinguish.

Implementation plan:

- Backend pipeline:
  - Update the extraction `tagging` step to resolve the current project active
    Chat LLM model and `PROMPT-001` System Prompt layers.
  - Generate document-level tags from the full document article / Markdown
    artifact and chunk-level tags from each chunk.
  - Persist tags through the existing canonical project-scoped tag model and
    document/chunk associations with `source = llm`, model id, prompt metadata,
    confidence when available, request id and audit-safe metadata.
  - Fail the `tagging` step closed when the Chat LLM model, credential, provider
    call, System Prompt resolver, canonical tag write or any chunk/document tag
    write fails. Preserve retryability and do not continue to embedding/staging
    as a successful extraction.
  - Remove or isolate deterministic/rule-based tagging from formal pipeline
    success; historical Milestone 6 rule tags may remain as old data only.
- Frontend UI:
  - Add more generous vertical rhythm to `.chunk-safe-markdown` and
    `.chunk-media-description` within Knowledge Detail Chunk cards.
  - Show Chunk auto-tagging results only once in the bottom tag row, hide
    historical `rule` tag links from current Knowledge Detail display, and show
    document-level tags directly in the Original/Markdown article area.
  - Move Chunk source/token/confidence metadata beside the top-left index badge
    as small gray text, and place Chunk body content in a visually separated
    content area so it does not stick to metadata or tag controls.
  - Label the upload/import Pipeline `auto_tag` step as AI auto tagging in the
    processing progress/current-step text and step-detail chips.
  - Preserve existing card header, UUID placement, metadata rows, tags, source
    selection, keyboard selection and graph preview behavior.
- i18n/API/schema:
  - Keep Traditional Chinese and English i18n aligned for the Chunk tag-result
    label and any document-tag visibility text.
  - Backend reuses existing canonical document/chunk tag APIs and metadata, and
    adds a schema migration only to change the `chunk_tags.source` default from
    historical `rule` to `llm`.

Verification:

- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor`.
- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace`.
- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved`.
- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh backend:syntax`.
- Run focused backend tests for pipeline Chat LLM document/chunk tagging,
  provider/config failures, retry and canonical tag writes if live prerequisites
  are configured; otherwise report blocked/unavailable under `TEST-002`.
- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:lint`.
- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:build`.
- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:frontend`.
- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh i18n:hardcoded`.
- Run `git diff --check`.

- Status: Approved by Peter on 2026-07-03.
- Approval wording: `Peter approves CHG-169 Pipeline Chat LLM Auto-tagging
  and Chunk Text Spacing`.

## CHG-172 Dense Knowledge Graph Progressive Disclosure Redesign

Scope:

- Redesign the document and project knowledge graph previews so dense Chunk and
  Tag data remains readable at default zoom.
- Preserve the CHG-171 type identity direction only where useful:
  - `Project`, `Document`, `Chunk` and `Tag` keep distinct icons/shapes.
  - Labels and metadata become zoom/hover/selection dependent rather than
    always visible.
- Keep graph API payloads, Neo4j data, authorization, active-version filtering,
  publication status rules, graph sync, zoom controls, pan, node drag, reset and
  selection behavior unchanged unless a UI-only helper state is needed.
- Replace the current crowded radial/card-like result with a calmer operational
  graph presentation:
  - Default view shows core structure and grouped summaries.
  - Dense Tag/Chunk rings are summarized or visually clustered.
  - Selected and hovered nodes reveal local relationships and full labels.
  - Complete node details live in the existing status/detail area instead of
    inside every node.

Implementation plan:

- Refine graph display semantics:
  - Introduce zoom-level detail thresholds for low, medium and high zoom.
  - At low zoom, hide most node labels and technical IDs; show only core
    Project/Document labels and group/count summaries.
  - At medium zoom, reveal selected path, neighboring labels and representative
    Chunk/Tag labels.
  - At high zoom, reveal more individual Chunk/Tag labels while retaining
    overlap protection.
- Add frontend-only grouping helpers:
  - Group dense Tags by readable label/category where possible, or by stable
    count buckets when no semantic category exists.
  - Group dense Chunks into document sections or ordered ranges when the graph
    would exceed the readable node threshold.
  - Keep individual node data available for selection/detail display; grouping
    is presentation-only.
- Update `DocumentGraphPreview`:
  - Use compact icon-first nodes by default.
  - Show document center, representative Chunk groups and Tag groups without
    an always-visible external label ring.
  - Reveal individual labels only for hovered, selected or high-zoom nodes.
  - Preserve content-type icons, neighbor highlighting, node drag and pan.
- Update `ProjectGraphPreview`:
  - Use the same progressive-disclosure rules for Project/Document/Chunk/Tag.
  - Avoid rendering dense active-project graphs as overlapping document/tag
    cards around the canvas edge.
  - Preserve live loading, empty, forbidden, unavailable and truncated states.
- Update shared graph styling:
  - Make nodes smaller, icon-led and label-light by default.
  - Reduce edge opacity and render non-neighbor edges as background context.
  - Add selected-path emphasis and readable hover/selected popover or inline
    label treatment without layout shift.
  - Remove oversized document-node/card-like label blocks and prevent the
    screenshot failure mode where labels form a crowded outer ring.
- Update frontend tests:
  - Assert graph components do not render all labels/technical IDs by default.
  - Assert zoom-level detail gating and selected/hovered label reveal hooks.
  - Assert dense Chunk/Tag grouping or summary helpers exist and remain
    presentation-only.
  - Assert Project/Document/Chunk/Tag still have distinct icons/shapes.
  - Assert no regression to card-heavy nodes, all-label radial rings, or
    overlapped default labels.
- Update `TEST_PLAN.md` and `TRACEABILITY.md` for `GRAPH-UI-002` before
  implementation starts.

Verification:

- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor`.
- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace`.
- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved`.
- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:lint`.
- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:build`.
- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:frontend`.
- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh i18n:hardcoded`.
- Run `git diff --check`.
- Start the frontend dev server after implementation and visually inspect the
  document and project graph previews at default, medium and high zoom.

Risks and mitigations:

- Grouping may hide useful data if it behaves like data loss; keep grouping
  presentation-only and reveal original nodes through zoom/selection/detail.
- Large project graphs may still be dense without backend bounded expansion;
  constrain this change to frontend readability and keep formal API contracts
  unchanged.
- Existing graph interaction tests may be brittle around markup changes; keep
  node buttons and event handlers stable while changing inner presentation.

Approval gate:

- Status: Approved by Peter on 2026-07-03.
- Approval wording: `Peter approves CHG-172 Dense Knowledge Graph Progressive
  Disclosure Redesign`.

## CHG-173 Knowledge Graph Ghost Node Removal and 300 Percent Zoom

Scope:

- Refine the CHG-172 document and project graph presentation so visible graph
  nodes remain clear and inspectable.
- Remove the current ghost-node effect caused by very low opacity display of
  non-current graph layers or non-related nodes.
- Raise the continuous graph zoom-in limit for both `DocumentGraphPreview` and
  `ProjectGraphPreview` to `300%`.
- Keep the following unchanged:
  - Graph API payloads and Neo4j graph data.
  - Authorization, active-version filtering, publication state and graph sync.
  - Progressive disclosure grouping semantics from CHG-172.
  - Pan, node drag, reset, hover reveal, selected first-degree highlighting and
    zoom percentage display.

Implementation plan:

- Update shared zoom constants:
  - Introduce or align explicit `MAX_ZOOM = 3` / `300%` constants in both graph
    preview components.
  - Keep button steps at `5%` and wheel zoom continuous with bounded deltas.
  - Ensure Zoom in buttons disable only at `300%`.
- Remove ghost-node rendering:
  - Stop multiplying visible display nodes by type-based opacity.
  - Treat grouped/hidden nodes as presentation-only data that is not rendered,
    instead of rendering them as very transparent nodes.
  - Keep a modest dimming state only for nodes outside the selected/hovered
    first-degree path, with opacity high enough to remain identifiable.
  - Keep edge dimming low-noise, but avoid edge/node combinations that imply
    invisible or disabled nodes.
- Adjust detail thresholds if needed:
  - Preserve structure/focus/detail levels while making the larger `300%`
    range meaningful.
  - Verify that high zoom still reveals individual Chunk/Tag labels and
    technical metadata through the existing label modes.
- Update CSS:
  - Remove or raise low-opacity node rules such as `0.22` when applied to
    visible nodes.
  - Keep label hiding based on `data-label-mode`, not by making entire nodes
    transparent.
- Update frontend static tests:
  - Assert both graph previews cap zoom at `3` / `300%`.
  - Assert no `1.35` graph zoom cap remains.
  - Assert graph nodes are not rendered through type-opacity fading.
  - Assert dimmed visible nodes use a legible opacity threshold.
  - Assert CHG-172 grouping/progressive disclosure hooks remain in place.
- Update `TEST_PLAN.md` and `TRACEABILITY.md` for the CHG-173 refinement.

Verification:

- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor`.
- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace`.
- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved`.
- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:lint`.
- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:build`.
- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:frontend`.
- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh i18n:hardcoded`.
- Run `git diff --check`.
- Keep or restart the frontend dev server and visually inspect that default
  graph nodes are not rendered as transparent ghosts and that zoom reaches
  `300%`.

Risks and mitigations:

- Removing node opacity may make dense graphs feel busier; rely on grouping and
  label hiding rather than transparency to manage density.
- A `300%` zoom range can make panning more important; keep existing pan and
  node-drag math tied to current zoom.
- Tests currently inspect source/CSS text; update them narrowly so they guard
  the visible behavior without requiring an exact visual implementation.

Approval gate:

- Status: Awaiting Peter approval before implementation or feature tests.
- Approval wording requested: `Peter approves CHG-173 Knowledge Graph Ghost Node
  Removal and 300 Percent Zoom`.

## CHG-174 Manual Role User Search and Draft Membership Clarity

Human confirmation:

- Confirmed by: Peter
- Confirmation date: 2026-07-04
- Confirmation summary: The manual role user modal should be redesigned so
  administrators can quickly search users and clearly understand who is already
  in the role, who is retained from external sync, and who is selected in the
  current unsaved edit session.
- Remaining open questions: none

Requirement IDs:

- `ROLE-UI-001`

Scope:

- Improve the System Management manual role user modal in
  `SystemManagementWorkspace` only.
- Add search/filter for active users by available identity fields: name, email,
  employee id or account identifier.
- Clearly show existing `manual` members, retained `external_sync` members,
  current-session pending additions and current-session pending removals.
- Add a persistent draft summary so selected additions/removals remain visible
  even when the search result changes.
- Keep the existing backend/API contract:
  - `GET /api/v1/roles/{role_id}/users` remains the source of current role
    membership.
  - `PUT /api/v1/roles/{role_id}/users` still receives only final manual
    `user_ids` plus `lock_version`.
  - `external_sync` relationships remain read-only and preserved by the
    backend.
- No database schema, API route or permission model change is expected.

Design direction:

- Use a compact enterprise list-picker pattern rather than a large checkbox
  block.
- Follow NomoSmart's calm green / white / cool gray operational style and
  lucide-react icons.
- Use visible text/badges in addition to color so membership state is not
  color-only.
- Keep the modal scannable: search at the top, summary directly below or beside
  it, result rows in a bounded scroll region, and existing save/cancel actions
  unchanged.

Implementation plan:

- Convert the role-user modal from uncontrolled checkbox defaults to a
  controlled draft state scoped to the open modal.
- Derive membership sets from live data:
  - Original manual member ids.
  - External-sync member ids.
  - Current draft manual member ids.
  - Pending additions: draft manual ids not in the original manual set.
  - Pending removals: original manual ids no longer in the draft set.
- Add role-user search state:
  - Filter active `liveUsers` by name, email and available identity fields such
    as employee id or account/raw id.
  - Show a localized no-results state with guidance to adjust the search.
  - Do not hide pending additions/removals from the draft summary when search
    results change.
- Redesign user rows:
  - Show name and secondary identity text in a stable row layout.
  - Show state badges for existing member, prepared add, prepared remove,
    external-sync retained and available.
  - Disable or otherwise protect external-sync-only membership from manual
    removal while still making its retained state visible.
  - Preserve keyboard-operable checkbox/list-row behavior and visible focus.
- Add a draft summary area:
  - Show counts for manual members and retained external-sync members.
  - Show compact chips or rows for prepared additions and removals.
  - Show a simple empty draft state when no unsaved membership changes exist.
- Preserve save behavior:
  - Reuse `saveRoleUsers` or an equivalent submit path that builds the same
    `user_ids` payload from the controlled draft.
  - Keep optimistic-lock conflict and forbidden handling unchanged.
- Update styles in `frontend/src/app/globals.css` using existing System
  Management naming conventions.
- Add Traditional Chinese and English i18n strings in
  `frontend/src/i18n/locales/zh.json` and
  `frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json`.
- Update frontend checks for the new modal structure and unchanged payload
  semantics.

Test strategy:

- Add focused frontend/static tests for `ROLE-UI-001`:
  - Search input and no-results state.
  - Matching by name/email/employee or account identity.
  - Existing manual member state.
  - Pending addition and pending removal states.
  - External-sync retained state and non-editability.
  - Draft summary remaining visible independent of search filtering.
  - Manual-only save payload semantics.
  - zh/en i18n key coverage.
- Run lint/build and, if the local dev server is available, visually inspect the
  modal at desktop and narrow widths.

Deployment and configuration impact:

- None expected. This is a frontend UI/interaction refinement under existing
  live API contracts.

Risks and mitigations:

- Controlled draft state could accidentally change the save payload; mitigate
  with static tests that assert only final manual user ids are submitted.
- External-sync users could be confused with editable manual users; mitigate
  with explicit retained badges, disabled manual removal affordance and summary
  counts.
- Search may hide context; mitigate with a draft summary that is independent
  from search results.
- Employee id/account fields may vary by live payload shape; search will use
  available typed fields and safe `raw` metadata without requiring a new API.
  If a required identity field is absent from the API contract, pause and update
  the API specification first.

Verification:

- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor`.
- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace`.
- Run `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor`.
- After plan approval, run `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved`.
- After implementation, run `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:lint`.
- After implementation, run `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:build`.
- After implementation, run `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:frontend`.
- After implementation, run `./HARNESS/harness.sh i18n:hardcoded`.
- Run `git diff --check`.

## CHG-177 Submit Review Success Feedback and Approval Workspace Redirect

Human confirmation:

- Confirmed by: Peter
- Confirmation date: 2026-07-04
- Confirmation summary: After Submit Review succeeds, users should see whether
  submission succeeded, see next approval-stage information, and then return to
  the Approval Workspace. Failed submissions must remain on the current
  submission page.
- Remaining open questions: none

Requirement IDs:

- `REVIEW-013`

Scope:

- Refine the frontend Submit Review route
  `/project/[id]/knowledge/[knowledgeId]/submit-review`.
- Use the existing `submitDocumentVersionReview` API response as the source of
  truth for submission result display.
- Show a successful submission state before navigation, including:
  - Success status.
  - Next stage as first-stage manager review.
  - `current_task_id` when returned by the backend.
  - Project/document/version display metadata already present in
    `ApprovalRequestResponse`.
  - A note that the item can be tracked in the Approval Workspace.
- Automatically navigate to `/approve` after a short, readable success state.
- On submission failure, keep the user on the submit-review page, show the safe
  backend error text, keep the evidence summary visible, and do not navigate.
- Keep backend API and database schema unchanged for this scope.

Out of scope:

- Adding readable manager / delegated assignee fields to the submit-review API.
  The current API returns `current_task_id`, status and display metadata but not
  next assignee display information. If product requires actual next-assignee
  name/email in the success state, update API specification and backend contract
  before implementation.
- Changing approval-task creation, review authorization, duplicate submission
  behavior, notifications or audit behavior.

Implementation plan:

- Replace the boolean success state with a typed submission result state based
  on `ApprovalRequestResponse`.
- On successful `submitDocumentVersionReview`:
  - Store the response.
  - Render a localized success panel/modal with next-stage details and
    tracking information.
  - Start a cleanup-safe redirect timer to `router.push("/approve")`.
  - Remove the current manual Back to Project / Go to Approval Center choice,
    or keep only non-primary text if needed without allowing project-list
    redirect as the main success path.
- On failed `submitDocumentVersionReview`:
  - Set `submitError` from the safe error message.
  - Do not set success state.
  - Do not start the redirect timer.
  - Leave document summary, extraction summary, graph summary and chat evidence
    visible.
- Add/adjust i18n strings in zh/en for:
  - Success result title.
  - Next-stage manager review label.
  - Current task tracking id.
  - Approval Workspace redirect message.
  - Failure-stays-on-page wording if needed.
- Add or update CSS only if needed for the success status panel layout, keeping
  the existing submission modal styling.
- Update frontend static checks in `frontend/tests/liveApi.test.mjs` to assert:
  - The submit API response is stored and used for success display.
  - Success path redirects to `/approve`.
  - Project import/list redirect is no longer used as the success path.
  - `current_task_id` or equivalent tracking detail is rendered.
  - Failure path sets `submitError` and does not set success state or redirect.

Test strategy:

- Focused frontend/static checks for `REVIEW-013` in the existing frontend
  suite.
- i18n key alignment and hard-coded text guard for new visible copy.
- Existing live API boundary checks remain sufficient for the backend contract
  because this scope does not change API behavior.

Deployment and configuration impact:

- None expected. This is a frontend flow refinement under the existing
  submit-review API.

Risks and mitigations:

- Auto-navigation might hide the success state too quickly; use a short readable
  delay and visible redirect message.
- Users may expect the next assignee name; mitigate by displaying the exact
  current task tracking information available from the API and documenting that
  readable assignee metadata needs a future API change.
- Redirect timers can fire after unmount; use effect cleanup for the timer.
- Failure handling must not accidentally navigate; add static checks for
  success-only redirect code.

## CHG-180 Approval Decision Persistence Repair and Workspace Redirect

Human confirmation:

- Confirmed by: Peter
- Confirmation date: 2026-07-04
- Confirmation summary: After an approval-detail decision succeeds, especially
  Owner approval, the system must actually close the approval task and should
  not leave the user on the completed task page. Investigation found existing
  data where the approval request and document version are approved, but the
  Owner approval task remains pending and can be approved repeatedly. The fix
  must repair decision persistence consistency, repair existing inconsistent
  data, show the decision result and next-step information, then return to the
  Approval Workspace. Failed decisions must remain on the current approval
  detail page.
- Remaining open questions: none

Requirement IDs:

- `REVIEW-014`
- `REVIEW-015`

Scope:

- Repair backend approval decision persistence for
  `/approvals/{approval_task_id}/approve` and
  `/approvals/{approval_task_id}/reject`.
- Refine the frontend Approval Detail route `/approve/[approvalTaskId]`.
- Apply the behavior to approval-detail decisions:
  - Manager approval success.
  - Owner approval success.
  - Manager or Owner rejection success.
- On successful backend decision:
  - Persist the current `approval_tasks` row as `approved` or `rejected`.
  - Persist `completed_at` and incremented `lock_version`.
  - Keep `approval_requests`, `document_versions`, review records, audit log
    and idempotency response consistent with the completed task.
  - Prevent a completed task from being accepted repeatedly as a new success.
- Repair existing inconsistent rows where request/version are already completed
  but the corresponding approval task is still pending, including the observed
  Owner task residue. The repair must be idempotent and auditable in the
  implementation notes or migration comments.
- On successful decision:
  - Show localized decision success text.
  - Show next-step context:
    - Manager approval: next stage is Project Owner review.
    - Owner approval: document version completed two-stage approval and is
      waiting for publish.
    - Rejection: task/request was rejected and can be tracked in the Approval
      Workspace.
  - Automatically navigate to `/approve` after a short, readable success state.
- On decision failure, optimistic-lock conflict, or already-completed task:
  - Stay on `/approve/[approvalTaskId]`.
  - Show the safe error reason.
  - Preserve the loaded evidence and decision context.
- Keep publish behavior unchanged unless a separate specification change is
  approved.
- Keep backend API shapes, schema, permission rules, notifications and publish
  contracts unchanged for this scope.

Out of scope:

- Changing Owner approval into automatic publish.
- Changing publication success behavior.
- Adding new assignee or next-task fields to approval decision responses.
- Fixing PipelineRunStep state transitions already covered by `CHG-179`.
- Rewriting the approval workflow model or introducing a new state machine.

Implementation plan:

- Backend persistence fix:
  - Remove or replace the premature `session.refresh(task)` after
    `approve_task` / `reject_task` so changed task status, `completed_at` and
    `lock_version` are not overwritten before commit while the session uses
    `autoflush=False`.
  - Flush after the decision mutation before building the idempotency response.
  - Ensure the response body reflects the completed task row.
  - Keep `_ensure_pending_task` authoritative so repeated non-idempotent
    decisions against completed tasks return the safe 409 path.
- Data repair:
  - Add an idempotent migration or repair script for existing inconsistent
    approval tasks where the request/version already reached `approved` or
    `review_rejected` but the task still says `pending`.
  - For Owner-approved residue, set the owner task to `approved`, set
    `completed_at` from the latest matching review record/audit timestamp when
    available, and increment or normalize `lock_version` so it no longer
    satisfies stale pending submissions.
  - Keep the repair conservative: only fix rows with matching review/audit or
    request/version terminal evidence; do not invent approvals for ambiguous
    data.
- Backend tests/static checks:
  - Add focused checks proving the approve route does not refresh stale task
    state before commit.
  - Add checks for Owner approval persistence: task status approved,
    completed_at present, request approved, current_task_id null and document
    version approved.
  - Add checks for repeated approval blocked after task completion.
  - Add checks that the repair migration/script targets inconsistent rows and is
    idempotent.
- Replace the current single string `result` state, or supplement it, with a
  decision outcome state that can distinguish success from error and carry
  next-step display content.
- Capture the current task `review_stage` and selected decision before calling
  `approveApprovalTask` or `rejectApprovalTask`, so the success message can
  show the correct next-step context even after the task completes.
- On successful `approveApprovalTask` / `rejectApprovalTask`:
  - Set a success outcome state with title, detail and redirect copy.
  - Close the decision modal and clear the comment.
  - Start a cleanup-safe timer that calls `router.push("/approve")`.
  - Avoid rendering active decision buttons for the completed task while the
    redirect state is visible.
- On failed `approveApprovalTask` / `rejectApprovalTask`:
  - Set an error outcome state with the safe error message.
  - Do not start the redirect timer.
  - Leave the decision page, evidence panels, workflow and loaded detail intact.
- Add localized zh/en strings for:
  - Manager approval submitted and next Owner-review context.
  - Owner approval submitted and approved-waiting-publish context.
  - Rejection submitted and tracking context.
  - Returning to Approval Workspace message.
- Reuse the existing operational result bar styling where practical; add only
  small scoped CSS if needed for success/error state clarity.
- Update frontend static checks in `frontend/tests/liveApi.test.mjs` to assert:
  - Decision success starts an automatic `/approve` redirect.
  - Owner approval success uses approved waiting-publish next-step copy.
  - Manager approval success uses Owner-review next-step copy.
  - Rejection success uses rejected tracking copy.
  - Error path sets an error state and does not redirect.
  - New i18n keys exist in zh/en.

Test strategy:

- Focused frontend/static checks for `REVIEW-014` in the existing frontend
  suite.
- i18n key alignment and hard-coded Traditional Chinese guard for new visible
  copy.
- Focused backend/static checks for `REVIEW-015` decision persistence and data
  repair. Live PostgreSQL verification should be run where local services are
  available; if unavailable, report blocked rather than mock-passing.
- Existing API client response shapes remain unchanged.

Deployment and configuration impact:

- Backend behavior fix plus an idempotent data repair artifact are expected.
- No new environment variables, services, ports or schema columns are expected.

Risks and mitigations:

- Repairing data too broadly could rewrite valid pending tasks; constrain the
  repair to rows with terminal request/version evidence plus matching review or
  audit evidence.
- Premature refresh could recur in reject or future decision endpoints; cover
  both approve and reject route patterns.
- Auto-navigation could hide the result too quickly; use the same short,
  readable redirect pattern as the approved Submit Review flow.
- Owner approval might be confused with publish; copy must explicitly say the
  version is approved and waiting for publish, not active.
- Error strings could accidentally trigger redirect if a generic `result` state
  is reused; distinguish success and error states in code and tests.
- Redirect timers can fire after unmount; use effect cleanup.

## CHG-182 Approval Workspace Pending Publish Visibility

Human confirmation:

- Confirmed by: Peter
- Confirmation date: 2026-07-04
- Confirmation summary: Peter, using `peter@example.test`, is a Project Owner
  with `Document.DocumentActivation.can_edit` and can publish the approved
  version, but the approved-unpublished document does not appear in `/approve`
  because the workspace only lists pending approval tasks and the user's own
  submissions. Publish availability must be driven by document-version status
  and publish authorization, not by whether the approval task is still pending.
- Remaining open questions: none

Requirement IDs:

- `REVIEW-017`

Scope:

- Add an Owner-visible pending-publish surface to the Approval Workspace
  (`/approve`) for approved, unpublished document versions.
- Include approved-unpublished versions in projects where the current user:
  - Is within project data scope.
  - Has a `project_owners` relationship for the project.
  - Has `Document.DocumentActivation.can_edit`.
- Ensure visibility does not depend on:
  - The current user being the submitter.
  - `approval_requests.owner_user_id` matching the current user.
  - `approval_requests.current_task_id` still being present.
  - A pending approval task still existing.
- Show enough row metadata for a Project Owner to identify and publish the
  item:
  - Project name.
  - Document title.
  - Version label.
  - Submitter display name/email.
  - Approval time.
  - Approved / waiting-publish status.
  - Document-version `lock_version`.
- Decouple publish enablement from approval task read-only state on Approval
  Detail:
  - Completed approval tasks remain read-only for approve/reject.
  - Publishing remains available when the version is `approved` and the user is
    authorized to publish.
- Preserve backend authorization as the final gate for publish.
- Preserve the existing publish endpoint and publish state transition.

Out of scope:

- Automatic publish after Owner approval.
- Changing the review approval workflow or approval-task persistence behavior
  already covered by `CHG-180`.
- Changing formal RAG, active manifest, OpenSearch or Neo4j publish semantics.
- Adding notification center behavior for pending-publish items.
- Redesigning project document list publishing controls.
- Allowing system administrators to publish without project Owner relationship
  unless a separate authorized publisher rule is specified later.

Implementation plan:

1. Backend API contract:
   - Add a small response schema for publishable approval workspace items, or
     extend an existing approval workspace response without breaking callers.
   - Include project/document/version identifiers and display metadata,
     submitter metadata, approval timestamp, version status and lock version.
   - Add a route such as `/approvals/pending-publish` that requires
     `Document.DocumentActivation.can_edit` and returns only approved,
     unpublished versions in current-user Owner projects.
   - Keep the query constrained to `context.visible_project_ids` and
     `project_owners.user_id = context.user_id`.
   - Exclude versions that already have `published_at`, `active` status or an
     active manifest for that version.
2. Frontend API client:
   - Add a typed client method for the pending-publish list.
   - Keep the existing publish client method unchanged.
3. Approval Workspace UI:
   - Load pending-publish rows when the user has
     `Document.DocumentActivation.edit`.
   - Add a compact operational panel under the existing pending/submission
     panels, or place it near the submission tracking panel, labeled as pending
     publish / waiting publish.
   - Render project, document, version, submitter, approved time and status.
   - Provide a clear action to open the related completed approval detail when
     a completed owner task exists, or to publish directly if the UI can do so
     safely with available lock version.
   - Ensure Peter's observed row is visible even though `current_task_id` is
     `null`.
4. Approval Detail publish gating:
   - Split approve/reject decision gating from publish gating.
   - Keep `canDecide` dependent on task pending and detail not read-only.
   - Make `canPublish` depend on version `approved` status, the user's
     `Document.DocumentActivation.edit` capability and publish submission
     state, not on approval-task read-only.
   - Preserve safe error display and optimistic-lock behavior.
5. i18n and styling:
   - Add zh/en keys for pending publish panel labels, empty state and action
     text if existing keys are insufficient.
   - Keep layout consistent with the dense Approval Workspace style and avoid
     nested card-heavy presentation.
6. Tests/static checks:
   - Add backend checks for query scope:
     - Owner with `DocumentActivation.edit` sees approved unpublished versions.
     - Non-submitter Owner still sees the item.
     - `current_task_id = null` does not hide the item.
     - Non-Owner or user lacking publish permission does not receive items.
   - Add frontend checks for:
     - Pending-publish API client and workspace loading.
     - Pending-publish panel rendering and metadata.
     - Completed approval detail publish button remains available for
       authorized users when version status is `approved`.
     - Approve/reject buttons remain disabled for completed tasks.
     - zh/en i18n coverage.

Test strategy:

- Focused backend/static or live-safe API query checks for `REVIEW-017`.
- Frontend static/contract tests in the existing frontend suite.
- Run lint/build because this touches typed API responses and route JSX.
- Run i18n hard-coded text check if new UI copy is added.
- Full `test:backend` remains subject to TEST-002 live prerequisites; if the
  shell lacks live environment variables, report it as blocked/unavailable
  rather than mock-passing.

Deployment and configuration impact:

- No schema migration expected.
- No new environment variables, services, ports or deployment config expected.
- No data repair expected; the current observed row is already correctly
  approved and unpublished.

Risks and mitigations:

- Risk: listing all approved unpublished versions too broadly could expose
  cross-project data. Mitigation: require both visible project scope and
  explicit `project_owners` membership for the current user.
- Risk: administrators with global-looking RBAC but no Project Owner
  relationship could see publish actions. Mitigation: require
  `project_owners` in the list API and keep publish endpoint Owner check.
- Risk: completed approval detail could accidentally re-enable approve/reject.
  Mitigation: keep separate `canDecide` and `canPublish` checks and test both.
- Risk: direct publish from workspace could duplicate complex publish feedback.
  Mitigation: prefer linking to the existing detail/publish path unless the
  implementation can safely render publish result in the workspace.
- Risk: stale version lock could cause publish failure. Mitigation: expose and
  use version `lock_version`, and display safe backend error if stale.

- Before implementation, run `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace`.
- Before implementation, run `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor`.

- After implementation, run `./HARNESS/harness.sh backend:syntax`.
- After implementation, run focused backend pending-publish checks.

- After implementation, run `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:build`.

## CHG-181 Approval Evidence Viewer Parity with Knowledge Detail

Human confirmation:

- Confirmed by: Peter
- Confirmation date: 2026-07-04
- Confirmation summary: The Approval Detail / approval evidence aggregation page
  must present document article and chunk results consistently with Knowledge
  Detail. The page is for review evidence, so it must remain read-only and must
  not expose Knowledge Detail editing interactions such as manual chunking,
  document/chunk tag add/delete, auto-tagging or chunk editing.
- Remaining open questions: none

Requirement IDs:

- `REVIEW-016`
- `VIEWER-001`
- `CHUNK-UI-001`
- `MOCK-003`

Scope:

- Refactor the Approval Detail document article and chunk evidence area so it
  visually and behaviorally matches Knowledge Detail's two-pane evidence
  viewer.
- Keep the existing Approval Detail route and approval decision workflow.
- Use live approval evidence only:
  - `document_layout` / structured original document evidence when available.
  - Markdown artifact/source text when available.
  - Chunk source mapping/source anchors.
  - Chunk metadata, technical id, content type, token count, confidence and
    tags.
  - Document-level tags if they are already available in the approval detail
    payload or can be safely mapped from existing evidence.
- Preserve read-only review behavior:
  - No manual chunking popover or selection toolbar.
  - No tag add/delete inputs or auto-tag buttons.
  - No chunk content/title editing controls.
  - No mutation API calls from the evidence viewer.
- Preserve bidirectional navigation:
  - Clicking/selecting a source block highlights and scrolls all matching
    chunks.
  - Clicking/selecting a chunk highlights and scrolls the matching source block
    in the current original/Markdown view.
  - Selection toggle semantics remain consistent with Knowledge Detail.
- Preserve safe rendering:
  - Use shared `SafeMarkdown` / `SafeMarkdownInline` rendering for text blocks,
    Markdown document content and text chunks.
  - Do not use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.
  - Retain pipe-table, list, heading cleanup and citation-marker display.
- Preserve live-only behavior:
  - No fixture, hard-coded sample paragraphs, fake Markdown, or chunk-concat
    fallback pretending to be original evidence.
  - Missing layout/Markdown/source mapping should render explicit unavailable,
    partial or missing-source states aligned with Knowledge Detail.

Out of scope:

- Changing approval state, approve/reject/publish behavior, permissions or
  backend workflow transitions.
- Adding edit capability to Approval Detail.
- Changing Knowledge Detail authoring behavior.
- Introducing a new approval API unless the current payload lacks required
  live evidence fields; any API addition must be read-only and traceable to
  `REVIEW-016`.
- Reworking graph preview, chat evidence or validation evidence beyond spacing
  adjustments needed around the evidence viewer.

Implementation plan:

1. Extract or reuse Knowledge Detail rendering primitives:
   - Move reusable helpers such as layout block/page rendering, Markdown block
     rendering, chunk display mapping and read-only chunk card rendering into a
     shared component module under `frontend/src/components`.
   - Keep Knowledge Detail-specific editing code in the route page or a clearly
     separated editable wrapper.
2. Replace the old Approval Detail chunk card markup:
   - Use the same chunk index badge, secondary metadata row and right-aligned
     technical id hierarchy as Knowledge Detail.
   - Render text chunk content with `SafeMarkdown` in the same content shell.
   - Keep image/table/chart preview behavior aligned with existing Knowledge
     Detail conventions.
   - Display tags as read-only chips with source labels when tag source detail
     exists; otherwise preserve live legacy tags as read-only fallback chips
     without edit controls.
3. Replace the old Approval Detail document article rendering:
   - Render structured `document_layout.pages[]` when present.
   - Preserve the Markdown original-file exception when approval evidence
     exposes enough metadata; otherwise render Markdown artifact in Markdown
     mode only.
   - Use the same source target classes and selected-state styling as Knowledge
     Detail.
4. Normalize approval evidence mapping:
   - Map Approval Detail `chunks` to the shared viewer chunk model without
     replacing UUIDs with artificial `C-001` identities for technical id.
   - Keep display index from `chunk_index`.
   - Resolve source anchors from source mapping using the same priority as
     Knowledge Detail.
   - Keep source labels page-aware where available.
5. Update Approval Detail route integration:
   - Pass live detail evidence into the shared read-only viewer.
   - Preserve loading/error/read-only/decision states outside the viewer.
   - Keep the graph preview and decision bar behavior unchanged.
6. Styling:
   - Reuse existing `.article-viewer`, `.document-page`, `.source-target`,
     `.extraction-chunks`, `.chunk-card`, `.chunk-title-row`,
     `.chunk-index-badge`, `.chunk-safe-markdown` and tag chip styles where
     possible.
   - Remove or narrow ApprovalEvidenceViewer-only styles that create a
     separate visual language.
   - Keep panes independently scrollable and responsive.
7. Tests/static checks:
   - Add focused frontend checks that Approval Detail imports/uses shared
     Knowledge Detail evidence rendering primitives.
   - Assert Approval Detail no longer renders the old `id · title` chunk header
     pattern.
   - Assert Approval Detail does not include manual chunking, tag add/delete,
     auto-tagging, or chunk editing controls.
   - Assert `SafeMarkdown` is used for approval chunk/document Markdown content.
   - Assert source/chunk bidirectional selection hooks remain present.
   - Assert zh/en i18n keys remain aligned if new empty/missing-state copy is
     added.

Test strategy:

- Use existing frontend static/contract tests for fast coverage of the route
  and component structure.
- Run frontend lint/build because this touches shared React/TypeScript
  components and CSS.
- Run `i18n:hardcoded` if new user-facing strings are added.
- Backend checks are only needed if the current approval detail API lacks
  required read-only evidence fields and a backend mapping addition is made.
  If no backend change is required, run backend syntax only as a broad sanity
  check if time permits.

Deployment and configuration impact:

- No new runtime configuration, environment variables, services, ports or
  migrations are expected.
- If an API read-only field is added, it remains backward-compatible and uses
  the existing approval detail authorization path.

Risks and mitigations:

- Risk: extracting Knowledge Detail helpers could accidentally pull editable
  behavior into Approval Detail. Mitigation: create read-only primitives first
  and keep editing controls in Knowledge Detail-specific wrappers.
- Risk: Approval Detail may not currently receive all Knowledge Detail layout
  metadata. Mitigation: inspect API payload first; add only read-only mapping
  fields if required.
- Risk: CSS changes could regress Knowledge Detail. Mitigation: reuse existing
  classes, avoid broad selector rewrites and run frontend build/tests.
- Risk: source anchors may differ between approval and knowledge payloads.
  Mitigation: preserve fallback anchors but show missing-source state instead
  of fake original evidence when mapping is unavailable.
- Risk: shared component extraction may be larger than needed. Mitigation:
  keep extraction focused on viewer rendering, not page-level workflow logic.

## CHG-184 Project Chat Conversation Delete

Gate 2 confirmation:

- Peter confirmed the understanding on 2026-07-04 with `OK`.
- Confirmed behavior: delete an entire project-level Project Chat
  conversation, not a single turn; deletion is soft-delete/archive behavior;
  already-submitted review evidence and audit/report traceability remain
  preserved.

Scope and requirement IDs:

- Primary requirement: `RAG-013`.
- Related requirements: `RAG-004`, `RAG-008`, `PERM-001`, `SEC-001`,
  `AUDIT-001`, `I18N-002` and `TEST-001`.
- Product surface: project-level Chat Test modal conversation history.
- Backend surface: Project Chat conversation list/get/delete APIs and
  `chat_records` persistence.
- Out of scope: deleting a single question/answer turn, deleting document-level
  chat records, deleting submitted approval evidence, hard-deleting
  `chat_records`, or changing report retention rules.

Backend approach:

1. Inspect existing `chat_records` schema and model fields to choose the
   smallest compatible soft-delete representation. Prefer existing nullable
   metadata/status fields if one already captures archived/deleted state;
   otherwise add an additive migration/model field such as `deleted_at` and
   `deleted_by`.
2. Add a project-scoped conversation delete endpoint, likely
   `DELETE /projects/{project_id}/chat/conversations/{conversation_id}`.
3. Enforce authorization on the backend:
   - current user must be able to view/use Project Chat for the project;
   - the conversation must belong to the project;
   - the conversation must have been created by the current user;
   - cross-project, cross-user, missing and already-deleted conversations must
     return safe structured errors.
4. Soft-delete all `chat_records` sharing the same project/conversation/current
   user scope without deleting citations, feedback, validation links or
   downstream review evidence.
5. Update list/get conversation APIs to exclude soft-deleted conversations from
   normal Project Chat history. Existing approval evidence hydration and
   reporting/audit paths must not depend on the visible conversation list for
   retained evidence.
6. Record an audit event for successful conversation deletion, including
   project id, conversation id, row count and request id, without logging prompt,
   question, answer or document content.

Frontend approach:

1. Add typed API client support for deleting a project chat conversation.
2. In `ProjectChatTest`, add a subtle trash icon action to each conversation
   history row with hover/focus feedback, accessible label and no accidental row
   switch when the delete action is clicked.
3. Show a confirmation popup/modal before deleting. Copy must explain that the
   conversation will be hidden from history while audit/review traceability is
   retained.
4. On successful deletion:
   - remove the conversation from local history;
   - if it was active, switch to the newest remaining conversation;
   - if none remains, show a blank new-conversation state with current
     available document scope;
   - keep the modal open and preserve document selection/search state.
5. On failure, keep the deleted conversation visible/active and show a localized
   error message.
6. Add Traditional Chinese and English i18n strings for delete action,
   confirmation, cancel/confirm, busy state and failure message.

Test strategy:

- Backend focused checks:
  - delete endpoint marks a whole conversation deleted without hard-deleting
    chat records;
  - list/get APIs exclude deleted conversations;
  - cross-project and cross-user deletes are denied;
  - already-deleted conversation delete is safe and does not alter unrelated
    records;
  - audit event is created without sensitive content.
- Frontend focused checks:
  - Project Chat history rows expose a delete icon/action and confirmation
    modal;
  - confirm calls the delete API, cancel does not;
  - deleting active conversation selects the newest remaining conversation or
    blank state;
  - failed delete rolls back/keeps visible state;
  - zh/en i18n keys are present and no hard-coded Traditional Chinese is added.

Deployment and configuration impact:

- No new runtime environment variables or external services are expected.
- If the selected soft-delete representation requires schema support, add a
  backward-compatible SQL migration and model update.

Risks and mitigations:

- Risk: deleting conversations could remove evidence used by approval pages.
  Mitigation: soft-delete only and keep approval evidence hydration tied to
  stored records, not visible Project Chat history.
- Risk: users may delete someone else's conversation if authorization is too
  broad. Mitigation: filter by project id, current user id and conversation id
  in one scoped backend operation.
- Risk: UI click conflicts with selecting a conversation row. Mitigation: make
  the delete button stop propagation and require confirmation.
- Risk: schema migration could be unnecessary if an existing field suffices.
  Mitigation: inspect schema first and choose the smallest compatible path.

Verification:

- Before implementation, run `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace`.
- Before implementation, run `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor`.
- After plan approval, run `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved`.
- After implementation, run `./HARNESS/harness.sh backend:syntax`.
- After implementation, run focused backend Project Chat conversation delete

- After implementation, run `cd frontend && node --test tests/liveApi.test.mjs`

## CHG-185 / CHG-186 Chat History Isolation and Review Extraction Lock

Gate 2 confirmation:

- Peter confirmed the understanding on 2026-07-04 with `OK`.
- Confirmed CHG-185 behavior: Project Chat history, Document Chat Test history
  and document-version-specific Document Chat Test history must be independent.
- Confirmed CHG-186 behavior: document versions in manager review, Owner
  review or approved waiting-publish state are locked against extraction/edit
  changes but remain readable; users continue work through a newly uploaded
  source version or a new extraction revision based on a rejected version.

Scope and requirement IDs:

- Primary requirements: `RAG-014` and `REVIEW-019`.
- Related requirements: `RAG-002`, `RAG-004`, `RAG-008`, `RAG-012`,
  `RAG-013`, `REVIEW-016`, `REVIEW-017`, `DOC-002`, `DOC-003`, `PIPE-004`,
  `TAG-002`, `PERM-001`, `AUDIT-001`, `I18N-002` and `TEST-001`.
- Product surfaces:
  - Project Chat modal conversation history, CSV validation and conversation
    delete/download actions.
  - Document Chat Test page, CSV validation, submission evidence and approval
    evidence.
  - Project document list, Knowledge Detail extraction/reprocess/edit controls
    and backend extraction/edit APIs.
- Out of scope:
  - Changing formal retrieval ranking, answer generation quality, model
    selection, graph design or publish behavior.
  - Hard-deleting historical chat records, approval evidence, rejected
    evidence, chunks, tags or audit records.
  - Allowing in-place edits to rejected, submitted or approved evidence.

Backend approach for `RAG-014`:

1. Inspect the current `chat_records`, validation-run and conversation API
   schema after CHG-184 to choose the smallest durable scope representation.
   Prefer a single additive discriminator such as `scope_mode`,
   `conversation_surface` or equivalent, aligned with existing request payloads
   that already distinguish `published` and `document_staging`.
2. Add a backward-compatible migration/model/schema update when no persisted
   discriminator exists. New records must store:
   - conversation surface / scope (`project_chat` / `published` versus
     `document_chat_test` / `document_staging` or equivalent);
   - exact `project_id`;
   - exact `document_version_id` for document-level records;
   - fixed selected document version ids for project-level records;
   - existing conversation id, creator, citations, feedback and soft-delete
     fields.
3. Persist scope on every new interactive chat answer, CSV validation item and
   feedback update. Document-level writes must bind to exactly the current
   document version; project-level writes must bind to the selected active
   published manifest versions.
4. Update Project Chat list/get/delete/download endpoints to fail closed to
   project-level published records only. They must not return, delete or export
   `document_staging` records even when project, user and conversation id match.
5. Update Document Chat Test history/download, submit-review evidence hydration
   and approval evidence hydration to fail closed to document-level staging
   records for the exact `document_version_id`.
6. Handle legacy records without reliable scope/version classification
   conservatively: preserve them for audit/report traceability but do not
   auto-display them in project, document or version history lists unless a
   migration can classify them with high confidence.
7. Keep CHG-184 soft delete scoped to visible project-level Project Chat
   conversations so deleting a project conversation cannot hide document-level
   evidence.

Backend approach for `REVIEW-019`:

1. Add a shared backend guard for review-locked statuses:
   `pending_manager_review`, `pending_owner_review` and approved
   waiting-publish. Treat the guard as status-based so existing rows become
   protected without data migration.
2. Apply the guard to all endpoints that can alter extraction evidence for the
   locked version, including extraction start/reprocess, manual chunk changes,
   tag add/delete/auto-tag actions, staging index rebuild/retry and graph
   preview rebuild/retry paths discovered during implementation.
3. Return structured safe conflict/locked errors with a stable code and
   localized frontend-facing message mapping. Do not mutate artifacts, chunks,
   tags, pipeline steps, staging index state, graph preview state or approval
   evidence when the guard blocks a request.
4. Keep read endpoints available subject to existing authorization, including
   Knowledge Detail evidence, document content, Markdown, chunks, tags, graph
   preview, chat evidence, review progress and pending-publish status.
5. Do not block uploading a new source version for the same document when the
   user has permission; the new version gets its own document-version id and
   independent Pipeline.
6. For `review_rejected`, preserve the rejected version as immutable evidence.
   Any "extract again" path must create a new extraction revision/Pipeline
   rather than overwriting the rejected version.
7. Record sanitized audit events for blocked mutation attempts where the
   repository already audits comparable governance-sensitive actions, without
   logging document content, prompt text or extracted text.

Frontend approach:

1. Update typed API contracts for any new scope discriminator, locked/error
   code, read-only reason or history filtering fields.
2. Project Chat modal:
   - load and display project-level published conversations only;
   - keep existing delete/download behavior scoped to visible project
     conversations;
   - show a true empty state when no project-level history exists, rather than
     borrowing document-level records.
3. Document Chat Test and submit-review pages:
   - load only the current `document_version_id` history/evidence;
   - keep histories independent across versions of the same document;
   - ensure CSV download and submitted evidence use the exact version scope.
4. Approval detail:
   - hydrate chat/CSV evidence using the submitted task's exact document version
     and document-level staging scope only.
5. Project document list and Knowledge Detail:
   - show a compact locked read-only state for versions in review or approved
     waiting-publish;
   - disable extraction/re-extraction, manual chunk, tag mutation and rebuild
     controls for the locked version;
   - keep content and evidence readable;
   - preserve or expose paths to upload a new source version and, for rejected
     versions, start a new extraction revision.
6. Add Traditional Chinese and English i18n strings for locked state titles,
   reasons, next-step helper text and safe conflict errors.

Test strategy:

- Backend focused checks for `RAG-014`:
  - project history excludes document-staging records;
  - document history excludes project-level records;
  - document `v1.0` and `v2.0` histories remain isolated;
  - project conversation delete does not hide document-level evidence;
  - CSV/download and submit-review evidence query exact scope;
  - legacy unclassified records are retained but hidden from normal history.
- Backend focused checks for `REVIEW-019`:
  - locked statuses reject extraction/reprocess/edit/tag/rebuild mutation
    endpoints without data changes;
  - read endpoints still return authorized evidence;
  - uploading a new source version remains available and creates an independent
    version/Pipeline;
  - rejected-version extraction creates a new revision and leaves rejected
    evidence immutable.
- Frontend focused checks:
  - Project Chat empty/history state does not show document-level records;
  - Document Chat Test history does not show project records or other versions;
  - submit-review and approval evidence render only the exact version's chat
    evidence;
  - locked Knowledge Detail/project list states disable mutation controls,
    preserve read-only viewing and show localized reason/next-step copy.
- Static/i18n checks:
  - zh/en locale keys remain aligned;
  - no new hard-coded Traditional Chinese appears outside locale files.

Traceability and test-plan updates after approval:

- Add/update `TRACEABILITY.md` rows for `RAG-014` and `REVIEW-019`, mapping
  requirements to backend routes, frontend components, tests and harness
  commands.
- Add/update `TEST_PLAN.md` sections covering project/document/version chat
  isolation and review-state extraction locks.

Deployment and configuration impact:

- No new runtime environment variables or external services are expected.
- A backward-compatible SQL migration is likely for `chat_records` scope
  persistence if the existing schema lacks a durable discriminator.
- Existing in-review and approved-unpublished versions become locked by their
  current status immediately after deployment.
- Existing legacy chat records without reliable scope/version classification may
  disappear from normal history lists while remaining available for audit/report
  traceability.

Risks and mitigations:

- Risk: hiding unclassified legacy chat records may surprise users who expected
  to see old history. Mitigation: fail closed for privacy/evidence correctness
  and document the legacy/unclassified behavior.
- Risk: over-broad locks could prevent new-version work. Mitigation: scope the
  lock to the submitted version id and explicitly allow new uploaded versions.
- Risk: under-broad locks could mutate submitted evidence. Mitigation: centralize
  backend status guards and add endpoint-level regression checks.
- Risk: Project Chat delete from CHG-184 could accidentally affect document
  evidence. Mitigation: add surface/version filtering to delete queries and
  tests.
- Risk: frontend disabled controls alone are insufficient. Mitigation: backend
  mutation guards are the source of truth; frontend only improves clarity.

## CHG-187 Document Reactivation Success Notification

Understanding:

- Peter confirmed that when a disabled document is changed back to enabled, the
  UI should show a popup notification.
- The behavior is limited to a persisted document lifecycle transition from
  `inactive` to `active` in the project document list.
- The notification is a lightweight localized popup/toast after backend success,
  not an extra confirmation modal before the operation.
- Existing lifecycle failure behavior remains unchanged: permission errors,
  optimistic-lock conflicts and API failures must not show a success
  notification.

Scope:

- Requirement: `DOC-007`.
- Change record: `CHG-187`.
- Frontend project import page lifecycle UX only.
- No backend API, database schema, permission model, deployment config or
  migration change is expected.

Out of scope:

- Changing inactive/delete confirmation flows.
- Changing document lifecycle authorization or backend state-machine rules.
- Adding a global notification center event.
- Showing success notifications for unrelated status changes unless a future
  requirement adds them.

Approach:

1. Add localized Traditional Chinese and English strings for the reactivation
   success title/message and dismiss action if needed.
2. Add a small Project Import page notification state for lifecycle success
   feedback.
3. In the existing live `inactive` to `active` update path, set the success
   notification only after `updateDocumentLifecycle` returns successfully.
4. Keep the existing error path untouched so failed reactivation continues to
   show the current safe error and leaves the document status unchanged.
5. Render the notification as a compact NomoSmart-style popup/toast with
   accessible status semantics, visible close control or bounded auto-dismiss,
   and no page navigation.
6. Add or update focused frontend regression coverage so the success and
   failure paths are both explicit.

Test strategy:

- Update `frontend/tests/liveApi.test.mjs` or the narrowest existing frontend
  contract test to verify:
  - inactive-to-active success triggers the notification state/copy;
  - failed lifecycle update does not show success copy;
  - the existing lifecycle API payload remains unchanged.
- Run i18n/static checks because user-visible copy is added.
- Run frontend lint/build for the touched UI code.

Verification:

- Before implementation, run `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor`.
- Before implementation, run `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace`.
- Before implementation, run `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor`.
- After plan approval, run `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved`.
- After implementation, run `cd frontend && node --test tests/liveApi.test.mjs`.
- After implementation, run `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:lint`.
- After implementation, run `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:build`.
- After implementation, run `./HARNESS/harness.sh i18n:hardcoded`.
- Run `git diff --check`.

Risks and mitigations:

- Risk: users may see a success notification before persistence is confirmed.
  Mitigation: set the notification only after the awaited lifecycle API returns.
- Risk: notification text could duplicate existing error/success surfaces.
  Mitigation: restrict it to the specific inactive-to-active success path.
- Risk: adding visible text without locale coverage could regress i18n.
  Mitigation: add matching zh/en locale keys and run the i18n guard.

Approval gate:

- Status: Approved by Peter on 2026-07-04 with `ＯＫ`; implemented and
  verified.
- Requested approval wording: `Peter approves CHG-187 Document Reactivation
  Success Notification`.

Implementation notes:

- Added Project Import lifecycle notification state and an accessible
  `lifecycle-notice-popup` toast.
- The toast is set only after the awaited live lifecycle update succeeds and
  only for `inactive` to `active`.
- Existing failure paths keep the current safe error handling and clear stale
  lifecycle notices before starting a new status change.
- Added zh/en locale strings and focused frontend regression checks.

Verification completed:

- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved`
- `cd frontend && node --test tests/liveApi.test.mjs`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:lint`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:build`

## CHG-202 Plan: REL-006 / UPLOAD-SEC-001 / CONFIG-002 / VERSION-002 Completion

Understanding confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-10 with `Ok`.

CHG-247 supersession notice: this historical plan remains evidence of the work
performed in CHG-202, but every global/cross-project graph access instruction
below is non-executable and cannot be reused as current acceptance. `GRAPH-008`
requires only Backend-authorized Project/Document graph APIs and UI; the former
global routes and popup entry must be removed.

Specification status:

- `SPECIFICATION.md` updated for CHG-202.
- `SPEC_CHANGELOG.md` records CHG-202.
- This plan covers four approved release-gap items:
  - `REL-006` / `GRAPH-001`: historical unified/global graph work, with its
    access scope now superseded by `GRAPH-008`.
  - `UPLOAD-SEC-001`: malware scanner and quarantine gate completion.
  - `CONFIG-002`: global typed document-size configuration and deployment wiring.
  - `VERSION-002`: Version Management old-version active-switch UI completion.

Scope:

1. Historical `REL-006` / `GRAPH-001` unified/global graph work
   - The former Knowledge Graph popup and unscoped access contract are
     superseded and must be removed under `GRAPH-008`.
   - Retain only historical characterization of the unified Backend model.
   - Document versions are returned only as document metadata and are not graph nodes.
   - Relationships are limited to:
     - Project -> Document source labels: upload, FTP, SFTP, FTPS, SSH, S3, HTTP API, reference project.
     - Document -> Chunk: split.
     - Document/Chunk -> Tag: tagging.
   - Add bounded loading, truncated metadata and node-level neighbor expansion.
   - Authorization is by omission: unauthorized nodes, edges, masked IDs and placeholder nodes are never returned.
   - Current frontend acceptance is permission-scoped Project/Document
     rendering under `GRAPH-008`; a combined global/cross-project result is not
     allowed.

2. `UPLOAD-SEC-001` Upload scanner gate
   - Add scanner state enforcement before extraction dispatch.
   - Development disabled scanner mode records explicit disabled scanner evidence but does not satisfy production/security acceptance.
   - Production scanner mode fails closed when scanner configuration is missing, unavailable, timed out or rejected.
   - Implement the shared scanner adapter interface and a ClamAV TCP adapter path first.
   - Preserve sanitized scanner errors; never expose scanner internals, paths, signatures or infrastructure details beyond safe codes.
   - Ensure parse / OCR / extraction Pipeline jobs are not created or dispatched before accepted scan state.

3. `CONFIG-002` Global document-size runtime config
   - Introduce typed setting `document_max_upload_size_mb` with env key `NOMOSMART_DOCUMENT_MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB` and 100 MB default.
   - Backend is the authoritative enforcement point for upload and data-source fetch size limits.
   - Frontend reads the effective backend value for upload Modal validation and display.
   - Wire Docker env template and Helm values / ConfigMap to the same setting.
   - Reject invalid config units/ranges during startup or config validation.

4. `VERSION-002` Old-version active-switch UI
   - Complete Version Management modal wiring for switching a compatible published old version to active.
   - Surface compatibility, published index readiness, active manifest readiness, affected references / project impact and blocking reasons.
   - Require explicit confirmation before switching.
   - Use the existing dedicated backend/API endpoint, optimistic lock and idempotency behavior.
   - Show success/error notification and refresh current/history version state after success.

Out of scope:

- New graph node types beyond Project / Document / Chunk / Tag.
- Separate app-wide graph route or report-style graph analytics.
- Replacing current graph visual design; only data/API/interaction completion is in scope unless required for expand/truncated states.
- External HTTP malware scanner execution beyond interface-compatible future wiring.
- Reworking the entire System Parameters UI; only required document-size config discovery/editing/wiring is included.
- Rebuilding the version management modal layout beyond the old-version switch flow.

Implementation approach:

1. Backend graph API
   - Inspect current graph API/data models and Neo4j sync payload.
   - Historical global/cross-project query-path work is superseded; remove
     unscoped aliases and implement only `GRAPH-008` Project/Document routes.
   - Normalize response nodes and edges to the specified node/relationship types.
   - Add pagination/bounds/truncated metadata and neighbor expansion parameters.
   - Add backend tests for authorized omission, bounds, no version nodes and expansion.

2. Frontend graph wiring
   - Replace global/cross-project client calls with `GRAPH-008` scoped
     Project/Document payloads.
   - Update graph popup state for truncated/expandable nodes and no-fixture error/empty states.
   - Preserve current approved node styling and spacing behavior.
   - Add i18n keys for graph scope, expansion and truncated states.

3. Upload security gate
   - Add scanner config and adapter boundaries.
   - Persist or expose scanner run/evidence state already expected by existing models where possible; add schema only if the current schema cannot represent required evidence.
   - Insert scanner gate before Pipeline dispatch.
   - Add safe failure handling and audit.
   - Add focused backend tests for accepted/rejected/disabled/unavailable/timeout/no-dispatch.

4. Typed document-size config
   - Add typed backend configuration and public effective-config API response if the current system-parameter API cannot supply it cleanly.
   - Replace hard-coded frontend upload limit with discovered backend value.
   - Wire Docker and Helm config templates.
   - Add backend/frontend/deployment validation tests.

5. Version Management UI
   - Locate current version-management modal and API client.
   - Add eligible old-version action, readiness/impact display, confirmation modal and busy/success/error states.
   - Refresh active/current version state after successful switch.
   - Add frontend tests and backend contract regression tests where needed.

Test strategy:

- Backend focused tests:
  - Graph authorization-by-omission, no version nodes, bounds/truncated metadata, neighbor expansion and relationship labels.
  - Upload scanner accepted/rejected/disabled-development/production fail-closed/timeout/no-dispatch/audit behavior.
  - Config default/override/range/backend upload rejection.
  - Version switch readiness and permission regressions if existing backend tests do not cover the UI contract fields.
- Frontend tests:
  - Scoped graph payload rendering, truncated/expand states, global-entry
    absence, no fixture fallback and i18n under `GRAPH-008`.
  - Upload Modal displays backend max size and blocks oversized files with the same value.
  - Version Management shows eligible switch action, blocking reasons, impact confirmation, success/error states and refreshed active version.
- Deployment/config tests:
  - Docker env template contains `NOMOSMART_DOCUMENT_MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB`.
  - Helm values and ConfigMap render the same setting.
  - Config policy check confirms no hard-coded divergent limit remains.

Verification commands:

```bash
./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor
./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace
./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor
./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved

```

Known risks:

- Graph data may reveal cross-project structure if filtering is applied after graph expansion. Mitigation: filter project visibility before node/edge materialization.
- Scanner integration can block all uploads if production config is incomplete. Mitigation: explicit config mode, startup validation and safe user-facing blocked state.
- Upload size config may currently exist in more than one location. Mitigation: backend effective config becomes authoritative; frontend and deployment consume the same key.
- Old-version switching can affect references and chat scope. Mitigation: show impact summary and rely on existing manifest/readiness/optimistic-lock backend checks.
