## CHG-209 / CHG-210 External Public API and API Key Management

Gate status:

- Gate 1 understanding: NomoSmart needs a public integration surface that lets
  external systems ask questions against already published knowledge only. The
  API must authenticate the external system as an Integration Client, require
  real end-user identity on every request, apply existing project/model/System
  Prompt behavior, preserve full citations and audit records, support both JSON
  and SSE response modes, and accept append-only feedback.
- Gate 2 confirmation: Peter confirmed the external API decisions on
  2026-07-11, including required `employee_id`, optional employee name and
  department, audit-only end-user identity, single-project request scope,
  optional stable `document_id` scoping, JSON plus SSE support, complete record
  retention, append-only feedback and System Management API Key lifecycle
  management.
- Gate 3 plan: this section.
- Gate 4 approval: approved by Peter on 2026-07-11 with `Ok`.

Scope:

1. `PUBLIC-API-001` public knowledge Q&A API:
   - add Integration Client authentication using generated API keys stored only
     as hashes;
   - require `end_user.employee_id` and accept optional employee name and
     department;
   - support `POST /api/public/v1/projects/{project_id}/chat`;
   - support `POST /api/public/v1/projects/{project_id}/chat/stream` with SSE
     events;
   - allow querying one authorized project per request;
   - default to all active published serving content in that project;
   - allow optional `scope.document_ids`, where each stable `document_id`
     resolves through Active Version Manifest to the current active published
     `document_version_id`;
   - reject inactive, deleted, unpublished, staging, processing,
     approved-unpublished, not-ready and cross-project scope;
   - reuse formal Project Chat retrieval and answer generation, including
     project Chat LLM settings, Embedding Profile and System Prompt layering;
   - return answer, status, response id, token usage, latency and complete
     citations containing document, version and chunk details.
2. `PUBLIC-API-002` public feedback API:
   - add `POST /api/public/v1/chat/responses/{response_id}/feedback`;
   - accept `rating = good | bad` and optional comment;
   - require the same end-user identity contract;
   - persist feedback as append-only events linked to the response, Integration
     Client, project and citations snapshot.
3. `FB-001` unified feedback history:
   - introduce feedback event persistence as the source of truth for UI and API
     feedback;
   - keep normal UI/API reads showing only the latest feedback;
   - preserve full feedback history for audit/reporting;
   - treat existing `chat_records.evaluation` style fields, if retained, only as
     denormalized latest state.
4. `APIKEY-001` System Management API Key Management:
   - add an API Key Management tab to System Management;
   - list Integration Clients with status, project summary, expiry, latest
     usage and success/failure summary;
   - create Integration Clients/API keys with multi-project allowlist,
     lifecycle fields and optional contact owner fields;
   - show generated API key plaintext exactly once;
   - support activation/deactivation, expiry extension, key rotation,
     revoke/delete-as-soft-delete and usage summary;
   - preserve audit and historical public API records after revocation.
5. Backend schema/migration alignment:
   - add integration client, project scope, public request log and feedback event
     schema;
   - add indexes and uniqueness constraints for key lookup, response lookup,
     client/project scope and feedback latest-history queries;
   - add safe audit records for lifecycle and public API calls.
6. Frontend/i18n:
   - add Traditional Chinese and English strings for all new System Management
     API Key states, modals, validations, copy-once warnings and lifecycle
     actions;
   - keep the UI consistent with existing System Management modal/table patterns.

Out of scope:

- External file upload, data-source creation, extraction, review, publish,
  reports, permission management, webhook or any mutation of knowledge content.
- Allowing an external request to query multiple projects at once.
- Allowing callers to specify `document_version_id` as normal public API scope.
- Allowing callers to override System Prompt, Chat Model or retrieval adapter.
- Hard-deleting Integration Clients, request logs, chat records, citations,
  feedback events or audit records.
- Full analytics/reporting beyond the basic usage summary specified in
  `APIKEY-001`.
- Helm-specific release work unless separately approved.

Implementation approach:

1. Schema and models:
   - add migration and ORM models for Integration Clients, client project
     scopes, public API request logs and chat feedback events;
   - include lifecycle fields (`valid_from`, `expires_at`, `revoked_at`,
     `revoked_by`, `revocation_reason`) and optional contact fields;
   - add key-prefix storage for safe display and key-hash lookup for
     authentication.
2. Security/authentication:
   - implement API key generation with a cryptographically strong random value;
   - hash keys before persistence and never log plaintext;
   - design a short non-secret key prefix for display and support one-time
     plaintext return on create/rotate;
   - add public API authentication dependency that fails closed for missing,
     invalid, inactive, expired, revoked or unscoped clients.
3. Public Q&A service:
   - create a service layer that resolves project allowlist, stable
     `document_id` scope and active published `document_version_id` scope;
   - reuse existing Project Chat retrieval/answer components where possible,
     while setting `source = public_api` and preserving external user metadata;
   - persist request/response/citation metadata before returning JSON or
     completing SSE.
4. SSE:
   - stream metadata, answer deltas, citations, usage, done and error events;
   - record partial/failed state when streaming fails after a response id exists;
   - keep error payloads safe and request-id correlated.
5. Feedback history:
   - add append-only feedback creation for public API;
   - adapt existing UI feedback update path to append a feedback event and
     update any latest-state denormalization in one transaction;
   - add read helpers that return latest feedback while keeping history
     available.
6. System Management APIs:
   - add internal `/api/v1/integration-clients` CRUD-style endpoints with
     lifecycle actions and project-scope update endpoints;
   - enforce `SystemManagement.can_*` permissions;
   - add safe usage-summary aggregation from public request logs.
7. System Management UI:
   - add API Key Management tab;
   - implement list, create modal, one-time key modal, detail/edit modal,
     rotate, activate/deactivate, extend expiry, revoke confirmation and filters;
   - use existing UI patterns, lucide icons, compact operational layout and no
     nested cards.

Test strategy:

- Backend API/security tests:
  - API key plaintext is returned only on create/rotate and never on list/detail;
  - API key hash validation accepts valid keys and rejects missing, malformed,
    inactive, expired, revoked and wrong-prefix keys;
  - project allowlist permits one authorized project and rejects unauthorized,
    deleted, inactive or multiple-project requests;
  - `document_id` scope resolves to current active published manifest and
    follows version switch/update without changing the external `document_id`;
  - inactive/unpublished/staging/not-ready document scope fails closed;
  - System Prompt metadata and model ids are persisted for public API calls;
  - citations are returned and persisted with document/version/chunk details;
  - JSON response and no-answer/error envelopes are safe and request-id
    correlated.
- SSE tests:
  - successful stream emits metadata/delta/citation/usage/done;
  - provider/retrieval failure emits safe error and stores failed state;
  - mid-stream failure stores partial state without losing response id.
- Feedback tests:
  - repeated public feedback for the same response and employee creates multiple
    events;
  - latest-feedback read returns the newest event only;
  - UI feedback path appends history and preserves prior events;
  - unauthorized response feedback is denied without leaking existence.
- System Management frontend tests:
  - tab visibility and permission gating;
  - create modal validation, multi-project selection and optional contact
    fields;
  - one-time key display/copy/close behavior;
  - list filters, lifecycle badges, expiry warning and usage summary rendering;
  - activate/deactivate, extend expiry, rotate and revoke confirmation states;
  - i18n key coverage for zh/en.
- Integration/live acceptance:
  - with configured Chat/Embedding/OpenSearch and at least one active published
    project, create an API key, call JSON API, call SSE API, submit feedback,
    verify persisted public records, then revoke key and verify denial.

Deployment/config impact:

- Requires a database migration and model/schema alignment.
- May require rate-limit configuration defaults, such as per-client requests per
  minute and maximum public API question length/output/citations.
- No new external service is introduced; public API depends on existing
  PostgreSQL, OpenSearch, provider credentials, System Prompt resolver and
  project serving readiness.
- API key generation must use runtime cryptographic randomness and must not
  require storing an encryption secret for key recovery because plaintext is not
  recoverable.

Risks and mitigations:

- Risk: public API accidentally exposes staging or inactive knowledge.
  Mitigation: resolve scope exclusively through Active Version Manifest and
  existing published retrieval guards; add denial tests for every non-serving
  status.
- Risk: API key plaintext leaks through logs, audit or UI state.
  Mitigation: generate server-side, hash immediately, return once, redact all
  logs/errors/audit and add regression tests.
- Risk: feedback append-only migration conflicts with existing
  `chat_records.evaluation` writes.
  Mitigation: introduce feedback events as the source of truth, update latest
  denormalized fields only transactionally, and add tests for history
  preservation.
- Risk: SSE implementation records incomplete or duplicated responses.
  Mitigation: create response id early, persist terminal state exactly once and
  include request id in every event/error.
- Risk: System Management UI becomes too dense.
  Mitigation: use one list plus focused modals, compact status chips, clear
  action grouping and existing System Management popup patterns.

Verification commands:

- `git diff --check`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:plan`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh backend:syntax`
- focused backend tests for `PUBLIC-API-001`, `PUBLIC-API-002`, `FB-001` and
  `APIKEY-001`
- focused frontend tests for System Management API Key Management
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:backend`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:frontend`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:lint`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:build`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh i18n:hardcoded`
- live public API acceptance against local configured services

## CHG-211 API Documentation Menu Page

Status: Approved by Peter with `Ok` on 2026-07-11; implemented and verified.

Specification scope:

  6.10.3.
- Add a logged-in Menu entry named `API說明` / `API Documentation`.
- Add a protected frontend route at `/api-docs`.
- Make the page visible to all authenticated and active users, regardless of
  first-level Menu permission grants.
- Keep `ApiDocumentation` out of the System Management permission matrix.
- Provide documentation only. The page must not create, revoke, rotate, display
  or manage API keys, projects, permissions or System Management settings.

Out of scope:

- No backend public API contract changes.
- No API Key Management lifecycle changes.
- No database migration.
- No OpenAPI export/download feature unless separately requested.
- No unauthenticated public documentation page.

Implementation approach:

- Reuse the existing protected App Shell route pattern so unauthenticated or
  expired sessions follow the current login flow.
- Add `/api-docs` under `frontend/src/app` with a dense operational layout
  matching NomoSmart's existing Cloud White / green enterprise style.
- Add a top-level menu item in the shared navigation alongside Home and Approval
  Workspace. This item will use system-default access instead of a permission
  matrix key.
- Keep the permission matrix data model limited to controlled menu features:
  `KnowledgeProjects`, `Reports` and `SystemManagement`.
- Use aligned zh/en i18n keys for all user-facing copy.
- Document the approved external API surface:
  - API Key authentication headers;
  - required end-user identity fields;
  - JSON Q&A request/response shape;
  - SSE Q&A event flow;
  - optional single-project and document scope behavior;
  - citations returned with answers;
  - feedback API good/bad/comment behavior;
  - common error envelopes/statuses;
  - rate-limit and request-id guidance;
  - security notes that examples use placeholders only.

Test strategy:

- Frontend navigation tests:
  - active logged-in users see `API說明` even when they have no
    `KnowledgeProjects`, `Reports` or `SystemManagement` grants;
  - inactive/unauthenticated users cannot treat `/api-docs` as a public page.
- Permission matrix regression:
  - System Management permission matrix must not render an
    `ApiDocumentation` row or toggle.
- Page content tests:
  - `/api-docs` renders JSON API, SSE API, feedback API, authentication,
    citation and error sections;
  - examples use placeholders and do not contain real secrets, API keys,
    tokens, private endpoints or System Prompt content.
- i18n tests:
  - zh/en keys remain aligned;
  - no new visible hard-coded application strings outside accepted technical
    identifiers and code examples.
- Build/static checks:
  - TypeScript, lint, frontend tests, build and existing hard-coded i18n guard.

Deployment/config impact:

- No runtime environment variable, database, migration, OpenSearch, Neo4j,
  Celery, S3, Docker or Helm change is expected.
- The route is a frontend-only documentation surface and uses existing auth
  context.

Risks and mitigations:

- Risk: users confuse `API說明` with API Key administration.
  Mitigation: include a short note that keys are created in System Management by
  administrators, while this page only explains integration.
- Risk: examples accidentally look like production credentials.
  Mitigation: use explicit placeholders such as `<api_key>`, `<project_id>`,
  `<response_id>` and add tests scanning for forbidden secret-like samples.
- Risk: menu gating regresses and hides the page from low-privilege users.
  Mitigation: add navigation regression coverage for users with no controlled
  menu grants.

## CHG-214 Post-upload Extraction Completion Gate

Status: Gate 4 approved by Peter on 2026-07-11 with `ＯＫ`.
Implementation and focused verification completed for the frontend scope.

Spec scope:

- Implements `PIPE-012` in `SPECIFICATION.md` sections 6.4, 6.8, 10 and 12.
- Keeps the completion threshold aligned with the existing Pipeline state:
  `submission_ready`.
- Preserves `PIPE-006` failed-step retry semantics.

Confirmed understanding:

- Users must not enter the full Knowledge Detail extraction screen after upload
  until OCR, chunking, AI auto tagging, Embedding and related automatic Pipeline
  steps have completed.
- Completion means the Pipeline reaches `submission_ready`.
- Failed progress UI must still expose the existing retry failed-step action
  when retry is allowed.
- Users must be able to close the progress surface and return to the current
  project document list / import page.

In scope:

- Single-file upload auto-extraction:
  - keep the upload/progress modal open after document and Pipeline creation;
  - poll live Pipeline detail until `submission_ready`, failed or another
    terminal state;
  - only navigate to full Knowledge Detail after `submission_ready`.
- Manual extraction entry points from the project document list:
  - keep the user in an extraction progress surface after starting a Pipeline;
  - apply the same `submission_ready` gate before opening full Knowledge Detail.
- Knowledge Detail direct URL guard:
  - when the selected version is not `submission_ready`, render a progress or
    failed blocker instead of the full two-pane evidence/editing layout;
  - include close/back navigation to `/project/[id]/import`;
  - show failed step, sanitized error and retry failed-step button when allowed.
- Reuse the existing Pipeline step labels, retry API, polling utilities and
  localized strings where possible.
- Add Traditional Chinese and English i18n strings only for genuinely new
  blocker/back/close copy.

Out of scope:

- No backend Pipeline state machine redesign.
- No database schema migration.
- No change to OCR, chunking, tagging, Embedding, OpenSearch or graph-preview
  execution behavior.
- No change to review, publish, Active Version Manifest, Project Chat or public
  API behavior.
- No fixture, deterministic fallback or client-only fake completion path.

Implementation approach:

1. Inspect current upload modal state transitions in
   `frontend/src/app/project/[id]/import/page.tsx` and Knowledge Detail gating
   in `frontend/src/app/project/[id]/knowledge/[knowledgeId]/page.tsx`.
2. Add a small frontend helper that determines whether full Knowledge Detail can
   render:
   - allowed when Pipeline status is `submission_ready` or later evidence-ready
     states already supported by the page;
   - blocked when Pipeline is queued/running/processing/waiting_action;
   - failed blocker when Pipeline or a step is failed.
3. Update single-file upload success behavior so it does not immediately
   navigate to Knowledge Detail before `submission_ready`.
4. Reuse or extract the existing `LayoutPipelineFallback` UI into a
   page-level/blocker-capable progress component with:
   - current step;
   - progress percent;
   - processing help text;
   - failed step and error;
   - retry failed-step action when eligible;
   - close/back to project document list.
5. Apply the blocker in Knowledge Detail before rendering article/chunk/tag
   controls, graph preview, chat-test link or submit-review link.
6. Keep project document list cards showing existing progress and retry
   controls so users can monitor a closed modal from the list.

Test strategy:

- Frontend focused tests:
  - single-upload path stays in processing/progress state before
    `submission_ready`;
  - direct Knowledge Detail URL with running Pipeline renders blocker, not full
    evidence/chunk/editing controls;
  - failed Pipeline renders failed step, safe error and retry failed-step button;
  - retry busy state remains visible and refreshes Pipeline detail;
  - close/back action points to `/project/[id]/import`;
  - `submission_ready` restores the full Knowledge Detail layout.
- Existing frontend suite should cover regressions around upload progress,
  pipeline labels, Knowledge Detail and i18n.
- Backend/API checks are expected to be unnecessary unless frontend inspection
  shows the detail payload lacks required Pipeline state. If needed, add focused
  backend coverage for detail payload status/step/error availability without
  changing Pipeline semantics.

Deployment/config impact:

- No runtime configuration, environment variable, secret, schema migration,
  Docker, Helm, OpenSearch, Neo4j, S3, Celery or Keycloak impact expected.

Risks and mitigations:

- Risk: Users may think the upload is stuck because the modal remains open
  longer. Mitigation: show current step, percent, details and close/back option.
- Risk: Direct URL guard could hide useful failed evidence for debugging.
  Mitigation: show failed step/error and retry, but keep full editing/evidence
  layout gated until `submission_ready`.
- Risk: Existing tests may assume immediate navigation after single upload.
  Mitigation: update expectations to match `PIPE-012` and keep the completed
  state navigation path covered.

## CHG-216 Security, Runtime Correctness and Release Remediation

### Status and Gate

- Gate 1 audit/understanding: complete on 2026-07-11.
- Gate 2 decision confirmation: complete on 2026-07-12 with Peter's `Ok`.
- Gate 3 development plan: this section.
- Gate 4 implementation approval: complete on 2026-07-12 with Peter's `Ok`.
- CHG-216 implementation may proceed in the approved batch order. Each batch
  still requires its own traceability and verification evidence.

### Confirmed Scope

- Requirements: `OIDC-REAUTH-001`, `INIT-006`, `CONNTEST-001`, `NET-002`,
  `UPLOAD-SEC-002`, `DEPSEC-002`, `PERM-003`, `PIPE-013`, `OFFICE-001`,
  `EMBED-003`, `DSYNC-004`, `PUBLIC-API-003`, `MIGRATE-001`, `TEST-005`,
  `API-COMPAT-001`, `CLEAN-001`, `ARCH-001`, `TRACE-002`.
- Appliance initialization accepts IPv4/IPv6 CIDR entries and requires a
  bootstrap token. Loopback is the only default network; forwarded client IP is
  trusted only from configured proxy CIDRs.
- Internal model/OCR/Embedding/FTP/FTPS/SFTP/S3 endpoints remain supported.
  HTTP/API document sources retain the existing SSRF policy. Endpoint changes
  invalidate tests and require explicit credential confirmation.
- Real provider connection acceptance runs only after an operator configures
  real provider parameters. Missing provider prerequisites are blocked, not
  substituted with fixed success.
- API inventory is reconciled item by item: document equivalent behavior,
  implement required gaps, or record an approved deferred item with owner and
  milestone.
- Paramiko remediation is in scope. If no fixed release exists at execution
  time, SFTP receives worker/container isolation and a time-bounded human risk
  acceptance before production readiness.

### Out of Scope

- Changing the product into a public-endpoint-only platform or globally
  blocking all private network destinations.
- Replacing Keycloak as the identity provider, Celery as the worker framework,
  Flyway as the migration tool, or the existing PostgreSQL/OpenSearch/Neo4j/S3
  architecture.
- New business features unrelated to the audited gaps.
- Destructive deletion of published knowledge, audit history, production
  objects, migrations or user-created configuration.

### Delivery Order

1. **Batch A: governance and emergency dependency baseline**
   - Reconcile active requirement/status contradictions and implement active
     change-aware `spec:trace` / `plan:approved` checks.
   - Produce the section 12 canonical API inventory with implemented,
     equivalent, required-gap or deferred classification.
   - Upgrade Next.js/PostCSS and cryptography to versions covering the audited
     advisories; re-audit Paramiko and define fix or isolation evidence.
   - Add production configuration validation for placeholder secrets, disabled
     scanner, localhost-only values and nonfunctional live-write settings.

2. **Batch B: identity, initialization and authorization**
   - Add durable one-time OIDC reauthentication state with PKCE, nonce, expiry,
     user/session/scope binding and consumed/revoked status.
   - Replace fixture reauthentication UI with Keycloak redirect/callback and
     candidate discovery/JWKS validation. Activate identity settings atomically
     and preserve last-known-good on failure.
   - Add typed `SYSTEM_INITIALIZATION_ALLOWED_CIDRS`,
     `SYSTEM_INITIALIZATION_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` and secret bootstrap-token
     settings. Enforce CIDR plus constant-time token validation before first-run
     validate/apply and preserve `INIT-005` for completed systems.
   - Replace recorded-only initialization with idempotent provisioning steps,
     durable status, compensation records and safe failure summaries.
   - Permit empty effective grants for active users while retaining route/data
     authorization; correct integration-client delete/revoke action checks.

3. **Batch C: ingestion security and asynchronous extraction**
   - Introduce quarantine object namespace/bucket, scanner task and atomic
     promote flow shared by upload and remote sync.
   - Add extraction outbox rows, dispatcher/task, idempotent step claim,
     recovery and duplicate-event suppression. API requests end after durable
     pipeline/outbox creation.
   - Add isolated `.doc` / `.docx` parser/converter worker with limits, cache,
     artifact contract and cleanup.
   - Persist canonical embedding builds and make staging indexing consume the
     saved vectors without a second provider call.
   - Build S3 clients from each data connection and resolve only that
     connection's encrypted/secret-ref credentials.

4. **Batch D: real connection tests and network contract**
   - Split schema/config validation from real connection testing.
   - Add bounded live probes and configuration fingerprints for model, OCR,
     Embedding, S3, FTP, FTPS, SFTP and HTTP/API sources.
   - Preserve internal endpoint support, HTTP/API SSRF protection, TLS and
     host-key verification. Bind credentials to provider/endpoint confirmation,
     remove query-string API keys where headers are supported, sanitize errors
     and audit endpoint changes.

5. **Batch E: public API and migration/deployment correctness**
   - Add atomic distributed rate limiting before retrieval/provider work,
     including failed-auth abuse accounting.
   - Add true incremental SSE, disconnect/cancellation handling and durable
     partial/error states.
   - Define typed retention/redaction settings, response/end-user feedback
     binding and persistent idempotency for cost/write endpoints.
   - Add Flyway Compose one-shot service and Helm install/upgrade migration Job,
     observability/failure blocking, and production values validation.
   - Replace ineffective runtime `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` mutation with an explicit
     build-time or server/runtime frontend configuration contract.

6. **Batch F: behavioral test and release evidence repair**
   - Include TSX and real statement/function/branch/line metrics in frontend
     coverage; preserve the 80% per-side threshold.
   - Replace source-regex-only acceptance with rendered component interaction,
     live API/integration tests and Browser E2E phase 2. Keep static tests only
     as guardrails.
   - Add dependency, config, migration, scanner, identity, authorization,
     public API and deployment checks to the harness with honest
     blocked/unavailable semantics.

7. **Batch G: verified cleanup and bounded architecture work**
   - Remove/archive only confirmed unused fixtures, legacy search/helper code,
     legacy mocked tests, generated output, prototype and stale assets; update
     ignore rules and verify imports/builds.
   - Move cross-route private helpers into domain services, then split the
     largest frontend workspaces and API client by existing feature boundaries.
   - Do not begin broad restructuring until the affected P0/P1 behavior has
     focused regression coverage.

### Data and API Changes

- Expected additive migrations include OIDC reauthentication state, extraction
  outbox/task claims, canonical embedding build/reference, scanner/quarantine
  evidence, public API rate/idempotency/retention metadata and migration-run
  evidence. Exact table/column names must be finalized in the relevant batch
  before its implementation.
- Batch C uses migration `V021__secure_async_ingestion.sql`: extend
  `file_scan_runs`, `outbox_events`, `pipeline_run_steps` and `embedding_builds`,
  add `embedding_build_vectors`, and add the uniqueness/index/lease constraints
  defined by the CHG-216 Batch C state contract. No destructive column removal
  is part of this batch.
- Batch D uses migration `V022__connection_test_evidence.sql` to add non-secret
  fingerprint, latency, detail-code, actor and tested-at evidence to AI models
  and data connections. It adds typed HTTP source host/CIDR allowlists and
  implements pinned-IP HTTP requests without changing the approved private
  endpoint policy for non-HTTP integrations.
- Existing API routes remain compatible unless the API inventory records an
  approved canonical replacement or alias. Removed/renamed behavior requires a
  deprecation window and updated API Documentation.
- No migration may delete published content, audit history, feedback history,
  citations or integration-client lifecycle evidence.

### Configuration and Deployment Impact

- New settings: `SYSTEM_INITIALIZATION_ALLOWED_CIDRS`,
  `SYSTEM_INITIALIZATION_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`, and secret
  `SYSTEM_INITIALIZATION_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN`.
- Additional typed settings are expected for quarantine storage, scanner worker,
  public API rate limiting/retention, converter limits and frontend runtime
  configuration. Safe examples go in env/values examples; real secrets do not.
- Docker Compose gains migration and isolated worker profiles/services as
  required. Helm gains migration Job/hook, restricted workload security context,
  config/secret wiring and production-values validation.

### Test Strategy

- Lowest useful level: parser/config/CIDR/action checks, state transitions,
  idempotency, fingerprint invalidation, error redaction and migration policy.
- Integration: real PostgreSQL, Redis/Celery, Keycloak, scanner, S3, OpenSearch,
  Neo4j, Office converter and configured model providers under `TEST-002`.
- Browser/component: real render and interaction for reauthentication,
  initialization, connection tests, pipeline progress/failure/retry and admin
  error states; both zh/en locales and responsive layouts.
- Security: dependency audit, SSRF regression for HTTP/API, credential routing,
  bootstrap token redaction, authorization matrix, quarantine isolation and
  container/workload hardening checks.
- Deployment: migration on fresh and existing database, failed-migration rollout
  block, Compose config, Helm lint/template, production values rejection,
  upgrade/rollback/restore evidence.
- Acceptance remains blocked rather than mocked when live credentials/services
  are unavailable.

### Risks and Controls

- Identity activation can lock out all users. Use candidate validation,
  last-known-good, atomic activation, break-glass runbook and rollback tests.
- Broad async extraction changes can duplicate cost or artifacts. Use durable
  outbox uniqueness, step claims, fingerprints and retry tests before switching
  traffic.
- Office conversion handles hostile files. Isolate processes, cap resources,
  disable network, clean temporary files and scan before conversion.
- Dependency upgrades may introduce framework/provider incompatibility. Upgrade
  in bounded commits and run build, live auth, upload and public API regression.
- The total scope is large. Each batch has its own traceability status and may
  not be marked complete from another batch's evidence.

### Planned Verification

- Governance: `spec:doctor`, `spec:trace`, `plan:doctor`, `plan:approved`,
  `test:plan`, `git diff --check`.
- Frontend: `test:frontend`, `frontend:lint`, `frontend:build`,
  `i18n:hardcoded`, Browser E2E and coverage check.
- Backend: `backend:syntax`, focused live API/integration suites,
  `test:backend`, Celery/Keycloak/scanner/provider acceptance and coverage check.
- Security: `npm audit --omit=dev`, `pip-audit`, secret/static/dependency/container
  scans and SBOM generation once selected tools are available.
- Deployment: `docker:config`, `helm:lint`, `deploy:config-policy`, migration
  fresh/upgrade/failure tests and release readiness review.

### Approval Record

`Peter approves CHG-216 Security Runtime Correctness and Release Remediation`

  snapshot, expiry, callback authentication, HttpOnly completion token,
  consumed/revoked state and replay protection.

## CHG-217 Permanent Chunk Deletion And Artifact Reconciliation

### Gate Status

- Gate 1: completed. Existing `CHUNK-001`, tag, review-lock, Pipeline,
  Embedding, OpenSearch and graph contracts were reviewed.
- Gate 2: completed on 2026-07-13. Peter confirmed permanent deletion, allowed
  zero Chunks, next-stage denial at zero, confirmed deletion UI, candidate-only
  mutation and OpenSearch/graph updates after both add and delete.
- Gate 3: this development plan is complete.
- Gate 4: approved by Peter on 2026-07-13 with
  `Peter approves CHG-217 Permanent Chunk Deletion and Artifact Reconciliation`.
  Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-07-13.

### Scope

- Add a top-right Trash2 action and confirmation Modal to editable Knowledge
  Detail Chunk cards, with zh/en strings, keyboard support and mobile target.
- Add the project/document/version-scoped permanent Chunk DELETE API with
  optimistic locking and the same effective mutation authorization as manual
  Chunk creation.
- Permanently remove the Chunk row and owned candidate-version relationships,
  vectors and stale staging-derived evidence without deleting shared canonical
  Tag rows still in use or copying deleted content into audit.
- Extend Knowledge Detail readiness with active Chunk count, artifact status,
  next-stage eligibility and safe block reason.
- Reconcile manual add/split/replace and permanent delete mutations into
  canonical Embedding, staging OpenSearch and version graph artifacts through
  durable outbox/Pipeline work.
- Enforce backend Chat Test and submit-review denial for zero Chunks or stale,
  queued, running or failed Chunk artifacts.

Out of scope:

- Mutating published, active, pending-review, approved waiting-publish or
  historical rejected versions.
- Deleting shared canonical Tag rows that still have assignments.
- Deleting or rewriting formal submitted approval evidence.
- Bulk delete, undo/restore, configurable retention or changes to published
  version serving.
- Helm verification, per Peter's current direction.

### Design And Implementation Tasks

1. Characterize the existing manual-chunk transaction, canonical build state,
   staging index naming, graph preview persistence, staging chat/validation
   references and worker/outbox idempotency. Record any newly discovered data
   contract in the specification before relying on it.
2. Extend `KnowledgeDetailResponse` with `active_chunk_count`,
   `chunk_artifact_status`, `next_stage_allowed` and
   `next_stage_block_reason`. Derive these server-side; frontend state is not an
   authorization or readiness source.
3. Add the nested DELETE route. In one PostgreSQL transaction: lock and validate
   the exact project/document/version/Chunk tuple, enforce editable candidate
   state and `lock_version`, collect safe IDs, delete only that version's stale
   candidate staging evidence, delete the Chunk and cascading owned rows,
   transactionally delete Tag rows only after locked no-assignment checks across
   both Chunk and document-version assignments, reindex only the target version,
   increment its lock, invalidate only its artifacts, write content-free audit
   and create one version-scoped durable reconciliation event.
4. Apply the same artifact invalidation/event creation to `CHUNK-001` manual
   create/split/replace. Avoid duplicate active reconciliation for one version
   revision and preserve current lineage behavior for superseded source Chunks.
5. Add a reconciliation worker/domain service. For nonzero active Chunks, build
   a canonical vector set with the configured real Embedding provider, publish
   the complete current snapshot to staging OpenSearch and rebuild the
   version-scoped graph. Publish readiness only after all required artifacts
   succeed and a final version-revision check still matches.
6. For zero active Chunks, skip provider calls, remove all candidate-version
   staging OpenSearch documents and version-scoped Chunk/Tag graph nodes/edges,
   then expose `chunks_required` while leaving source views and manual creation
   available.
7. Make reconciliation retry idempotent and fail closed. Stale worker revisions
   must not overwrite newer mutations; partial external writes must be replaced
   from the current complete snapshot on retry.
8. Enforce `active_chunk_count > 0` and artifact `ready` in backend document Chat
   Test and submit-review entry points. Return stable `chunks_required` or
   `chunk_artifacts_not_ready` errors.
9. Add frontend API typing and deletion state. Restructure the Chunk header so
   UUID and the 40px Trash2 control do not overlap; stop delete events from
   selecting the card; clear selected/source-highlight state after success.
10. Add confirmation, busy, error, locked and zero-Chunk empty states. Hide the
    control for permission denial and all read-only approval evidence; show a
    disabled reason for a temporarily locked otherwise-editable candidate.
11. Update API compatibility documentation, traceability and acceptance records
    after implementation evidence exists.

### Test Strategy

- Backend/API: live PostgreSQL tests for authorization, cross-project omission,
  editable-state matrix, lock conflict, FK cascade, shared Tag preservation,
  staging evidence deletion, last-Chunk deletion, active reindex, audit content
  safety, duplicate request and transaction rollback.
- Artifact behavior: live Redis/outbox worker, OpenSearch and Neo4j tests for
  add, split, delete-one and delete-last snapshots; stale-node/document absence,
  zero-Chunk cleanup, revision race, duplicate delivery, partial failure and
  retry. Real provider success remains blocked until operator configuration;
  provider absence must produce a real fail-closed result, not a fake success.
- Workflow: backend Chat Test and submit-review denial at zero/non-ready, then
  success only after nonzero reconciliation is ready.
- Frontend: rendered interaction for icon placement, tooltip/aria, event
  isolation, confirmation/cancel/busy/error, technical-ID wrapping, empty state,
  locked/read-only behavior and mobile target; browser acceptance against the
  live Backend remains the formal behavioral proof.
- Regression: manual Chunk selection/source highlighting, tag actions, review
  read-only evidence, Pipeline retry, published retrieval and graph display.
- Coverage thresholds remain unchanged. This feature adds useful coverage but
  does not claim to close the repository's existing global coverage gap alone.

### Deployment And Configuration Impact

- No new runtime secret or environment setting is expected.
- Reuse current PostgreSQL, Redis/Celery, OpenSearch, Neo4j and Embedding provider
  configuration.
- No migration is expected because Chunk FK cascades, status strings, outbox and
  Pipeline state already exist. If characterization proves durable readiness
  requires schema state, add an additive V025 migration and update the spec,
  changelog and traceability before implementation.
- Docker Compose behavior tests use the prepared services. Helm checks remain
  intentionally skipped unless Peter changes the current instruction.

### Risks And Controls

- Permanent deletion is irreversible. Require explicit confirmation, backend
  state/permission checks, optimistic locking and content-free audit metadata.
- Shared Tag deletion could damage other evidence. Delete assignments with the
  Chunk, lock candidate Tag rows, check both assignment tables across all
  documents/versions and delete only immediate true orphans.
- An incorrectly broad reconciliation could damage another version. Every DB,
  OpenSearch and graph query must carry the full target scope; add negative
  same-project/same-document/different-version fixtures and assert byte-for-byte
  unchanged non-target artifacts.
- PostgreSQL and external stores cannot share one transaction. Invalidate
  readiness in the DB transaction and restore it only through idempotent durable
  reconciliation after complete external success.
- A stale worker could reintroduce deleted content. Bind reconciliation to the
  document-version revision and publish only when the revision still matches.
- Zero Chunks could dead-end the UI. Keep Original/Markdown and manual creation
  available while blocking only Chat Test and submit-review.
- Existing manual mutation currently leaves artifacts stale. CHG-217 treats
  add/split/replace and delete as one consistency boundary instead of fixing
  deletion alone.

### Planned Verification

- Governance: `spec:doctor`, `spec:trace`, `plan:doctor`, `plan:approved`,
  `test:plan`, `git diff --check`.
- Backend: focused CHG-217 live tests, `backend:syntax`, `test:backend`.
- Frontend: focused rendered/live tests, `frontend:lint`, `frontend:build`,
  `test:frontend`, `i18n:hardcoded`.
- Integration: live PostgreSQL, Redis/worker, OpenSearch and Neo4j mutation
  reconciliation; provider success when the operator configures it.
- Broader: `test:e2e` for delete-last, blocked Chat Test, recreate Chunk,
  reconciliation and next-stage re-enable where provider prerequisites exist.
- Deployment: `docker:config`, `deploy:config-policy`; Helm intentionally skipped.

### Approval Request

Gate 4 approval phrase:

`Peter approves CHG-217 Permanent Chunk Deletion and Artifact Reconciliation`

Approval received from Peter on 2026-07-13. Implementation and feature tests
may proceed under the approved scope.

### Implementation And Verification Result

  candidate-only state guard, active-only reindex, content-free audit, FK vector

- Implemented version-revision readiness metadata and durable

- Knowledge Detail includes readiness fields and exposes a 40px Trash2 action,

Verification evidence on 2026-07-13:

## CHG-218 Unified AI Model Usage Statistics

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-13. Gate 3 development plan
written on 2026-07-13. Gate 4 approved by Peter on 2026-07-13 with `Ok`.

### Scope

Implement `USAGE-001` and `REPORT-010`:

- Record every real AI model provider invocation in a unified usage ledger.
- Cover `Chat`, `Embedding`, `OCR` and `Judge` model types.
- Cover UI chat, Public API chat, validation answer generation, Judge scoring,
  document/chunk/Pipeline auto-tagging, OCR extraction, embedding build, query
  embedding and connection tests.
- Expand Reports so model usage can be grouped and filtered by project, model
  type, model/provider, usage purpose, source channel, status and Integration
  Client/API Key where applicable.
- Backfill existing historical usage where source records already contain safe
  usage metadata.

Out of scope:

- Storing prompt text, document text, user question text, answer text, provider
  raw response text, API keys, credentials or full end-user identity in usage
  rows.
- Changing provider pricing automatically from external billing APIs unless the
  provider response for the same request already includes official cost.
- Replacing audit logs. Usage rows are operational/cost accounting records and
  may reference audit/request IDs, but they are not a substitute for audit.

### Approach

1. Add an additive database migration and ORM/API schema for a unified usage
   table, tentatively `ai_model_usage_events`.
2. Add a provider usage normalizer that maps provider-specific payloads into
   stable fields:
   - input/output/total token;
   - embedding token;
   - OCR pages/images;
   - vector count and chunk count;
   - raw safe usage;
   - provider-reported cost where present.
3. Add a cost resolver:
   - official provider-reported per-request cost wins;
   - otherwise estimate from model/config pricing using per-million-token
     input/output/embedding pricing or OCR per-page/per-image pricing;
   - require an ISO 4217 currency for every non-null configured unit price,
     including zero;
   - accept zero as an explicit free/not-billed price, reject negative prices,
     and preserve null as unavailable;
   - leave cost null with `cost_source = unavailable` when pricing or currency
     is incomplete.
4. Add a single recording service used by all model adapters and model-consuming
   domain services. It must record success, failure, timeout, cancellation and
   partial outcomes.
5. Wire usage recording through:
   - RAG answer generation and streaming finalization;
   - Public API JSON and SSE flows;
   - validation answer generation and Judge scoring;
   - auto-tagging APIs and Pipeline auto-tagging;
   - OCR extraction adapters;
   - embedding build and query embedding paths;
   - AI model connection tests.
6. Add idempotency/retry controls:
   - every real provider call creates one usage event;
   - artifact/idempotency reuse with no provider call creates no new cost event;
   - retry attempts are linked with attempt/retry metadata.
7. Add a best-effort backfill script:
   - read existing `chat_records`, `public_api_request_logs`,
     `validation_run_items`, `embedding_builds` and tag metadata;
   - insert source-marked usage events only where model/context/usage can be
     safely inferred;
   - do not fabricate missing OCR/Judge/cost usage.
8. Expand report backend:
   - add model-usage aggregation from the usage ledger;
   - support filters/grouping by project/model/model type/purpose/source/status;
   - support Integration Client/API Key summaries for Public API usage;
   - group cost totals by ISO currency and never add unlike currencies because
     v1 does not perform foreign-exchange conversion;
   - preserve RBAC/project-scope enforcement and CSV safety.
9. Update frontend Reports:
   - refine the model usage tab;
   - add grouping/filter controls;
   - show business usage separately from connection-test usage;
   - show cost unavailable/estimated/provider-reported states;
   - show currency beside every cost and separate totals by currency;
   - extend AI model create/edit pricing UI with ISO currency selection,
     zero-price support and non-negative validation;
   - update zh/en i18n.
10. Update traceability, API compatibility notes if report/export contracts gain
    fields, and final verification evidence.

### Data Contract

The usage event record must include:

- IDs: event id, model id, project id, optional document/document version,
  pipeline run/step, chat record, validation run/item, public API request log,
  Integration Client, actor user and request/correlation ids.
- Classification: model type, provider, usage purpose, source channel, status,
  attempted/provider-called marker and error code.
- Usage: input/output/total token, embedding token, OCR page/image counts,
  vector count, chunk count, safe raw usage.
- Cost: provider-reported cost, estimated cost, ISO 4217 cost currency,
  `provider_reported | estimated | unavailable` cost source and cost-estimation
  metadata. Zero is a valid amount; null is unavailable.
- Timing: latency, created/started/completed timestamps where available.
- Safety: no prompt/content/secrets/tokens/full provider responses.

### Test Strategy

- Backend live tests for every wired call path and failure mode.
- Provider usage normalization tests for OpenAI-compatible, Gemini, Claude,
  Anthropic, Ollama, vLLM, OCR and Embedding payload shapes.
- Cost tests for provider-reported cost precedence, per-million pricing
  fallback, required ISO currency, zero/null distinction, negative rejection,
  unavailable cost null state and no cross-currency summation.
- Idempotency/retry tests for no double counting on artifact reuse and accurate
  counting for real repeated provider attempts.
- Backfill dry-run/apply tests against live PostgreSQL test data.
- Report authorization/filter/grouping/CSV tests.
- Frontend report UI/i18n tests.
- Existing coverage threshold remains unchanged; this feature adds targeted
  coverage but does not relax current coverage gates.

### Deployment And Configuration Impact

- Additive database migration is expected.
- Existing model config may need new optional non-secret pricing keys:
  `input_cost_per_million_tokens`, `output_cost_per_million_tokens`,
  `embedding_cost_per_million_tokens`, `ocr_cost_per_page`,
  `ocr_cost_per_image`, `cost_currency`. `cost_currency` becomes conditionally
  required whenever any pricing key is non-null, including zero.
- Existing prices without a reliable currency are not silently assumed to be
  USD or TWD; they remain unavailable until an administrator confirms currency.
- No exchange-rate service or base-currency conversion is added in v1.
- No new secret is expected.
- Backfill should be operator-run, idempotent and safe by default, with dry-run
  output before apply.

### Risks And Controls

- Risk: double-counting retries. Control: record only actual provider calls and
  include attempt/correlation metadata.
- Risk: undercounting streaming or cancelled calls. Control: persist final usage
  when provider emits it and record cancelled/partial status when it does not.
- Risk: leaking sensitive content. Control: whitelist usage fields, reject prompt
  and document content from raw usage, and add tests for redaction.
- Risk: provider-specific token names are missed. Control: central normalizer
  with fixtures for supported providers.
- Risk: cost is mistaken as exact when estimated. Control: separate
  provider-reported and estimated cost fields and label the source in UI/CSV.
- Risk: unlike currencies are added into a misleading total. Control: retain
  ISO currency on every cost and aggregate only within the same currency.
- Risk: zero is mistaken for missing pricing. Control: use nullable decimal
  fields, explicit cost source and tests that distinguish `0` from `null`.
- Risk: report scope leaks unauthorized cost/count. Control: reuse `REPORT-009`
  authorization and add negative project/API-client tests.

## CHG-219 OIDC Silent SSO login_required Callback Recovery

Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-13 with `ＯＫ`. Gate 3 plan prepared on
2026-07-13. Gate 4 approved; Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-07-13 with
`Peter approves CHG-219 OIDC Silent SSO login_required Callback Recovery`.

### Confirmed Understanding

- The observed failure is an OIDC recovery bug: a protected route can start
  silent SSO with `prompt=none`; when Keycloak has no active SSO session it
  returns `/auth/callback?error=login_required...`.
- The callback page currently depends on client-side execution to detect the
  error and route back to login. If hydration or client JavaScript is delayed or
  broken, the user stays on `正在完成企業登入...` and cannot reach the login page.
- The expected behavior is not to remove silent SSO. It is to make callback
  error handling fail closed, route reliably back to `/login?error=oidc`, and
  let the user start an interactive Keycloak login from the login page.

### Scope

- Requirement IDs: `AUTH-010`, related `AUTH-001`, `AUTH-002`, `AUTH-009`.
- Frontend OIDC callback recovery and login error display.
- Frontend auth start route guardrails for silent versus interactive login.
- Tests and i18n for the new callback-error path.
- No backend database, permission, role, Keycloak realm, schema or deployment
  migration change is expected.

### Implementation Approach

1. Add a hydration-independent guard in the `/auth/callback` route so callback
   requests with `error`, missing `code` or missing `state` redirect to
   `/login?error=oidc` before rendering the client callback component.
2. Clear transient OIDC cookies (`nomosmart_pkce`, `nomosmart_state`,
   `nomosmart_nonce`, `nomosmart_return`) on callback failure when the route can
   issue a response.
3. Keep the client `OidcCallback` fail-closed behavior as a secondary guard and
   make sure it never calls `/api/auth/exchange` when the URL already contains
   an OIDC error or incomplete parameters.
4. Ensure `/login?error=oidc` renders the login page with localized safe error
   feedback and an interactive login link that calls `/api/auth/start` without
   `prompt=none`.
5. Preserve the existing safe internal `returnTo` behavior and callback-loop
   rejection.

### Test Strategy

- Extend frontend OIDC/static tests for callback route error handling, missing
  parameter denial, no token exchange on error, interactive login without
  `prompt=none`, safe return path behavior and i18n coverage.
- Add or update focused tests for `OidcCallback` source behavior so the client
  fallback still fails closed.
- Run browser smoke only if local frontend/backend/OIDC are reachable; otherwise
  report the exact blocked command and keep static/frontend checks as completed
  guardrails.

### Verification Commands

- `git diff --check`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:plan`
- focused frontend OIDC tests
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:frontend`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:lint`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:build`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh i18n:hardcoded`

### Risks And Controls

- Risk: redirecting all callback errors hides useful diagnostics. Control: show
  safe localized login feedback only, while keeping token/code/secret details
  out of URL, storage and logs.
- Risk: clearing transient cookies breaks a valid callback. Control: only clear
  cookies on explicit error or missing required callback parameters.
- Risk: silent SSO loops back to callback repeatedly. Control: reject callback
  return paths and keep interactive login separate from `prompt=none`.

### Approval

Gate 4 approved by Peter on 2026-07-13 with:

`Peter approves CHG-219 OIDC Silent SSO login_required Callback Recovery`

### Implementation And Verification Result

- Implemented a server-rendered callback guard for explicit OIDC errors and
  missing `code` / `state`, with a dedicated no-store recovery route that clears
  all four transient OIDC cookies before returning to the canonical
  `/login?error=oidc` URL.
- Added localized, accessible login failure feedback while keeping the
  interactive login action on `/api/auth/start` without `prompt=none`.
- Focused OIDC tests passed 8/8. Frontend contract tests passed 75/75 and
  component tests passed 5/5; the unchanged repository-wide frontend coverage
  gate remains open at 7.25% lines against the required 80%.
- Frontend lint, production build, i18n hard-coded-text scan, specification,
  traceability, plan approval, test-plan and diff checks passed.
- Local HTTP smoke confirmed `login_required` resolves through the recovery
  route to `http://127.0.0.1:3000/login?error=oidc` with HTTP 200 and expires
  `nomosmart_pkce`, `nomosmart_state`, `nomosmart_nonce` and
  `nomosmart_return`. A callback with no matching state cookie also failed
  closed to that login page, while a callback with a matching state cookie kept
  the normal callback route available with HTTP 200.

## CHG-220 Complete Authentication State Routing And Login Recovery

Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-13 with `ＯＫ`. Gate 3 plan prepared on
2026-07-13. Gate 4 approved; Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-07-13 with
`Peter approves CHG-220 Complete Authentication State Routing and Login Recovery`.

### Confirmed Understanding

- Opening `/` or any protected route with no memory token starts one silent SSO
  check. Valid Keycloak SSO restores the requested safe route; no SSO session
  reaches exact `/login` without an error notice.
- Session expiry, explicit logout, login cancellation, disabled or
  unsynchronized users, IdP unavailability and callback validation failures all
  end on exact `/login`, with a localized notice appropriate to the state and no
  raw provider detail in the URL or UI.
- A successful auth flow consumes its state-bound safe internal `returnTo` and
  uses `/` only when no usable destination exists. A valid but unauthorized
  destination renders its normal forbidden state.
- Permission/scope 403 and non-auth business/API failures remain in the
  application; they must not be converted into login redirects.
- Session expiry redirects automatically after one refresh/retry. Eligible
  opt-in non-sensitive form data keeps the existing encrypted database-draft
  recovery, but draft failure cannot block the login redirect.
- The reproduced endless loading also had an operational cause: `next build`
  overwrote assets used by a running `next dev`. Dev and production output roots
  must be isolated, and the initial auth shell needs a hydration-independent
  fallback to `/login`.

### Scope

- Requirement IDs: `AUTH-011`, refinements to `AUTH-009` and `AUTH-010`, and
  related `AUTH-001`, `AUTH-006`, `UI-002`, `TEST-002`.
- Frontend `AuthProvider`, OIDC start/exchange/callback/logout recovery routes,
  login page, transient auth helpers, i18n and auth-shell styling.
- Safe internal return routing and fixed login-notice classification.
- Next.js dev/build output isolation, active-dev build conflict rejection and
  local/harness regression verification.
- Reuse existing Backend logout, denylist, `/auth/me` and encrypted session-draft
  APIs. No schema, data migration, role, permission or Keycloak realm change is
  planned.

### Implementation Approach

1. Introduce one typed frontend auth-transient module for cookie names, allowed
   flow modes, allowed login notice codes, common secure cookie options,
   transient cleanup and safe internal return-path validation. Keep notices
   enumerated and never store provider text, tokens or secrets.
2. Extend `/api/auth/start` to bind `state`, the validated one-time return path
   and a short-lived flow marker for silent, interactive or expiry reauth.
   Preserve interactive login without `prompt=none` and make the initial silent
   redirect single-flight in `AuthProvider` before assigning `window.location`.
3. Refine the server callback guard to validate state and flow before
   classifying `login_required`. Trusted silent `login_required` becomes normal
   anonymous recovery; missing/mismatched state or flow and other OIDC errors
   become fixed safe notices. All failure paths clear transient cookies and
   avoid exchange.
4. Add a same-origin login-recovery route/helper that sets only a short-TTL
   HttpOnly notice code, clears the appropriate transient auth state and
   redirects to canonical `oidcConfig().logoutUrl` with no query. Reuse it for
   callback failures, normal anonymous recovery, expiry and account-unavailable
   transitions.
5. Make client exchange failures leave the callback screen through the same
   recovery route. Preserve successful exchange destination precedence:
   validated current-flow return path, original protected route, then `/`.
   Consume the return state exactly once and retain callback/open-redirect loop
   rejection.
6. Replace the protected-page session-expired modal with one bounded transition:
   one refresh/retry, optional eligible encrypted draft capture, auth-state
   cleanup, then canonical login recovery with `session_expired`. Draft capture
   failure or timeout must not strand the user.
7. Classify auth responses by safe error code. A repeated 401 expires the
   session; `user_disabled` and `user_not_synchronized` end the session with an
   account notice; permission/project-scope 403 and non-auth 4xx/5xx responses
   remain page-level results. Use cloned responses where global inspection is
   needed so callers retain the original body.
8. Render fixed localized notices on `/login` from the HttpOnly flash state and
   keep the login action interactive. Normal anonymous login renders no alert;
   logout and cancellation use non-error tones. An already authenticated user
   who reaches `/login` returns to the valid current-flow destination or `/`.
9. Keep logout denylist/end-session behavior, but set a logout-success notice
   and clear every auth flow/notice/return cookie at the correct boundary.
10. Add a server-rendered auth-shell fallback that becomes usable within five
    seconds without React and provides a safe `/login` path plus no-script
    handling. The normal hydrated state machine hides it when startup succeeds.
11. Configure separate Next output roots for development and production, update
    ignore/config coverage as needed, and reject a production build before it
    can rewrite shared Next TypeScript declarations while a live development
    lock is present. Derive allowed development origins from runtime
    configuration so the documented `127.0.0.1` entry can hydrate normally.

### Test Strategy

- Extend frontend OIDC contract and rendered-component tests for every fixed
  flow/notice code, exact `/login`, cookie attributes/cleanup, no raw errors,
  interactive versus silent start, state/flow validation and no exchange on
  failures.
- Add return-path cases for safe path/query, missing/expired destination,
  external/protocol-relative/auth-loop paths, one-time consumption, home
  fallback and a valid forbidden destination.
- Add AuthProvider cases for valid SSO restore, single-flight initial redirect,
  refresh success, repeated 401 expiry, disabled/unsynchronized user, permission
  403, ordinary API errors, Strict Mode and concurrent requests.
- Verify automatic expiry redirect and existing encrypted draft behavior,
  including capture success, timeout/failure, sensitive-field exclusion,
  restore/discard and user/path/nonce/TTL mismatch.
- Add auth-shell no-hydration/no-script structure checks and an operational
  regression that proves an active dev server rejects production build before
  shared declarations change, then reloads `/` and proves hydration/auth
  redirect still executes. Run production build after dev stops.
- Run live browser acceptance against the configured Keycloak and Backend for
  anonymous, existing SSO, interactive login, safe return path, logout and
  callback-error flows. TEST-002 forbids fake provider success.

### Deployment And Configuration Impact

- No database migration or new secret is expected.
- New transient cookies are HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure in production,
  path-scoped to `/`, short-lived and fixed-code only.
- Next development and production artifacts use separate output roots. Because
  Next also rewrites shared `next-env.d.ts`, `npm run build` verifies the live
  `.next-dev/dev/lock` and refuses the conflict before spawning `next build`.
  Docker and Helm runtime behavior remains production build/start; local and
  harness commands must use the matching directory without committing artifacts.

### Risks And Controls

- Risk: an attacker forges a notice or `login_required`. Control: state-bound
  flow marker, fixed notice allowlist, short TTL and no authorization effect.
- Risk: return routing creates an open redirect or loop. Control: existing
  same-origin path parser tightened for login/callback/auth API exclusions and
  one-time state consumption.
- Risk: automatic expiry navigation loses edits. Control: bounded best-effort
  encrypted draft capture with existing sensitive exclusions; login navigation
  remains fail-open when capture cannot complete.
- Risk: global 403 handling logs out authorized users. Control: classify only
  explicit account-state codes; all permission/scope codes stay forbidden.
- Risk: IdP reachability checks create false failures. Control: use bounded real
  discovery/readiness evidence and a retryable service notice, without a mocked
  or cached fake-success path.
- Risk: output isolation or conflict detection breaks type generation or
  production start. Control: lint/build/start checks, live-lock rejection before
  file mutation and a live hydration/login regression.

### Verification Commands

- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:plan`
- focused frontend OIDC/auth-state tests

- live Keycloak/Backend browser acceptance when prerequisites are available

### Implementation And Verification Result

- Implemented on 2026-07-13 in the frontend auth provider, typed auth-state
  helper, OIDC start/exchange/callback/logout routes, canonical login recovery
  and continuation routes, login UI/i18n, safe return-path validation and Next
  output configuration.
- Focused OIDC/auth-state tests passed `11/11`; the complete frontend contract
  suite passed `78/78` and component suite passed `5/5`.
- `frontend:lint`, `frontend:build`, `plan:approved` and the live anonymous auth
  route checks passed. A follow-up callback reproduction exposed two development
  hydration defects: `useSearchParams` left the callback in its fallback, and
  Next blocked `127.0.0.1` development resources while production verification
  could still rewrite shared `next-env.d.ts`. The callback now receives validated
  server props, uses an eight-second fail-closed exchange timeout, and the server
  layout owns the hydration watchdog. Allowed dev origins derive from configured
  app origin, and active dev lock detection rejects production build with status
  `2` before file mutation. After restart, a real existing Keycloak SSO session
  completed `/api/auth/exchange` and `/api/backend/auth/me` with HTTP `200`, then
  reached `/` as `peter chu`.
- `test:frontend` remains non-passing only at the repository-wide coverage gate:

- Live interactive credential submission, logout end-session and forced
  disabled/revoked-account scenarios were not exercised because no credentials
  or destructive identity-state change were used during this acceptance run.

## CHG-221 DOCX-only Pandoc Ingestion

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-13; Gate 3 plan written; Gate 4
approved by Peter on 2026-07-13 with `OK`. Implementation may proceed.

### Confirmed Understanding

- Microsoft Word input is DOCX-only for every path that creates or replaces
  document content: initial upload, `DOC-005` update, remote data-source import
  and any equivalent ingestion entry point.
- Existing `.doc` history and published artifacts remain accessible, but `.doc`
  cannot be uploaded, re-extracted or used to create a new version. Updating a
  legacy `.doc` document requires a `.docx` replacement and creates a new working
  version without changing the active version.
- DOCX is converted directly to canonical GitHub-Flavored Markdown by Pandoc.
  LibreOffice and plain-text conversion are removed from the new pipeline.
- Extracted images are retained as version-scoped artifacts. Final visible
  tracked-change content enters the body; comments are excluded from body text
  but their presence and processing policy are recorded in parser metadata.
- Image-only DOCX OCR is explicit only. The system may OCR safely extracted
  images when OCR is selected, but it does not convert DOCX to PDF.
- Pandoc failure is fail closed and has no LibreOffice fallback.

### Scope

In scope:

1. Authoritative DOCX-only extension, MIME and magic-byte validation shared by
   upload, update and remote ingestion paths, plus matching zh/en UI guidance.
2. Replacement of the Office parser with a sandboxed Pandoc DOCX-to-GFM parser
   that returns canonical Markdown, layout/parser metadata and media inventory.
3. Version-scoped media validation, S3 persistence, URL rewriting, cleanup and
   authorized retrieval compatibility.
4. Pipeline wiring so canonical DOCX Markdown drives layout, chunking and the
   Markdown artifact instead of reconstructed chunk text.
5. Legacy `.doc` read/download/serve compatibility and explicit re-extraction /
   update behavior.
6. Typed runtime/deployment settings, pinned Pandoc installation and removal of
   the LibreOffice runtime and obsolete converter configuration.
7. Focused automated, integration, container and browser acceptance coverage.

Out of scope:

- Converting legacy `.doc` files to `.docx` automatically.
- DOCX-to-PDF conversion or whole-document OCR.
- Editing Office documents, preserving Word comments as answerable body text,
  or executing macros / external links.
- Destructive migration or reprocessing of existing published versions.

### Implementation Approach

1. **Format contract and validation**
   - Centralize the allowed extension and canonical extension definitions so
     frontend hints and all backend ingestion routes agree.
   - Require `.docx`, ZIP/OOXML magic and a valid Word package; reject `.doc`
     before storage or Pipeline dispatch with a localized safe error.
   - Preserve legacy `.doc` download and existing-artifact reads, while blocking
     re-extraction and requiring `.docx` for `DOC-005` updates.

2. **Pandoc parser boundary**
   - Replace the LibreOffice invocation in the Office parser with a typed Pandoc
     result containing Markdown, media manifest, parser/version metadata and
     warning flags for revisions/comments.
   - Invoke the configured binary with `--from=docx --to=gfm --wrap=none` and a
     private version-scoped extraction directory inside the existing no-network
     sandbox. Do not invoke a shell or interpolate user-controlled arguments.
   - Enforce timeout, memory/process/filesystem limits, bounded DOCX ZIP entries
     and expansion, and deterministic temp/cache cleanup.

3. **Canonical Markdown and media**
   - Persist the Pandoc output as the canonical Markdown artifact and feed it to
     layout/splitting so headings, tables, lists, links, footnotes and reading
     order survive ingestion.
   - Validate every extracted media path remains below the extraction root,
     verify MIME/magic/size/count, upload to a document-version artifact prefix,
     and rewrite Markdown references to stable authorized artifact references.
   - Persist only non-sensitive parser metadata and artifact identities; do not
     expose temp paths, subprocess command lines or external URLs.

4. **Tracked changes, comments and OCR**
   - Use final visible Word content for the body. Record comment/revision presence
     and policy in parser metadata, without placing comment text in the body.
   - If explicit OCR is selected and the DOCX body has no useful text, enqueue
     OCR only for validated extracted images and merge results in source order.
     Automatic DOCX-to-PDF or LibreOffice fallback is prohibited.

5. **Failure and lifecycle behavior**
   - Treat missing Pandoc, unsupported version, malformed package, timeout,
     nonzero exit, empty Markdown, unsafe media or upload failure as terminal or
     retryable Pipeline failure according to existing step semantics; never mark
     a blank artifact completed.
   - Reuse Pipeline/outbox idempotency and fingerprinting so retry does not
     duplicate media, parser artifacts or provider work.

6. **Runtime and deployment**
   - Add typed `PANDOC_COMMAND`, `PANDOC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`,
     `PANDOC_MAX_MEMORY_MB` and `PANDOC_CACHE_DIR` configuration and document the
     retained sandbox runner contract.
   - Pin Pandoc in the backend image, retain non-root/bubblewrap-style isolation,
     remove LibreOffice from runtime packages and deprecate `OFFICE_CONVERTER_*`.
   - Update safe environment templates, Compose/Helm configuration and health /
     readiness evidence without adding secrets.

### API, Data And UI Contract

- Existing document/version API shapes remain additive. Invalid `.doc` input
  returns the existing validation envelope with a stable machine-readable code
  and localized UI copy; it is not reported as a generic server error.
- No destructive schema migration is planned. Existing artifact/metadata JSON is
  used where its contract supports parser/media metadata; characterization must
  stop and amend the specification if durable fields require a migration.
- The upload and update modals list DOCX, not DOC, and explain that legacy Word
  updates require DOCX. Remote-source validation reports the same rule.
- User-facing error, format and OCR copy is added to both Traditional Chinese
  and English locale files.

### Test Strategy

- Unit/API: extension/MIME/magic/package validation, every ingestion route,
  `DOC-005` update, legacy `.doc` reads, permission and no-storage-on-rejection.
- Real parser corpus: headings, nested lists, tables, links, code, footnotes,
  images, Unicode, tracked changes, comments and image-only DOCX.
- Security: malformed OOXML, ZIP bomb/entry limits, path traversal, symlinks,
  external references, bad media, timeout/memory/process limits, command
  injection resistance, temp/cache cleanup and secret/log redaction.
- Integration: version-scoped S3 media persistence, Markdown URL rewrite,
  canonical artifact consumption by layout/chunking, retry idempotency and
  explicit image OCR with real configured services under `TEST-002`.
- Frontend/browser: accepted-format guidance, `.doc` rejection, DOCX update,
  localized errors, progress/failure state and desktop responsive behavior.
- Deployment: backend image contains pinned Pandoc and sandbox but no
  LibreOffice executable; Compose/config-policy/container checks remain valid.

### Deployment And Configuration Impact

- Backend container package set changes from LibreOffice to pinned Pandoc while
  keeping the sandbox/runtime libraries needed for no-network execution.
- Operators migrate `OFFICE_CONVERTER_*` values to `PANDOC_*`; obsolete values
  are ignored after the documented compatibility window and never trigger a
  LibreOffice fallback.
- Existing database rows and S3 source/artifacts are retained. New DOCX media is
  additive under version-specific artifact prefixes.

### Risks And Controls

- **Markdown fidelity varies by DOCX authoring tool.** Maintain a real corpus and
  persist Pandoc version/parser warnings for reproducibility.
- **DOCX is a ZIP attack surface.** Validate package structure and enforce entry,
  expansion, media, resource and path boundaries before publishing artifacts.
- **Media rewrite may leave broken references.** Upload and verify all media
  before completing the parser step, then commit the manifest atomically.
- **Legacy `.doc` users may expect reprocessing.** Preserve existing reads and
  show a precise DOCX replacement requirement instead of silently converting.
- **Removing LibreOffice may affect PDF behavior accidentally.** Keep PDF/OCR
  paths independent and add a regression that no PDF behavior changes.

### Planned Verification

- `git diff --check`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:plan`
- focused DOCX parser/upload/update/backend tests
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:backend`
- focused frontend upload/update contract and component tests
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:frontend`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:lint`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:build`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh i18n:hardcoded`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh docker:config`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh deploy:config-policy`
- backend container Pandoc/sandbox/no-LibreOffice runtime acceptance
- live S3/Pipeline/OCR and desktop-browser acceptance when configured

`CHG-221 DOCX-only Pandoc Ingestion`.

## CHG-222 AppShell Page Header Eyebrow Removal

Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-13 with `OK`. Gate 3 plan prepared on
2026-07-13. Gate 4 approved by Peter on 2026-07-13 with
`Peter approves CHG-222 AppShell Page Header Eyebrow Removal`.
Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-07-13.

### Confirmed Understanding

- Remove only the green eyebrow line above the primary page title in the shared
  authenticated `AppShell` title bar.
- Preserve the readable page `h1` and close the vertical spacing left by the
  removed line.
- Apply the change consistently to every current `AppShell` route and state,
  including Home, Projects, Import, Knowledge Detail, document Chat Test,
  Submit Review, Approval Workspace/Detail, Reports, System and API Docs.
- Preserve contextual eyebrows inside modals, cards, content sections, graph or
  citation detail, Login and Setup.
- Do not change routes, APIs, data, permissions, authentication, translations or
  deployment behavior.

### Scope And Approach

1. Remove the optional `eyebrow` field from the `AppShell` TypeScript props and
   remove its conditional paragraph from the shared page title bar.
2. Remove `eyebrow={...}` from every `AppShell` call site, including loading,
   forbidden and not-found return paths, so the type contract catches future
   reintroduction.
3. Adjust only the shared topbar heading spacing needed to keep the title row
   compact after removal. Do not globally hide `.eyebrow`, because content and
   modal instances remain valid under `UI-003`.
4. Add a narrow frontend contract regression that enumerates `AppShell` call
   sites and verifies the shared component has no eyebrow prop or rendering.

### Test Strategy

- Static/component contract: `AppShell` accepts `children` and `title` only;
  its topbar contains one `h1` and no `.eyebrow`; no `AppShell` invocation
  supplies an eyebrow prop.
- Scope regression: representative modal/content `.eyebrow` instances remain
  present, proving the change is not implemented as a global CSS hide.
- Visual/browser: inspect representative Home, Reports, Knowledge Detail and
