## CHG-226 Interactive Reports Query, Pagination And Per-Report CSV

Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-14 with `OK`. Gate 3 plan prepared on
2026-07-14. Gate 4 approved by Peter on 2026-07-14 with
`Peter approves CHG-226 Interactive Reports Query Pagination and Per-Report CSV`.
Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-07-14.

### Confirmed Understanding

- Replace the top-level CSV action with an explicit Query action. Common filter
  edits are draft-only and apply together when Query is pressed; first entry
  automatically queries the defaults once.
- Remove the global CSV topic selector. Every table-backed report Panel owns its
  topic-specific CSV action and exports all authorized rows matching applied
  filters rather than the visible page.
- Query every topic required by the active tab; do not reuse one topic response
  for a second table.
- Give each table independent server pagination fixed at 20 rows and return
  total/page metadata.
- Move model-usage filters below KPI cards and directly above the model usage
  table. They participate in the same draft/applied Query workflow.
- Use scoped Loading states for full queries, individual pagination and each
  CSV export, preserving safe empty/partial/forbidden/error behavior.
- Make current scope, project and API Key-short-code controls real authorized
  Backend filters instead of cosmetic or result-derived options.

### Backend And API Approach

1. Extend report summary query with canonical `scope`, `page` and fixed
   `page_size=20` parameters while preserving date/project/model filters.
2. Extend `ReportSummaryResponse` with `page`, `page_size`, `total_rows` and
   `total_pages`. Apply stable topic-specific ordering before offset/limit.
3. Refactor topic builders so totals and page rows are computed within the
   authorized scope; avoid materializing unrelated unauthorized rows merely to
   paginate them.
4. Add an authorized report filter-options endpoint returning only permitted
   scope choices, projects and safe Integration Client/API Key prefixes.
5. Enforce requested-scope semantics server-side. System scope is limited to
   authorized system report users; every other scope is intersected with live
   project membership, ownership, reviewer relationship and actor boundaries.
6. Change CSV export to use the same canonical applied filters and topic, stream
   all matching authorized rows without silent page/5,000-row truncation, and
   retain localized headers, request ID and final audit row count.

### Frontend Approach

1. Replace individual filter state as the query source with typed draft and
   applied filter objects. Initial auth readiness applies defaults once; input
   changes mark filters dirty without calling summary APIs.
2. Remove the global CSV topic control/action and render Query on the right of
   the common filter bar. Add validation and a visible unapplied-change notice.
3. Store report responses by topic. Query the complete active-tab topic map in
   parallel and isolate per-topic loading/error/page state.
4. Introduce a table-backed report Panel abstraction with its own CSV button,
   pagination metadata, local loading state, empty/partial/error state and
   stable accessible labels.
5. Keep common KPI cards bound to the latest applied query and show a stable
   report-area loading treatment during full queries. Page changes update only
   the selected topic using applied filters.
6. Move the model filter row to the models content flow immediately before its
   Panel; populate project/API Key choices from authorized filter options.
7. Add Traditional Chinese and English copy for Query, dirty-filter notice,
   loading, pagination, row totals and per-report export states.

### Test Strategy

- Backend live/API: authorized filter options, scope denial/omission, project
  isolation, date and page validation, first/middle/last/empty pages, fixed 20
  row size, stable ordering, totals, every topic, model filters and independent
  multi-topic requests.
- CSV live/API: per-topic canonical filters, more than 5,000 rows without silent
  truncation, localized headers, streaming/error behavior, permission isolation,
  no secret/content leakage and accurate audit row count/request ID.
- Frontend behavior: initial default query, no request while editing drafts,
  dirty notice, Query atomic apply/reset, tab topic map, cached tab behavior,
  per-table page loading, independent pagination, exactly 20 rows, per-Panel CSV
  topic/filter correctness and local export loading/errors.
- UI/i18n/accessibility: no global CSV topic/action, model filters directly above
  model table, stable skeleton/overlay dimensions, disabled query during load,
  aria-live status, keyboard pagination, responsive overflow and zh/en parity.
- Broader regression: report permissions, live-only data boundary, existing CSV
  formatting and audit contracts, frontend/backend coverage and browser flow.

### Deployment And Configuration Impact

- No schema, migration, secret, Docker or Helm change is expected. Streaming
  response behavior must remain compatible with existing reverse-proxy timeout
  and buffering configuration; any required proxy change discovered during live
  testing must be recorded before relying on it.

### Risks And Controls

- Large grouped reports may make count queries expensive. Use indexed filters,
  stable grouping/order and topic-specific count queries; record explain/latency
  evidence during live verification.
- Draft UI values could be mistaken for applied data. Keep the applied-filter
  summary and dirty notice visible until Query succeeds.
- Multi-topic tabs can partially fail. Keep per-topic error state and mark the
  tab partial without replacing successful tables with fixtures.
- CSV streaming can fail after headers are sent. Validate authorization and
  query shape before streaming, log safe failure metadata and write success
  audit only with the actual emitted row count.
- Page changes during a new full query can race. Cancel/ignore stale requests
  by query generation and disable pagination while its topic is loading.

### Planned Verification

- `git diff --check`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:plan`
- focused Backend report API/live tests
- focused frontend report contracts/components
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:backend`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:frontend`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh coverage:check`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:lint`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:build`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh i18n:hardcoded`
- authenticated desktop browser acceptance for initial query, dirty filters,
  multi-topic tabs, 20-row pagination, scoped Loading and per-report CSV

### Approval

Gate 4 implementation approval was granted by Peter on 2026-07-14 with:

`Peter approves CHG-226 Interactive Reports Query Pagination and Per-Report CSV`

### Implementation And Verification Result

- Backend now exposes authorized report scope/project/API Key-prefix options,
  enforces Owner/access/reviewer/system scope server-side, treats an empty
  visible-project set as empty rather than system-wide, and returns fixed
  20-row pages with page and total metadata.
- Existing summary/CSV callers that omit scope now retain role-aware behavior:
  System Management viewers resolve to system scope and other users resolve to
  their accessible-project scope; the reports UI continues to send scope
  explicitly.
- CSV export now belongs to each report topic, reuses the applied canonical
  filters and exports every matching authorized row without the previous

- Frontend now separates draft and applied filters, queries only on the Query
  action after the initial default load, loads every topic required by a tab,

- Focused live Backend behavior passed against local Keycloak/PostgreSQL with

`Peter approves CHG-228 API Documentation Synchronized Equal-height Navigation`.
Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-07-14.

### Confirmed Understanding

- On desktop, the lower API Documentation navigation/content area becomes an
  equal-height reading workspace bounded by the available viewport rather than
  two natural-height columns.
- The left navigation remains visible while only the right card list scrolls.
  Selecting a left item moves the right pane to the corresponding whole card.
- The active left item follows both navigation clicks and manual right-pane
  scrolling. Safe section hashes and browser back/forward remain functional.
- Motion respects `prefers-reduced-motion`, and anchors remain keyboard
  operable with an explicit current-location state.
- At the existing single-column breakpoints, fixed pane height and nested
  scrolling are removed; navigation uses natural page scrolling instead.
- Documentation content/order, authentication, permissions, API contracts and
  backend behavior remain unchanged.

### Scope And Approach

1. Add client state/refs to `/api-docs` for the right scroll container, each
   card-level section target and the active section ID.
2. Keep semantic anchor links. Intercept valid in-page navigation to update the
   hash/history and scroll the correct container with smooth behavior unless
   reduced motion is requested. Handle initial hash and browser hash changes.
3. Observe or calculate the right pane's visible card positions during manual
   scrolling and update `aria-current="location"` on exactly one left item,
   without pushing a new history entry for passive scroll changes.
4. Move each section ID to a wrapper around the complete `Panel`, so navigation
   aligns the card rather than only its inner body below the Panel title.
5. Add desktop-only equal-height grid/pane CSS with right-side `overflow-y` and
   stable scrollbar space. Reset height, overflow, sticky behavior and nested
   scrolling in the existing single-column media rule.
6. Add focused API Documentation tests for synchronized navigation semantics,
   layout boundaries and preservation of all current sections/content.

### Test Strategy

- Interaction contract: clicking every nav item targets its matching card,
  updates the hash and active state, and chooses smooth versus immediate motion
  from the reduced-motion preference.
- Scroll synchronization: manual right-pane scroll updates one active nav item
  without history churn; initial hash and browser back/forward restore the same
  card and state.
- Structure/layout: IDs identify complete Panel wrappers; desktop layout has
  equal-height left/right panes, left nav stays visible and right pane alone
  scrolls with no horizontal overflow.
- Responsive/accessibility: existing single-column breakpoints reset fixed
  height/overflow, anchors remain keyboard operable, current state uses
  `aria-current`, and sticky Header does not cover the target.
- Regression: all nine existing sections, order, content, examples, protected
  route semantics, no-secret rules and zh/en dictionaries remain unchanged.
- Run focused API Docs tests, complete frontend contracts/components, lint,
  build, i18n and responsive browser acceptance. The existing repository-wide
  80% frontend coverage gate remains unchanged.

### Deployment And Configuration Impact

- None. No backend, database, migration, secret, runtime configuration, Docker
  or Helm change is expected.

### Risks And Controls

- Risk: native hash scrolling moves the whole document instead of the right
  pane. Control: handle valid section links explicitly on desktop and retain a
  natural-page fallback at single-column breakpoints.
- Risk: IntersectionObserver uses the viewport rather than the pane. Control:
  scope observation/calculation to the right scroll root and use deterministic
  card-top selection.
- Risk: active-state updates pollute browser history. Control: push history only
  for explicit navigation and never for passive scroll synchronization.
- Risk: fixed height is too short for the navigation. Control: use a bounded
  responsive height with a minimum that fits all current targets and remove the
  constraint at the existing single-column breakpoint.

### Planned Verification

- `git diff --check`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:plan`
- `cd frontend && node --test tests/apiDocs.test.mjs`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:frontend`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:lint`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:build`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh i18n:hardcoded`
- authenticated desktop and narrow-browser acceptance for click, manual scroll,
  initial hash, back/forward, equal heights and single-column reset

## CHG-229 Full-stack Single-domain Deployment

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-14. Gate 3 development plan is
complete. Gate 4 was approved by Peter on 2026-07-20 with
`Peter approves CHG-229 Full-stack Single-domain Deployment`; deployment
implementation and the approved verification work may proceed.

### Confirmed Understanding And Decisions

- Docker Compose and Helm must each deploy NomoSmart plus PostgreSQL, Redis,
  RustFS/S3, OpenSearch, Neo4j, Keycloak and ClamAV as one self-contained stack.
- Helm bundles every peripheral by default and lets an operator switch each one
  independently to an external managed service.
- Each environment uses one public host. NomoSmart remains at `/`, the existing
  frontend/API proxy contract remains under `/api/backend`, and Keycloak uses
  `/identity`; the existing NomoSmart `/auth/callback` route remains untouched.
- Production exposes only TCP 80 and 443. Port 80 redirects to HTTPS 443.
  Development may use HTTP 80. Data-service and management ports remain on the
  internal network; loopback-only debug access is opt-in for Compose.
- Kubernetes Ingress Controller, LoadBalancer, DNS, StorageClass/CSI and TLS
  certificate lifecycle are platform prerequisites and are not installed as
  cluster-scoped resources by this application chart.
- The bundled baseline uses one replica for stateful services and PVCs for
  persistence. Frontend/backend/worker replicas remain configurable. This
  baseline is documented as non-HA; external services or a separately approved
  HA profile are used when HA is required.
- Keycloak bootstrap creates the NomoSmart realm, frontend/backend/sync clients,
  mapper/theme and break-glass evidence, but never creates enterprise users.
  LDAP/AD federation is configured by an authorized administrator in Keycloak.
- Compose reads operator-provided certificate files; Helm reads an existing TLS
  Secret or cert-manager-managed Secret through operator annotations.

### Scope

1. Update the typed runtime/deployment configuration contract for the one-host
   origin, Keycloak `/identity` context, edge/TLS/admin CIDRs, internal OIDC
   discovery/JWKS transport, bundled/external service selection, persistence,
   image pins and secrets.
2. Convert Docker Compose to an edge-fronted full stack that publishes only
   80/443 by default, provides loopback-only debug profiles, separates
   NomoSmart and Keycloak PostgreSQL ownership, and gates app workloads on real
   bootstrap/migration/readiness evidence.
3. Expand the NomoSmart Helm chart into a bundled full-stack application chart
   with namespaced Deployments/StatefulSets, Services, Jobs, ConfigMaps, Secret
   references, PVCs, NetworkPolicies, probes, resources and one-host Ingress.
4. Add idempotent PostgreSQL, Flyway, S3 and Keycloak bootstrap lifecycle for
   fresh install, restart, upgrade, rollback and external-service mode.
5. Add operator documentation for install, upgrade, rollback, uninstall,
   persistence, backup/restore, TLS and secret rotation, debug access and
   Keycloak LDAP/AD User Federation.
6. Extend harness/config policy and live deployment tests so both packaging
   modes prove the same service, security and lifecycle contract.

### Out Of Scope

- Installing a Kubernetes cluster, Ingress Controller, LoadBalancer,
  StorageClass/CSI implementation, DNS server or certificate controller.
- Implementing self-hosted HA PostgreSQL, Redis clustering, distributed
  OpenSearch/Neo4j/RustFS or multi-site Keycloak in the bundled baseline.
- Automatically creating enterprise LDAP/AD users, changing directory
  memberships, or saving LDAP/AD bind credentials in NomoSmart.
- Replacing Keycloak, Flyway, Celery, PostgreSQL, Redis, RustFS, OpenSearch,
  Neo4j or ClamAV with a different product.
- Deleting existing volumes/PVCs or silently migrating production identity data
  without an operator backup and explicit migration action.

### Target Runtime Topology

| Boundary | Public path / internal endpoint | Planned ownership |
|---|---|---|
| Edge | `:80`, `:443` | Compose edge proxy or platform Ingress; TLS and redirects |
| NomoSmart | `/`, `/api/backend`, `/auth/callback` | Frontend server and internal backend proxy |
| Keycloak | `/identity/realms/nomosmart`, required resources | Public OIDC on the same host |
| Keycloak admin | `/identity/admin/`, master realm | Same host but restricted by trusted admin CIDRs/network |
| PostgreSQL | `postgresql:5432` | Internal only; separate NomoSmart and Keycloak DB/users |
| Redis | `redis:6379` | Internal only |
| RustFS | `rustfs:9000` | Internal only; no browser/public S3 endpoint required |
| OpenSearch | `opensearch:9200` | Internal only |
| Neo4j | `neo4j:7474/7687` | Internal only |
| ClamAV | `clamav:3310` | Internal only |
| Keycloak management | management health/metrics port | Internal probes/metrics only |

### Configuration Design

- Add one canonical public host/origin contract used by frontend runtime config,
  CORS, redirects, Keycloak hostname and realm issuer. Production values reject
  localhost, HTTP public origins and an issuer outside `/identity/realms`.
- Keep `OIDC_ISSUER_URL` as the exact public token issuer. Add typed optional
  `OIDC_DISCOVERY_URL` and `OIDC_JWKS_URL` transport overrides for internal
  Keycloak access; discovery must still advertise the public issuer, and JWT
  validation must always compare the token to that public issuer.
- Keep `KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_API_URL` as the HTTPS public administrative origin and
  add typed `KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_INTERNAL_URL` transport override for application
  and bootstrap traffic. Add Keycloak hostname, relative path,
  proxy-header/trusted-proxy and admin CIDR settings without accepting arbitrary
  client-supplied forwarding headers.
- Split non-secret values into Compose env/Helm ConfigMaps and credentials into
  the uncommitted Compose env or Kubernetes Secret references. Production
  values contain no credential defaults and reject placeholder/all-zero values.
- Add per-service `enabled`, external endpoint/Secret reference, image
  repository/tag/digest, resources, persistence and storage settings. Exactly
  one bundled or external provider must be effective for each required service.

### Docker Compose Work

1. Add an edge proxy with checked-in safe templates and uncommitted certificate
   mounts. Route NomoSmart and Keycloak on one host, preserve path/query on the
   80-to-443 redirect, overwrite forwarding headers and restrict admin/master
   paths by configured CIDRs.
2. Remove default host `ports` from frontend, backend and every peripheral.
   Use internal `expose`/networks and an opt-in debug profile whose bindings are
   fixed to `127.0.0.1`.
3. Add least-privilege PostgreSQL bootstrap for separate application and
   Keycloak databases/users. Keep Flyway as the only NomoSmart schema runner.
4. Add idempotent S3 bucket and Keycloak realm/client bootstrap jobs with health
   gates. Replace development-only Keycloak startup with a production-capable
   command in production mode while retaining an explicit development profile.
5. Ensure backend, worker and Beat wait for migration plus required services;
   edge readiness must not report success before application readiness.
6. Add upgrade notes for existing volumes, including Keycloak backup/restore
   from the current shared database arrangement.

### Helm Work

1. Add namespaced, single-instance bundled templates for PostgreSQL, Redis,
   RustFS, OpenSearch, Neo4j, Keycloak and ClamAV using pinned upstream images.
   Avoid cluster-scoped operators and unpinned runtime chart dependencies.
2. Add ClusterIP Services, StatefulSets/PVC retention for stateful components,
   Deployments where state is externalized, pod/container security contexts,
   resource requests/limits, probes, service accounts and NetworkPolicies.
3. Add one-host Ingress paths for NomoSmart and public Keycloak endpoints.
   Render the restricted Keycloak admin path separately so operator-provided
   ingress annotations/CIDR controls do not affect public login paths.
4. Implement fresh-install database/bootstrap/migration Jobs that can run after
   bundled PostgreSQL becomes ready while app init containers wait on durable
   completion evidence. Implement a pre-rollout upgrade migration hook/Job
   against the existing database so failure blocks new app pods.
5. Add values/schema branches for bundled and external modes, persistence,
   storage classes, TLS Secret, ingress class/annotations, public host, admin
   access, image pins and all credential Secret keys.
6. Preserve uninstall PVCs by default and document explicit data deletion.
   Rollback reuses retained state and never attempts automatic down-migration.

### Keycloak And LDAP/AD Administration

- Bootstrap the `nomosmart` realm, branded theme, PKCE frontend client,
  confidential backend/sync clients, audience/group claims and safe redirect /
  post-logout URLs for the single public host.
- Configure `KC_HOSTNAME` with the full HTTPS `/identity` URL,
  `KC_HTTP_RELATIVE_PATH=/identity`, trusted proxy headers and internal-only
  management health/metrics. Public routes exclude admin/master/metrics/health
  unless the admin path is explicitly restricted.
- Document administrator access at
  `https://<public-host>/identity/admin/` from the allowed network. In the
  `nomosmart` realm, use User Federation -> Add LDAP provider.
- Recommend Active Directory vendor mode for AD and the matching LDAP vendor
  mode otherwise; use verified `ldaps://...:636` or StartTLS, a least-privilege
  read-only Bind DN, `READ_ONLY`, Import Users enabled and Sync Registrations
  disabled.
- Document Users DN/Groups DN plus username (`sAMAccountName` for typical AD or
  `uid` for typical LDAP), UUID (`objectGUID` or `entryUUID`), email, name,
  employee number, department, manager, disabled-state and group membership
  mappers. Values are examples and must be verified against the real directory
  schema.
- Require Keycloak connection/authentication tests, initial full sync, changed-
  user sync, group verification and then NomoSmart external-group-to-role
  mapping. Rotation changes the Keycloak-side bind credential and verifies sync;
  NomoSmart never receives or displays the credential.

### Test Strategy

- Static/config: Compose config, Helm lint/template/schema, image pin and
  secret/config policy, no public native ports, TLS/issuer/path invariants and
  bundled/external exclusivity.
- Docker live: full clean install, restart with retained volumes, migration
  rerun, bucket/realm bootstrap rerun, 80 redirect, 443 app/OIDC login, admin
  access denial/allow, real PostgreSQL/Redis/S3/OpenSearch/Neo4j/ClamAV health,
  worker task and intentional dependency/migration failure.
- Kubernetes live: install into a disposable namespace/cluster with a real
  StorageClass and Ingress, wait for Jobs/PVCs/pods, exercise HTTPS app/OIDC,
  inspect NetworkPolicies/Services, restart stateful pods, upgrade, failed
  migration block, rollback, uninstall and PVC retention.
- External mode: switch each peripheral independently to a real isolated test
  service, prove the bundled workload is absent and NomoSmart still reaches the
  external endpoint through its Secret/config contract.
- Identity: verify public issuer, internal discovery/JWKS transport, realm and
  clients, callback/logout, forwarded-header hardening and no public management
  endpoints. Run LDAP/AD federation acceptance only against an operator-
  supplied non-production directory; otherwise record it as blocked under
  `TEST-002` without fake success.
- Operations: backup/restore rehearsal for PostgreSQL, Keycloak, RustFS,
  OpenSearch and Neo4j; log/redaction checks; secret and TLS rotation; resource
  and non-HA documentation review.

### Risks And Controls

- Existing Keycloak tables share the NomoSmart PostgreSQL database. Control:
  require backup plus tested database export/import or explicit development
  realm rebuild before separating credentials; never auto-drop old tables.
- Helm first install cannot run a pre-install migration against a PostgreSQL
  StatefulSet that does not exist yet. Control: concurrent install bootstrap /
  migration Jobs plus app init gates, followed by pre-rollout upgrade hooks
  once the database already exists; test `helm upgrade --install --wait`.
- Path-based Keycloak hosting can emit an incorrect issuer or intercept the
  NomoSmart `/auth/callback`. Control: reserve only `/identity`, set Keycloak
  hostname/relative path explicitly and test discovery, callback, logout,
  static resources and admin restrictions through the real edge.
- Internal workloads may be unable to hairpin through the public host. Control:
  separate public issuer validation from internal discovery/JWKS transport and
  test issuer equality rather than weakening hostname or JWT validation.
- Bundled stateful services are resource-heavy and non-HA. Control: expose
  explicit resources/storage values, document minimum capacity and support
  per-service external mode without claiming HA for the baseline.

### Planned Verification After Gate 4

- `git diff --check`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:plan`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh docker:config`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh helm:lint`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh deploy:config-policy`
- focused deployment/config security tests
- live Docker Compose full-stack acceptance
- live disposable-cluster Helm install/upgrade/failure/rollback acceptance
- relevant backend/frontend/OIDC integration and coverage checks

### Gate 4 Approval Request

Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-07-20 with:

`Peter approves CHG-229 Full-stack Single-domain Deployment`

### Implementation And Verification Result

- Root Compose now publishes only the Nginx edge on 80/443 by default and
  bundles PostgreSQL, Redis, RustFS, OpenSearch, Neo4j, Keycloak and ClamAV via
  independently removable profiles. A loopback-only `debug` profile exposes
  selected native ports for troubleshooting.
- Helm chart `0.2.0` defaults every peripheral to `bundled`, renders only
  namespaced ClusterIP workloads, PVC retention, probes, resources,
  NetworkPolicy, one-host Ingress and restricted Keycloak admin/master paths,
  and suppresses each workload independently when its mode is `external`.
- Public OIDC issuer validation remains HTTPS and exact while typed internal
  discovery, JWKS and Keycloak Admin transport endpoints avoid hairpin routing.
  RustFS and OpenSearch use operator-provided TLS certificates and CA bundles.
- The custom NomoSmart PostgreSQL image is based on pinned `18.4-alpine` and
  mounts the PostgreSQL 18 official volume root. Flyway is pinned to current
  Engine `13.0.0`; the live database and repository migration chain both
  report `V032`.
- `git diff --check`, governance gates, backend syntax, Compose config (normal
  and debug), Helm lint/render (development, production, each external mode and
  all-external), deployment policy, upstream registry tag checks and focused Backend
  deployment/config/live-service tests `31/31` passed.
- An isolated disposable Compose PostgreSQL instance created separate
  `nomosmart` and `keycloak` databases owned by separate non-superuser roles.
  Flyway applied all 32 migrations, a second run was idempotent, and restart
  preserved `V032`, role attributes and database ownership. The exact test
  container, network and named volume were removed afterward.
- Full Backend live regression reached `164 passed`; two cases were blocked by
  the unavailable local ClamAV endpoint, and the unchanged aggregate coverage
  gate failed at `68.74%` versus 80%. A disposable Kubernetes API is not

## CHG-230 Identity Settings Keycloak Popup Reauthentication

Gate 2 was confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-14 with `OK`. Gate 3 plan prepared on
2026-07-14. Gate 4 was approved by Peter on 2026-07-14 with
`Peter approves CHG-230 Identity Settings Keycloak Popup Reauthentication`.
Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-07-14.

Requirement under change: `AUTH-013`, refining the existing `AUTH-003` and
`OIDC-REAUTH-001` Identity Settings unlock flow.

### Confirmed Understanding

- The current button is wrong in two ways: it is rendered even when the current
  user lacks `SystemManagement.edit`, and its confirmed action navigates the
  whole System Management page to Keycloak.
- A view-only user may keep viewing the locked Identity Settings content, but
  must not see any edit/unlock entry or post-unlock controls.
- An edit-capable user first sees a NomoSmart confirmation Modal. Continuing
  opens a Keycloak-owned Popup for fresh authentication while the parent System
  Management page remains in place.
- NomoSmart does not render a password input and never receives password, OTP,
  Passkey, MFA or LDAP/AD credential values. Keycloak remains the only
  credential surface and Authorization Code + PKCE remains the protocol.
- Successful validation of the same current user/session and latest edit
  permission closes the Popup and unlocks the existing page for the retained
  10-minute server-side grant. Failure stays locked with retry feedback.
- This change applies only to the locked Identity Settings area. System
  Parameters, initial `draft_unvalidated` identity setup and normal
  login/session-expiry routing are unchanged.

### Scope And Approach

1. Gate the locked Identity Settings action on the same effective
   `SystemManagement.edit` union used by backend authorization. Do not render
   the action for view-only users; keep all backend permission checks.
2. Replace the current explanatory/full-page flow with an accessible Modal that
   identifies the protected action, explains Keycloak verification and exposes
   cancel/continue states without any credential field.
3. On the explicit Continue click, synchronously create a bounded blank Popup
   so browser popup blockers see a direct user gesture, then request the
   existing backend-issued authorization URL and navigate only that Popup. If
   creation or URL acquisition fails, close any blank Popup and keep the parent
   locked.
4. Keep the existing OIDC flow state, nonce, PKCE, `prompt=login`, `max_age=0`,
   five-minute flow TTL, one-time completion cookie and ten-minute
   `IdentityUnlockGrant`. Change only the Identity Settings callback completion
   presentation so it reaches a fixed same-origin Popup completion route rather
   than `/system?identityReauth=...`.
5. The completion route sends only an enumerated success/cancel/error message to
   its opener using the exact application origin and closes itself. It never
   displays or posts tokens, code, state, nonce or provider error data.
6. The parent accepts a result only when both `event.origin` equals the current
   application origin and `event.source` is the exact Popup handle. On success
   it calls the existing authenticated complete API, whose HttpOnly cookie and
   backend flow binding remain authoritative, then enters the existing unlocked
   state and countdown without reloading.
7. Detect blocked Popup, user-close/cancel, callback error and flow timeout.
   Clean up message listeners, polling/timers and Popup references on every
   terminal state and component unmount. Keep the Modal available with a safe
   localized error and Retry action.
8. Preserve candidate validation, atomic activation, last-known-good rollback,
   explicit lock, leave-tab revocation, unlock expiry, audit redaction and all
   existing backend authorization behavior.

### API And State Contract

- `POST /api/v1/system/identity-settings/reauth/start` remains edit-protected
  and returns an opaque Keycloak `authorization_url`; the URL is sent only to
  the newly created Popup.
- `GET /api/v1/system/identity-settings/reauth/callback` retains code/state
  validation and the HttpOnly one-time completion cookie. It redirects to a
  fixed same-origin Popup result route with only an enumerated result.
- `POST /api/v1/system/identity-settings/reauth/complete` remains bearer-session
  and edit-protected and returns `status` plus `expires_at` only after same-user,
  same-subject, same-session, scope, auth-time and one-time-flow validation.
- Direct start/complete/lock/validate/activate requests by a view-only or
  newly-revoked user remain 403 even when called outside the UI.
- No password-verification endpoint, Direct Access Grant, iframe, token-bearing
  message, browser credential storage or database migration is introduced.

### Frontend Work

- Update `SystemManagementWorkspace` permission-based rendering and replace
  full-page `window.location.assign` with a small explicit Popup state machine.
- Add reusable localized Modal states for ready, opening, waiting, blocked,
  cancelled, timed out, provider error, completion error and success.
- Add a same-origin Popup completion page/component whose only responsibility is
  safe parent notification and window close, including a visible close fallback
  when automatic close is unavailable.
- Keep focus inside the Modal, return focus to the trigger after failure/cancel,
  support Escape before the Popup starts and provide understandable live status.
- Update both Traditional Chinese and English dictionaries and remove obsolete
  copy that says the whole page will redirect.

### Backend Work

- Refine the Identity Settings callback success/error destinations to the fixed
  Popup completion route while retaining fail-closed OIDC verification.
- Use fixed enumerated result codes only; provider error strings and query
  payloads must not cross into the parent page.
- Retain current permission checks at start, complete, lock, validate and
  activate. Add or extend tests proving permission removal between start and
  complete/save cannot unlock or mutate settings.
- Preserve one-time completion, replay rejection, flow expiry/revocation,
  session binding, audit records and redaction.

### Out Of Scope

- A NomoSmart password field or API, Keycloak Direct Access Grant/ROPC, embedded
  Keycloak iframe, password reset, MFA enrollment or credential management.
- Changes to ordinary login, silent SSO, session-expiry recovery, logout,
  Keycloak client authentication policy or the 10-minute unlock duration.
- Changes to System Parameters, initial first-run identity draft behavior,
  LDAP/AD credentials, database schema or deployment topology.

### Test Strategy

- Frontend contracts/components cover edit-only rendering, complete absence for
  view-only users, no password/iframe/location-assign path, synchronous Popup
  creation, exact origin/source validation, close/timeout cleanup and every
  localized terminal state.
- Backend focused tests cover edit denial, same-user/session/auth-time binding,
  state/nonce/PKCE callback behavior, fixed result destinations, one-time
  completion/replay, expiry/revocation and no credential/error leakage.
- Regression checks preserve the existing identity candidate validation,
  activation, 10-minute grant, explicit lock and last-known-good behavior.
- Authenticated Browser acceptance verifies view-only hiding and edit-capable
  Popup behavior against real Keycloak. Actual credential/MFA completion must
  use a real authorized test account or be reported blocked under `TEST-002`;
  no fake success may satisfy acceptance.

### Deployment And Migration Impact

- No database migration is expected. The existing reauth flow and unlock grant
  records are reused.
- No new secret or Keycloak client capability is expected. The frontend public
  client must keep `directAccessGrantsEnabled=false` and PKCE S256.
- The same-origin Popup completion route must be included in frontend route and
  security-header verification. Existing callback allowlists remain unchanged
  unless characterization proves a fixed safe route addition is required.

### Risks And Controls

- Popup blocker: open synchronously from the Continue gesture; on failure show
  a retry state and never claim unlock.
- Spoofed cross-window message: require exact origin and exact Popup source;
  treat messages as notification only and let the HttpOnly completion cookie
  plus backend binding authorize unlock.
- Popup closed during authentication: poll only the known handle, stop at close
  or five-minute timeout and clean all resources.
- Permission changes mid-flow: recheck effective permission at complete and at
  mutation; frontend state cannot override backend denial.
- Credential leakage: keep authentication entirely in Keycloak and assert no

## CHG-231 Deployment-only Initialization and Setup Wizard Removal

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-14 with `1. 是`, `2. 是`, `3. 是`.
Gate 3 development plan is complete and Gate 4 approved. Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-07-14 with
`Peter approves CHG-231 Deployment-only Initialization and Setup Wizard Removal`.
Implementation is complete. Repository, frontend, backend, migration and rendered
deployment verification are complete; disposable-cluster Helm lifecycle acceptance
and the repository-wide 80% coverage release gate remain open.

Requirement under change: `DEPLOY-006`, superseding the active behavior of
`INIT-001` through `INIT-006` while preserving historical migrations for safe
upgrades.

### Confirmed Understanding

- Remove the `/setup` Wizard completely, including its frontend route, auth
  allowlist behavior, components, styles, locale text and API client contracts.
- Remove the backend system-initialization HTTP router, application/domain
  behavior, bootstrap-token/CIDR boundary, schemas, active ORM access and
  runtime configuration. The removed API is not replaced by another HTTP or UI
  initialization path.
- `/setup` and every `/api/v1/system-initialization/*` request return the normal
  framework `404` in every authentication state. They do not redirect, expose a
  retired notice, accept an old token or mutate initialization records.
- Docker Compose and Kubernetes through the existing Helm chart are the only
  supported formal/deployable installation methods. No raw Kubernetes manifest
  set or second chart is introduced.
- Direct frontend/backend execution remains available to engineers for
  development and testing when external configuration and initialized real
  dependencies are supplied. It is not a supported deployment artifact and
  does not restore first-run initialization behavior.
- Existing `system_initialization_state` and `system_initialization_steps`
  tables/migrations remain in upgraded databases. Runtime code stops importing,
  mapping, reading or writing them; no destructive drop migration is added.

### Characterization Findings

- The current frontend still defines `/setup`, treats it as a public auth path,
  includes it in the root-layout hydration fallback and retains a large
  setup-specific style/i18n surface.
- The backend still includes `system_initialization` in the API router and has
  route, domain, access-control, schema, model and configuration code for the
  retired workflow.
- Root Compose already runs a one-shot Flyway `migration` service and gates the
  backend on its success, but it still exposes initialization environment
  variables and has no explicit deployment bootstrap completion gate.
- The existing Helm chart renders application Deployments, Services,
  ConfigMap/Secret and Ingress only. It currently has no migration/bootstrap
  Job or workload init gate, although backend readiness probes already exist.
- Broader bundled-service parity, one-domain edge/TLS and external-service
  switching remain separately governed by pending CHG-229. Approving CHG-231
  does not implicitly approve that larger topology change.

### Scope And Approach

1. Remove the Web/API initialization surfaces and every runtime dependency on
   the retired initialization state.
2. Move required first-install and upgrade work to explicit one-shot deployment
   commands used by Compose services and Helm Jobs only.
3. Make migration/bootstrap idempotent, secret-safe and fail closed. Application
   backend, worker and Beat cannot become ready until required deployment work
   has completed successfully.
4. Keep schema history forward-only and retain legacy initialization tables
   without runtime access or a drop migration.
5. Update operator documentation to present only Compose and Helm install,
   upgrade, retry, rollback and log-inspection procedures while retaining
   engineering-only direct-run instructions as unsupported development setup.

### Frontend Work

- Delete `frontend/src/app/setup/page.tsx` and any setup-only component/module.
- Remove `/setup` from `AuthProvider` public-path logic, root-layout hydration
  fallback and any navigation, callback, redirect, sitemap or route allowlist.
- Remove setup API request/response types and helpers from `frontend/src/lib/api.ts`.
- Remove setup-only CSS and Traditional Chinese/English locale keys after a
  reference scan proves they are unused; keep unrelated data-service “setup”
  wording and identity/MFA setup copy intact.
- Add a route contract proving anonymous and authenticated visits receive the
  standard Next.js not-found result without login/home redirection.

### Backend Work

- Remove `system_initialization` from the API router and delete its route,
  domain and initialization-access modules.
- Remove system-initialization request/response schemas, active ORM model
  mappings and imports. Retain SQL migration files that created or extended the
  historical tables.
- Remove `SYSTEM_INITIALIZATION_*` settings, bootstrap-token secret checks,
  CIDR parsing dedicated to initialization, config-file mutation and appliance
  Flyway execution from the runtime configuration layer and examples.
- Add only a non-HTTP deployment bootstrap command with a narrow exit-code
  contract for one-shot Compose/Helm execution. It must not import the API
  router, expose a network listener, accept a browser token or read/write legacy
  initialization tables.
- Reuse typed runtime configuration and real service clients where practical.
  Bootstrap verifies required schema/dependencies and creates only explicitly
  deployment-owned idempotent resources, such as required S3 buckets and
  operator-approved Keycloak bootstrap artifacts. Secrets and document content
  must not appear in command output or logs.
- Keep `/api/v1/health` process-liveness semantics and make `/api/v1/ready`
  reflect required migrated/bootstrap-ready dependency evidence, never legacy
  Wizard state.

### Docker Compose Work

- Retain Flyway as the only schema migration owner and keep `migration` as a
  one-shot `service_completed_successfully` dependency.
- Add an idempotent one-shot deployment-bootstrap service after migration and
  required real services. Gate backend on both migration and bootstrap success;
  worker and Beat remain transitively gated by healthy backend.
- Remove all `SYSTEM_INITIALIZATION_*` values from Compose and
  `deploy/docker/nomosmart.env.example`.
- Prove clean install, restart and rerun do not duplicate schema/resources or
  overwrite operator data. A forced migration/bootstrap failure must leave app
  workloads unavailable and expose only redacted service/job evidence.
- Document retry and recovery through Compose service/job commands; never direct
  operators to `/setup` or an initialization API.

### Helm Work

- Extend only `deploy/helm/nomosmart` with migration and deployment-bootstrap
  Job templates plus values/schema for images, command, retry/backoff, timeout
  and existing Secret references. Do not add raw Kubernetes manifests.
- Use install/upgrade lifecycle ordering that works with externally supplied or
  chart-managed dependencies. Application pods receive an init gate or durable
  equivalent and cannot become ready before the current release's migration and
  bootstrap evidence succeeds.
- A failed migration/bootstrap Job must fail the install/upgrade and prevent new
  application readiness. Retry after correcting configuration is idempotent;
  rollback does not run a down migration or delete retained data.
- Remove initialization settings and bootstrap token from values, schema,
  ConfigMap/Secret rendering and environment-specific values.
- CHG-231 does not add the bundled PostgreSQL/Redis/RustFS/OpenSearch/Neo4j/
  Keycloak/ClamAV topology or one-host edge defined by CHG-229; its Jobs operate
  against the chart's typed configured service endpoints.

### Data And Compatibility

- Do not edit or delete historical Flyway files that created
  `system_initialization_state` or `system_initialization_steps`.
- Do not add a migration that drops or rewrites those tables. Existing rows are
  inert compatibility data and are excluded from readiness and bootstrap.
- Fresh databases still apply the immutable historical migration chain, then
  ignore the legacy tables. Upgraded databases preserve row counts/content.
- Remove active ORM mappings so accidental runtime access becomes visible
  during review/tests. Any remaining historical documentation must label the
  tables and old API as retired rather than supported behavior.

### Out Of Scope

- CHG-229 full-stack Helm bundling, one-domain 80/443 edge, Keycloak
  `/identity`, service external-mode switches and stateful HA architecture.
- A replacement administrator Wizard, hidden setup route, authenticated setup
  page, bootstrap-token endpoint, raw Kubernetes YAML distribution or a second
  Helm chart.
- Dropping legacy initialization tables, down migrations, deleting existing
  operator data or automatically rewriting an existing environment file.
- Removing ordinary engineering commands for lint, build, tests or running an
  app process against already configured dependencies.

### Test Strategy

- Frontend contracts prove `/setup` source/allowlist/API/styles/locale removal
  and real anonymous/authenticated standard 404 behavior without redirects.
- Backend contracts and live API tests prove the complete retired endpoint
  family returns 404, ignores old bootstrap headers and creates no DB/audit
  state. Source/config tests prove no active initialization module, schema,
  model or environment key remains.
- Compose acceptance covers clean migration/bootstrap, readiness ordering,
  idempotent restart/rerun, missing config, dependency failure, migration
  failure, bootstrap failure, corrected retry and redacted logs.
- Helm static/live acceptance covers lint/schema/rendering, Jobs and app gate,
  clean install, upgrade, failure block, corrected retry, rollback and no raw
  manifest alternative in a disposable real namespace.
- Upgrade tests snapshot legacy initialization rows before and after app startup,
  deployment bootstrap and ordinary requests to prove preservation and zero
  runtime writes.
- Run focused tests first, then frontend/backend suites, deployment checks and
  the unchanged 80% coverage gate. `TEST-002` forbids a fake migration,
  bootstrap, dependency or Kubernetes success result.

### Deployment And Documentation Impact

- This is a breaking removal for prior appliance/Web-initialized operation.
  Release notes must direct operators to externalize settings and choose Compose
  or Helm before upgrade.
- Update `deploy/README.md`, chart notes and safe examples with prerequisites,
  install/upgrade/retry/rollback/uninstall and migration/bootstrap log commands.
- Configuration examples contain placeholders only. Existing real secrets are
  never migrated into source-controlled files or printed during validation.
- Direct-run development documentation must clearly state that it assumes
  already initialized real services and is not a supported production install.

### Risks And Controls

- Removing the Wizard before deployment gates exist would make fresh installs
  unusable. Control: deliver route/API removal and both deployment gates in the
  same approved change and accept only after live install evidence.
- Helm hook ordering can deadlock when a bundled database is not present yet.
  Control: support the chart's configured endpoint contract, use explicit Job
  completion evidence and test install/upgrade ordering in a disposable cluster;
  CHG-229 owns future bundled-database ordering.
- Historical tables can tempt later code to reuse obsolete state. Control:
  remove ORM mappings/imports and add source plus runtime no-I/O regression.
- Job retries can repeat external side effects. Control: use deterministic
  resource identifiers, create-or-verify semantics and fail on incompatible
  existing configuration instead of overwriting it.
- Removing old environment keys can hide operator misconfiguration. Control:
  document removed keys and fail startup on missing required current typed
  configuration without falling back to setup mode.

### Planned Verification After Gate 4

- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved`

## CHG-232 Keycloak Authentication Experience Redesign

### Status and Gate

- Gate 1 specification understanding: complete.
- Gate 2 human confirmation: confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-14 with
  `1. A`, `2. B`, `3. A`.
- Gate 3 development plan and test design: complete.
- Gate 4 implementation approval: approved by Peter on 2026-07-14 with
  `Peter approves CHG-232 Keycloak Authentication Experience Redesign`.
  Implementation, live realm mutation and feature tests may proceed.

Requirement under change: `AUTH-005`, with `AUTH-001`, `AUTH-009` through
`AUTH-013`, `I18N-001`, `SEC-001` and `TEST-002` retained as governing
authentication, locale, security and live-verification boundaries.

### Specification Understanding

- The screenshot is Keycloak's default polygon login theme, not the repository's
  NomoSmart theme. The current live `nomosmart` realm has no selected
  `loginTheme`, and internationalization is disabled.
- A minimal theme already exists under `deploy/keycloak/themes/nomosmart`, but
  it customizes only login and OTP markup and has an eleven-line CSS surface.
  Enabling it without further work would still leave recovery, error,
  information and required-action pages inconsistent.
- The requested result is one coherent NomoSmart public authentication journey,
  not a cosmetic background replacement. It must remain calm, operational and
  consistent with the main application while Keycloak remains the exclusive
  credential owner.
- Locale is selected from browser preference when no explicit or existing
  Keycloak locale exists. `zh-TW` and `en` remain manually switchable, and
  unsupported browser languages fall back to `zh-TW`.
- CHG-232 does not edit Browser Flow, force OTP, enroll existing users, assign a
  required action or change any LDAP/OIDC security behavior. The theme styles
  the OTP surface when the current operator-managed policy reaches it.
- A credential page must not claim that every login has two steps when OTP is
  not required. Page labels describe the current task, such as enterprise
  account or security verification, without predicting a later execution.

### Discussion and Confirmation Items

1. Complete public-authentication coverage versus login/OTP only: resolved as
   complete public-authentication coverage (`1. A`).
2. Default locale behavior: resolved as browser-driven with a manual language
   switch (`2. B`).
3. OTP enforcement: resolved as presentation-only with no authentication-policy
   change (`3. A`).
4. No open design, API, data, permission, deployment or testability question
   remains for Gate 3.

### Human Confirmation

Peter completed Gate 2 on 2026-07-14 with `1. A`, `2. B`, `3. A`. This confirms
the full Theme scope, browser-driven locale behavior and unchanged OTP policy.
Gate 4 was subsequently approved by Peter on 2026-07-14, authorizing the
planned implementation, live Keycloak realm update and feature verification.

### Characterization Findings

- `deploy/keycloak/themes/nomosmart/login/login.ftl` and `login-otp.ftl` use
  Keycloak's parent layout but provide only a small brand row, labels, inputs and
  submit buttons. Password visibility, busy state, locale navigation and a
  reusable authentication shell are absent.
- The CSS still uses a decorative gradient and only styles the card, two forms,
  generic inputs/buttons and an error border. It does not define robust mobile,
  inherited-page, focus-visible, reduced-motion or overflow behavior.
- `theme.properties` declares `en,zh-TW`, but the live realm does not enable
  internationalization or supported locales, so those resources are not active.
- Root Compose already mounts the theme read-only and pins Keycloak `26.0` with
  theme caches disabled. No new public service, port, volume or secret is needed.
- Deployment bootstrap sets `loginTheme=nomosmart` only when creating a missing
  realm. It does not reconcile an existing realm and currently does not declare
  the required locale settings.
- The NomoSmart frontend `/login` page already supplies the target brand,
  typography, palette and enterprise trust language. The Keycloak Theme should
  converge on that language without copying frontend credential handling.

### Development Plan

1. Build a Keycloak 26-compatible shared authentication shell.
   - Add the smallest child-theme layout override needed to supply semantic
     brand context, a bounded form workspace, status/message placement and
     locale navigation across inherited public authentication pages.
   - Continue inheriting stable Keycloak page logic and macros where possible;
     do not fork every upstream FreeMarker page.
   - Keep NomoSmart as the first-viewport brand signal and keep Admin Console and
     Account Console outside this theme.
2. Refine credential and OTP templates.
   - Preserve Keycloak form actions, hidden fields, autocomplete semantics,
     username retention rules and message sanitization.
   - Add an accessible password-visibility icon control and submission busy /
     duplicate-submit protection using only same-origin theme assets.
   - Replace unconditional numeric step text with current-task wording so a
     password-only Browser Flow is not misrepresented.
3. Replace the visual system and complete responsive states.
   - Use the repository palette, Noto Sans TC/system fallback, solid surfaces,
     restrained borders/shadows and radii no larger than 8px.
   - Define a desktop brand/context plus form layout and a compact single-column
     tablet/mobile layout with stable controls at `1440`, `1024`, `768` and
     `375` widths.
   - Cover normal, hover, focus-visible, error, information, disabled, busy and
     reduced-motion states without overlap, horizontal overflow or decorative
     polygon/gradient/orb backgrounds.
4. Complete Traditional Chinese and English theme resources.
   - Add every custom brand, trust, field helper, action and accessibility label
     to both Keycloak message bundles.
   - Enable Keycloak locale navigation, select from browser preference and use
     `zh-TW` as unsupported-language fallback.
   - Do not duplicate locale state in NomoSmart storage or add analytics.
5. Reconcile realm configuration without changing authentication state.
   - Extend the idempotent Keycloak realm bootstrap path so missing and existing
     realms converge on `loginTheme=nomosmart`, internationalization enabled,
     supported locales `zh-TW`/`en` and fallback `zh-TW`.
   - Read and preserve LDAP federation, users, groups, clients, roles, mappings,
     Browser Flow, required actions and OTP policy; fail on an incompatible
     response rather than recreating or overwriting the realm.
   - After tests pass, apply the same bounded settings to the current local
     `nomosmart` realm and verify the effective configuration.
6. Add focused automated and real-browser verification.
   - Extend theme contracts for required files, message-key parity, safe
     FreeMarker use, semantic labels/messages, same-origin assets and absence of
     default Keycloak visual artifacts.
   - Add non-destructive bootstrap tests proving existing realm resources and
     authentication executions are preserved while theme/locale settings
     converge.
   - Exercise the mounted theme against real Keycloak and capture desktop,
     tablet and mobile evidence for the common public authentication states.

### Implementation Areas

- `deploy/keycloak/themes/nomosmart/login/`: common FreeMarker layout, focused
  login/OTP templates, CSS, optional minimal same-origin behavior module and
  `zh-TW`/`en` messages.
- `backend/app/deployment/bootstrap.py`: idempotent existing-realm Theme/locale
  reconciliation only; no authentication-flow mutation.
- `deploy/keycloak/README.md`: Theme activation, locale behavior, upgrade and
  troubleshooting notes.
- Focused frontend/deployment tests that inspect the Theme contract and real
  Keycloak behavior. No NomoSmart credential form is added.

### Test Strategy

- Static contracts validate FreeMarker structure, sanitized Keycloak messages,
  key parity, local assets, locale declarations, accessible control semantics,
  responsive CSS contracts and no external asset/tracking URLs.
- Bootstrap tests compare a real realm's authentication executions, LDAP
  federation and identity/client/mapping inventory before and after
  reconciliation. Only Theme and locale properties may change.
- Real Keycloak Browser tests cover invalid credentials, successful LDAP-backed
  Peter login, information/error/session paths and disposable Keycloak-local
  required-action users. Temporary test users are removed afterward and LDAP is
  never modified.
- Browser locale tests use real `zh-TW` and `en` preferences, unsupported-locale
  fallback and manual switching across page transitions.
- Visual acceptance covers `1440x900`, `1024x768`, `768x1024` and `375x812`,
  plus keyboard-only focus order, password visibility, alert announcement,
  busy-state stability, reduced motion and no horizontal overflow.
- OTP rendering uses a real disposable Keycloak test identity/realm state when
  needed. A fake OTP success path is not accepted under `TEST-002`; lack of a
  safely disposable OTP prerequisite is reported as blocked rather than passed.
- Focused checks run first after Gate 4, followed by relevant frontend,
  deployment, OIDC regression and unchanged 80% coverage gates.

### Deployment and Configuration Impact

- No database schema, migration, API route, frontend route, permission, LDAP
  data, OIDC client secret, network port, Docker volume or Helm behavior changes.
- The existing Compose bind mount and Keycloak cache-disabled development flags
  are reused. Production image packaging must continue to include the same
  versioned theme path when CHG-229 later changes deployment topology.
- Existing realms receive a bounded Admin API update for Theme and locale only.
  New realms receive the same settings at creation. Rollback selects the prior
  login theme/locale properties without deleting realm state.

### Risks and Controls

- A copied upstream template can break on Keycloak upgrades. Control: target the
  pinned Keycloak `26.0` baseline, override only the shared shell and focused
  pages, retain parent behavior and exercise inherited pages in the real image.
- CSS that looks correct on login can hide controls on required-action pages.
  Control: use scoped common selectors, stable width/overflow constraints and
  real required-action visual acceptance at four viewports.
- Locale selection can conflict with explicit user choice. Control: preserve
  Keycloak's supported locale resolution order, limit choices to two and test
  browser preference, manual override and fallback separately.
- Realm reconciliation could overwrite operator authentication policy. Control:
  use a minimal read/merge/update payload, compare execution/federation/resource
  inventory before and after, and fail closed on unexpected drift.
- Busy-state scripting could block valid submission or expose credential data.
  Control: keep the script local and behavior-only, never read/store/log field
  values, preserve native form submission and test keyboard/retry behavior.

### Out of Scope

- Enabling or requiring OTP/MFA, enrolling Peter/John, changing Browser Flow,
  setting organization password policy or migrating credentials.
- Styling Keycloak Admin Console or Account Console.
- Changing the NomoSmart `/login` OIDC redirect page, callback, token storage,
  JWT validation, LDAP federation or system role mappings.
- Introducing a frontend styling framework, remote font/CDN, analytics,
  marketing illustration or a second Keycloak theme.

## CHG-233 Local Role and LDAP Group One-to-One Mapping

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-15 with `1A, 2A, 3A, 4A, 5A,
6A`. Gate 3 plan prepared on 2026-07-15. Gate 4 approved by Peter on
2026-07-15 with `Peter approves CHG-233 Local Role and LDAP Group One-to-One
Mapping`; implementation and focused/live acceptance are complete. The
repository-wide 80% coverage gate remains open and Helm verification remains
deferred by Peter.

### Confirmed Understanding

- NomoSmart owns Local roles. LDAP groups remain read-only identity objects
  synchronized through Keycloak and are not role records.
- Each active Local role and each active LDAP group can participate in at most
  one mapping. A Local role may remain unmapped and still have manual members.
- Mapping changes take effect immediately and transactionally in
  `role_users.source=external_sync`; they do not wait for the next scheduled
  identity sync.
- The member UI labels manual, LDAP-derived and protected break-glass sources.
  A user may retain more than one source, and effective membership is their
  union.
- `system-admin` is the only protected default role. Its LDAP mapping remains
  optional and editable, but the role itself cannot be renamed, disabled or
  deleted. The existing `systemadmin` mapping is retained and the broad `users`
  mapping is removed.
- Other existing seeded roles become normal Local roles. New installations
  must not finish with those historical roles as defaults.
- Local-role Delete remains a soft delete. It releases the LDAP mapping and
  derived memberships but preserves the role row, manual membership,
  permissions and audit history.

### Scope

1. Update the PostgreSQL/ORM contracts for LDAP origin, one-to-one mappings and
   deployment-protected break-glass role membership.
2. Replace the bulk mapping write with a role-scoped optimistic API and
   immediate reconciliation service.
3. Update identity sync and deployment bootstrap so mapper-path classification,
   normal sync, mapping changes and break-glass access converge on the same
   membership result.
4. Redesign the existing System Management role/group area into clearly
   separated Local-role and LDAP-group operational views with complete
   permissions, source labels and states.
5. Add forward-only migration, API compatibility notes, deployment parameters,
   bilingual copy, tests and traceability.

### Data And Migration Approach

1. Add `external_groups.identity_origin` with a constrained value set and
   backfill LDAP origin only from the configured, boundary-safe `/ldap` path;
   never infer origin from a group display name.
2. Replace the composite-only mapping uniqueness with independent unique
   constraints for `role_id` and `external_group_id`. Before constraints are
   installed, preserve the confirmed `system-admin -> systemadmin` mapping,
   remove `system-admin -> users`, and fail closed on any other ambiguous
   duplicate rather than silently choosing one.
3. Extend the allowed `role_users.source` contract with `break_glass`. Keep
   manual and break-glass rows during identity/mapping reconciliation and
   remove only affected `external_sync` rows.
4. Use a new forward migration; do not edit V003 or another applied migration.
   On an upgrade, preserve `project-owner`, `knowledge-editor` and `reviewer`
   with all data while changing them to ordinary Local roles. For a pristine
   database with no users, role usage, audit evidence or prior deployment
   bootstrap evidence, remove those historical seed rows so a fresh deployment
   ends with only `system-admin` as the protected default.
5. Snapshot the existing LDAP-group identity by stable Keycloak ID and LDAP DN
   while moving the Keycloak mapper root to `/ldap`; reconcile the NomoSmart
   group row and confirmed mapping after resync without deleting any LDAP group
   or LDAP member. Stale root-path snapshots become inactive only after a
   complete successful sync.
6. Supply rollback documentation. Schema rollback must not drop identity or
   role history; application rollback requires resolving one-to-one-only data
   into the older bulk contract without recreating the removed broad mapping.

### Backend And API Approach

1. Add one domain service for map, remap, unmap and soft-delete reconciliation.
   It locks the role, verifies active LDAP origin and unique ownership, updates
   the mapping, rebuilds only that role's `external_sync` rows, increments the
   role `lock_version`, writes audit and commits once.
2. Add `PUT /api/v1/roles/{role_id}/external-group-mapping` with
   `external_group_id | null` and `lock_version`. Return the current mapping,
   new lock version and derived-member count. Return safe `403`, `404`, `409`
   or `422` errors with no partial mutation.
3. Retain mapping GET. Remove the bulk PUT route and record the breaking
   administration contract in `API_COMPATIBILITY.md`; no public answering API
   behavior changes.
4. Enforce `SystemManagement.view/create/edit/delete` independently. Mapping
   and manual membership require edit; Local-role soft delete requires delete;
   `system-admin` protection applies regardless of permission union.
5. Preserve separate rows when one user is both manual and LDAP-derived. Return
   every source needed for the UI to render both badges.
6. Reuse the same reconciliation function after a complete identity sync so
   scheduled sync and immediate mapping changes cannot drift.
7. Extend deployment bootstrap to maintain the break-glass user's protected
   `system-admin` membership without mapping the Keycloak-local
   `/system-admin` group as LDAP or exposing it to the manual membership API.

### Frontend Approach

1. Split the current mixed workspace into Local Roles and LDAP Groups views
   using a compact segmented control or equivalent accessible subnavigation.
   Keep dense full-width operational layouts and avoid nested cards.
2. Local roles show protected/active state, mapped LDAP group, distinct manual
   and LDAP member counts, and edit/users/permissions/map/unmap/delete actions
   according to backend permissions. `system-admin` omits prohibited controls.
3. LDAP groups use a read-only table with group, `/ldap/**` path, sync status,
   member count and mapped Local role. No delete/edit/member-control action is
   rendered.
4. Mapping uses a focused dialog that excludes already mapped groups, supports
   explicit unmapping, explains immediate access impact, prevents double
   submission and handles stale/conflict responses by refreshing authoritative
   data.
5. Role users collapse duplicate people into one row while showing every
   applicable Manual, LDAP Group and Emergency Administrator badge. Only manual
   membership controls are interactive.
6. Soft delete uses a destructive confirmation naming the role and explaining
   mapping release and immediate LDAP-derived access removal. Add matching
   Traditional Chinese and English copy and responsive/error/empty/loading
   states.

### Test Strategy

- Migration: disposable fresh and populated upgrade databases, independent
  uniqueness, known duplicate cleanup, ambiguous-duplicate failure, legacy-role
  preservation/removal rules, idempotent bootstrap evidence and non-destructive
  rollback guidance.
- Backend live integration: real PostgreSQL plus isolated Keycloak/OpenLDAP
  groups for origin classification, zero-or-one mappings, stale lock, same-role
  and same-group conflicts, rollback on reconciliation failure, immediate
  derived membership, dual-source union, sync convergence, soft delete and
  `system-admin`/break-glass protection.
- Authorization: view/create/edit/delete combinations, disabled users, inactive
  roles/groups and denied destructive operations, with audit assertions and no
  sensitive LDAP/token content.
- Frontend: separated views, read-only LDAP actions, protected role controls,
  available-group filtering, conflict refresh, source badges including dual
  source, delete warning, loading/empty/forbidden/error states, zh/en, keyboard
  focus and narrow-screen behavior.
- Browser acceptance: use Peter for System Admin behavior and an isolated LDAP
  test identity plus Local role for map/unmap/manual-union flows. Do not alter
  permanent enterprise LDAP data; create and clean a disposable test namespace
  under `TEST-002`.
- Run focused checks first, then full frontend/backend suites and both aggregate
  80% coverage gates. Existing repository-wide deficits remain release blockers
  and are not waived by focused passing tests.

### Deployment And Configuration Impact

- Add `KEYCLOAK_LDAP_GROUP_PATH=/ldap` to typed backend/deployment settings,
  Docker example configuration and Helm ConfigMap/value/schema contracts.
- Update Keycloak federation documentation and deployment verification to
  require the LDAP mapper `groups.path` to match. Mapper-path migration needs a
  backup and a successful full identity sync before stale root groups are
  deactivated.
- Docker Compose configuration and real configured service acceptance are in
  scope. Per Peter's standing instruction, Helm runtime testing remains
  deferred; Helm templates/configuration still must be updated and the skipped
  verification documented as an acceptance gap until that deferral is lifted.
- No OpenSearch, Neo4j, S3 or answering/retrieval data changes are expected.

### Risks And Controls

- Changing Keycloak group paths can duplicate or orphan cached groups. Preserve
  stable IDs/DNs, resync completely, compare before/after memberships and only
  deactivate stale snapshots after success.
- Installing unique constraints with dirty mappings can silently revoke access.
  Handle only the approved known duplicate automatically and fail closed on
  every other ambiguity with an operator-readable migration error.
- Immediate reconciliation can race identity sync. Use the existing PostgreSQL
  identity synchronization lock plus role row locking and one transaction.
- Manual plus LDAP source rows can overcount users. UI/API report distinct
  effective users separately from per-source counts and retain both provenance
  rows.
- Removing seeded role assumptions can affect permission tests and reports.
  Replace name-based system-role assumptions with `system-admin` protection or
  ordinary Local-role fixtures and run full authorization/report regression.
- Break-glass access must not depend on LDAP. Keep it deployment-managed,
  non-editable and covered by real OIDC/MFA readiness evidence from `AUTH-004`.

### Out Of Scope

- Editing or deleting LDAP groups/users from NomoSmart.
- Direct NomoSmart LDAP bind or bypassing Keycloak federation.
- Many-to-many role/group mapping, automatic mapping by matching display name,
  or mapping Keycloak-local groups as LDAP.
- Permanent deletion of role history, permissions or manual membership.
- Changes to project Owner relationships, Public API answering, retrieval,
  reranking, citations, OpenSearch or Neo4j.
