Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-07-20 with:

`Peter approves CHG-242 First-use Break-glass And One-time Secret Packaging`

## CHG-244 Local-first Packaging Defaults And CHG-243 Community Neo4j Production Exception

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-20 with the exact combined
CHG-243/CHG-244 confirmation recorded in `SPEC_CHANGELOG.md`. Gate 3 development
plan is complete. Gate 4 was approved by Peter on 2026-07-20 with
`Peter approves CHG-243 Community Neo4j Production Exception and CHG-244 Local-first Packaging Defaults`;
implementation and the approved feature tests may run.

Requirements: refined `AUTH-016`, refined `DEPLOY-003`, `DEPLOY-005`,
`DEPLOY-007`, new `DEPLOY-008`, `TEST-002`, and the existing 80% release
coverage gate.

### Confirmed Understanding And Decisions

- Bundled Neo4j uses Community for development, factory acceptance and
  production. Peter accepts that every Community native user is
  admin-equivalent and role-level least privilege cannot be enforced.
- Neo4j bootstrap `neo4j` and runtime `nomosmart-service` identities remain
  separate for rotation, attribution and audit. This is not described or tested
  as an authorization boundary. Compensating network, Secret-mount and accepted-
  risk evidence are mandatory before production readiness can pass.
- The overridable default public host is `nomosmart.local`; Peter's workstation
  maps it to `127.0.0.1`. Compose and Docker-driver minikube expose the same
  single-domain HTTPS contract on loopback ports 80/443, but never run as two
  complete stacks simultaneously.
- Every package target/profile includes non-overwriting self-signed edge,
  RustFS and OpenSearch certificate material. Operator-provided trusted files or
  existing TLS Secrets take precedence. A client must explicitly trust the
  bundled CA; bypassing certificate verification is not acceptance evidence.
- Every first-use profile, including production onboarding, starts with Portal/
  Keycloak break-glass `nomosmart / nomosmart`. It is allowed only while the
  whole onboarding entry point is restricted to localhost or an explicit admin
  allowlist and Keycloak forces Update Password plus Configure TOTP. The known
  value must stop authenticating after password update and is forbidden after
  onboarding. Operational emergency enablement still generates a fresh random
  temporary password.
- All non-break-glass peripheral credentials keep CHG-242 independent random
  generation, one-time TTY handoff, scoped Secret mounts and redaction rules.
- The already requested destructive cleanup is complete: the old `minikube`
  profile and `nomosmart-chg242` containers/networks/volumes were removed. Images,
  repository files and unrelated Docker projects were retained.

### Scope And Implementation Approach

1. Characterize current CHG-242 package, TLS helper, Compose/Helm validation,
   Neo4j bootstrap/finalize behavior and focused tests before editing. Preserve
   all unrelated worktree changes and previously passing Secret boundaries.
2. Change package generation so `break_glass_initial_password` is exactly
   `nomosmart` for factory and production first-use packages. Remove only the
   CHG-242 production rejection for this one key; keep random generation,
   uniqueness, strength and placeholder rejection for every other Secret.
   Persist only its fingerprint/source/temporary state in safe metadata.
3. Enforce the known-password boundary at three layers: CLI/profile validation,
   deployment bootstrap/readiness and edge/Ingress configuration. Production
   accepts it only in `onboarding` with a localhost/admin source allowlist,
   `UPDATE_PASSWORD` and `CONFIGURE_TOTP`. Finalize and operational emergency
   paths continue to reject or rotate it.
4. Remove the production Enterprise requirement for bundled Neo4j. Keep the
   pinned Community image, distinct bootstrap/service credentials and bootstrap-
   only admin mount. Replace Enterprise fail-closed evidence with explicit
   `neo4j_community_admin_equivalent` accepted-risk evidence plus validation of
   internal-only services, no public native ports and least-scope NetworkPolicy.
   Do not weaken PostgreSQL/OpenSearch/Redis/RustFS/Keycloak controls.
5. Extend the package TLS workflow to Compose and Helm in every profile. Generate
   an environment-local CA and SAN-correct edge, RustFS and OpenSearch certificates
   atomically without overwrite; protect private keys; record safe certificate
   metadata; support explicit operator/existing-Secret precedence; and wire CA
   verification so normal health/OIDC/S3/OpenSearch clients do not use insecure
   bypasses.
6. Align base/dev/prod Compose and Helm defaults to `nomosmart.local` while
   retaining one-value FQDN overrides. Bind Compose edge to
   `127.0.0.1:80/443`. Document and validate the Docker-driver minikube profile
   with `--listen-address=127.0.0.1`, `--ports=127.0.0.1:80:80` and
   `--ports=127.0.0.1:443:443`, then
   enable Ingress without a public NodePort/LoadBalancer.
7. After Gate 4, update Peter's `/etc/hosts` idempotently so exactly one active
   `127.0.0.1 nomosmart.local` mapping exists. Resolve and show the exact existing
   entry before the privileged edit; do not replace unrelated host mappings.
8. Document a mutual-exclusion runbook: inspect current state, stop the selected
   NomoSmart runtime without deleting state, verify ports/workloads are released,
   and only then start the other. Add preflight evidence that fails acceptance
   when both complete NomoSmart stacks or a non-loopback 80/443 listener exist.
9. Update safe examples, package/Compose/Helm runbooks, release readiness,
   certificate trust/rotation, first-login/finalize and risk-acceptance guidance.
   Never include real generated private keys, peripheral passwords or Secret
   values in Git, Helm notes, logs or support bundles.
10. Build fresh live acceptance in sequence, not concurrently: first Compose
    from empty volumes through trusted-CA OIDC/password/TOTP and restart; stop it
    while retaining state; then create `nomosmart-acceptance` minikube, load the
    exact images, install the chart into an isolated namespace, repeat onboarding,
    restart/upgrade/rollback/PVC-retention checks, and stop the cluster before any
    Compose restart.

### Data, API And Configuration Impact

- No application business-table or Flyway migration is planned. Existing Neo4j
  graph data remains compatible because edition selection does not change the
  graph model or Cypher contract.
- No NomoSmart Web/API endpoint receives or returns the break-glass password,
  TOTP seed, CA private key or peripheral Secret. System Management remains
  read-only evidence.
- Configuration changes cover public host/origin/issuer defaults, loopback edge
  binding, onboarding allowlist/phase evidence, TLS source and file/Secret
  references, certificate status metadata and Neo4j accepted-risk evidence.
- The public OIDC issuer remains browser/token-facing while Frontend server-side
  discovery, code exchange and refresh use a separate internal Keycloak service
  issuer in Compose/Helm; the chart NetworkPolicy grants this exact Frontend path.
- Break-glass provisioning fills only missing Keycloak profile fields with the
  approved non-personal local defaults so first-use remains exactly password
  update plus TOTP; existing operator profile values are preserved.
- Existing CHG-242 production Secret packages are incompatible with the new
  first-use fingerprint/TLS inventory and require controlled regeneration or
  import; no automatic overwrite or deletion is allowed.
- Kubernetes scalar Secret staging files contain exact newline-free bytes so
  `kubectl create secret --from-file` cannot inject a trailing LF into Redis,
  OpenSearch, PostgreSQL, Keycloak or URL credentials. PEM and JSON files keep
  their required structured formatting.
- Application and migration images use a deterministic numeric non-root
  UID/GID matching Helm `securityContext`. The official ClamAV entrypoint keeps
  only its startup ownership/drop-user capabilities. RustFS uses the packaged
  TLS-capable image, and self-readiness probes use certificate-valid loopback
  resolution so default-deny NetworkPolicy cannot block a Pod from probing itself.

### Test Strategy

- Focused package tests cover the fixed break-glass value in both profiles,
  random/unique remaining credentials, no plaintext receipt, safe file modes,
  idempotency/no-overwrite, phase/allowlist rejection and operational random
  emergency rotation.
- TLS tests use real generated certificates and cryptographic inspection for CA,
  SAN, subject, expiry, private-key match, permissions, target/profile parity,
  trusted-source precedence, client trust and rotation/no-overwrite behavior.
- Package/Kubernetes tests prove scalar Secret files have no trailing CR/LF and
  real PostgreSQL, Redis, OpenSearch and Keycloak consumers receive identical
  bytes. Rendered security tests prove numeric non-root application/migration
  identities, the bounded ClamAV capability set and loopback self-probes.
- Deployment-policy tests cover loopback-only Compose/minikube exposure,
  `nomosmart.local` issuer/path consistency, onboarding source allowlist,
  mutual-exclusion preflight, no native public ports and no credential in rendered
  config/logs.
- Live Neo4j Community tests prove bootstrap/service credential separation,
  absence of admin Secret from app workloads, successful application graph
  behavior, explicit admin-equivalent risk status, NetworkPolicy boundaries,
  rotation, restart and backup/restore. No test claims role-level denial that
  Community cannot provide.
- Real Compose and minikube/Helm journeys use the trusted bundled CA, Keycloak
  first login, forced password update, TOTP, NomoSmart System Admin access,
  finalization preconditions, restart persistence and one-runtime-at-a-time
  evidence. Missing LDAP, browser credentials or cluster prerequisites are
  blocked under `TEST-002`, never replaced by mocks or TLS bypasses.
- Run focused checks first, then complete Backend/Frontend/E2E, coverage,
  dependency/static/container/image scans, SBOM, backup/restore and release-
  readiness gates without relaxing the 80% thresholds.

### Deployment, Migration And Rollback

- Back up state and retain the previous Secret/TLS generation before upgrading.
  Apply new package metadata and Secret references without overwriting the prior
  generation; verify trusted access before revoking old material.
- Rollback may restore the preceding image/config/Secret/TLS generation only
  while those credentials and certificates remain valid. A consumed fixed
  first-use credential is never restored; rollback after password update uses a
  new controlled emergency rotation.
- Compose/minikube switch operations preserve volumes/PVCs by default. Deleting
  a named project/profile remains a separate explicit operator action and is not
  part of normal start/stop or rollback.
- Real enterprise FQDN/trusted-certificate overrides remain forward compatible.
  Reverting to `nomosmart.local` requires loopback/allowlist and CA-trust evidence.

### Risks And Controls

- Known production first-use password is probed before claim. Control: edge is
  unreachable outside localhost/admin allowlist until required password/TOTP
  actions complete; phase and source restrictions are enforced independently by
  config policy, edge and bootstrap readiness.
- Self-signed TLS teaches users to bypass warnings. Control: ship/import the CA,
  require verified clients, reject `curl -k`/verify-false as acceptance evidence,
  show expiry/source, and prefer trusted operator material automatically.
- Community service identity performs administrative Cypher. Control: accepted
  residual risk is visible; native ports and admin Secret stay internal/scoped;
  network access, rotation and audit are mandatory. Do not advertise least
  privilege that does not exist.
- Two full local stacks exhaust resources or collide on ports. Control: loopback
  port ownership and workload preflight, explicit sequential runbook, and test
  evidence showing the inactive runtime stopped before the other starts.
- Host-file automation changes unrelated entries. Control: exact read-before-
  write, one hostname/address target, privileged approval, idempotent validation
  and no broad rewrite.

## CHG-245 Identity Settings Form Alignment And Validation Presentation

### Gate Status

- Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-20 with `ＯＫ`: make the Identity
  Settings form orderly and aligned, and include correction of the stale false

### Scope

- Refine only `/system?tab=identity`, preserving the existing NomoSmart palette,
  section hierarchy, lock state, controls and information content.
- Keep OIDC labels and controls aligned in two columns on desktop, with stable
  40px control heights, independent helper/error rows and a full-width long URL
  field.
- Keep directory synchronization policy, schedule, timezone, provider filters
  and actions aligned to the same form rhythm without changing their behavior.
- Revalidate the exact effective configuration received from the Backend so
  initial empty-state errors cannot survive a successful configuration load.
- Present every existing validated field's error at its own field with aligned
  Traditional Chinese and English copy and accessible relationships.
- Preserve responsive single-column behavior without overlap or horizontal
  overflow.

### Out Of Scope

- Any Backend, API, database, deployment or Keycloak configuration change.
- Changes to URL, Cron, timezone or LDAP Filter validation semantics.
- Changes to `AUTH-003` / `AUTH-013` fresh authentication, unlock duration,
  edit permission, save, manual synchronization or Secret masking behavior.
- Redesign of other System Management tabs or shared application navigation.

### Frontend Approach

1. Add a scoped Identity OIDC form class instead of changing the shared
   `.identity-form-grid` behavior used by unrelated model and prompt forms.
2. Make field groups top-aligned and keep controls at a stable 40px height;
   reserve no fake blank error area, but let helper/error rows flow below their
   own control without stretching the paired field.
3. Keep the desktop two-column arrangement, make Discovery / JWKS span the full
   row and use the existing narrow breakpoint for a one-column full-width form.
4. Apply similarly scoped alignment rules to the directory schedule/timezone
   row and preserve existing provider-filter structure.
5. Initialize Identity validation without rendering errors for unloaded blank
   defaults. After `GET /system/identity-settings` succeeds, set settings and
   validation from the same normalized response in one state transition.
6. Represent validation outcomes with stable codes or translation keys, while
   keeping the existing validation predicates unchanged. Render Issuer, Realm,

   fields.
7. Give controls stable IDs plus `aria-invalid` and conditional

8. Add aligned `zh-TW` and `en` locale entries and remove no still-used copy.

## CHG-246 Application-tier High Availability

### Gate Status

- Gate 1 understanding completed on 2026-07-21 after reviewing the existing
  `DEPLOY-005` non-HA baseline, production replica values and Helm workloads.
- Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-21: Helm/Kubernetes is the formal HA
  environment; Docker Compose remains single-host non-HA; Backend HA includes
  Celery Worker as recommended; Celery Beat remains single-active; and the claim
  is Application-tier HA while all bundled peripherals remain outside scope.
- Gate 3 development and test plan is recorded below.
- Gate 4 was never independently approved. Before any implementation or
  CHG-246 feature-test execution, this unchanged `DEPLOY-009` design was
  absorbed into CHG-247; the CHG-247 Gate 4 decision is now authoritative.

### Scope And Availability Contract

- Add `DEPLOY-009` as a formal Release blocker for Helm production.
- Require at least two Frontend, Backend API and Celery Worker replicas.
- Keep Celery Beat at exactly one active replica to prevent duplicate schedules;
  do not describe Beat as HA.
- Require the same component's replicas to run on different Kubernetes worker
  nodes, with at least two schedulable application nodes as a production
  prerequisite.
- Preserve service during one application Pod failure, one application-node
  drain and a compatible rolling upgrade/rollback.
- Keep authentication, authorization and API correctness independent of sticky
  sessions or pod-local state, and preserve existing worker lease/idempotency
  protections with multiple workers.
- Keep Docker Compose supported as a single-host non-HA deployment and clearly
  identify that boundary in operator/release documentation.

### Out Of Scope

- HA for PostgreSQL, Redis, RustFS, OpenSearch, Neo4j, Keycloak, ClamAV,
  Ingress Controller, Kubernetes control plane, storage, DNS, TLS or network.
- End-to-end service availability when an excluded peripheral is unavailable.
- HPA, predictive autoscaling, multi-cluster, multi-region and disaster recovery.
- Active-active Celery Beat or a new distributed scheduler/leader-election
  mechanism.
- Docker Swarm or multi-host Docker Compose orchestration.
- Closing LDAP, provider, coverage, backup-custody, scan/SBOM or other existing
  formal Release gaps.

### Helm And Configuration Approach

1. Add a typed application-HA values group with an explicit enabled state,
   node topology key, disruption budget, rollout surge/unavailable values and
   termination grace controls. Development/factory values may keep it disabled;
   production must enable it.
2. Extend `values.schema.json` so `APP_ENV=production` rejects Frontend,
   Backend or Worker replica counts below two, disabled application HA,
   `minAvailable < 1`, `maxUnavailable != 0`, missing surge capacity or an
   invalid topology key. Preserve one-replica development/factory rendering.
3. Render Frontend, Backend and Worker PodDisruptionBudgets with selectors
   scoped to the exact release and component. Baseline production uses
   `minAvailable: 1` for two replicas.
4. Add hard same-component Pod anti-affinity on
   `kubernetes.io/hostname`. Keep optional operator zone spread additive and do
   not relax the node-level constraint when zone labels are absent.
5. Configure Frontend, Backend and Worker Deployments with a rolling strategy
   of `maxUnavailable: 0` and at least one surge Pod. Keep existing bootstrap
   init/readiness gates authoritative before traffic or work begins.
6. Add bounded termination/drain behavior. Characterize Next.js, Uvicorn and
   Celery signal handling first; add lifecycle hooks only where the existing
   runtime cannot safely leave endpoints or stop taking new work by itself.
7. Keep Beat fixed at one replica and `Recreate`, documenting its scheduler
   availability boundary separately from the application-tier HA claim.
8. Do not add session affinity to Services. Prove Frontend server-side OIDC and
   Backend requests can alternate replicas using shared/signed state, and prove
   multiple workers cannot duplicate terminal state or external side effects.

### Expected Files

- `deploy/helm/nomosmart/values.yaml`
- `deploy/helm/nomosmart/values-prod.yaml`
- `deploy/helm/nomosmart/values.schema.json`
- Frontend, Backend, Worker and Beat templates under
  `deploy/helm/nomosmart/templates/`
- a new or consolidated PodDisruptionBudget template and shared Helm helpers
- `deploy/README.md`, `deploy/RELEASE_READINESS.md` and Helm notes
- focused deployment tests, expected under
  `backend/tests/test_chg246_application_tier_ha.py`
- a bounded multi-node live-acceptance entry point under the existing harness or
  deployment scripts
- Frontend/Backend application code only if characterization finds correctness
  dependent on pod-local state; any newly discovered behavior change must first
  refine the specification and traceability.

### Test Strategy

- Add static/schema tests for production minima, PDB selectors, hard node
  separation, rollout strategy, readiness, termination and Beat singleton.
- Add negative render tests for one replica, disabled HA, missing disruption
  control and relaxed same-node placement while confirming development/factory
  profiles remain valid.
- Run existing OIDC/frontend/backend behavior against requests distributed over
  multiple ready replicas, without sticky sessions.
- Run real multi-worker work with forced Worker termination/redelivery and
  verify one terminal transition/publication/external effect.
- In a disposable cluster with at least two application worker nodes, sustain
  authenticated traffic while deleting each component Pod, draining one node,
  upgrading and rolling back compatible images.
- Record peripheral failure as outside the HA claim; readiness may fail closed
  without converting the event into false application-tier success.
- Follow `TEST-002`: no mock, fake or deterministic success adapter may satisfy
  live HA acceptance.

### Deployment And Migration Impact

- No database migration or public API contract change is planned.
- Production platform prerequisites increase to at least two schedulable worker
  nodes plus capacity for one surge Pod per rolling application Deployment.
- Existing single-node development/factory environments remain supported but
  cannot produce production HA evidence.
- The current one-node `nomosmart-acceptance` Minikube profile is retained only
  as historical packaging evidence. CHG-247 `DEPLOY-009` live acceptance
  requires a separate disposable multi-node run, sequential with all other
  complete NomoSmart local runtimes as required by CHG-244.
- Existing bundled peripherals remain deployable, but their single-replica
  availability must stay visible in runbooks and release notes.

### Risks And Mitigations

- **False HA from replica count alone:** require node separation, PDB, rollout
  and live disruption evidence together.
- **Unschedulable production install:** fail preflight/acceptance with explicit
  node/capacity guidance rather than relaxing anti-affinity.
- **OIDC callback or refresh tied to one Pod:** alternate requests across Pods
  and reject any correctness dependency on sticky sessions/local memory.
- **Duplicate background side effects:** retain PostgreSQL locks, leases,
  idempotency and terminal-state guards; kill a real Worker during acceptance.
- **PDB blocks maintenance:** document the need for a second ready replica and
  controlled emergency override instead of weakening the default budget.
- **Surge exceeds cluster resources:** document minimum capacity and validate it
  before upgrade.
- **Overstated product availability:** use the exact term Application-tier HA
  and list every excluded peripheral/platform boundary.

## CHG-247 Release Gap Remediation, Scoped Knowledge Graph And Bundled Vault Integration

### Status And Gates

- Gate 1 completed on 2026-07-26 by comparing `SPECIFICATION.md`,
  implementation, tests and deployment artifacts and identifying twenty
  definite implementation gaps.
- Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-26. Peter rejected any global Knowledge
  Graph frontend or unscoped graph enumeration; retained one unified internal
  graph model exposed only through Backend-authorized Project/Document scopes;
  selected HashiCorp Vault; accepted Kubernetes Auth for Helm/Kubernetes,
  AppRole for Docker Compose and Vault KV v2 with mandatory TLS/CA; retained
  general webhook behavior as deferred/non-v1; and accepted the recommendations
  for the remaining eighteen audited items. Peter then expanded and reconfirmed
  the Vault deployment boundary with the exact phrase
  `接受 DEPLOY-011 隨包 Vault 建議`: Vault is part of the NomoSmart deployment
  package in both bundled Compose and bundled Helm modes while an explicit
  external-Vault mode remains supported.
- Gate 3 is recorded in this plan, the CHG-247 section of `TEST_PLAN.md` and the
  CHG-247 rows of `TRACEABILITY.md`.
- Gate 4 implementation approval: approved by Peter on 2026-07-26 with
  `Peter approves CHG-247 Release Gap Remediation, Scoped Knowledge Graph And Bundled Vault Integration`.
  Product implementation, database migration execution and CHG-247 feature or
  live-test execution may proceed under this approved plan.

### Specification Understanding

CHG-247 is one coordinated v1.0 correctness and release-remediation scope. The
twenty gaps are not independent UI polish: they share authorization, immutable
evidence, durable command, deployment and live-verification boundaries. The
Backend remains authoritative for scope and actions; work that can outlive an
HTTP request uses transactions, idempotency, outbox/lease and generation
fences; production configuration fails closed; and prior static-only or
historical completion claims do not satisfy the new requirements.

The Knowledge Graph remains a unified Neo4j/Backend data model so relationships
do not become isolated by storage design. It has no global user surface:
every content response is rooted in an authorized Project or Document, a
cross-project relationship is visible only when the caller can view both ends,
System Admin grants no knowledge-content bypass, and former unscoped routes are
removed rather than retained as compatibility aliases.

Vault is the only formal secret provider in this scope. It is delivered as a
NomoSmart-owned `bundled | external` deployment choice rather than an
external-only prerequisite. Bundled Compose runs one persistent,
TLS-protected, non-dev Vault server with Integrated Raft and is explicitly
single-host/non-HA. Bundled formal-production Helm vendors a pinned release of
the official HashiCorp Vault chart and runs a three-server Integrated Raft HA
topology with persistent data/audit storage, hard cross-node placement,
disruption protection and no public Ingress or UI. External mode points the
same application contract at an operator-managed Vault without installing a
server.

The application resolves canonical `vault://<mount>/<path>#<field>` references
from Vault KV v2, authenticates with Kubernetes Auth in Helm and AppRole in
Compose, validates HTTPS certificates and hostnames, uses short-lived
least-privilege credentials, keeps resolved values only in bounded process
memory and fails closed without logging or returning secret material. The sole
narrow filesystem exception is an owner-only `0700` ephemeral directory/`0600`
file for an SFTP library that cannot memory-load a private key; it is excluded
from backup/core collection and unlinked after success, failure, timeout or
cancellation.

Vault initialization, seal state, policy/auth bootstrap, snapshot/restore,
upgrade compatibility and key custody are first-class package lifecycle
concerns. Formal production defaults to operator-supplied KMS/HSM/Transit
auto-unseal. A self-contained Shamir deployment is permitted only with an
explicit `5/3` ceremony and acceptance of manual unseal/recovery duties. The
package may validate and orchestrate the ceremony, but never persists plaintext
or package-decryptable unseal/recovery shares, the initial root token,
auto-unseal credentials or resolved application secrets in its generated
bundle, Kubernetes Secrets, Compose files, receipts, logs or repository.
PGP ciphertext may be delivered only to an explicit owner-controlled
destination outside those surfaces, and the package retains no copy.

### Discussion And Confirmation Items

All blocking Gate 2 choices are resolved:

1. No global Knowledge Graph frontend, global count, unscoped query alias or
   unrestricted administrator view will be built.
2. Vault KV v2, Kubernetes Auth and workload-specific Compose AppRoles are fixed
   for v1.0. Both Compose and Helm support `vault.mode=bundled|external`;
   bundled is the new-install default, and external remains an explicit
   enterprise integration mode.
3. Compose Backend and Worker use distinct least-privilege AppRoles. Each Role
   ID is non-secret configuration; each Secret ID is supplied through its own
   uncommitted read-only file and is never placed in the repository or image.
4. Existing application-encrypted secret values remain readable during a
   controlled migration, but are not silently copied to Vault.
5. General webhooks are explicitly deferred beyond v1.0 and require a future
   companion specification before implementation.
6. Every other audited item follows the recommended contract now recorded in
   `SPECIFICATION.md` section 10.4.
7. Bundled Compose is persistent single-node Integrated Raft with TLS and is
   never presented as HA or permitted to use Vault dev mode.
8. Bundled formal-production Helm is a three-server HA Integrated Raft
   deployment delivered through a pinned and vendored official HashiCorp Vault
   chart dependency, with internal-only networking, persistent audit/data
   storage, anti-affinity, PDB and resources.
9. Formal production defaults to operator-provided auto-unseal. Shamir `5/3` is
   the explicit self-contained alternative; encrypted shares and the initial
   root token stay in separate operator custody outside the generated package.
10. NomoSmart owns redacted status/preflight, one-time initialization guidance,
    auth/policy/KV/audit bootstrap, root-token revocation verification,
    snapshot/restore and upgrade/rollback lifecycle tooling. It does not own an
    external KMS/HSM, external Vault, off-host backup repository or human key
    custodians.

No unresolved product choice remains before Gate 4. A new behavior decision
found during implementation must stop the affected batch and update the
specification, changelog, plan and traceability before code relies on it.

### Out Of Scope

- Any global or all-visible-project Knowledge Graph page, route, count,
  neighbor/path query or administrator bypass.
- AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, Google Secret Manager or a general
  multi-provider plugin framework in v1.0. A minimal typed secret-reference
  boundary remains in scope, with Vault as its only formal implementation.
- Provisioning or administering the operator's external KMS/HSM/Transit seal
  service, an external Vault cluster, the off-host encrypted backup repository,
  human key-custodian identities or enterprise recovery/DR replication.
- Public Vault Ingress/UI, Vault dev mode, automatic storage of root/unseal
  material, automatic copying of legacy credential values, and production
  single-node Vault.
- Producing a separate offline container-image tarball. The package pins and
  vendors the official Helm dependency and image identity; air-gapped operators
  mirror the pinned image through the documented registry override.
- General webhook delivery/trigger behavior, HMAC/replay policy or webhook UI.
- Database-table import, arbitrary CSV/JSON file upload or `.doc` ingestion.
- HA for PostgreSQL, Redis, RustFS/S3, OpenSearch, Neo4j, Keycloak, ClamAV,
  ingress, control plane, DNS, TLS or network; active-active Beat, HPA,
  multi-cluster and multi-region are also excluded. `DEPLOY-011` is the narrow
  exception: bundled formal-production Vault has its own three-server HA Raft
  requirement and storage/quorum acceptance.
- Implementation or feature/live-test execution before Gate 4.

### Development Plan

All numbered implementation, migration and test-code work in Batches 0-7 starts
only after Gate 4. Before Gate 4, Batch 0 is limited to the governance documents,
test design and non-feature governance checks already allowed by `AGENTS.md`.

#### Batch 0 — Contracts And Safety Baseline

1. Keep `SPECIFICATION.md`, `SPEC_CHANGELOG.md`, `API_COMPATIBILITY.md`,
   `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md`, `TEST_PLAN.md` and `TRACEABILITY.md` synchronized.
2. Add migration/API/deployment decision records before implementing each
   contract-changing batch.
3. Create shared stable error identities, audit action names, idempotency states
   and the fixed `PERM-005` capability vocabulary without weakening existing
   authorization.
4. Implement the AST/ESLint i18n guard, negative fixtures and narrow typed
   allowlist before Batches 1-4 add or change user-facing surfaces.
5. Strengthen governance tooling: `spec:trace` must reject duplicate stable IDs,
   active/historical status contradictions and missing mappings; an upgraded
   `coverage:check` or new `coverage:evidence` must bind reports to commit,
   dirty diff including untracked source/test files, generated full-suite
   manifest, timestamp and report hash.
6. Add focused negative tests first, including forbidden graph disclosure,
   stale completion claims and secret leakage.

#### Batch 1 — Authorization And Information Scope

1. Implement the central report policy and `Report.ModelReport` seed/migration;
   apply it consistently to summaries, detail fields, options, export and audit.
2. Add a Backend capability projection for Project/Document actions and consume
   it in update, re-extract, chunk and graph UI without using it as the
   authorization source.
3. Remove every global Knowledge Graph frontend entry and unscoped route.
   Build only scoped Project/Document graph, neighbors, paths and
   version-evidence surfaces with bounded payloads and side-channel-safe
   authorization-by-omission.
4. Implement one-time API key secret handling and paged/filtered key inventory.

#### Batch 2 — Durable Commands, Archive And Notifications

1. Add reusable idempotency records/response replay, request-hash conflict
   detection, transactional outbox and Worker lease/terminal-state primitives.
2. Apply them to switch-active and graph retry; HTTP graph retry creates only
   the durable attempt/outbox and never performs Neo4j work synchronously.
3. Add the shared signed/versioned cursor codec, stable envelope and
   cursor-supporting index primitives; migrate Notification and command/job
   inventories needed by this batch before later consumers depend on them.
4. Add Project archive generation/cancellation state. Every Worker validates the
   current generation before external writes and again before committing
   terminal state; archive cleanup covers every unfinished PostgreSQL and
   external artifact while preserving explicitly retained published evidence.
   Revoke local Vault references/scopes and emit secret-safe operator cleanup
   evidence; workload roles remain read-only and never delete operator-managed
   Vault KV values.
5. Produce notification source events in the same transaction as business
   transitions, expand recipients by authorized scope, dedupe per recipient and
   resolve notifications only on their specified business terminal event.

#### Batch 3 — Import, Version And Chunk Correctness

1. Centralize source-aware extension, MIME, magic/package, size and legacy `.doc`
   policy and expose the same limits/formats to frontend controls.
2. Implement independent per-file transactions, idempotency identities, S3
   compensation and an ordered partial-result response for multi-file upload.
3. Implement the source-locked re-extract command with Document/version locking,
   fingerprint/capability checks, unique revision allocation, immutable source
   linkage, Pipeline/outbox creation and stable conflict results.
4. Complete the update confirmation flow using live capabilities and version
   impact, without creating state when the modal opens or a file is selected.
5. Add append-only chunk edit revisions for mutable candidate versions, lock
   reconciliation across artifacts/index/graph preview, and render safe source
   and artifact previews with explicit one-source-to-many-chunks mapping.

#### Batch 4 — Conversation, Submission And Review Evidence

1. Make Document and Project conversation identities, scope, active version and
   persisted history explicit; remove fixture/client-only success paths and
   expose live configured model/readiness metadata.
2. Complete validation CSV import, row lifecycle, rerun, filters, judge evidence
   and bounded export against real configured providers/services.
3. Build the Backend Submission Evidence/readiness response and require
   submit-time compare-and-set revalidation of evidence revision, version,
   pipeline and lock state.
4. Persist an immutable approval evidence manifest and make all four approval
   workspaces use real server filters, stable cursors and evidence, with no
   placeholder UUID, count or local-only decision state.

#### Batch 5 — Bundled Vault, Operations And Non-HA Application Policy

1. Add `vault.mode=bundled|external` to the package generator, Compose inputs,
   Helm values/schema, safe examples, preflight and redacted status. New
   installations default to bundled; external mode requires an explicit
   TLS-verified address/CA/auth contract and renders no bundled Vault workload.
   Upgrade preflight requires an existing installation to acknowledge the new
   mode and blocks application readiness until that mode is valid.
2. Pin the HashiCorp Vault server image by supported version and immutable
   digest. Add the official HashiCorp Vault chart as a pinned parent-chart
   dependency, commit `Chart.lock`, vendor the exact chart archive under
   `deploy/helm/nomosmart/charts/`, verify its checksum/provenance in packaging,
   lint and release checks, and permit air-gapped registry overrides without
   fetching an unreviewed chart at install time. Record the supported
   NomoSmart/chart/Vault upgrade matrix and dependency license.
3. Add a Compose `vault` profile for bundled mode: one TLS-only Vault server in
   non-dev server mode, Integrated Raft on a retained named volume, persistent
   audit storage, an internal-only service with no published host port or UI,
   and a health contract that distinguishes uninitialized, sealed, active and
   unavailable states. Generate or validate the Vault service certificate/CA
   through the existing package TLS generation, including the actual Compose
   service DNS. Label the profile single-host/non-HA in CLI status, manifests
   and operator documentation.
4. Configure the vendored Helm dependency for bundled formal production as a
   three-server Integrated Raft HA StatefulSet with three retained data PVCs,
   persistent audit storage, hard cross-node anti-affinity, topology-aware
   placement, PDB, resource requests/limits and quorum-aware rolling updates.
   Disable the injector, public Ingress and UI because Backend/Worker use direct
   Kubernetes Auth. Expose only cluster-internal TLS services, restrict
   Backend/Worker/bootstrap and Vault peer traffic with NetworkPolicy, and
   reject fewer than three schedulable nodes or missing storage/capacity in
   production preflight. Parent values translate the single `vault.mode`
   discriminator into dependency enablement and schema/template tests reject a
   contradictory render.
5. Extend `nomosmart-package` with a secret-safe Vault lifecycle: redacted
   status/preflight; an explicit initialize ceremony that refuses a previously
   initialized store; one-time KV v2, audit, Kubernetes Auth/AppRole,
   least-privilege policy/role and sentinel bootstrap; bootstrap-token
   revocation verification; seal/quorum readiness; snapshot; guarded restore;
   and upgrade/rollback preflight. Inputs such as the initial root token or
   recovery material use an interactive terminal or inherited file descriptor,
   never arguments, environment variables or logs. Commands are idempotent
   where safe and refuse to turn destructive restore/re-initialization into an
   automatic startup side effect.
6. Make seal configuration explicit before startup. Formal production defaults
   to operator-provided KMS/HSM/Transit auto-unseal with non-secret seal
   configuration separated from workload identity/external-secret material.
   The self-contained alternative is a witnessed Shamir `5/3` ceremony with
   separate PGP recipients. Encrypted shares and the encrypted initial root
   token are written only to an explicit owner-controlled destination outside
   the generated package and are never copied to Kubernetes Secret, Compose
   Secret/env, package receipt, backup set, log or repository. Complete
   bootstrap, revoke the initial root token and record only redacted hashes,
   timestamps, approver/custodian references and success evidence.
7. Add the typed secret-reference resolver boundary and Vault KV v2
   implementation. Use distinct K8s ServiceAccount JWT/Kubernetes Auth roles
   for Backend/Worker and distinct Compose AppRoles with per-workload Role IDs
   and read-only Secret ID files; renew/re-authenticate bounded tokens without
   persistence and fail closed on Vault/TLS/path/field errors. Neither workload
   receives Vault administration, mount, policy, auth, snapshot or delete
   capability.
8. Route SFTP private keys and all listed Chat/Judge/Embedding/OCR and
   FTP/FTPS/SFTP/HTTP/S3 runtime credentials through canonical references.
   Production create/reset/rotation stores only references. Retain encrypted
   legacy reads only in a tracked migration mode, never auto-copy values, and
   require operator-created references plus per-consumer live validation before
   `vault_migration_complete` can disable legacy reads. Switching between
   bundled and external Vault changes only connection/auth configuration:
   operators must deliberately populate and validate the target paths; the
   package never exports or transfers secret values between clusters.
9. Retain Compose Vault volumes and Helm Vault PVCs by default on stop,
   uninstall and rollback. Create scheduled/operator-triggered Integrated Raft
   snapshots into an operator-selected encrypted off-host destination, record
   checksum/version/seal metadata without key material, enforce retention, and
   prove isolated restore and post-restore unseal/auth/application reads.
   Require a current verified snapshot, healthy quorum and compatibility check
   before upgrade; upgrade one HA server at a time; reject an image/chart
   rollback that cannot read the current Raft/storage format and direct the
   operator to the documented restore or roll-forward path.
10. Replace any OCR success shortcut with a resource-bounded, non-networked,
    pinned real Tesseract execution path and observable fail-closed errors.
11. Separate `/api/v1/health`, `/api/v1/ready` and
    `/api/v1/system/status`, add dependency probes, metrics and
    security/governance audit events, and remove environment-based hard-coded
    readiness success. Backend/Worker readiness stays false until Vault is
    initialized, unsealed, TLS-valid, bootstrap-complete and the workload can
    authenticate/read only its sentinel path; it returns to false on expired
    auth or an unavailable sealed/quorum state. Public status remains redacted.
12. Extend Helm production schema/template/live preflight rejection with Vault
    mode, topology, seal, auth, TLS, NetworkPolicy, storage, snapshot target,
    migration-completion and upgrade-compatibility policy. Preserve safe
    single-host Compose and explicit external mode. The application-tier
    HA/PDB/anti-affinity/capacity policy still closes in Batch 6, while
    `DEPLOY-011` independently requires Helm Vault HA in Batch 5.
13. Migrate the remaining Audit, Pipeline, Sync, Approval, Validation, Graph-job
    and API-key inventories to the Batch 2 cursor foundation, then retire offset
    assumptions through the approved expand/contract phases.
14. Complete aligned locale contracts and rendered/live bilingual checks across
    affected surfaces using the Batch 0 guard; this item does not establish the
    guard after the UI has already changed.
15. Include the vendored chart, Vault image and lifecycle tooling in dependency,
    static/configuration and container scans, signed/provenance release
    inventory and SBOM. High/Critical findings, an unverifiable chart archive,
    image-tag/digest mismatch or omitted Vault artifact fails the release.
16. Add documented harness entries `test:vault-package`,
    `integration:vault-compose-live`, `integration:vault-helm-live` and
    `integration:vault-recovery-live`. Each command must fail as blocked when
    its real Docker/Kubernetes/Vault/KMS or operator-custody prerequisite is
    unavailable; no static render, fake service or skipped ceremony may be
    translated into a passing live result.

#### Batch 6 — Application-tier HA

1. Implement the absorbed `DEPLOY-009` Helm design for at least two Frontend,
   Backend and Worker replicas, hard same-component node separation,
   PodDisruptionBudgets and readiness-gated `maxUnavailable: 0` rollouts.
2. Complete the HA-specific `DEPLOY-010` values schema, template cross-field
   validation and cluster preflight for replicas, PDBs, hard anti-affinity,
   schedulable nodes and surge capacity; `DEPLOY-010` cannot close before this.
3. Keep Beat exactly single-active and keep Compose explicitly non-HA.
4. Prove request/session correctness without sticky sessions and background
   exactly-once terminal effects through the Batch 2 durability primitives.
5. Run disposable multi-node Pod-delete, node-drain, Worker-redelivery,
   compatible upgrade and rollback acceptance; never count a single-node
   Minikube render as HA evidence.

#### Batch 7 — Release Acceptance

1. Run the full live service matrix, migrations, deployment lifecycles, browser
   journeys, negative security/authorization tests and secret-leak scans.
2. Generate Frontend and Backend coverage from the same source state and full
   suites; each must reach at least 80% and include all critical flows.
3. Run Docker Compose and Helm validation, security scans/SBOM, backup/restore
   and release-readiness review, recording any unavailable prerequisite as an
   open release blocker rather than a passing result.
4. Update traceability with exact implementation paths, test IDs, commands,
   report hashes and acceptance status before declaring any requirement done.

### Batch Dependencies And Exit Gates

- Gate 4 precedes every numbered code/migration/test task. Batch 0 then becomes
  a prerequisite for every implementation batch; no batch starts while its
  contract, migration/API decision, test cases, trace rows, i18n guard or
  governance evidence foundation is missing.
- Batches 1 and 2 must complete Backend authorization/capabilities plus
  idempotency, outbox, cursor and generation primitives before Batch 3 can close
  an import/version/chunk workflow.
- Batches 1, 2 and 3 must provide authoritative scope, stable cursor identities,
  immutable version/evidence identities and candidate reconciliation before
  Batch 4 can close chat, validation, submission or approval evidence.
- Batch 6 depends on Batch 2 durability and Batch 5 truthful readiness,
  bundled/external Vault lifecycle and non-HA application policy. Batch 6
  implements the Application-tier HA-specific schema, template and cluster
  preflight rules; `DEPLOY-009` and the full `DEPLOY-010` close together only
  after its live multi-node evidence passes. It does not defer or replace the
  independent three-node bundled Vault HA obligation in `DEPLOY-011`.
- Batch 5 Vault/configuration work may begin alongside Batches 1-4 after Batch
  0, but no dependent integration can close until real Vault acceptance passes.
  `DEPLOY-011` closes only after both modes, Compose lifecycle, three-node Helm
  quorum/disruption, secure init/seal/bootstrap, snapshot/restore and
  upgrade/rollback evidence pass; a rendered chart or external-only test is not
  sufficient.
- Batch 7 starts only after Batches 1-6 meet their focused exit criteria. A
  partial batch may merge only when it is backward-compatible, disabled from
  formal serving and cannot create a false Ready/Implemented status.
- Every batch exit requires updated traceability, focused positive/negative
  tests, no new High/Critical security finding and no regression of previously
  satisfied authorization, immutable evidence or live-only guarantees.

### Data, API And Compatibility Impact

- Expected additive migrations cover `Report.ModelReport`, Project archive
  generation/cancellation, durable idempotency/outbox/lease identities,
  notification source/dedupe/resolution state, chunk edit lineage, immutable
  submission/approval evidence, and cursor-supporting compound indexes.
- Migrations are forward-only through the existing release mechanism. They need
  fresh, upgrade, checksum, rerun, interrupted-run and compatible rollback
  evidence; no destructive cleanup may be hidden inside startup.
- `PROJECT-006` migration initializes a baseline generation for active Projects
  with old Workers drained. Only validated unclaimed queued jobs/outbox rows may
  receive that baseline. Running/leased work is expired and reconciled:
  ambiguous external effects become `needs_reconciliation`; proven no-effect
  work is retried through the same idempotent command. Archived Project work is
  cancelled/superseded, and every late legacy message still fails the
  generation/state fence.
- `REVIEW-023` migration marks completed legacy approvals that cannot be
  reconstructed as `legacy_evidence_unavailable`. Pending approval evidence is
  backfilled only when the locked version and every required hash/reference are
  verifiable; otherwise it fails closed and must be resubmitted.
- Every release publishes an application/schema/API compatibility identity.
  Rollback may select only an image declared compatible with the migrated schema
  and current security contract. After unscoped graph routes are removed, a
  rollback image that would register them, omit mandatory idempotency or bypass
  the new authorization/evidence rules must fail preflight; operators must roll
  forward to a compatible image instead of reopening the vulnerability.
- Removing `/api/v1/knowledge-graph*` unscoped routes is intentional. They return
  normal 404 and are not preserved as optionally scoped aliases.
- Requiring `Idempotency-Key`, adding capability/evidence contracts and moving
  offset lists to cursors use explicit expand/contract phases: compatible
  Backend support lands first, clients switch under telemetry, and the later
  contract phase removes the bounded old mode. Supported endpoints remain
  continuous during compatible mixed-version rollout; one replica may not
  randomly emit a different schema for the same compatibility identity.
- The exact CHG-247 API additions and corrections are the section 12 contract:
  scoped Project/Document detail capabilities; `200` ordered/idempotent upload
  results; re-extract, chunk edit and submission evidence; one-time API-key
  create/rotate responses; scope/version-bound conversation lifecycle and
  Backend export; canonical validation list/detail/items/retry/cancel/export;
  report streaming, cursor inventories and scoped graph routes. Implementation
  must not substitute an unlisted alias or leave these methods/status/envelopes
  for Frontend and Backend to infer independently.
- Removing `/api/v1/knowledge-graph*` is a security cutover and never retains an
  insecure alias. Use blue-green coordinated cutover with the old stack
  isolated after traffic switches, or Backend-first 404 with that retired
  surface explicitly excluded from compatible-endpoint continuity. A rollback
  image that reopens it is rejected and operators roll forward.
- Existing published versions/evidence remain readable under their documented
  compatibility contract. Completed legacy approval evidence may explicitly be
  unavailable; pending evidence is backfilled only when verifiable. Existing
  encrypted Vault-capable credential rows are read-only migration inputs with
  owner/deadline/status and are not silently copied or accepted by production
  once `vault_migration_complete` is set.
- Fresh package generations default to bundled Vault. An upgrade from a release
  that had no packaged Vault must explicitly acknowledge bundled or external
  mode before workloads start, even when the resulting value is the new
  default. Bundled selection creates new empty Vault state and never imports
  historical encrypted values; external selection preserves the operator's
  endpoint while adopting the same auth, TLS and reference contract.
- The first bundled deployment is an additive service/storage change, not an
  application database migration. Package state records the Vault mode,
  immutable image/chart identity, initialization/bootstrap state, seal method
  identifier, Raft snapshot compatibility identity and retained volume/PVC
  ownership without recording keys or tokens. Switching modes is a planned
  drain/validate/cutover operation and does not delete the prior Vault storage.
- A NomoSmart rollback is permitted only when the target application,
  parent/vendored Vault chart and Vault server/storage versions appear in the
  tested compatibility matrix. A chart/image downgrade that could read or write
  Raft data incompatibly is rejected; operators retain the PVCs/volume, restore
  a verified compatible snapshot into isolation or roll forward.
- Vault has no public NomoSmart CRUD, proxy, UI or secret-value response API.
  Existing health/readiness/status contracts gain redacted Vault
  initialization/seal/quorum/bootstrap/auth dependency states; these are
  additive operational fields and never reveal mount paths, key names, policy
  text, tokens or credential values.
- `WEBHOOK-001` has no runtime route/schema migration because it is not a v1.0
  implementation target.

### Deployment And Configuration Impact

- Add typed Vault mode, address/service name, mount, auth path, workload role,
  CA path, timeouts, seal mode identifier, persistent storage/audit settings,
  snapshot destination reference, pinned chart/image identities and reference
  policy to the appropriate values/schema/package manifests. Only non-secret
  values enter ConfigMap/environment or redacted receipts. Tokens, Secret IDs,
  unseal/recovery shares, auto-unseal credentials, private keys, root/bootstrap
  tokens and resolved values remain in approved identity/Secret/file/runtime
  memory or separate operator-custody surfaces.
- Root `docker-compose.yml` gains a bundled Vault profile and retained named
  volumes for Raft and audit data. The server uses the active package TLS set
  extended for Vault service DNS, exposes no host port and does not use
  `-dev`, an in-memory storage backend or plaintext listener. Compose Backend
  and Worker each receive their own Role ID as non-secret configuration and
  their own operator-created, uncommitted, read-only Secret ID file; neither
  AppRole may read the other's paths or administer Vault.
- `deploy/helm/nomosmart/Chart.yaml` gains the pinned official HashiCorp Vault
  dependency, `Chart.lock` and a committed vendored chart archive. Bundled
  values configure three Integrated Raft servers, retained data/audit PVCs,
  TLS, Kubernetes Auth, internal Services, hard anti-affinity, PDB, resources
  and NetworkPolicy. Backend and Worker receive distinct ServiceAccounts and
  least-privilege roles. External mode disables every bundled subchart workload
  and instead allows only required TLS egress to the operator endpoint.
- Values JSON Schema, template policy and live preflight reject production
  bundled mode with dev/standalone Vault, fewer than three servers/PVCs,
  public UI/Ingress/listener, plaintext/TLS bypass, shared or administrative
  workload roles, missing audit persistence, soft/no anti-affinity, unsafe PDB,
  insufficient nodes/capacity, implicit seal choice or unverified
  snapshot/upgrade compatibility. They also reject contradictory bundled and
  external enablement.
- `nomosmart-package init/status/rotate/finalize/preflight` remains the package
  generation boundary and gains explicit Vault lifecycle commands or phases
  for redacted status, initialization, bootstrap, snapshot, restore and
  upgrade/rollback preflight. Lifecycle output is atomic and auditable but
  excludes secrets; destructive restore requires an isolated target, current
  backup checksum/compatibility evidence and explicit operator confirmation.
- The package-generated TLS surface adds Vault server/peer identities and CA
  validation for both Compose and the supported Helm release/service DNS.
  Operator-provided certificates must cover the rendered endpoints; hostname
  mismatch or untrusted/missing CA fails before initialization.
- Formal production auto-unseal references an operator-managed KMS/HSM/Transit
  service through workload identity or an approved external Secret; the
  package neither provisions nor backs up that service. Shamir `5/3` is the
  self-contained option and requires five distinct PGP recipients plus a
  witnessed three-share unseal and restore drill. Neither option may introduce
  a secret dependency cycle that prevents Vault recovery.
- Vault Raft and audit storage is retained by default. Snapshot tooling writes
  only to an explicit encrypted off-host destination, never the repository or
  generated deployment directory. Restore, upgrade and rollback runbooks state
  quiescing, quorum, unseal, validation and recovery order, and release
  acceptance proves them on disposable state before production use.
- Development shortcuts such as Vault root tokens in workloads, dev mode,
  shared overbroad AppRoles, plaintext committed credentials, unencrypted
  shares/snapshots, public Vault exposure or TLS bypass are not accepted.
- Production create/reset/rotation for the listed Vault-capable runtime
  consumers stores references only. A migration inventory records every legacy
  encrypted row's status, owner and deadline; operators create and rotate Vault
  values through the separately authorized Vault operator/bootstrap workflow,
  attach references, and prove each consumer class live. Production preflight
  rejects active legacy rows or legacy-read mode once the compatibility
  identity declares `vault_migration_complete`.
- Production Helm validation becomes a release gate and includes application
  and Vault readiness, secret references, seal/bootstrap, three-node Vault HA,
  application-tier HA, PDB, anti-affinity, rollout, storage, snapshot and
  capacity preflight. Development/factory profiles may remain smaller only
  where explicitly allowed and cannot claim production readiness or HA;
  Compose always remains non-HA.
- New runtime parameters are documented in safe example files and values
  schemas. Real secret values, endpoints containing credentials and private
  material are never committed.

### Test Strategy

- Design all CHG-247 tests in `TEST_PLAN.md` before implementation and map each
  requirement in `TRACEABILITY.md`.
- Use the lowest useful unit/component level for parsers, policies, state
  machines and UI states, then real PostgreSQL, Keycloak, Redis/Celery,
  RustFS/S3, OpenSearch, Neo4j, Vault, SFTP, Tesseract, Docker and Kubernetes
  services for integration/release evidence.
- Follow `TEST-002`: mocks, fakes, deterministic adapters and hard-coded success
  states may support isolated development diagnostics but cannot satisfy live
  acceptance.
- Include concurrency, crash/redelivery, stale generation, replay/conflict,
  permission-union, both-end graph authorization, secret leakage, side-channel,
  cursor mutation and rollback-negative cases.
- Add package/static tests for the `bundled|external` discriminator, JSON Schema
  and template cross-field rejection, exact vendored chart/checksum/lock
  identity, image digest, air-gapped render, license inventory, internal-only
  exposure, TLS names, NetworkPolicy and absence of unseal/root/Secret ID/value
  material from Git, manifests, receipts, logs, process arguments and SBOM.
- Run a real Compose lifecycle with the bundled profile: initialize once,
  reject re-initialization, complete Shamir `5/3` PGP bootstrap, unseal with the
  threshold, configure KV/auth/policies/audit, revoke the bootstrap root token,
  prove distinct Backend/Worker AppRole allow/deny matrices, restart with
  retained Raft state, snapshot/restore in isolation and prove sealed/outage/TLS
  failure makes application readiness fail closed. A separate external-mode run
  must prove that no bundled server/volume is rendered.
- Run a disposable three-schedulable-node Kubernetes lifecycle for the vendored
  bundled Helm dependency: verify three Raft peers/PVCs and audit persistence,
  direct Kubernetes Auth allow/deny matrices, no public listener/UI/Ingress,
  hard placement and PDB, one-pod deletion, node drain, leader change, loss and
  restoration of quorum, seal/unseal or configured auto-unseal recovery,
  snapshot/isolated restore, supported upgrade and rollback rejection/roll
  forward while authorized traffic continues according to the readiness
  contract. A single-node Minikube render cannot satisfy `DEPLOY-011`.
- Test the lifecycle CLI's idempotency and redaction: safe repeat status and
  bootstrap checks, refusal of initialized-store init, refusal of destructive
  restore without explicit isolated target/evidence, input through TTY/file
  descriptor rather than argv/env, partial-failure cleanup, root-token
  revocation, incorrect shares/PGP recipients, unavailable KMS/Transit, corrupt
  snapshot, version mismatch and retained storage on uninstall/rollback.
- Run dependency, static/configuration, Vault container vulnerability,
  provenance and SBOM checks against the exact vendored chart/image. No
  High/Critical finding or untracked/unscanned Vault release artifact may be
  waived by calling it an optional dependency.
- Measure Frontend and Backend independently at 80% or higher from full suites,
  and bind coverage evidence to the same source commit/dirty-diff fingerprint,
  command, time, report hash and suite manifest. A stale or focused-only report
  fails the release gate.

### Risks And Mitigations

- **Cross-batch authorization drift:** centralize Backend policy/capability
  vocabulary first and run denied-path tests in every batch.
- **Late Worker resurrects archived or superseded state:** require generation,
  lease and terminal-state checks before external writes and before commit.
- **Graph side-channel disclosure:** authorize both endpoints before building
  payloads and keep forbidden/missing responses, counts, truncation and timing
  behavior indistinguishable within bounded acceptance.
- **Duplicate costly/external effects:** use request-hash idempotency,
  transactionally created outbox records, leases and immutable terminal state.
- **Vault outage or credential renewal failure:** fail closed with bounded
  retries/readiness impact, retain no disk cache and expose only secret-safe
  operational error identities.
- **Bundled Vault expands the NomoSmart failure and support boundary:** isolate
  Vault storage/network/policies from application workloads, expose redacted
  lifecycle diagnostics and make initialization, unseal, quorum, snapshot and
  upgrade evidence explicit release and operator responsibilities.
- **Lost or concentrated Shamir/root custody:** require five PGP recipients,
  three-share threshold, separate custodians, witnessed recovery drills and
  verified root-token revocation; never let the package retain plaintext or a
  complete decryptable key set.
- **Auto-unseal dependency unavailable or circular:** require an independently
  recoverable operator KMS/HSM/Transit service and credentials/workload identity
  outside Vault's own secret store, test cold-start failure/recovery and keep
  the documented Shamir `5/3` alternative for accepted self-contained
  installations.
- **Raft quorum, PVC or audit loss:** enforce three formal-production members,
  hard placement, PDB and retained volumes; monitor peer/quorum/audit health;
  create encrypted off-host snapshots and prove isolated restore rather than
  treating PVC retention as a backup.
- **Vendored chart/image drift or vulnerable dependency:** lock chart, archive,
  image digest, checksum/provenance, license and compatibility matrix together;
  include every artifact in scan/SBOM gates and require an explicit reviewed
  update instead of a floating dependency fetch.
- **Unsafe Vault downgrade after storage migration:** snapshot before upgrade,
  roll one peer at a time, validate quorum/application reads and reject
  unsupported rollback in favor of tested restore or roll-forward.
- **Evidence changes after submission:** snapshot immutable identities/hashes and
  compare evidence revision/state under transaction at submit time.
- **Cursor gaps/duplicates during concurrent writes:** use immutable ordering
  keys plus a unique tie-breaker and test insertion/deletion between pages.
- **Large CSV/report resource pressure:** v1 uses typed-batch keyset/server-cursor
  streaming with pre-header authorization/query validation, disconnect/timeout
  cancellation, partial-file failure semantics and audit. Background jobs need
  a future companion contract.
- **HA overclaim:** require separate real multi-node disruption evidence for
  Application-tier `DEPLOY-009` and bundled Vault `DEPLOY-011`, and state that
  Compose remains non-HA and other peripheral/control-plane HA remains outside
  this release.
- **Historical false completion:** CHG-247 trace rows supersede conflicting
  historic statuses; only fresh requirement-specific evidence can close them.

### Provisioning And Platform Approach

1. Re-run read-only ESXi, datastore, port-group, DNS and IP preflight. Record
   exact VM names, datastores and ISO paths before any creation.
2. Create four VMs with VMXNET3, paravirtual SCSI, EFI/Secure Boot where
   supported and the approved CPU/RAM/disk placement. Use the existing Rocky
   Linux 9.6 Minimal ISO plus a generated unattended Kickstart/OEMDRV image.
3. Install and harden Rocky Linux: hostname/time sync, static network,
   `peteradmin`, sudo audit, firewalld rules, SELinux enforcing, required RKE2/
   Longhorn packages, persistent Longhorn mount, log rotation and security
   updates. Do not place supplied or generated passwords in Kickstart committed
   files or process arguments.
4. Install the three-node RKE2 cluster against the kube-vip API endpoint,
   validate certificate SANs, etcd membership and node topology, and export a
   restricted admin kubeconfig to the encrypted handoff package.
5. Install MetalLB in L2 mode, ingress-nginx if not provided by the pinned RKE2
   distribution, and Longhorn. Use two storage replicas by default so bundled
   single-replica stateful services can survive one storage-node loss while
   staying within the approved 300 GiB-per-node data capacity. Enforce disk
   reservation, capacity alerting and replica anti-affinity.
6. Install single-node management RKE2 and Rancher on the management VM with
   FreeIPA-signed TLS. Import the workload cluster and verify Rancher can read
   nodes, workloads, events, logs and cluster health without changing the
   managed cluster unexpectedly.
7. Install an authenticated TLS private OCI registry on the Rancher VM, with
   persistent storage and LAN/management-only access. Build NomoSmart images
   from the exact source fingerprint, push immutable tags/digests, scan them and
   generate retained SBOMs before deployment.
8. Generate the NomoSmart production package outside version control. Create
   the namespace, operator-owned runtime Secret, edge/internal TLS Secrets and
   exact production overlay without rendering plaintext secret values.
9. Install the NomoSmart Helm chart in phases: platform preflight, Vault
   servers, witnessed Vault initialization/unseal/bootstrap/root revocation,
   migration/bootstrap Jobs, then application and bundled peripherals.
10. Configure Keycloak federation to FreeIPA using LDAPS/StartTLS and a
    least-privilege dedicated bind account. Create/map the required UAT
    administrator group without storing FreeIPA admin credentials in Keycloak
    as the long-term bind credential.
11. Complete first-use NomoSmart onboarding, password/TOTP and non-break-glass
    administrator evidence with Peter at the interactive checkpoint. Bootstrap
    and one-time credentials are rotated or revoked after their required use.
12. Run live acceptance and disruption/recovery exercises, restore all services,
    verify continuous UAT access, then freeze the accepted version/configuration
    fingerprint while leaving the environment powered on.

### Backup, Recovery And Rollback

- Before disruptive acceptance, capture RKE2 etcd snapshots, Longhorn volume
  snapshots and application-level backups for PostgreSQL/Keycloak, RustFS,
  OpenSearch, Neo4j and Vault Integrated Raft.
- Encrypt an acceptance copy and transfer it to the Mac handoff directory as an
  operator-managed off-cluster/off-host copy. Record hashes, timestamps,
  versions, retention and the decryption reference held in KeePass.
- Prove Vault snapshot restore and representative application datastore restore
  only in isolated namespaces/volumes. Never restore destructively over the live
  UAT environment.
- VM creation failure rolls back only newly created `nms-uat-*` VMs and new DNS
  records after exact target verification and explicit destructive approval.
  Existing VMs and legacy DNS records are never rollback targets.
- Cluster/package failure uses Helm rollback or a forward fix while retaining
  PVCs and external Secrets. Database migrations are forward-only unless an
  isolated full restore with compatible images is explicitly selected.
- Temporary test resources are removed only after their identities and
  isolation are proven. Material deletion is reported with recoverability.

### Risks And Controls

- **Legacy collision:** existing Rancher/RKE2 endpoints are live. Use a distinct
  prefix, address range and FreeIPA records; fail closed on any discovered
  collision.
- **Standalone ESXi:** no vCenter/DRS/live migration exists. Place one workload
  node per physical host, document manual recovery and do not claim hypervisor
  HA.
- **Single Rancher VM:** management availability is non-HA. Preserve workload
  cluster independence, back up Rancher state and prove VM-reboot recovery.
- **Shared OS password:** the confirmed common password increases lateral
  movement risk. Restrict SSH, disable root SSH, retain audit, install a key and
  recommend rotation before production reuse.
- **Centralized Vault custody:** Peter initially receives every package. Mark
  separation-of-duty incomplete until packages are distributed; never weaken
  Shamir threshold or retain an active root token to compensate.
- **Longhorn capacity:** two-replica storage, snapshots and retained images must
  stay within three 300 GiB data disks. Run fail-closed capacity preflight,
  reserve free space, alert on pressure and do not reduce PVC/retention
  requirements merely to make installation pass.
- **UAT disruption:** quorum-loss, drain and rollback tests can temporarily
  degrade the new environment. Run them before handoff, isolate them from the
  legacy cluster and finish only after full health and laptop access return.
- **Missing provider credentials:** model success paths cannot be honestly
  accepted without real provider configuration. Keep the gap visible while the
  rest of UAT remains available.
- **Secret leakage:** use TTY/file-descriptor input, encrypted KDBX/custodian
  packages, mode restrictions and redacted evidence; scan repository, manifests
  and logs before handoff.
