## CHG-255 Keycloak Cascaded Identity Synchronization

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-08-08 with `同意 CHG-255 Gate 2`.
Gate 3 development and test planning is prepared below. Gate 4 was approved by
Peter on 2026-08-08 with
`Peter approves CHG-255 Keycloak Cascaded Identity Synchronization`;
repository implementation and non-destructive feature verification are
authorized. Any mutation of the current UAT directory/realm remains outside
this approval and requires separate authorization.
Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-08-08.

### Confirmed Understanding And Decisions

- The current NomoSmart manual run reads a Keycloak snapshot but does not ask
  Keycloak to refresh LDAP/AD users or group mappers. A directory group created
  after the last Keycloak Federation sync therefore remains invisible no matter
  how often the existing NomoSmart button is pressed.
- One NomoSmart run must own the complete ordered journey: enabled-provider
  discovery, scope-specific Keycloak user/mapping sync, fresh Keycloak snapshot,
  and atomic NomoSmart reconciliation.
- Every enabled LDAP/AD provider is included in stable provider-ID order;
  disabled providers are skipped. Manual and scheduled runs use the same
  lifecycle and effective scope.
- `people`, `groups` and `people_and_groups` remain real scopes. The worker
  calls only the corresponding explicit Keycloak user-storage and/or LDAP
  mapper fed-to-Keycloak actions and only applies that NomoSmart domain.
- Any enabled-provider failure fails the parent run before NomoSmart
  reconciliation and preserves the last successful NomoSmart data. Upstream
  Keycloak changes already completed before a later provider fails cannot be
  rolled back transactionally; safe partial evidence is retained and retry
  starts the complete provider set with a new lease.
- The action retains `SystemManagement.edit` and does not require a fresh-auth
  unlock. It uses the existing sync service account and never performs a direct
  LDAP bind/search/write or handles human/directory credentials.

### Scope

1. Extend `AUTH-015` run lifecycle with `AUTH-017` requested scope, current
   phase and ordered provider result evidence.
2. Add bounded Keycloak Admin API operations for provider user sync and LDAP
   group-mapper fed-to-Keycloak sync, with strict provider/mapper discovery,
   response validation, timeout, redaction and stable error codes.
3. Execute the cascading lifecycle from both manual and scheduled worker paths,
   preserving lease, heartbeat, duplicate delivery and stale-run guarantees.
4. Add additive run list/detail fields and a localized System Management
   progress/result presentation without changing the existing queue endpoint,
   permission or 202/409/503 contract.
5. Add forward-only persistence, deployment configuration, audit,
   observability and real-service verification for multiple providers and all
   supported scopes.

### Data And Migration Approach

1. Add `sql/migrations/V043__keycloak_cascaded_identity_sync.sql`; do not edit
   the applied V028 lifecycle migration.
2. Add non-null `requested_scope` and `phase` columns to
   `identity_sync_runs`, with check constraints for
   `people|groups|people_and_groups` and the specified lifecycle phases. Queue
   creation copies the effective scope so later settings changes cannot alter
   an accepted run.
3. Add `identity_sync_provider_results` with a UUID primary key, parent run FK,
   stable provider ID/name/vendor, requested scope, status, timestamps,
   allowlisted user-sync counters, group-mapper phase status and safe error
   code. Enforce one result per run/provider, non-negative counters and bounded
   strings.
4. Backfill historical terminal runs as `requested_scope=people_and_groups` and
   `phase=completed`; safely classify active historical rows without creating
   provider-result rows or claiming upstream success. Preserve all run,
   identity, group, role, mapping and audit history.
5. Update SQLAlchemy models and API schemas. Provider results never persist
   full Keycloak component JSON, endpoint, DN, Filter, credential, token, raw
   response prose or exception text.

### Keycloak And Backend Approach

1. Extend `KeycloakAdminClient` with allowlisted provider/mapper inventory and
   two explicit actions:
   - user-storage `triggerFullSync` for scopes containing `people`;
   - LDAP mapper sync with `direction=fedToKeycloak` for scopes containing
     `groups`.
2. Include only enabled LDAP `UserStorageProvider` components. Resolve compatible
   group mappers by parent provider; a scope requiring groups fails with a safe
   mapper-missing/ambiguous/unsupported code rather than pretending success.
3. Process providers in stable ID order. Persist a provider result before its
   first external call, move it through running/terminal state, and commit
   heartbeat/evidence in short independent transactions. A background heartbeat
   guard must keep long Keycloak calls from being mistaken for abandoned work.
4. Add typed `IDENTITY_SYNC_KEYCLOAK_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, default 600 and
   range 30-1800, to Settings, safe Docker env template, Compose, Helm values,
   schema and ConfigMap. The parent run timeout remains the outer bound; do not
   begin another provider when the remaining run budget is insufficient.
5. After every required provider action succeeds, fetch one fresh Keycloak
   snapshot. Reconciliation must honor `requested_scope`:
   - `people`: update/create/disable only user-domain fields and preserve current
     external groups/mappings/derived memberships;
   - `groups`: update groups/memberships/derived roles using already known users
     and preserve user lifecycle/profile fields;
   - `people_and_groups`: apply the existing complete atomic reconciliation.
6. If provider, mapper, authentication, timeout, response validation or snapshot
   fails, mark the parent failed with a stable code and do not enter NomoSmart
   reconciliation. Existing successful data stays unchanged. Late or duplicate
   messages remain no-op through the current lease token.
7. Add phase/provider audit and structured log fields containing only run ID,
   provider ID/name/vendor, scope, phase, result, safe counters, attempt,
   duration and error code. Do not log secret-bearing URLs, DNs, Filters,
   tokens, component payloads or raw Keycloak/LDAP errors.
8. Keep `POST /api/v1/identity-sync/run` permission and response status
   compatible. Add `requested_scope`, `phase` and ordered `provider_results` to
   list/detail schemas; parent users/groups/role counters continue to describe
   only successful NomoSmart reconciliation.

### Keycloak Privilege And Deployment Approach

1. Reuse the current `nomosmart-sync` client and previously approved
   realm-management roles. Bootstrap/readiness must verify that the pinned
   Keycloak version and service account can invoke user-storage and mapper sync
   endpoints plus read snapshots; do not add a new secret or use bootstrap
   administrator credentials.
2. Preserve Keycloak provider `READ_ONLY`, disabled Direct Access Grant,
   trusted LDAPS/StartTLS and existing bind custody. The new action writes only
   Keycloak's imported user/group state and never writes LDAP/AD or Federation
   configuration.
3. Ensure Backend Worker NetworkPolicy and trusted CA paths permit internal
   Keycloak Admin API calls in Docker Compose and Helm. API-only reachability is
   insufficient; worker-driven live sync is the readiness/acceptance path.
4. Document operator rollback as application rollback plus retention of V043
   additive history. Do not down-migrate or delete provider evidence; disabling
   cascading behavior after rollback returns to the prior snapshot-only binary
   behavior while retained columns remain compatible.

### Frontend Approach

1. Keep the existing Identity Source "Sync now" button, permission, duplicate
   prevention and polling behavior. Show the run's current phase and provider
   ordinal/name while it is active.
2. At terminal state, show a compact ordered provider result summary followed
   by the existing NomoSmart users/groups/role counters. A no-enabled-provider
   run shows localized skipped/warning evidence and may still complete the
   Keycloak-local snapshot.
3. Map every new phase/status/error code to aligned Traditional Chinese and
   English keys. Runtime state stores codes/parameters rather than a formatted
   sentence so locale switching updates active progress, failure, retry,
   `aria-live` and screen-reader copy immediately.
4. Never render Backend safe-message prose as the final known error, and never
   render raw Provider errors, DN, endpoint, mapper config, Filter or credential.
   Unknown codes use the existing localized safe fallback plus request ID.
5. Preserve current dense layout, keyboard behavior, visible focus, non-color
   status cues, 40px mobile target and narrow-width non-overlap.

### Test And Verification Strategy

- Migration: real disposable PostgreSQL fresh/upgrade/backfill/constraint/
  rollback-preservation cases for V043.
- Keycloak/OpenLDAP: real isolated realm, service account and LDAP subtrees;
  add/update/disable users and groups after an earlier Keycloak sync, invoke the
  NomoSmart API, and prove both Keycloak and NomoSmart converge without direct
  NomoSmart LDAP access.
- Scope: real `people`, `groups` and `people_and_groups` paths prove only the
  selected NomoSmart domain changes. Provider user and mapper endpoints must be
  observed from real Keycloak evidence, not an HTTP mock.
- Multi-provider: enabled/disabled ordering, no-provider skip, mapper missing,
  first-provider success/second-provider failure, timeout, Keycloak restart,
  retry convergence and non-rollbackable upstream evidence.
- Lifecycle/security: worker unavailable, duplicate queue/delivery, stale
  lease, run heartbeat, total/per-provider timeout, view-only denial, edit
  success, scheduled/manual parity, audit/log/API redaction and existing role
  preservation.
- Frontend/browser: loading, phase progress, provider results, safe retry,
  locale switching, accessibility and responsive layout against real API/OIDC
  services. No request interception, mocked Keycloak, fixture LDAP or synthetic
  success may pass TEST-002 behavioral acceptance.
- After Gate 4, run the focused live suite first, then governance, syntax,
  frontend, backend, E2E, migration, deployment/config, security and independent
  80% coverage gates. Missing services/credentials are reported blocked, never
  mock-passed.

### Expected Implementation Areas

- `sql/migrations/V043__keycloak_cascaded_identity_sync.sql`
- `backend/app/db/models.py`
- `backend/app/api/schemas.py`
- `backend/app/api/routes/identity.py`
- `backend/app/core/config.py`
- `backend/app/integrations/keycloak.py`
- `backend/app/services/identity_sync.py`
- `backend/app/services/identity_sync_jobs.py`
- `backend/app/worker.py`
- `backend/app/deployment/bootstrap.py`
- `frontend/src/components/SystemManagementWorkspace.tsx`
- `frontend/src/i18n/locales/zh.json`
- `frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json`
- Docker Compose/Helm typed configuration and NetworkPolicy/readiness surfaces
- Focused real-service Backend, Frontend contract/component and Browser tests

### Compatibility, Risks And Controls

- Cross-system atomic rollback is impossible. Control: do not reconcile
  NomoSmart until every enabled Provider succeeds; persist safe partial upstream
  evidence and rerun the complete set on retry.
- Keycloak versions can change Admin endpoint/result behavior. Control: pin the
  supported version, validate response shapes, verify the live API in bootstrap
  acceptance and fail closed on unsupported mapper sync.
- Large directories can exceed HTTP and run timeouts. Control: typed bounded
  per-provider timeout, total budget, durable heartbeat, deterministic order and
  truthful timeout codes. Do not claim success from an accepted HTTP request.
- A people-only Keycloak user sync may internally execute attached mappers in
  the provider. Control: report actually invoked phases, never invoke the
  explicit group-mapper action for people-only, and apply only the selected
  NomoSmart domain.
- Broad sync can disable missing imported users or delete stale imported groups
  according to existing Keycloak mapper settings. Control: use only the
  operator-configured provider behavior, show scope/provider before execution,
  retain NomoSmart data on failure, and cover disposable live delete/disable
  cases before release.
- Existing current UAT data cannot be used as a destructive test fixture.
  Feature/live tests use isolated realms/subtrees and require separate explicit
  authorization before any UAT mutation.

### Out Of Scope

- Editing Provider host, port, DN, bind credential, TLS/truststore, Filter,
  mapper configuration or directory objects from the Sync action.
- Writing users/groups/memberships back from Keycloak or NomoSmart to LDAP/AD.
- Provider selection UI, per-provider manual buttons, cancellation of an
  already-running Keycloak full sync, or automatic compensation/rollback in
  Keycloak.
- Changing normal login, MFA, break-glass, external-group-to-role mapping,
  permission matrix or direct Keycloak Admin Console behavior.

Implementation and non-destructive verification may proceed. Current-UAT

## CHG-256 Effective-permission Application Admission Gate

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-08-08 with
`同意 CHG-256 Gate 2（三項皆採建議）`. Gate 3 development, test and
traceability planning is prepared below. Gate 4 was approved by Peter on
2026-08-08 with
`Peter approves CHG-256 Effective-permission Application Admission Gate`;
repository implementation and non-destructive feature tests are authorized.
Current-UAT identity/group/role/directory mutation remains separately gated.

### Confirmed Understanding And Decisions

- The reported `user02` behavior is a global authorization-boundary gap, not a
  Home-only error. The Backend currently accepts any synchronized active user
  at `/auth/me`, even when the resolved permission union is empty; the
  Frontend then mounts AppShell and Home, whose Project request fails later.
- Keycloak OIDC authentication proves identity only. NomoSmart application
  admission requires at least one positive `can_view`, `can_create`,
  `can_edit`, `can_delete` or `can_execute` value from a currently active,
  undeleted NomoSmart role.
- Admission uses the union of `external_sync`, `manual` and `break_glass` role
  memberships. Raw Keycloak/LDAP group presence, an unmapped group, an
  all-false permission row, an inactive/deleted role, or Project Owner/member
  scope alone does not admit the user. A valid manual positive role can admit a
  user who is not in an LDAP group.
- A synchronized active user with no positive effective permission receives
  stable `403 application_access_denied` from `/auth/me` and protected
  business APIs. It is distinct from unauthenticated/session-expired 401,
  account-unavailable 403 and an admitted user's feature-specific
  `permission_denied`/`project_scope_denied`.
- The Frontend must present an authenticated `/access-denied` boundary before
  AppShell, Home, Notification or any business-data request. It keeps the
  memory-only SSO session and offers localized recheck and logout actions; it
  does not auto-logout or start a silent-login/refresh loop.
- Home, ApprovalWorkspace and ApiDocumentation remain default surfaces only
  after the global admission gate. An account that loses its final positive
  permission during a session is moved to the same boundary at the next
  protected request.

### Scope

1. Add one Backend-owned effective-permission admission predicate and enforce
   it consistently at auth bootstrap and every protected business request.
2. Add the stable `application_access_denied` API result and safe denial audit
   while preserving existing 401, unavailable-account and feature-forbidden
   semantics.
3. Add a Frontend auth-state transition and canonical `/access-denied` surface
   that prevents AppShell and business effects from mounting while denied.
4. Add recheck, successful convergence, safe return-path and existing logout
   behavior without persistent token/return-path storage.
5. Add aligned Traditional Chinese/English operational copy, accessibility,
   responsive behavior and real-service authorization/browser acceptance.

### Backend And Authorization Approach

1. Add a small pure permission helper that returns true only when at least one
   resolved grant from an active, undeleted role has an allowed `can_*` value
   set to true. Do not infer admission from token groups, group count, user
   existence or project scope.
2. Keep identity resolution able to distinguish these ordered states:
   invalid/revoked JWT, unsynchronized user, disabled user, synchronized active
   user without admission, and admitted user. Do not collapse them into one
   generic forbidden result.
3. Use a bootstrap-aware context for `GET /auth/me` so it can record the safe
   denial transition and return the API-001 `403 application_access_denied`
   envelope. Keep the normal protected-route identity dependency fail closed
   with the same code after a final grant is revoked.
4. Continue resolving role membership from the current NomoSmart database on
   every request. Existing manual/external/break-glass union, role active and
   tombstone filters remain authoritative; no token-side permission cache may
   delay revocation.
5. Ensure admission denial happens before route-specific business queries or
   mutations. `/auth/me` recheck and the existing authenticated logout endpoint
   remain usable; no other protected application endpoint is allowlisted for a
   denied user.
6. Add `auth.application_access_denied` or an equivalently stable audit action
   with user ID, irreversible subject/session fingerprint, reason
   `no_effective_permission`, request ID and result only. Initial bootstrap has
   one in-flight request, and the Frontend denial circuit breaker stops new
   business dispatch after a mid-session denial; already in-flight requests
   remain independently auditable without logging tokens, raw claims or group
   lists.
7. Preserve admitted-user authorization: a missing permission for one Menu,
   project or action remains the existing in-page 403 and must not be promoted
   to global access denial while any positive effective permission remains.

### Frontend Auth-state And UX Approach

1. Extend AuthProvider with an explicit application-admission state such as
   `checking|granted|denied`, rather than treating every non-401 auth error as
   loading completion. Only `granted` may render protected children.
2. Detect only stable `application_access_denied` as the global denied state.
   `user_not_synchronized`/`user_disabled` retain account-unavailable recovery;
   401 retains one controlled refresh/session-expired path; ordinary
   `permission_denied` remains page-local.
3. Render the denial boundary outside AppShell so its navigation, search,
   Notification effects, Home effects and route page effects never mount.
   Canonicalize to `/access-denied` without triggering the protected-route
   silent SSO effect again.
4. The denial surface shows a safe current-account label, title, explanatory
   copy, administrator guidance, locale selector, recheck and logout. It does
   not show Header/Menu, API Documentation, approval content, system metadata
   or business data.
5. Recheck performs one coalesced `/auth/me` call. While pending, disable repeat
   submission and announce progress. Continued denial updates the same safe
   state; success installs the fresh CurrentUser/permission state and returns
   to the current-tab safe original internal target or `/`.
6. Preserve the return target only in current in-memory auth transition state.
   Reuse existing same-origin path validation; reject external, protocol-
   relative, login/callback/auth API and denial-loop targets. Do not use
   localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, URL secrets or readable cookies.
7. In the shared API client, the first mid-session
   `application_access_denied` opens a circuit breaker, clears the admitted
   CurrentUser permission state without clearing valid tokens, and moves to the
   denied boundary. Repeated/in-flight denials must not cause refresh, silent
   SSO, navigation or audit request storms.

### i18n, Accessibility And Visual Approach

1. Add matching zh-TW and English keys for denial title, explanation,
   administrator guidance, signed-in account, recheck, rechecking, still
   denied, restored access and logout states. Known stable codes are localized
   client-side; Backend prose is not the translation source.
2. Use the existing enterprise authentication visual language: Cloud White,
   restrained Mint/Sage context, Slate text and an icon plus text status. The
   page is operational and compact, not a marketing or generic error page.
3. Use semantic heading, `role=alert`/bounded `aria-live`, keyboard order,
   visible focus, non-color status cues and at least 40px mobile targets.
   Desktop, tablet and 375px layouts must avoid clipping or horizontal scroll.
4. Locale switching must work while denied without requiring AppShell or an
   admitted CurrentUser and without resetting the denial/recheck state.

### Data, API, Deployment And Rollout Impact

- No database schema migration is planned. Existing `users`, `roles`,
  `role_users`, `role_permissions`, project membership and audit storage are
  reused.
- `GET /api/v1/auth/me` intentionally changes for the zero-positive-permission
  edge case from `200` with an empty permission list to
  `403 application_access_denied`; positive-permission response fields remain
  unchanged.
- Protected business APIs gain the same pre-handler admission denial. Their
  admitted-user method, payload, response and route-specific authorization
  contracts remain unchanged.
- No new environment variable, secret, Keycloak client/realm setting, LDAP
  mapper, Docker Compose service or Helm resource is expected. Frontend and
  Backend should deploy together because an old Frontend would present the new
  403 as a generic auth-load error instead of the approved denial surface.
- Rollback restores the former zero-permission entry behavior and is therefore
  authorization-weaker. Deployment notes must call out coordinated rollback;
  no data rollback is needed.

### Test And Verification Strategy

- Backend tests use real disposable PostgreSQL state and valid test OIDC/JWT
  infrastructure under TEST-002. Cover positive permissions from
  external/manual/break-glass sources, unmapped groups, all-false grants,
  inactive/deleted roles, project-only scope, exact error envelopes, no
  business mutation/query, safe audit and distinction from 401/unavailable and
  route-specific forbidden.
- Revocation/convergence tests remove the last positive grant during a session,
  prove the next request fails globally, add a mapped/manual positive grant,
  and prove `/auth/me` recheck succeeds without a new credential exchange.
- Frontend component/contract tests render the real auth state machine and API
  responses without inventing a passing provider. Prove no AppShell/Home/
  Notification/API Docs effect is mounted while denied, single recheck,
  existing logout, safe return target, no refresh/redirect loop, ordinary 403
  parity, zh/en and accessible responsive states.
- Browser E2E uses an isolated real Keycloak realm, LDAP subtree and PostgreSQL
  dataset: one zero-permission user, one external-mapped user and one
  manual-role user. Exercise login denial, group/role grant plus recheck,
  final-grant revocation and logout at desktop and narrow widths. Current UAT
  identities are not mutated without separate authorization.
- Run focused tests first after Gate 4, then governance, Backend/Frontend,
  i18n, E2E, coverage, security and deployment regression gates. Unavailable
  services are reported blocked and are never replaced by mock success.

### Expected Implementation Areas

- `backend/app/security/permissions.py`
- `backend/app/security/context.py`
- `backend/app/api/routes/auth.py`
- `backend/app/services/audit.py` or the existing safe audit call boundary
- `frontend/src/components/AuthProvider.tsx`
- `frontend/src/app/access-denied/page.tsx` or a thin route using a shared
  authenticated denial component
- `frontend/src/lib/api.ts`
- `frontend/src/lib/operationalMessages.ts`
- `frontend/src/i18n/locales/zh.json`
- `frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json`
- Existing auth/backend/frontend/browser test suites plus focused CHG-256 tests

### Risks And Controls

- Risk: checking raw group presence would reject valid manual/break-glass users
  or admit an unmapped group. Control: evaluate only current positive NomoSmart
  role permissions and test all three membership sources.
- Risk: a global 403 handler could turn an admitted user's page-level forbidden
  result into full application denial. Control: transition globally only on the
  exact `application_access_denied` code and retain existing feature error
  paths.
- Risk: `/access-denied` could enter silent SSO or callback loops. Control: make
  it an authenticated AuthProvider state with explicit canonical-route guards;
  keep valid tokens and never auto-refresh/relogin for this 403.
- Risk: route components or AppShell effects may issue requests before the
  guard settles. Control: AuthProvider owns the render boundary and tests assert
  zero child, Home and Notification calls before admission.
- Risk: permission is granted while a denied page is open but stale client
  state persists. Control: recheck always calls the authoritative `/auth/me`,
  installs its fresh response atomically and coalesces duplicate clicks.
- Risk: coordinated Backend-first rollout gives old Frontend poor UX. Control:
  deploy together and verify the new Frontend against both granted 200 and
  denied 403 before promotion; no authorization bypass compatibility mode is
  allowed.

### Out Of Scope

- Automatically assigning a default role or placing every synchronized user in
  a group.
- Editing LDAP/Keycloak groups, external-group mappings or role permissions
  from the denial page.
- Treating Project Owner/member scope as a replacement for a system role.
- Logging the user out automatically, adding a NomoSmart local login or
  changing Keycloak credentials/MFA/session policy.
- Redesigning ordinary feature-forbidden pages, Home content, AppShell
  navigation or the role/permission management UI beyond the admission gate.

## CHG-257 Repository Hygiene And README Alignment

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-08-18 with
`同意 CHG-257 Gate 2（三項皆採建議）`. Gate 3 specification, development,
test and traceability planning is complete below. Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-08-18 with
`Peter approves CHG-257 Repository Hygiene And README Alignment`; scoped
implementation and verification may proceed.

### Confirmed Understanding And Decisions

- This is repository hygiene and documentation alignment, not a product,
  API, schema, permission, runtime configuration, deployment or UAT change.
- Add only the exact root `/component_edit/` ignore needed for the observed
  tool-generated Python component. Existing Secret, installer, release,
  coverage and build rules remain; application source, tests, migrations,
  docs, design assets, Helm lock files and documented vendored charts remain
  visible to Git.
- Root `.DS_Store` already matches an ignore rule but is tracked. Remove it
  from the Git index only and retain the local file. Do not delete or untrack
  any other user file.
- Rewrite the 378-line root README as a concise repository entry guide. Keep
  detailed deployment and installer operations in their authoritative files,
  summarize current approved capabilities and state open live/coverage gates
  explicitly.

### Scope And Implementation Approach

1. Add a root-anchored `/component_edit/` entry under a clearly named local
   tool/generated-artifact section in `.gitignore`.
2. Preserve all existing ignore rules and validate negative examples for
   representative source, test, migration, documentation, design, Helm lock
   and vendored-chart paths.
3. Remove only root `.DS_Store` from Git tracking with a cached/index-only
   operation after confirming its exact tracked path and existing ignore rule.
   Do not remove the local file.
4. Replace the root README with a concise structure: product and authoritative
   specification; approved capabilities; honest release status; repository
   map; engineering prerequisites and quick start; deployment profiles and
   authoritative runbooks; harness; Secret/repository hygiene; specification-
   driven contribution workflow.
5. Summarize CHG-250/254/255/256 outcomes without turning README into a change
   log: three required active compatible AI model types, live-derived Home KPI
   helpers, cascading Keycloak directory sync, effective-permission admission
   and localized operational messages.
6. Keep commands repository-relative and link detailed deployment, installer,
   release-readiness, harness and governance documents instead of duplicating
   their procedures.

### Test And Verification Strategy

- Use `git check-ignore --no-index -v` to prove `.DS_Store` and
  `component_edit/` are ignored, plus negative checks proving intentional
  repository artifacts are not ignored.
- Use `git ls-files` and filesystem checks to prove `.DS_Store` is absent from
  the index but remains on disk; confirm no other tracked path was removed.
- Parse README relative Markdown links and verify each local target exists.
  Validate every documented `./HARNESS/harness.sh <command>` selector against
  the harness help/dispatch surface.
- Scan README for personal absolute paths, credential-like material and
  unqualified release-complete claims; inspect section structure and size to
  confirm it is an entry guide rather than a duplicated runbook.
- Run `spec:doctor`, `spec:trace`, `plan:doctor`, `plan:approved`, `test:plan`,
  `repo:doctor` and `git diff --check`. Product feature, live integration,
  Browser and coverage suites are unchanged and not required to prove a
  documentation/ignore-only change.

### Deployment, Compatibility And Data Impact

- No image, Compose, Helm, installer runtime, environment variable, Secret,
  migration or release-package behavior changes.
- No application or UAT data is read or mutated.
- `.DS_Store` is the only planned Git index removal. `component_edit/` remains
  on disk as ignored local generated content.
- README remains subordinate to `SPECIFICATION.md` and the linked operator
  runbooks. Existing external links, if retained, are descriptive only; local
  repository validation covers relative links.

### Risks And Controls

- Risk: a broad ignore rule hides real source or release inputs. Control: use
  a root-anchored exact path and explicit negative `git check-ignore` cases.
- Risk: index cleanup deletes the local file or unrelated work. Control:
  resolve the exact tracked root file first and use cached/index-only removal.
- Risk: README duplicates details and drifts again. Control: keep overview and
  minimum quick-start commands only; link authoritative runbooks.
- Risk: README overstates release readiness. Control: list current live
  integration/E2E and independent 80% coverage gates as open.
- Risk: existing dirty-worktree changes are overwritten. Control: edit only
  the approved target/governance files and preserve all unrelated diffs.

### Out Of Scope

- Deleting `component_edit/`, design assets, docs, source, tests, migrations,
  vendored charts or any other existing user file.
- Changing application behavior, dependencies, lock files, Docker/Helm
  templates, installer implementation or UAT state.
- Completing live E2E, integration, coverage, security-image or release gates.
- Staging, committing, pushing or opening a pull request.

### Planned Verification Commands After Gate 4

```bash

./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace
```

## CHG-259 Guided Step-by-step README Installation Walkthroughs

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-08-18 with
`同意 CHG-259 Gate 2（三項皆採建議）`. Gate 3 specification, development,
test and traceability planning is complete below. Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-08-18 with
`Peter approves CHG-259 Guided Step-by-step README Installation Walkthroughs`;
scoped README implementation and documentation acceptance may proceed.

### Confirmed Understanding And Decisions

- Replace the current environment entry summaries with four independent,
  sequential walkthroughs: engineering Development, Docker Compose,
  Kubernetes `bundled` and Kubernetes `external-services`.
- Give every numbered step the same five-part contract: required input,
  safe command or linked operator action, expected result, failure stop with
  diagnostic source, and explicit next step.
- Make normal preparation, configuration, read-only planning, startup, status
  and post-install verification directly followable from README.
- Treat credentials, Vault custody and destructive/rollback/recovery lifecycle
  operations as explicit stop-points owned by authoritative runbooks. README
  never reproduces their sensitive commands or values.

### Scope And Implementation Approach

1. Add a short walkthrough usage contract explaining that users select exactly
   one environment path and never mix commands/configuration between profiles.
2. Declare neutral placeholder names before commands, such as
   `OPERATOR_CONFIG_PATH`, `RELEASE_REVISION` and profile-specific configuration
   paths. Use literal safe placeholder tokens, not shell metacharacters or real
   values.
3. Expand Engineering Development into ordered repository checkout/tool,
   dependency/configuration, migration/bootstrap, Backend/Worker/Beat,
   Frontend and focused verification steps, while retaining the non-Production
   and real-dependency boundaries.
4. Expand Docker Compose into ordered tool/revision, operator package/env/TLS,
   configuration validation, security stop-point, stack start, migration/
   bootstrap status, workload/readiness and application verification steps.
   Link the exact package/Vault lifecycle to deployment/package runbooks.
5. Expand Kubernetes `bundled` into ordered cluster/profile/config/TLS/image/
   directory preparation, read-only one-click plan, digest/change approval,
   guided execution, action-required checkpoint handling, status/verify and
   application verification. Do not reproduce internal installer stages.
6. Expand Kubernetes `external-services` with an earlier operator-owned service
   inventory, endpoint/TLS/minimum-permission/readiness and existing Secret/CA
   gate, followed by the same safe guided installer path and verification.
7. For every step, format the required inputs, action, expected result,
   stop/diagnostic and next step consistently enough for structural validation.
8. End every path at the existing layered post-install checklist and distinguish
   environment installation completion from Production release acceptance.

### Test And Verification Strategy

- Validate exactly four walkthrough headings and profile-specific start/end
  boundaries; no walkthrough directs users into another profile's commands.
- Parse each numbered walkthrough step and require labels for inputs/action,
  expected result, failure stop/diagnostic and next step.
- Validate phase order and minimum content for each path: preparation before
  config, config before plan/start, status/readiness before application and
  release verification.
- Extract placeholders, require prior declarations, reject shell redirection/
  substitution ambiguity and scan for real-looking credentials, endpoints,
  hostnames, kube contexts and image digests.
- Validate every local link, repository executable/path and harness selector.
  Documentation validation does not execute install/live commands.
- Reject duplicated internal installer-stage tables, Vault custody/credential
  handling, restore/rollback/uninstall/factory-reset/permanent-delete sequences
  and destructive commands.
- Validate every walkthrough points to health/readiness, OIDC/admission,
  directory sync, three-model readiness, i18n/Home, background/data dependencies
  and E2E/coverage/release evidence with honest static-vs-live wording.
- Run `spec:doctor`, `spec:trace`, `plan:doctor`, `plan:approved`, `test:plan`,
  `repo:doctor` and `git diff --check`; retain the known `output/playwright/`
  doctor result unless separately authorized cleanup occurs.

### Deployment, Compatibility And Data Impact

- Documentation-only; no code, dependency, API, schema, migration, Compose,
  Helm, installer or environment configuration behavior changes.
- No walkthrough command is executed during implementation or documentation
  acceptance, and no external service, Secret, cluster or UAT state is read or
  mutated.
- Existing `README-001/002`, environment profiles, installer contracts and
  authoritative runbooks remain compatible. `README-003` only makes the safe
  navigation sequence explicit.

### Risks And Controls

- Risk: a copy/paste command targets the wrong environment. Control: mutually
  exclusive walkthroughs, declared placeholders and visible profile labels.
- Risk: users continue after a failed prerequisite. Control: every step has an
  observable expected result and mandatory fail-stop/diagnostic instruction.
- Risk: README duplicates sensitive runbook procedures. Control: explicit
  security stop-points and automated forbidden-detail scans.
- Risk: a running container/Pod is mistaken for acceptance. Control: every path
  ends at dependency-aware application and release verification.
- Risk: unrelated dirty work is changed. Control: modify only README and
  CHG-259 governance artifacts; do not stage, delete or reformat other files.

### Out Of Scope

- Provisioning VM/OS/Kubernetes/CNI/CSI/Ingress/DNS/CA/registry/directory server
  or external data services.
- Executing installation, migration, bootstrap, Vault, identity sync, AI model,

- Embedding real environment values or replacing deployment/package/installer/
  release-readiness runbooks.
- Closing runtime, E2E, coverage, security, backup or Production release gates.
- Committing, pushing or altering unrelated working-tree content.

```bash

./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor
```

## CHG-260 Vault And Upload Scan Removal With Simplified Credentials And Authentication

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-08-18 with
`同意 CHG-260 Gate 2（五項皆確認並接受列示風險）`. Gate 3 specification,
development, test and traceability planning is complete below. Gate 4 was
approved by Peter on 2026-08-18 with
`Peter approves CHG-260 Vault And Upload Scan Removal With Simplified Credentials And Authentication`;
repository implementation and non-destructive/disposable verification may proceed.

### Confirmed Understanding And Decisions

- Remove every NomoSmart-owned Vault runtime, deployment, installer, package,
  readiness, backup/recovery and documentation contract. Kubernetes uses
  namespaced Kubernetes Secrets; Compose uses uncommitted Docker Secret files.
- Remove ClamAV and external malware-scanner support completely. Validated files
  go directly to final object storage and the existing single/multi-file
  extraction behavior, with no scan/quarantine evidence for new uploads.
- For new bundled installations, default supported peripheral principals/access
  keys to `nomosmart` and password/secret keys to `P@ssw0rd`. Product-mandated
  bootstrap identity names may remain temporarily; external services are never
  reset. Non-password cryptographic material remains distinct.
- Make the NomoSmart-managed bundled Keycloak realm password-only. Remove TOTP
  flows, required actions, checkpoints and evidence without deleting existing
  OTP credentials or bypassing an external Provider's authentication policy.
- Preserve historical scan/quarantine/OTP evidence non-destructively, block
  active `vault://` and mixed contracts before rollout, and record the accepted
  scanner/TOTP/shared-password risks in release evidence.

### Scope And Implementation Approach

1. Freeze the compatibility boundary before code changes. Add one typed
   CHG-260 security-contract identity, inventory all active `vault://` refs,
   Vault settings/resources and non-terminal scan work, and fail the upgrade
   plan before mutation when any unresolved dependency remains.
2. Replace the Vault resolver with a closed Secret resolver supporting only
   `k8s-secret://<name>#<key>` from explicitly mounted same-namespace Secret
   volumes and `compose-secret://<logical-name>` from allowlisted read-only
   files. Remove Vault errors/config/client code and keep value/path redaction.
3. Migrate every platform and business/integration consumer: database, Redis,
   S3, OpenSearch, Neo4j, OIDC/Keycloak, model/OCR and data-source credentials.
   Add operator migration inventory and real-consumer verification; never read
   Vault values for automatic transfer and never grant Kubernetes Secret API
   list/write permission to application workloads.
4. Remove scan lifecycle creation and dispatch from upload/data-sync domains,
   Worker/Celery routing, configuration, health and operational messages.
   Directly write a validated object to the canonical final key, atomically
   publish its document/version pointer and use existing compensation when
   object/database/outbox work fails. Remove `file_scan` from new pipelines/UI.
5. Retain `file_scan_runs` and existing quarantine objects as read-only history.
   Upgrade preflight rejects non-terminal scan work; no migration promotes,
   deletes or fabricates outcomes. A later retention/deletion request remains
   separately gated.
6. Change the package/installer credential generator and Helm/Compose defaults
   to the confirmed mapping. Generate actual Kubernetes/Docker Secret objects
   outside Git; preserve product-required bootstrap names only for initialization
   and switch runtime clients to `nomosmart`. Keep keys/tokens/certificates
   random, protocol-valid and separately scoped.
7. Reconcile the bundled Keycloak Browser Flow to password-only, remove
   `CONFIGURE_TOTP`, TOTP status/evidence and Theme pages, and simplify first-use
   and emergency break-glass finalization to password-update/OIDC/role/sync
   evidence. Do not delete stored OTP credentials. Leave external realm/IdP
   policy untouched.
8. Remove Vault/ClamAV/TOTP workloads, dependencies, ports, volumes, probes,
   NetworkPolicies, image/SBOM inventory, Helm values/schema/templates,
   Compose services, installer stages, release checks and backup/restore paths.
   Rebuild the stage order and status/receipt schemas around Secret delivery,
   direct ingestion and password-only onboarding.
9. Update Backend contracts, migrations/compatibility guards, frontend progress
   and authentication surfaces, zh-TW/en catalogs, README/deployment/package/
   installer/release runbooks and risk disclosures. Remove only obsolete strings
   and retain localized safe errors for missing Secret or denied admission.
10. Perform a coordinated rollout. Mixed Vault/scanner-dependent and CHG-260
    images are rejected. Rollback requires the complete former topology and
    references; otherwise repair by roll-forward. No current UAT mutation,
    Secret creation or external-system change is authorized by Gate 4 alone.

### Implementation Task Breakdown

1. **Compatibility and inventory**
   - Add CHG-260 compatibility identity and preflight diagnostics.
   - Detect active `vault://`, Vault config/resources, non-terminal scan runs,
     stale scanner outbox/tasks and mixed release images without logging values.
   - Define an operator-owned migration report and exact unblock conditions.
2. **Secret runtime**
   - Implement strict Kubernetes-mounted and Compose-file reference parsing.
   - Convert all credential consumers and connection tests.
   - Remove Vault client/config/errors/readiness and persistent/leak surfaces.
3. **Ingestion**
   - Remove ClamAV adapter, scanner domain/worker dispatch and scanner config.
   - Rework upload/data-sync transactions, compensation and pipeline steps.
   - Preserve historical scan/quarantine records without active mutation.
4. **Credentials and bootstrap**
   - Apply exact default username/password mapping and bootstrap exceptions.
   - Keep Secret manifests/generated files untracked and redact every output.
   - Preserve override and external-services non-mutation behavior.
5. **Authentication**
   - Reconcile password-only bundled Keycloak flow and Theme.
   - Remove TOTP required-action/checkpoint/finalization contracts.
   - Preserve password update, OIDC PKCE, fresh auth, admission and external MFA.
6. **Deployment and operations**
   - Update Compose, Helm, installer, package, release, readiness, network,
     backup/restore, image inventory and compatibility policy in one change.
   - Update status/receipt/risk evidence without Secret values.
7. **Frontend, i18n and docs**
   - Remove scan/TOTP states and update upload/auth operational messages.
   - Align Traditional Chinese and English catalogs and accessibility behavior.
   - Rewrite README and authoritative runbooks to remove obsolete procedures.
8. **Verification and release handoff**
   - Run focused static/unit/component/integration/deployment tests first.
   - Run real Kubernetes/Compose/Keycloak/data-service/browser paths under
     `TEST-002`; report missing prerequisites as blocked, never simulated pass.
   - Re-run independent Frontend/Backend coverage, security, image/SBOM and
     release gates and document every accepted/open risk.

### Test And Verification Strategy

- Parser and mount tests prove only same-namespace allowlisted Kubernetes
  Secret and declared Compose Secret references resolve; missing, empty,
  traversal, cross-namespace, permission and leak cases fail closed.
- Migration/preflight tests cover every active Vault reference/config/resource,
  non-terminal scan and mixed-image combination, plus a complete no-Vault
  success path using real consumers.
- Upload/API/Worker tests cover valid single and multiple files, remote sync,
  duplicate delivery, DB/object/outbox failure compensation, no scan row/event/
  task/step, historical-row immutability and no fake clean status.
- Credential tests cover each bundled service, product-required bootstrap-name
  exceptions, generated Secret bytes, override behavior, external non-mutation,
  redaction and cryptographic-material exclusion.
- Real Keycloak tests cover new/existing realms, password login, password update,
  fresh authentication, no TOTP page/action/checkpoint, retained unused OTP
  credential, external Provider MFA preservation and `AUTH-018` admission.
- Helm/Compose/installer/package/release tests prove Vault/ClamAV resources,
  dependencies, ports, values and images are absent and Secret/risk evidence is
  present. Roll-forward/rollback compatibility is exercised on disposable data.
- Frontend component/browser tests cover password-only login, upload progress
  without scan, missing-Secret failures, zh-TW/en parity, keyboard/focus/alerts
  and responsive behavior.
- All runtime acceptance uses real configured services under `TEST-002`; static
  absence checks are guardrails, not live evidence. Frontend and Backend each
  retain the independent >=80% release gate.

### Deployment, Configuration And Data Impact

- Breaking Helm/Compose/install/package/release configuration change: all Vault,
  ClamAV and TOTP keys/stages/resources are removed. Existing overlays and
  automation must migrate before rollout.
- Kubernetes gains mounted/runtime Secret references; Compose retains generated
  uncommitted Secret files. No plaintext credential is committed to values,
  env templates, images, SQL, logs or receipts.
- No destructive scan-table or OTP-credential migration is planned. Historical
  records stay readable only where audit/retention requires; new runtime paths
  never create them.
- Current UAT/Production secrets, Vault, ClamAV, Keycloak, uploads and data are
  not changed by repository implementation. Live mutation or deletion requires
  an exact environment plan and separate explicit authorization.

### Risks And Controls

- Risk: uploaded malware reaches parser/OCR. Control retained by decision:
  strict type/package validation, isolated non-root no-network parsers,
  resource limits and accepted-risk release evidence; no scanner claim.
- Risk: shared known peripheral password increases blast radius. Control:
  namespaced/file Secret custody, network isolation, runtime/bootstrap Secret
  separation, operator override/rotation and explicit non-secret risk identity.
- Risk: password-only login weakens account protection. Control retained by
  decision: Keycloak password/lockout policy, TLS, OIDC PKCE, session controls,
  admission/permissions, audit and external Provider policy preservation.
- Risk: Vault migration loses or exposes credentials. Control: operator-created
  target Secrets, no automatic export, redacted inventory, real-consumer proof
  and fail-closed preflight.
- Risk: old and new contracts coexist. Control: compatibility identity,
  preflight rejection, coordinated rollout and roll-forward default.
- Risk: unrelated dirty work is altered. Control: implementation must inspect
  and preserve existing modifications, stage only CHG-260-owned paths and never
  delete unrelated/untracked content.

### Out Of Scope

- Deleting operator-owned Vault/ClamAV deployments, Vault data, quarantine
  objects, historical scan rows or OTP credentials from a live environment.
- Disabling or bypassing MFA on an external operator-managed Keycloak/OIDC IdP.
- Replacing cryptographic keys, client secrets, tokens or certificates with
  `P@ssw0rd`.
- Provisioning Kubernetes, DNS, CA, registry, directory services or external
  data services; destructive UAT reinstall; production rollout or credential
  rotation without separate authorization.
- Committing, pushing or modifying unrelated working-tree content.

  is not pre-authorized by this plan.

  infer targets from globs, broad directories or unresolved variables.

  and must identify the exact certificate fingerprint before approval.

- The dirty working tree reduces reproducibility; exact source status and image
  identity must be recorded, and no claim may be attached only to the base SHA.
- Docker Desktop restarts can change the API endpoint or invalidate the cluster;
  every mutating phase must revalidate the target.
- The three nodes, local-path storage and one-host network share a single Docker
  Desktop failure domain. Replica count is not evidence of HA.
- The bundled stack is resource- and disk-intensive. Capacity exhaustion,
  `arm64` image incompatibility and local-image visibility are fail-stop risks.
- Default local credentials, a user-trusted development CA and password-only
  Keycloak are accepted only for the bounded localhost environment.
- Because no AI providers or external directory are configured, corresponding
  workflows remain intentionally blocked or incomplete. Existing Frontend
  coverage of `7.33%` also leaves the independent 80% release gate open.

## CHG-261 README Information Architecture Consolidation And Root Guide Refresh

### Status And Planning Gates

- Gate 1 completed on 2026-08-19 through a read-only inventory of every
  repository-owned README, its headings, cross-links, duplicated installation
  material, current CHG-260 terms and the existing dirty working tree.

  2026-08-19 with `同意 CHG-261 Gate 2（三項皆採建議）`.
- Gate 3 specification, development plan, test design and traceability are
  complete in the current governance documents.
- Gate 4 implementation approval: approved. Peter approved Gate 4 on
  2026-08-19 with
  `Peter approves CHG-261 README Information Architecture Consolidation And Root Guide Refresh`.

### Confirmed Understanding And Decisions

- Retain all nine repository-owned README files because each has a distinct
  product, development, deployment, component or design responsibility.
- Make root `README.md` the single repository entry and keep the four guided
  environment paths required by `README-003`, but compress repeated prose and
  refer deep component/lifecycle work to one authoritative child README.
- Remove normal-path CHG history and repeated Vault/ClamAV/TOTP transition
  wording. Preserve retired terms only where upgrade compatibility or historical
  evidence requires them, without presenting a retired feature as available.
- Use Traditional Chinese as the primary explanatory language across all nine
  documents while keeping filenames, commands, API paths, environment variables,
  product names and CLI flags unchanged.
- Centralize public default credential documentation in the Package guide, with
  only the root first-use summary repeated where a user needs it. Never introduce
  actual operator values, UAT endpoints, personal paths, tokens or private keys.

### Scope And Documentation Architecture

1. **Root entry guide**
   - Keep product purpose, current operational baseline, release-readiness
     honesty, repository map and environment-selection matrix.
   - Rebuild the four walkthroughs in a compact common structure while retaining
     prerequisites/input, safe action, observable result, fail-stop and next
     verification entry for every profile.
   - Keep one post-install verification overview and one authoritative document
     index; remove component internals and repeated lifecycle procedures.
2. **Engineering guide**
   - Limit `backend/README.md` to Development dependencies/configuration,
     Flyway, Backend/Worker/Beat processes and focused verification.
3. **Deployment guide and runbooks**
   - Turn `deploy/README.md` into the deployment decision/responsibility/lifecycle
     index rather than a second full installer.
   - Keep `deploy/package/README.md` authoritative for generated Secret/TLS
     package, defaults, preflight and rotation.
   - Keep `deploy/installer/README.md` authoritative for the Kubernetes guided
     install/resume/status/verify/doctor sequence.
4. **Specialized component guides**
   - Restrict Keycloak, release, OpenSearch and branding README content to the
     responsibilities enumerated by `README-004` and add clear parent/related
     navigation where useful.
5. **Cross-document consistency**
   - Align all normal installation language to `SECRET-002`, `UPLOAD-SEC-003`,
     `DEPLOY-019` and `AUTH-020`.
   - Preserve security stop-points for Secret custody, destructive lifecycle,
     backup/restore, rollback/uninstall and release signing.
   - Validate every relative link, path, executable, harness selector, profile,
     default and placeholder against the same working-tree revision.

1. Capture the exact nine-file baseline and build an internal responsibility,
   navigation and duplicate-content checklist before editing.

   usage rules are listed and that links point to files that exist.
5. Run cross-document searches for duplicated command sequences, credential
   matrices, post-install checklists, retired technology and CHG history. Keep
   only explicitly allowed compatibility/evidence occurrences.
6. Validate links, commands, executable paths, selectors, language, sensitive
   strings and the root `README-001/002/003/004` contract; correct documentation
   defects only within the approved nine README files.
7. Update CHG-261 governance results and traceability with exact pass, failure or
   known-gap evidence. Do not infer runtime or release acceptance from document
   validation.

### Test And Verification Strategy

- Inventory validation proves exactly the nine scoped README files remain and
  no dependency/generated README is treated as project documentation.
- Ownership review proves each child README stays inside its assigned domain,
  root remains the only cross-project entry and every child is reachable from a
  parent or related-document link.
- Root contract validation proves all four environments remain distinct and
  executable through safe general preparation/config/plan/start/status and
  verification entries, including the required expected-result and fail-stop
  semantics.
- Duplicate-content inspection permits a repeated one-line entry command or
  first-use prompt where usability requires it, but rejects a second complete
  multi-step procedure, credential table, post-install checklist or lifecycle
  runbook.
- Compatibility search classifies every Vault/ClamAV/scanner/quarantine/TOTP
  and `CHG-NNN` occurrence; only explicitly marked upgrade, historical or stable
  trace references may remain.
- Link and command validation resolves relative Markdown targets, repository
  paths, executable files and harness selectors without executing deployment,
  installation, migration or live-service commands.
- Sensitive-content validation allows only the documented public first-use and
  bundled default credentials in their approved locations, and rejects actual
  Secret material, environment-specific endpoint/identity, private path,
  unbounded placeholder or destructive shortcut.
- Governance and Markdown/diff hygiene run independently. This documentation-
  only scope does not require application, integration, E2E or coverage tests
  and cannot close any existing runtime/release gate.

### Deployment, Configuration And Data Impact

- No application, API, schema, migration, frontend locale, deployment manifest,
  runtime configuration, Secret, external service or data changes are planned.
- No installation, package generation, image build, cluster mutation, identity
  synchronization, credential rotation or live verification is authorized.
- Existing CHG-260 implementation and open release gaps remain unchanged; the
  work documents them more clearly but does not supply new runtime evidence.
- The dirty worktree is preserved. Only the nine README files and CHG-261
  governance records may be edited; unrelated current modifications are neither
  reverted, reformatted, staged nor deleted.

### Risks And Controls

- Risk: over-compression breaks the step-by-step contract. Control: validate
  each of the four root paths against `README-003` fields before handoff.
- Risk: moving text creates broken or circular navigation. Control: resolve all
  local links and confirm each specialized guide has a clear parent/related path.
- Risk: removal hides a critical safety condition. Control: retain explicit
  Secret custody, destructive lifecycle, backup/restore, rollback/uninstall and
  release-signing stop-points in their authoritative documents.
- Risk: historical terms are mistaken for active features. Control: place any
  necessary retired term under a labelled compatibility/history boundary and
  verify the normal installation path is CHG-260-only.
- Risk: translation changes a technical contract. Control: never translate
  literal commands, paths, flags, environment variables, API routes, profile
  values or upstream identity names.
- Risk: unrelated dirty work is changed. Control: inspect file-specific diffs
  and restrict edits to the approved documentation/governance paths.

### Out Of Scope

- Deleting any of the nine README files or consolidating non-README documents
  under `docs/`, `HARNESS/` or governance artifacts.
- Changing product behavior, deployment implementation, defaults, authentication,
  upload processing, Secret resolution, API/schema contracts or test thresholds.
- Executing README walkthrough commands, live services, Docker/Helm install,
  migration/bootstrap, Browser E2E, backup/restore, rollback or uninstall.
- Committing, pushing, cleaning generated evidence or modifying unrelated files.

## CHG-264 Docker OpenLDAP And phpLDAPadmin Local Test Directory

### Status And Gate Scope

- Gate 1 completed on 2026-08-19 through read-only Docker, Docker network,
  Kubernetes, port, chart and directory-integration inventory.
- Gate 2 confirmation: complete. Peter confirmed Gate 2 on 2026-08-19 with
  `同意 CHG-264 Gate 2，採用上述建議`.
- Gate 3 specification, changelog, development plan, test design and
  traceability are complete.
- Gate 4 implementation approval: approved. Peter approved Gate 4 on
  2026-08-19 with
  `Peter approves CHG-264 Docker OpenLDAP And phpLDAPadmin Local Test Directory`.
- Non-destructive repository implementation, bounded local installation and
  live verification may begin after action-time target/security preflight.
- Requirements under change: `DEPLOY-021` and `LDAP-001..005` in specification
  section 10.21. This is a local-development integration and does not alter the
  Production/UAT deployment claims.

### Specification Understanding

Peter needs a real OpenLDAP directory and phpLDAPadmin UI in local Docker so
the already-running `nomosmart-local` release on Docker Desktop Kubernetes can
exercise strict LDAPS federation, Keycloak user/group import and NomoSmart's
cascaded identity synchronization. The directory stack is independent of the
NomoSmart Helm chart. It seeds only synthetic entries, persists across
container recreation and is reachable by Keycloak without exposing LDAP ports
to the host or LAN. phpLDAPadmin is local-only at `127.0.0.1:8080`.

The directory administrator and read-only bind account receive distinct random
owner-only credentials; only the synthetic users use the explicitly accepted
local-test password `P@ssw0rd`. Keycloak uses a READ_ONLY provider and a single
`/ldap` group mapper. No LDAP group receives a NomoSmart role in this change.
Consequently the strongest end-to-end acceptance is successful directory and
Keycloak authentication followed by NomoSmart's expected
`application_access_denied`, while the existing administrator remains usable.

### Discussion And Confirmation Items

Gate 2 resolved every blocking choice as follows:

1. Use a separate Compose stack, digest-pinned native-arm64 images, persistent
   OpenLDAP database/configuration and a safe committed template with runtime
   credentials, LDIF and private key outside Git.
2. Use Base DN `dc=nomosmart,dc=test`, `ou=users`, `ou=groups`, a read-only bind
   account, two synthetic users and synthetic `groupOfNames` groups.
3. Expose only phpLDAPadmin HTTP on `127.0.0.1:8080`; do not publish host ports
   389 or 636. Keycloak reaches strict LDAPS through the Docker `kind` network.
4. Preserve the Helm templates. Add only a new CA Secret/trust values reference
   and a separate bind Secret, then reconcile the provider/mapper through the
   Keycloak Admin API.
5. Perform full Keycloak user/group sync and a real NomoSmart identity sync,
   but create no NomoSmart local-role mapping and require denied application
   admission for the synthetic identities.
6. Preserve all current NomoSmart resources and directory volumes by default.
   Gate 4 does not authorize destructive cleanup.

### Human Confirmation

Peter confirmed this understanding and all recommended decisions on
2026-08-19 with:

`同意 CHG-264 Gate 2，採用上述建議`

This confirmation authorized Gate 3 planning only. Peter subsequently supplied
the separate Gate 4 approval recorded in this section.

### Development Plan

   specification, changelog, plan, test plan and traceability matrix.
2. Capture a redacted, exact pre-mutation inventory of Docker Desktop context,
   Docker architecture, `kind` network subnet/occupancy, relevant host

### Test Strategy

- Run governance and focused static/render checks before any live mutation.
- Verify actual OpenLDAP protocol operations over TLS rather than container
  status alone: anonymous denial, admin/read-only bind behavior, ACL denials,
  entry attributes, group membership and persistence.

  listeners to prove no LDAP/LAN publication.

  actual NomoSmart identity-sync queue/worker/API path.

  successful admission for the preserved local administrator.
- All evidence is redacted. Passwords, tokens, private keys and complete LDIF
  content are never captured in command output, screenshots or handoff.

### Deployment And Configuration Impact

- New local-only Compose artifacts under `deploy/docker/ldap-test/` and

  NomoSmart role mapping, database migration or application code behavior.
- Existing NomoSmart release/PVC/data/TLS/runtime Secret/Ingress and host trust

### Risks And Mitigations

- A fixed `kind` network IP can drift or collide. Revalidate subnet, occupancy,
  route and leaf SAN immediately before startup and fail closed on mismatch.
- phpLDAPadmin is intentionally HTTP. Bind only to `127.0.0.1`, reject any
  wildcard/LAN listener and never save credentials in the browser.
- The synthetic password is public. Limit it to invented users in this isolated
  local directory, label the risk, and never reuse it for admin/bind/shared
  environments.
- UI administrator access can write synthetic LDAP data. Separate it from the
  read-only Keycloak bind, verify ACLs and keep all seed/lifecycle actions
  bounded to the test Base DN.
- A Keycloak trust upgrade can restart login service. Render/fingerprint first,
  retain prior values/revision and verify existing administrator login after
  readiness.
- Imported LDAP users/groups can outlive provider rollback. Preserve history by
  default and require a separate exact-target deletion approval for purge.
- The worktree contains existing CHG-262/263 changes. Use scoped diff review;
  never revert, stage or attribute unrelated user work to CHG-264.

## CHG-266 Keycloak Boolean Ignored Identity Sync Compatibility Fix

### Status And Gate Scope

- Gate 1 diagnosis completed on 2026-08-20 through read-only application code,
  database, worker log, Keycloak API and LDAP-synchronized inventory evidence.
- Gate 2 completed when Peter confirmed
  `同意 CHG-266 Gate 2，採用上述建議`.
- Gate 3 specification, changelog, test design, traceability and this plan are
  complete.
- Gate 4 implementation approval: approved. Peter approved Gate 4 on
  2026-08-20 with
  `Peter approves CHG-266 Keycloak Boolean Ignored Identity Sync Compatibility Fix`.
  The bounded source implementation, additive migration, versioned image build,
  non-destructive local Helm upgrade and one real identity-sync run are
  authorized subject to the action-time preflight.
- Requirements: specification section 10.23 and `IDENTITY-SYNC-001..005`.

### Confirmed Understanding And Decisions

Keycloak 26 returns `ignored` as a boolean on a successful full-sync result.
NomoSmart currently parses it with the integer-only `_sync_counter`, so
`ignored=false` is rejected before group sync, snapshot and reconciliation.
The four recorded NomoSmart failures are therefore accurate application
failures even though the upstream Keycloak LDAP import succeeded. The fix is a
strict contract correction, not a relaxation: counters remain non-negative
integers, `ignored` becomes an explicit boolean, false continues the lifecycle,
and true fails safely with a distinct stable error.

Persistence receives additive `V044`. The legacy `users_ignored` integer is
retained and fixed to zero for one compatibility window; the new
`user_sync_ignored` boolean carries the Keycloak meaning. The four failed runs
remain immutable history. Local deployment requires newly versioned
backend/worker/migration images and one non-destructive Helm upgrade; all
OpenLDAP, Keycloak, Helm, Secret, PVC, TLS, Ingress, Redis and authorization
boundaries remain unchanged.

### Development Plan

#### Batch 0 — Baseline And Governance Guard

1. Keep CHG-266 as the active change and map `IDENTITY-SYNC-001..005` across
   all five governance artifacts before implementation.
2. After Gate 4, repeat read-only action-time preflight: exact
   `docker-desktop` context, `nomosmart-local` release/revision, Ready workload
   inventory, current image IDs, seven PVC/Secret UIDs, Keycloak provider and
   mapper IDs, seven LDAP-linked users/six `/ldap` groups, four failed run IDs,
   and absence of the five/four target NomoSmart rows.
3. Fail closed on context, release, provider, schema or resource drift. Record
   only redacted IDs, counters, hashes and non-secret inventory.

#### Batch 1 — Strict Keycloak Result Domain

1. Change the Keycloak sync result domain so `ignored` is boolean and add an
   explicit strict boolean parser. Keep `_sync_counter` unchanged for
   `added`, `updated`, `removed` and `failed`.
2. Require `ignored` to be present and boolean for the pinned Keycloak 26
   contract. Reject missing, null, numeric, string and collection values;
   reject boolean/negative/non-integer counters.
3. Extend focused adapter tests for exact false, exact true, all malformed
   variants, HTTP/JSON/provider errors and counter regression without using a
   hard-coded success path as live evidence.

#### Batch 2 — V044 And Contract Compatibility

1. Add idempotent Flyway `V044` with
   `user_sync_ignored boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`; prove clean-database,
   upgrade/backfill and migration-rerun behavior while preserving historical
   rows.
2. Add the boolean field to SQLAlchemy/Pydantic/API serialization and frontend
   TypeScript types. Keep `users_ignored` integer in database and API,
   deprecated and always zero.
3. Add schema/API tests that distinguish the fields, reject type confusion
   and prove the four previous failed results are not rewritten.

#### Batch 3 — Worker Lifecycle And Safe Observability

1. For `ignored=false`, persist both compatibility values and proceed through
   existing group sync, snapshot and reconciliation code without duplicating
   side effects.
2. For `ignored=true`, persist boolean evidence, terminate provider/run with
   `keycloak_provider_sync_ignored`, and prove no group request, snapshot,
   reconciliation or last-success mutation occurs.
3. Preserve existing retries, outbox dispatch and terminal-state semantics.
   Structured logs and API errors must distinguish ignored from invalid
   response without exposing raw response, tokens or directory credentials.

#### Batch 4 — Images And Non-destructive Local Upgrade

1. Run focused application, migration and contract checks, then build new
   immutable versioned backend, worker and migration images. Verify the
   backend/worker application generation and image digests before deployment.
2. Update only the Docker Desktop local package/value image references needed
   for those images. Do not change Helm template behavior, LDAP/Keycloak
   configuration, role mappings, credentials, network policy, persistence or
   Production/UAT values.
3. Render and diff the Helm upgrade; require only expected workload/image and
   additive migration effects. Upgrade `nomosmart-local`, wait for migration
   completion and workload readiness, then compare all immutable exclusions.
4. Rollback procedure is Helm rollback to the prior app revision while V044
   remains additive. Never delete the new column, data, PVCs or Secrets.

#### Batch 5 — Real Sync Acceptance And Handoff

1. Through the existing NomoSmart API/outbox path, enqueue exactly one real
   identity sync for the existing Keycloak provider. Do not call reconciliation
   internals or fabricate database rows.
2. Require terminal success and provider evidence with
   `user_sync_ignored=false`, `users_ignored=0`, valid integer counters, group
   sync, snapshot and reconciliation completion.
3. Read back the live stores: Keycloak remains seven users/six groups;
   NomoSmart contains `user01` through `user05` and HR/IT/FIN/nomosmart-admin
   with exact group memberships and the two manager relationships.
4. Prove no new Keycloak/NomoSmart role mapping or permission exists, the five
   identities remain application-denied, four old failures remain unchanged,
   and every preserved resource fingerprint still matches.
5. Run the broader authorized harness suite and report coverage/security or
   unavailable-service gaps honestly; do not treat static/fake adapters as the
   real integration acceptance.

### Test Strategy

- Focused unit/contract tests cover strict integer and boolean parsing plus
  false/true lifecycle branches.
- Real PostgreSQL migration checks cover fresh, upgrade/backfill and rerun
  paths and exact preservation of history.
- Worker integration checks cover outbox ownership, stop/continue boundaries,
  persistence and API serialization.
- Gate 5 uses the existing live OpenLDAP, Keycloak and PostgreSQL services and
  the normal NomoSmart queue/worker path per `TEST-002`; mocks, fixture-created
  success rows and direct reconciliation calls do not satisfy acceptance.
- Deployment checks compare image generation, Helm render/revision, readiness,
  rollback safety and immutable resource identities.

### Deployment And Configuration Impact

- Application source changes are bounded to the Keycloak response domain,
  worker persistence/lifecycle, ORM/API/TypeScript contracts and tests.
- One additive `V044` database migration and new local backend/worker/migration
  image references are required.
- One new Helm revision and one real identity-sync run are expected after Gate
  4. No secret, endpoint, LDAP entry, Keycloak provider/mapper, role, permission,
  PVC, TLS/CA, Ingress or Production/UAT configuration change is in scope.

### Risks And Mitigations

- Python `bool` is an `int` subtype. Retain explicit bool rejection in integer
  parsing and use an exact boolean parser for `ignored`.
- Treating `ignored=true` as success can silently publish stale identity data.
  Use a stable terminal error and prove all downstream actions are absent.
- Removing `users_ignored` immediately can break clients. Keep it as zero for
  one compatibility window and add the new boolean without overloading types.
- Image drift can deploy mismatched API and worker contracts. Require the same
  application generation and verified digests.
- Helm rollback cannot safely remove an additive column after data exists.
  Leave V044 in place and roll back application images only.
- The worktree contains earlier CHG-262/264/265 changes. Preserve all unrelated
  user work and isolate CHG-266 review by exact files/hunks.
