## CHG-267 Localized Person Name Ordering And LDAP Mapper Correction

### Status And Gate Scope

- Gate 1 read-only diagnosis completed on 2026-08-20. The existing local
  Keycloak mapper is `cn -> firstName`, while `sn -> lastName`; the five target
  NomoSmart rows therefore contain duplicated surnames.
- Gate 2 completed when Peter confirmed
  `同意 CHG-267 Gate 2，採用上述建議`.
- Gate 3 specification, changelog, this plan, test design and traceability are
  complete.
- Gate 4 implementation approval: approved. Peter approved Gate 4 on
  2026-08-20 with
  `Peter approves CHG-267 Localized Person Name Ordering And LDAP Mapper Correction`.
  The bounded source/V045/images/non-destructive local deployment, single mapper
  reconciliation and two real sync operations are authorized subject to the
  action-time preflight.
- Requirements: specification section 10.24 and `PERSON-NAME-001..005`.

### Confirmed Understanding And Decisions

The local duplicate is not a Frontend-only string bug. Keycloak currently
stores full LDAP `cn` as `firstName` and the LDAP surname as `lastName`, while
NomoSmart persists only one already-formatted `display_name`. Correct
locale-aware ordering therefore requires both a source correction and a
structured application contract.

The approved design updates only the existing local first-name mapper from
`cn` to `givenName`, adds nullable `given_name` and `family_name` to NomoSmart,
keeps `display_name` for compatibility, and formats names at render time. zh is
family then given; en is given then family; both use one U+0020 separator. The
rule applies across current live person-name surfaces and updates immediately
on locale change. Historical free-text/evidence values are retained unchanged.

### Development Plan

#### Batch 0 — Governance And Action-time Baseline

1. Keep CHG-267 as the active change and map its five requirements across all
   governance artifacts before implementation.
2. After Gate 4, re-run a read-only preflight for exact `docker-desktop`, Helm
   revision/schema/images, Provider and every mapper ID/config, five duplicated
   target rows, seven Keycloak users/six groups, identity/role mappings, seven
   PVC/Secret/Ingress fingerprints, Redis HA and LDAP volume identities.
3. Fail closed on target, mapper ambiguity, source-field, release, schema or
   immutable-resource drift. Evidence must exclude credentials and raw tokens.

#### Batch 1 — V045 And Structured Sync Domain

1. Add V045 nullable `users.given_name` and `users.family_name`, update ORM and
   real migration acceptance for fresh, V044 upgrade, null backfill, rerun and
   non-destructive rollback compatibility.
2. Extend snapshot normalization/reconciliation to trim and persist independent
   first/last values and construct compatibility `display_name` exactly once.
   Cover two-part, multi-part, one-part, missing and invalid cases without
   splitting an existing full name heuristically.
3. Ensure retries and repeated syncs are idempotent and cannot append a surname
   repeatedly. Preserve managers, groups, roles and last-success semantics.

#### Batch 2 — Additive API And Shared Locale Formatter

1. Add nullable structured fields to `UserSummary`, `/auth/me`, Project member
   and live actor/person responses plus matching TypeScript types. Preserve all
   existing `display_name` fields.
2. Make `/auth/me` load the synchronized User name fields rather than using a
   stale OIDC `name` claim as its person-name source; authentication decisions
   and token validation remain unchanged.
3. Add one pure shared Frontend formatter using the current `useI18n().locale`,
   exact zh/en order, one-space joining and the specified fallback chain.

#### Batch 3 — UI Surface, Search And Accessibility Migration

1. Apply the formatter to AppShell/Header, System Management user rows/modals/
   actions, role member selection, Project member search/list and Approval live
   actor surfaces.
2. Keep person data structured in component state so locale switching rerenders
   mounted visible names, confirmation text and ARIA names without reload or
   refetch.
3. Search both orderings and individual parts plus existing display/email/
   employee/account identifiers. Keep Backend pagination/sort and historical
   snapshot strings stable.

#### Batch 4 — Bounded Local Mapper Reconciliation

1. Extend the existing local Keycloak reconciliation utility to require exactly
   one existing `firstName` mapper, preserve its ID/config except changing
   `ldap.attribute` from `cn` to `givenName`, and prove `sn -> lastName` plus
   every security/group/role mapper remains identical.
2. Make the operation exact-or-already-correct and idempotent; conflict or
   unexpected current value fails before mutation. Do not add an application
   runtime endpoint for provider editing.
3. Add metadata-only pre/post evidence and a safe rollback statement. The
   corrected mapper remains compatible with prior app images and is not
   destructively reverted during application rollback.

#### Batch 5 — Images, Local Upgrade And Live Acceptance

1. Run focused/backend/frontend/migration checks, then build one versioned
   CHG-267 backend/worker/migration/frontend generation. Change only required
   Docker Desktop local image tags; do not change Helm templates.
2. Render/diff and non-destructively upgrade `nomosmart-local`; wait for V045,
   migration/bootstrap and all workloads to become Ready, then compare every
   exclusion fingerprint.
3. Apply the approved mapper reconciliation, run exactly one Keycloak full user
   sync and exactly one NomoSmart people-and-groups sync through the normal
   UI/API/outbox/worker path.
4. Read back Keycloak and NomoSmart structured/canonical values for all five
   targets, then use the authenticated Browser to prove the exact zh/en names,
   immediate switching, search, Modal/action/ARIA parity and no duplicate.

### Test Strategy

- Pure domain tests cover normalization, canonical compatibility name,
  multi-part/one-part/missing values and idempotence without treating static or
  fake success as live acceptance.
- Real PostgreSQL tests cover V045 fresh/upgrade/null backfill/rerun and exact
  preservation of users, roles and CHG-266 history.
- API/component tests cover additive structured fields, DB-backed `/auth/me`,
  all shared formatter call sites, zh/en mounted switching, fallback, search and
  accessibility.
- Real Keycloak/OpenLDAP/PostgreSQL/queue/worker/Browser acceptance is mandatory
  under `TEST-002`; a fixture mapper or manually edited User row cannot satisfy
  the live cases.

### Deployment And Configuration Impact

- One additive V045 and one versioned local application generation are planned.
- The existing local first-name mapper config changes in place only after Gate
  4 and action-time preflight; Provider/mapper IDs and all other configs remain.
- No Helm template, LDAP entry, Secret, PVC, network, role, permission,
  Production or UAT change is planned.

### Risks And Mitigations

- Display-only patching would leave corrupt structured input. Correct the local
  mapper and persist structured values before formatting.
- Splitting arbitrary legacy full names is culturally unsafe. V045 backfills
  null and a real sync supplies first/last; no heuristic database split.
- OIDC tokens may retain an old `name` claim. `/auth/me` uses the synchronized
  User row for name display while retaining existing JWT security semantics.
- Formatting a name before storing component state prevents live locale change.
  Store structured values and format at render time.
- A broad mapper update could weaken federation. Require exact ID/config drift
  guards and change only `ldap.attribute` on the one approved local mapper.
- The worktree contains earlier CHG-262/264/265/266 changes. Preserve them and
  isolate CHG-267 review by exact files/hunks.

## CHG-268 OpenAI OCR And Batch Model Compatibility Repair

Gate 4 implementation approval: APPROVED by Peter on 2026-08-24.

### Status And Gate Scope

- Gate 1 completed on 2026-08-24 with real Docker Desktop database evidence,
  one no-document `/models` readiness call and bounded synthetic request
  contracts. No API Key, response body or document content was recorded.
- Gate 2 completed when Peter confirmed
  `同意 CHG-268 Gate 2，採用上述建議`.
- Gate 3 specification, changelog, this development plan, test design and
  traceability are complete.
- Gate 4 implementation approval is complete. Peter approved on 2026-08-24
  with `Peter approves CHG-268 OpenAI OCR And Batch Model Compatibility Repair`.
  Bounded Gate 5 execution is authorized subject to the action-time preflight.
- Requirements: specification section 10.25 and `OCR-COMPAT-001..005`.

### Confirmed Understanding And Decisions

The restored OCR credential is valid and `gpt-5.6-sol` is visible to the
configured account. The current failure is a request-contract bug: the OCR
adapter always adds `temperature=0.0`; the Provider returns HTTP 400 and the
same synthetic request succeeds when that field is omitted. This is not a PDF,
RustFS, authentication or Worker-OOM diagnosis.

A one-line OCR change alone would let the current run advance only to another
known incompatibility. Its downstream Chat Model `gpt-5.6-luna` receives the
legacy Chat Completions `max_tokens` payload and rejects it; an equivalent
Responses request succeeds. The local Chat/Judge configs must therefore select
the already-supported Responses mode explicitly. Model names will not be used
as capability heuristics.

The model editor also violates its retain-existing label by sending null
credential fields. The Backend validates against the old credential and then
clears it. CHG-268 will repair this tri-state contract in the same bounded
change so any post-repair edit cannot recreate the original missing-key failure.

### Development Plan

#### Batch 0 — Governance And Action-time Baseline

1. Keep CHG-268 as the active change and map all five requirements before
   implementation.
2. After Gate 4, capture exact `docker-desktop`, Helm revision/schema/images,
   Backend/Worker readiness, four model IDs/config versions/configured flags,
   safe config excluding credentials, target Pipeline/step status/retry count,
   seven PVCs, protected Secrets/Ingress UIDs, allowlists, Redis HA and current
   external-role mapping state.
3. Fail closed on context/release/model/run/resource drift. Never read or print
   secret/encrypted values or document content in evidence.

#### Batch 1 — OCR Responses Payload And Safe Provider Evidence

1. Refactor `_openai_ocr_payload` so the base request contains model, input and
   `max_output_tokens`; add `temperature` only when explicitly present in model
   config. Preserve prompt, file/image encoding, timeout and snapshot behavior.
2. Keep explicit incompatible sampling settings fail-closed rather than
   silently removing them. Do not infer capabilities from `gpt-*` names.
3. Reduce Provider failure details to an allowlist of status/type/code/param and
   persist them in existing usage metadata/log evidence without raw messages,
   bodies, headers, keys, token or document content. No database migration is
   expected.

#### Batch 2 — Credential Tri-state And Early OCR Readiness

1. Add an explicit clear-credential request signal, mutually exclusive with a
   new API key or Secret reference. Omitted fields preserve the current value;
   a non-empty value atomically replaces it.
2. Calculate the final credential state before provider validation or writes.
   Reject active remote models without a credential and reject ambiguous
   changes without partial mutation or config-version drift.
3. Update the model form so a blank password field is omitted during edit,
   current Secret references remain unchanged, and clear requires a dedicated
   confirmation. Add Traditional Chinese and English text for any new control
   or error.
4. Reject creation/start of new remote-OCR work before a half-created Pipeline
   when the selected model is not credential-configured. Existing jobs retain
   their normal runtime revalidation.

#### Batch 3 — Explicit OpenAI Chat/Judge API Mode

1. Validate `config.api_mode` as `responses` or `chat_completions` for OpenAI
   Chat/Judge models. Expose the provider-specific mode in the Frontend; default
   new OpenAI Chat/Judge forms to Responses while preserving existing models
   whose mode is absent.
2. Keep Responses payload behavior: `max_output_tokens`, and sampling fields
   only when explicitly configured. Do not silently change external or legacy
   Chat Completions models.
3. After deployment and exact read-back, update only Docker Desktop models
   `nomosmart-chat` and `nomosmart-judge` to `api_mode=responses`. Preserve IDs,
   endpoint, credential identity/configured state, pricing, Chat/Embedding
   pairing, active/default flags and every other config field.

#### Batch 4 — Tests, Images And Non-destructive Upgrade

1. Add pure payload, real database/API and Frontend component/contract tests
   for omission-by-default, explicit value, credential preserve/replace/clear,
   no-partial-write, API mode and redaction.
2. Run focused checks, broader Backend/Frontend suites, coverage evidence,
   security/config checks and Docker/Helm render/lint checks. Do not reduce
   thresholds or convert synthetic tests into live success claims.
3. Build versioned CHG-268 Backend/Worker and Frontend images. Change only the
   required Docker Desktop image references and perform a non-destructive Helm
   upgrade; no migration image/schema or Helm-template behavior change.

#### Batch 5 — Live Provider And Existing-Pipeline Acceptance

1. Through the application-supported connection/probe boundary, verify OCR,
   Chat and Judge configured credentials/model/mode without exposing keys. A
   no-document synthetic request is diagnostic evidence, not PDF acceptance.
2. Invoke the normal retry API/UI exactly once for failed `ocr_extract` on run
   `5768d46c-d748-43f9-83ac-840d6be8d2c6`. Do not mutate the database directly,
   upload a replacement or delete either failed history.
3. Wait for the same run to reach `submission_ready`. Read back all required
   steps, artifacts, model/usage evidence and staging state; Browser acceptance
   must show completed batch progress and the resulting extraction detail.
4. Compare every exclusion fingerprint. If any later real dependency fails,
   stop and report its exact safe evidence rather than broadening scope or
   marking the batch successful.

### Test Strategy

- Payload tests are pure contract assertions and never fake Provider success.
- Credential/API tests use a real PostgreSQL test database and transactions;
  they verify ciphertext/reference identity by digest/boolean only and never
  print credential material.
- Frontend component tests prove edit omission, explicit clear confirmation,
  API-mode selection and zh/en messages.
- `TEST-002` acceptance uses the configured real OpenAI endpoints, real
  PostgreSQL/RustFS/Redis/Worker/OpenSearch and the existing PDF Pipeline.
  Synthetic calls cannot satisfy the document-flow case.
- Existing full-suite and 80% Backend/Frontend release gates remain mandatory;
  a pre-existing global coverage gap must be reported, not relaxed.

### Deployment And Configuration Impact

- No Flyway migration is planned.
- Versioned Backend/Worker and Frontend images plus a Docker Desktop values-only
  upgrade are planned; Helm templates and migration image remain unchanged.
- Two local DB model config versions will increment only for explicit
  `api_mode=responses`. No credential value/reference rotation is planned.
- One existing failed Pipeline step will be retried once after deployment.
- Tesseract security context, Kubernetes Secrets/PVCs, identity/authorization,
  networking and Production/UAT are excluded.

### Risks And Mitigations

- Omitting an operator-set sampling value would hide configuration errors. Omit
  only absent values; preserve explicit values and fail visibly if unsupported.
- Capability inference by model-name prefix will age poorly. Use explicit API
  mode and Provider response contracts.
- Empty form values can erase secrets. Use omitted/replace/explicit-clear states
  end-to-end and validate final state before writes.
- A successful `/models` check does not prove PDF execution. Require the real
  existing Pipeline to complete through `submission_ready`.
- Enabling Bubblewrap by privilege escalation would violate the approved
  boundary. Leave Tesseract remediation to a separate specification.
- Retrying more than once could add cost and obscure evidence. Bind acceptance
  to the exact run/step and one approved action after preflight.

The current first table column renders the NomoSmart configuration name from
`AIModel.name` under `Model`. The fourth column renders `AIModel.endpoint` under

`AIModel.config.model_name`. To avoid two columns named Model, the first header
will become `Name`/`名稱`; the fourth will become `Model`/`模型` and render only a
trimmed non-empty `config.model_name`, otherwise `—`.

the model popup and available to runtime adapters. No API, database, credential,
model config, pagination, sorting, action, permission or Backend behavior is
changed.

## CHG-270 Knowledge Graph Chunk Content Identity And Inspector Detail

Gate 4 implementation approval: APPROVED by Peter on 2026-08-25.

### Status And Gate Scope

- Gate 1 completed on 2026-08-25 through read-only specification, Frontend,
  Backend, PostgreSQL and current Docker Desktop runtime inspection.
- Gate 2 completed when Peter confirmed
  `同意 CHG-270 Gate 2，採用上述建議`.
- Gate 3 specification section 10.27, changelog, this plan, test design and
  traceability are synchronized.
- Gate 4 is complete. Peter approved on 2026-08-25 with
  `Peter approves CHG-270 Knowledge Graph Chunk Content Identity And Inspector Detail`.
  Bounded Gate 5 execution is authorized subject to action-time preflight.
- Requirements: `GRAPH-CHUNK-001..005`.

### Confirmed Understanding

Both graph surfaces currently identify Chunk nodes from persisted
`Chunk.title`, which extraction generates as the document title plus its
one-based `chunk_index`. The Document surface strips the suffix and therefore
shows only the document title; the Project surface uses the Neo4j title label
and prefixes a local array position. Neither inspector receives full content.

Both surfaces will instead use one shared content-preview formatter: normalize
whitespace only for preview, take exactly 24 Unicode extended grapheme clusters
without splitting user-perceived characters, and append `…` only when more
content remains. The inspector will display canonical `#<chunk_index>` in its
own Number field and original untruncated content in a safe scroll region. The
stored title/content and all graph topology remain unchanged.

The Project graph requires an additive API response change. After existing
Project and active-version authorization has selected the visible graph, the
Backend will batch-hydrate only those Chunk IDs from PostgreSQL. It will not
copy full content into Neo4j or expose it through logs/evidence. Document graph
already has authorized content and needs only typed Frontend plumbing.

### Development Plan

#### Batch 0 — Action-time Baseline And Safety Boundary

1. Confirm exact `docker-desktop` context, `nomosmart-local` release/revision,
   schema, Backend/Worker/Frontend/migration images and Ready state.
2. Capture safe counts and digests for the current active graph: Project,
   authorized active-version IDs, visible Chunk IDs/indexes, content lengths and
   hashes, Neo4j node/edge counts and current persisted-title pattern. Do not
   print chunk content, credentials, Endpoint or Secret values.
3. Capture protected PVC, Secret/TLS, Ingress/allowlist, Redis, LDAP, model,
   Pipeline and graph fingerprints. Fail closed on context, authorization,
   release or operator-state drift.

#### Batch 1 — Shared Preview And Inspector Contract

1. Add a narrow shared Frontend chunk presenter that accepts original content
   and canonical index. Use Unicode grapheme segmentation, normalized preview
   whitespace, the exact 24-grapheme/ellipsis rule and localized empty-content
   fallback from `GRAPH-CHUNK-001`.
2. Extend `GraphExplorerNode` with explicit canonical chunk index and full
   content fields instead of hiding these values in title/meta strings.
3. For selected Chunk nodes, render dedicated localized Number and Full content
   fields. Preserve original newlines as React-escaped plain text, wrap long
   tokens and use a bounded keyboard-accessible scroll region. Keep technical
   metadata, neighbors, edge detail and non-Chunk inspectors unchanged.
4. Ensure node cards, edge labels, neighbor chips and accessibility summaries
   use only the bounded preview/metadata and never duplicate full content.

#### Batch 2 — Document Knowledge Graph Plumbing

1. Extend `DocumentGraphChunk` with required `content` and canonical
   `chunkIndex` values and map them from the already-authorized Knowledge Detail
   `displayChunks` payload.
2. Remove document-title and local `index + 1` presentation paths for Chunk
   nodes. Use the shared presenter for node title and explicit inspector fields.
3. Preserve source/tag metadata, filtering, selection, semantic zoom, graph
   counts and the Knowledge Detail API contract; add no request or datastore
   mutation.

#### Batch 3 — Formal Project Graph Authorized Hydration

1. Refactor graph response assembly so graph, neighbors and paths all pass the
   final visible node set and authorized active-version scope to one bounded
   PostgreSQL batch-hydration helper.
2. Query only Chunk IDs in that visible set and additionally constrain by
   current Project ID, active authorized document-version IDs and active-row
   semantics. Add `content` and canonical `chunk_index` only to matching
   authorized Chunk metadata; omit content on any mismatch without an existence
   oracle or per-node query.
3. Map formal Project Chunk nodes to the same Frontend presenter and inspector
   fields. Treat missing authorized content as the localized unavailable state,
   never as a reason to use Neo4j/document title.
4. Preserve Neo4j write/sync contracts, stored properties, node/edge IDs,
   topology, counts, truncation, limit semantics and non-Chunk response fields.

#### Batch 4 — Focused, Integration And Regression Verification

1. Add focused Frontend tests for whitespace normalization, exact grapheme
   boundary/ellipsis, emoji and combining sequences, empty fallback, canonical
   number stability, safe full-content rendering, i18n and no title/index
   duplication.
2. Add real configured Backend integration cases proving one batch query,
   Project/active-version binding, graph/neighbors/paths parity and no content
   for unauthorized, mismatched, hidden or truncated nodes. Do not satisfy
   `TEST-002` with mocks, fixtures or hard-coded success adapters.
3. Run existing graph API/component regressions, Backend syntax/tests, Frontend
   lint/build/tests and coverage evidence. Do not lower the 80% release gate;
   report any existing repository-wide gap unchanged.
4. Record equality using IDs, canonical index, length and SHA-256 only. Test and
   application output must not print live full chunk content.

#### Batch 5 — Bounded Docker Desktop Delivery And Live Acceptance

1. Build versioned `0.1.0-chg270` Backend/Worker and Frontend images. Keep the
   CHG-267 migration image and schema `045`; render/lint the existing chart and
   perform a non-destructive reuse-values upgrade only after preflight passes.
2. Wait for all workloads and hooks to become Ready/complete, then compare every
   protected image/resource/data fingerprint and graph count with the baseline.
3. Through the real authenticated UI, verify one authorized live Chunk on both
   Document and Project graph surfaces in Traditional Chinese and English.
   Compare preview/index/full-content equality by safe digest/length and verify
   scroll/newline behavior without copying full content into evidence.
4. Exercise an authorized graph response and a denied/mismatched scope response
   to prove content remains bounded by `GRAPH-008`; do not mutate memberships or
   manufacture unauthorized live data merely for acceptance.

### Test Strategy

- Pure shared-formatting and React rendering cases use deterministic Unicode and
  markup-shaped inputs to prove the presentation contract without claiming live
  integration success.
- Backend behavior tests run against real configured PostgreSQL/Neo4j and the
  real authorization path. SQL statement observation may prove bounded query
  count, but no mock repository/graph result can satisfy authorization or
  hydration acceptance.
- Existing Document/Project graph tests protect node/edge counts, search,
  filters, semantic zoom, details and truncation behavior.
- `TEST-002` live acceptance uses the current authenticated Document and Project
  graph plus their live authorized API/datastore values. Evidence is content-
  minimizing and records only digest, length and equality, not source text.

### Deployment And Rollback

- No database or Neo4j migration, extraction rerun, graph resync, OpenSearch
  re-index, content/title rewrite or persistent-resource recreation is planned.
- Backend/Worker and Frontend images advance together because formal Project
  graph response metadata and UI consumption are coupled. Beat may use the same
  Backend repository image as dictated by existing Helm values but receives no
  new behavior or configuration.
- Rollback restores prior CHG-268 Backend/Worker and CHG-269 Frontend image tags
  through Helm. The additive response metadata disappears safely; schema 045,
  chunks, Neo4j, PVCs and all other persistent state stay untouched.

### Risks And Mitigations

- Full Chunk content is more sensitive than a title. Hydrate only after existing
  visibility selection, bind every SQL row to Project and active version, avoid
  N+1, render escaped plain text and prohibit content in evidence/log surfaces.
- JavaScript string slicing can split grapheme clusters. Centralize standards-
  based grapheme segmentation and test CJK, combining marks, emoji modifiers
  and zero-width-joiner sequences at the 24th boundary.
- Project graph Neo4j data may lag PostgreSQL. Treat PostgreSQL as content
  authority only for already-authorized visible Chunk IDs; mismatch omits
  content and never broadens graph topology or falls back to a misleading title.
- Graph sorting/truncation can make array indexes unstable. Carry the persisted
  one-based `chunk_index` end-to-end and never calculate the displayed number
  from UI order.

```bash
./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor
./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace
./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor
./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved
./HARNESS/harness.sh test:plan
node --test frontend/tests/chg270KnowledgeGraphChunkDetail.test.mjs
./HARNESS/harness.sh backend:syntax
./HARNESS/harness.sh test:backend
./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:lint
./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:build
./HARNESS/harness.sh test:frontend
./HARNESS/harness.sh test:e2e
./HARNESS/harness.sh coverage:check
./HARNESS/harness.sh helm:lint
./HARNESS/harness.sh deploy:config-policy
git diff --check
```

Gate 5 completed on 2026-08-25 after a passing action-time preflight. The

## CHG-271 Local Backend OIDC Ingress Alignment

Gate 4 implementation approval: APPROVED by Peter on 2026-08-25.

### Status And Gate Scope

- Gate 1 completed on 2026-08-25 through read-only repository, runtime listener,
  phpLDAPadmin container and real strict-TLS OIDC discovery inspection.
- Gate 2 completed when Peter replied `OK` after confirming phpLDAPadmin need not
  move and accepting the existing HTTPS Keycloak Ingress as the host Backend
  endpoint.
- Gate 3 specification section 10.28, changelog, this plan, test design and
  traceability are synchronized.
- Gate 4 is complete. Peter approved on 2026-08-25 with
  `Peter approves CHG-271 Local Backend OIDC Ingress Alignment`. Bounded Gate 5
  execution is authorized subject to action-time preflight.
- Requirements: `LOCAL-OIDC-001..004`.

### Confirmed Understanding

phpLDAPadmin and Keycloak do not have a real listener conflict. phpLDAPadmin is
healthy on loopback port 8080, while the Docker Desktop Keycloak realm is already
available through `https://nomosmart.local:443/identity`. The failure occurs
because the ignored host Backend `.env` and its example still route OIDC and
Keycloak Admin calls to phpLDAPadmin. Real discovery returned the exact issuer
`https://nomosmart.local/identity/realms/nomosmart` with no TLS bypass.

The correction will preserve phpLDAPadmin on port 8080 and update only the host
Backend's non-sensitive issuer/Admin URLs. It will also remove the live
prerequisite's hard-coded OIDC port 8080 assumption and require real exact-
issuer discovery. Internal Docker/Helm `keycloak:8080` values are separate
container-network endpoints and remain unchanged.

### Development Plan

#### Batch 0 — Redacted Action-time Preflight

1. Confirm Docker context, healthy `nomosmart-phpldapadmin`, exact loopback
   `127.0.0.1:8080 -> 8080` binding and absence of a configured 8081 listener.
2. Confirm `https://nomosmart.local/identity/realms/nomosmart/.well-known/openid-configuration`
   passes strict TLS and returns the exact configured issuer. Record only public
   endpoints, status and certificate fingerprint.
3. Capture hashes/metadata for the ignored `.env`, phpLDAPadmin/OpenLDAP
   containers and volumes, Helm release revision/images, Namespace, protected
   Secrets/PVCs and realm/client metadata. Never print credential values; fail
   closed on context, certificate or resource drift.

#### Batch 1 — Safe Example And Live-prerequisite Contract

1. Change only `OIDC_ISSUER_URL` and `KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_API_URL` in
   `backend/.env.example` to the canonical HTTPS Ingress values. Preserve empty
   discovery/JWKS overrides so application derivation remains authoritative.
2. Refine the URL port helper used by live prerequisites: explicit port wins;
   otherwise HTTPS resolves to 443 and HTTP to 80. Remove the OIDC-specific 8080
   fallback without changing PostgreSQL, Backend, OpenSearch, Neo4j, Redis or S3
   defaults.
3. Add a strict live discovery check that validates HTTP success, JSON shape and
   exact issuer equality. It must reject phpLDAPadmin HTML, issuer mismatch,
   redirect substitution and TLS failure.
4. Add focused tests for HTTPS/HTTP/explicit-port parsing and the static safe-
   example/no-phpLDAPadmin-OIDC contract. Do not use a mock response as passing
   live discovery evidence.

#### Batch 2 — Ignored Local Runtime Configuration

1. Patch only the two approved URL lines in ignored `backend/.env`; preserve all
   credential and unrelated lines exactly. Verify a redacted before/after
   comparison names changed keys without printing their neighboring values.
2. Use the existing trusted `nomosmart.local` CA. If the Backend Python runtime
   does not inherit macOS trust, resolve the exact matching owner-only active
   edge CA and set a Git-ignored standard CA bundle variable; never disable TLS
   or export/import private material.
3. Do not modify Backend application defaults, Frontend configuration, root
   Compose, LDAP Compose, Helm values/templates, Kubernetes Secrets or Keycloak
   realm/client configuration.

#### Batch 3 — Real Verification And Preservation

1. Run strict curl and Backend `.venv` Python checks for discovery and JWKS,
   requiring exact issuer and valid TLS/hostname verification. Evidence excludes
   tokens and credentials.
2. Run focused CHG-271 tests, Backend syntax and the broad Backend harness. Prove
   it no longer fails by reaching phpLDAPadmin; report any later independent
   live-service/test failure without changing TEST-002 or expected behavior.
3. Recheck phpLDAPadmin health/loopback binding, no 8081 publication, OpenLDAP
   container/volume identity and all Kubernetes protected fingerprints. No
   restart, image build, Helm upgrade or data mutation is permitted.
4. Run governance, traceability and diff hygiene checks and record the exact
   Gate 5 result in all five governance artifacts.

### Test Strategy

- Pure URL parsing tests cover implicit HTTPS 443, implicit HTTP 80, explicit
  nonstandard ports, missing hosts and canonical path preservation.
- A static configuration contract proves safe examples contain no credential
  and cannot route host OIDC/Admin calls to phpLDAPadmin.
- TEST-002 live evidence uses the real Docker Desktop Ingress, certificate,
  discovery/JWKS endpoints and configured Backend client. Static inspection or
  mocked HTTP success cannot substitute for this acceptance.
- Broad-suite success is not assumed. CHG-271 passes endpoint routing when the
  former phpLDAPadmin 404/non-OIDC failure is eliminated; unrelated service or
  test gaps remain separately visible.

### Deployment, Security And Rollback

- This change has no application/container deployment. The only runtime change
  is two non-sensitive lines in ignored `backend/.env`, plus an owner-only CA
  bundle path only if strict Python verification requires it.
- Rollback restores those two ignored URL values and the safe example/test code.
  phpLDAPadmin, OpenLDAP and Kubernetes require no rollback because they are not
  changed.
- URL diagnostics must use an allowlist and must never print request bodies,
  Authorization headers, client secrets, tokens, cookies or complete environment
  files. TLS bypass is prohibited even for local development.

## CHG-273 Canonical Markdown Source And Chunk Alignment

Gate 4 implementation approval: APPROVED by Peter on 2026-08-26.
Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-08-26 with
`Peter approves CHG-273 Canonical Markdown Source And Chunk Alignment`.

### Status And Confirmed Understanding

- Gate 2 confirmation: complete. Peter confirmed the understanding on
  2026-08-26 with `同意 CHG-273 Gate 2，採用上述建議`.
- Gate 1 read-only diagnosis completed on 2026-08-26. The current local PDF's
  completed `generate_markdown` artifact and `split_paragraphs` reconstruction
  are both 4,021 characters and digest-equal. `document_versions.chunk_strategy`
  has no `markdown_text`, so both detail APIs currently fall back to a 5,143-
  character active-Chunk join with a different digest.
- Automatic Chunk creation injects a 46-character synthetic Markdown heading
  around the observed early chunks. Frontend blank-line splitting then assigns
  these synthetic headings and contents separate `paragraph-N` IDs, shifting
  Chunk #2 to Chunk #1 content. The Markdown pane uses `SafeMarkdown`, so it
  renders syntax and inherits dark heading/strong colors on the dark viewer.
- The live version contains 26 active Chunks and 25 distinct anchors. Twenty-
  four active ranges match canonical-global offsets exactly; the two manually
  created `paragraph-3` Chunks match anchor-local offsets exactly. The persisted
  field does not declare which basis applies. Knowledge Detail also selects the
  first matching anchor only, while Approval already has a limited multi-match
  helper.
- Peter completed Gate 2 on 2026-08-26 with
  `同意 CHG-273 Gate 2，採用上述建議`, confirming canonical artifact identity,
  literal black/white Markdown source, explicit Unicode dual-coordinate
  mapping, shared Approval parity and non-destructive compatibility for current
  data.
- Gate 3 synchronized the specification, changelog, this plan, test design and
  traceability. Gate 4 now authorizes scoped implementation and feature tests;
  image build and live Helm action remain subject to the bounded deployment and
  separate action-time Job approval below.

### Scope And Architecture

1. Canonical artifact resolution:
   - Add one shared Backend resolver used by Knowledge Detail and Approval
     Evidence. It receives the authorized exact `DocumentVersion`, resolves the
     latest completed `generate_markdown` step for that same version and verifies
     the version-scoped artifact reference/payload before returning its Markdown.
   - Preserve the artifact string exactly; do not call `.strip()`, render it,
     inject a title/index or join Chunks. A missing/running/failed/invalid/stale
     artifact returns `markdown_artifact_status` plus the specified allowlisted
     `markdown_artifact_reason_code` and `markdown_text=null`. `available` is the
     only status with non-null exact Markdown.
   - Approval resolution remains bound to the task's submitted version and must
     never switch to a document's latest version.

2. Exact source-mapping normalization:
   - Add a shared pure normalizer over the canonical Markdown, its stable
     paragraph/layout anchors and each persisted mapping. Offsets use Unicode
     code points and half-open ranges.
   - A resolved response mapping exposes `source_anchor`,
     `offset_unit=unicode_code_point`, canonical-global
     `markdown_start_offset`/`markdown_end_offset`, anchor-local
     `anchor_start_offset`/`anchor_end_offset`, explicit `offset_scope` for the
     retained legacy pair and `mapping_status`.
   - Compatibility order is deterministic: validate the stored pair as an
     exact canonical-global range; if that fails, validate it as an exact range
     within the exact anchor. Accept only full content equality and a unique
     coordinate result. Missing, ambiguous, overlapping-invalid or out-of-bounds
     data becomes `unresolved`; no fuzzy search or first-hit fallback is allowed.
   - Update future automatic Chunk creation to persist both coordinate systems
     and explicit scope/unit. Update manual Chunk creation/splitting to translate
     the selected view range to both coordinates inside the transaction and
     reject a range that cannot round-trip exactly. Preserve append-only lineage.

3. Shared literal-source presenter:
   - Introduce one reusable Frontend raw Markdown source component for Knowledge
     Detail and Approval Evidence. It renders source only as escaped text nodes
     inside semantic `pre/code`; concatenated DOM `textContent` must remain
     exactly equal to the API source despite range wrappers.
   - Replace the Markdown pane's `SafeMarkdown`/paragraph reconstruction and
     synthetic block IDs. Keep `SafeMarkdown` for Chunk previews and rendered
     `.md` Original mode, where it remains appropriate.
   - Give the raw source an explicit near-black/black background, white
     monospace text, visible focus state and green range highlight whose text
     remains white. Preserve whitespace, wrapping/scroll behavior, keyboard
     use, selection/copy and narrow-layout containment.

4. Bidirectional interaction:
   - Build ordered source segments from resolved canonical ranges. Right-side
     Chunk selection scrolls to and highlights only that Chunk's segment(s).
     Clicking or keyboard-activating a left segment selects and scrolls to all
     exactly overlapping Chunks, including same-anchor siblings.
   - Original layout uses the resolved anchor-local range; Markdown uses the
     canonical-global range. Switching views preserves Chunk IDs and re-resolves
     the active range without relying on generated `paragraph-N` positions.
   - Replace Knowledge Detail's first-match `find` behavior with shared
     many-to-many selection logic. Approval keeps read-only behavior but uses the
     same mapping/presenter semantics.
   - Manual Markdown selection computes Unicode code-point offsets from the
     canonical source root rather than from a rendered Markdown subtree.
   - New manual requests send explicit `offset_unit` and `offset_scope` matching
     `view_mode`; the Backend accepts omitted fields only through the specified
     legacy inference and rejects every inconsistent or non-round-tripping pair
     with `422 chunk_source_mapping_invalid` before mutation.

### Expected Implementation Areas

- Backend: a shared version-scoped artifact/mapping domain helper,
  `backend/app/api/schemas.py`, Knowledge Detail and Approval routes, automatic
  extraction mapping creation, and manual Chunk range validation/splitting.
- Frontend: a shared raw-source component and mapping utilities, Knowledge
  Detail, `ApprovalEvidenceViewer`, typed API contracts and the narrowly scoped
  Markdown/source-range CSS.
- Tests: focused Backend resolver/mapping/manual-edit contracts, Frontend pure
  mapping and component tests, existing live API contracts, Approval parity,
  security/i18n/responsive checks and TEST-002 live acceptance.
- Governance: update the CHG-273 result only after commands and live evidence
  actually complete. Existing unrelated dirty-worktree changes remain preserved.

### Data, API And Compatibility Impact

- API changes are additive within each Chunk's source mapping plus exact
  `markdown_artifact_status`/`markdown_artifact_reason_code` fields. Existing
  identity, content, title, tag, lineage and
  workflow fields remain compatible. No unscoped artifact endpoint is added.
- No database schema migration is planned. Existing JSONB mapping rows are not
  rewritten in bulk; they are normalized on authorized read. Only future normal
  extraction/manual-edit mutations write the explicit fields.
- The current 26 active Chunks, 25 anchors, two manual `paragraph-3` ranges,
  canonical artifact, pipeline history, OpenSearch/Neo4j state and review
  evidence are immutable during local acceptance. No retry, OCR, re-extraction,
  re-index, graph sync, submission, approval or publication is needed.
- If implementation reveals that an exact existing mapping cannot be resolved,
  stop and report it as `unresolved`; do not repair persistent data outside a
  separately specified and approved migration.

### Security, Accessibility And Observability

- Raw Markdown is emitted only through React text nodes. HTML-like text, script,
  links and image syntax must never execute or cause network loading in raw mode.
- Existing Project/Document/version authorization applies before artifact or
  mapping resolution. Error/status output contains stable codes and counts only,
  never artifact content, credentials, cookies or tokens.
- Range wrappers remain keyboard operable and expose selected/current state
  without color-only meaning. The black/white surface must retain readable
  contrast in both locales and at narrow widths.
- Logs and acceptance evidence may record version/run/step IDs, status, counts,
  lengths and cryptographic digests, but not document text.

1. Add focused failing characterization tests for canonical artifact precedence,
   current fallback rejection, exact global/local range normalization and raw
   source behavior.
2. Implement the shared Backend resolver and typed availability/mapping response;
   wire both Knowledge Detail and exact submitted-version Approval Evidence.
3. Correct automatic and manual mapping production/validation without rewriting
   current data or breaking append-only lineage.
4. Implement the shared Frontend raw-source/range component and update both
   surfaces, manual selection, many-to-many navigation and styles.
5. Run focused Backend/Frontend tests, then syntax/lint/build, complete Backend/
   Frontend/E2E suites, coverage and governance/deployment static checks. Do not
   weaken thresholds or substitute fixture evidence for live acceptance.

   after; record gaps exactly and keep rollback image-only.

### Risks And Controls

- Risk: resolving a stale or cross-version pipeline step. Control: exact
  `document_version_id`, completed status and artifact-ref validation; otherwise
  unavailable.
- Risk: Python/JavaScript offset drift for emoji or supplementary characters.
  Control: one Unicode-code-point, half-open contract and round-trip tests on
  both sides.
- Risk: range wrappers alter source/copy or execute Markdown HTML. Control:
  escaped text-only segmented rendering and exact `textContent`/inertness tests.
- Risk: overlapping or legacy mapping silently selects the wrong Chunk. Control:
  exact equality, deterministic dual-basis validation, explicit unresolved state
  and no fuzzy/first-hit fallback.
- Risk: a local Helm upgrade runs data-adjacent retained Jobs. Control: exact
  server-side dry run, separate action-time approval, atomic upgrade and schema/
  data/resource pre/post fingerprints.

- `query_project_chat()` adds the new ChatRecord but does not flush it before
  passing only `record.id` to `record_model_usage()`. That helper immediately
  flushes its new usage child; without an ORM object relationship, the current
  unit of work emitted the child INSERT before the parent.
- CSV validation answer persistence has the same sequence. Public API JSON/SSE
  already flushes its request-log parent in `_create_public_log()` and is a
  regression-only scope.
- Gate 2 confirmation: complete. Peter confirmed the understanding on
  2026-08-26 with
  `同意 CHG-274 Gate 2，採用上述建議`, confirming both synchronous Chat scopes
  and CSV validation, no automatic replay, real PostgreSQL evidence and the
  non-schema/non-Frontend boundary.

### Scope And Implementation Approach

1. Parent-first persistence:
   - After constructing and adding a success ChatRecord in
     `query_project_chat()`, explicitly flush that parent before calling
     `record_model_usage()` with its ID.
   - Apply the identical ordering in validation answer persistence before
     linking the validation item or recording `validation_answer` usage.
   - Keep parent, child, answer/citations and surrounding state within the same
     transaction; do not insert a commit between them.

2. Minimal shared-contract hardening:
   - Prefer an explicit, reviewable parent flush at the two affected call sites
     over removing the generic usage helper's flush or changing every caller.
     Other callers rely on immediate usage validation and generally reference
     parents that are already persistent.
   - Add a narrowly named helper only if it reduces duplication without hiding
     transaction ownership. Do not add schema, deferred constraints or a broad
     ORM relationship rewrite for this bounded repair.

3. Tests:
   - Add source/transaction contract coverage that both affected ChatRecord
     paths flush their parent before success usage creation.
   - Use a real PostgreSQL FK test to persist a minimal parent/child pair through
     the production helper, assert exact linkage and rollback cleanup, without
     stubs or disabled constraints.
   - Exercise real Document Chat/Project Chat and validation-answer paths where
     current live prerequisites permit. Confirm Public API retains its existing
     parent-first behavior.
   - Run focused Backend tests, Backend syntax, broad Backend/coverage and all
     governance/deployment checks. Existing independent environment or coverage
     failures remain explicit and thresholds remain unchanged.

4. Local delivery and acceptance:
   - Build one new local Backend image only after Gate 4. The chart's shared
     Backend tag necessarily rolls Backend, Worker and Beat and supplies the
     revision-scoped bootstrap Job; Frontend and Migration remain unchanged.
   - Lint/render/server-dry-run revision 19, enumerate exact image and retained
     migration/bootstrap Jobs, capture revision-18/schema/PVC/Secret/Ingress/
     identity/LDAP/Keycloak/model/index/data baselines, then request separate
     exact action approval before Helm write or a billable live query.
   - After that approval, run one content-minimized fresh conversation. Assert
     HTTP success, non-empty backend citations, persisted history reload, one
     new ChatRecord and exactly one linked success usage event. Do not replay or
     backfill the failed 01:43 request.

No Frontend, SQL migration, Helm template or runtime configuration source change

### Risks And Rollback

- A parent flush can expose a later constraint error earlier inside the same
  transaction, but cannot make the row durable without commit. Tests must prove
  later failure still rolls both parent and child back.
- Re-running a real question invokes the provider again and may incur cost;
  therefore live acceptance is separately approved and creates a fresh record
  rather than pretending to recover the rolled-back request.
- Rollback is image-only to revision 18 Backend/Worker/Beat values. No schema,
  ChatRecord, usage-ledger or index rollback operation is required.

## CHG-275 Chat Citation Identity, Turn Count And Loading Feedback

Gate 4 implementation approval: APPROVED by Peter on 2026-08-26.
Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-08-26 with
`Peter approves CHG-275 Chat Citation Identity, Turn Count And Loading Feedback`.

Gate 1 read-only diagnosis and Peter's Gate 2 confirmation completed on
2026-08-26 with `同意 CHG-275 Gate 2，採用上述建議`. This plan covers
`CHAT-CITE-001..003`, `CHAT-TURN-001` and `CHAT-WAIT-001`. Peter approved Gate 4
repository implementation and feature tests on 2026-08-26 with
`Peter approves CHG-275 Chat Citation Identity, Turn Count And Loading Feedback`.
The later digest-bound revision-20 image build and Helm action was separately
approved and completed as recorded below. Provider queries and unrelated
persistent runtime-data mutations remain unauthorized.

### Confirmed Understanding And Decisions

- Citation card identity is the cited Chunk, not its parent document. The title
  uses the first 24 Unicode grapheme clusters of the authorized citation excerpt,
  after the same whitespace normalization used by Knowledge Graph, and appends
  `…` only when content is longer. Empty content uses the localized Chunk
  fallback; the stale persisted document-title suffix is never parsed.
- Answer markers such as `[1]`, `[3]` and `[5]` are source ordinals within the
  returned citation array. Each card displays the same `[1]..[N]` ordinal and a
  separate canonical `切片 #N` / `Chunk #N` label. Selecting a marker opens or
  focuses exactly its matching citation card.
- The Backend citation contract gains an additive nullable `chunk_index`.
  Newly retrieved citations populate it from the authoritative Chunk row.
  Authorized legacy history or review evidence that lacks it may be hydrated by
  one bounded batch query after scope authorization; existing ChatRecord JSON is
  not rewritten and no per-card query is permitted.
- A new answer containing a numeric marker outside `1..N` is an invalid provider
  response. It fails closed with a stable safe error, creates no normal ChatRecord,
  records the one already-consumed provider usage exactly once and never retries
  the provider automatically. Existing no-marker answers remain valid. A legacy
  invalid marker stays non-interactive and displays a localized mismatch state.
- One persisted question/answer ChatRecord is one conversation turn. Pending,
  failed and unpersisted entries do not increment history. Traditional Chinese
  displays `N 輪對話`; English uses locale-correct singular/plural turn wording.
- During a request, one low-distraction Lucide loading indicator and localized
  status are exposed through `role="status"`, polite live announcement and
  `aria-busy`. Duplicate submission is disabled, typed input may remain visible,
  success/error restores controls, and reduced-motion preferences suppress
  non-essential animation.
- The presentation contract applies consistently to Document Chat, Project Chat,
  submit-review chat evidence and Approval chat evidence. It does not change
  retrieval ranking, prompt context, answer content, Chunk content, schema or
  existing application rows.

### Scope And Implementation Approach

1. Backend citation contract and validation:
   - Extend the internal/API citation schema with optional `chunk_index` and
     populate it from the authoritative Chunk selected by retrieval.
   - Centralize source-ordinal validation for provider answers without rewriting
     valid markers. Keep usage accounting inside the existing transaction/error
     lifecycle so rejection records one failed provider-response-contract event,
     no successful ChatRecord and no second provider request.
   - Add an authorization-preserving, scope-bound batch hydrator for legacy
     citation IDs used by history and review evidence. Preserve array order,
     tolerate unavailable/deleted Chunks with an explicit fallback and never
     infer the canonical index from `citation.title`.

2. Shared Frontend citation presentation:
   - Reuse the Knowledge Graph 24-grapheme preview formatter through a shared
     utility, including whitespace normalization, exact ellipsis and safe empty
     fallback behavior.
   - Render a stable source ordinal, content preview and optional canonical Chunk
     number on every card. Enhance safe Markdown citation rendering with an
     allowlisted numeric-marker callback and accessible focus/selection behavior;
     it must not inject raw HTML or turn invalid legacy markers into links.
   - Apply the same presenter to Document Chat, Project Chat, submit-review and
     Approval evidence rather than maintaining divergent title logic.

3. Turn counting and waiting feedback:
   - Use persisted conversation-entry count directly instead of doubling it.
     Keep pending client state separate and add Traditional Chinese/English
     singular/plural translations.
   - Introduce the accessible in-flight status, duplicate-submit guard, error
     restoration and reduced-motion CSS on both interactive Chat surfaces.

4. Verification and regression:
   - Add focused Backend tests for canonical index propagation, legacy batch
     hydration authorization/order and valid/invalid marker lifecycle using real
     configured services where product behavior is exercised.
   - Add Frontend utility/component/page tests for Unicode previews, source
     ordinal mapping, canonical labels, click/focus behavior, turn counts,
     loading accessibility, reduced motion and shared-surface parity.
   - Run the focused checks first, then the complete relevant harness, unchanged
     80% coverage gates and deployment-policy checks. Record unavailable live
     prerequisites as gaps; do not substitute fixture success.

5. Local delivery and acceptance:
   - After repository Gate 4, any versioned Backend/shared Worker and Frontend
     image build, Helm revision, migration/bootstrap Job, Kubernetes rollout or
     provider-billable wait-state query requires a separate exact action approval
     based on a rendered preflight.
   - Existing CHG-274 history may prove legacy hydration, preview, marker/card
     alignment and turn count without a provider call. A real waiting-animation
     lifecycle needs a separately approved new provider query and must not be
     inferred from a static screenshot.

  `TEST_PLAN.md`, `TRACEABILITY.md`

No SQL migration, existing-row rewrite, document re-extraction, re-indexing,
provider/model configuration or secret change is planned.

### Risks And Rollback

- Unicode code-unit slicing would split emoji or combining characters; the
  shared formatter and focused grapheme tests are mandatory.
- Confusing source ordinal with canonical Chunk index recreates the reported
  mismatch. Types, labels and tests keep these concepts separate.
- Legacy batch hydration must run only after existing authorization and remain
  bounded to citation IDs in the response, or it could leak metadata or create
  N+1 load.
- Provider-output rejection happens after billable work. Usage must be retained
  exactly once while the invalid answer is withheld, and no automatic retry may
  multiply cost.
- Repository rollback reverts the additive citation/presentation changes. A later
  local deployment rolls Backend/shared Worker and Frontend image values back;
  no schema, ChatRecord, Chunk or index rollback is required.

## CHG-276 Consecutive Used Citations And Structure-Aware Retrieval

Gate 4 implementation approval: APPROVED by Peter on 2026-08-26.
Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-08-26 with
`Peter approves CHG-276 Consecutive Used Citations And Structure-Aware Retrieval`.

Gate 1 read-only diagnosis completed on 2026-08-26. Peter confirmed Gate 2 on
2026-08-26 with `同意 CHG-276 Gate 2，採用上述建議`. Gate 3 is complete in
this plan. Peter approved Gate 4 repository implementation and feature tests on
2026-08-26 with
`Peter approves CHG-276 Consecutive Used Citations And Structure-Aware Retrieval`
and explicitly requested image build and Kubernetes deployment. This authorizes
post-verification versioned image builds and exact Helm preflight. The live
cluster write remains subject to a later render-bound action approval; no
Provider query is authorized.

### Confirmed Understanding And Decisions

- The five cards currently labelled as citations are the five prompt retrieval
  candidates. A provider marker references that raw candidate array, so `[3]`
  without `[1]` is valid under CHG-275 but is not an intuitive user-facing
  citation list.
- User-facing citations must contain only sources actually referenced by valid
  provider markers. They are compacted in first-marker order and displayed as
  consecutive `[1]..[M]`; all prompt candidates and raw provider marker numbers
  remain persisted internal audit evidence.
- The reported unable-to-confirm answer was grounded in the prompt it actually
  received: all five excerpts were headings or lead-ins. Canonical Chunk #5,
  which contains the complete three principles, is the active adjacent successor
  of retrieved lead-in Chunk #4 and was absent from the prompt.
- Hybrid fusion must include the union of vector-only, keyword-only and shared
  hits. A structural-only candidate must promote its first authorized contiguous
  content-bearing successor within the bounded same-section lookahead, without
  merging two Chunk identities or exceeding `top_k`.
- Existing and new raw ChatRecord/Validation audit rows are not rewritten.
  Immediate responses, history, exports, submission/Approval evidence and Public
  API output use a deterministic compact view. Existing unable-to-confirm text
  is not regenerated without a separately approved Provider query.
- This is a shared Backend retrieval/response-contract change with defensive
  shared Frontend presentation coverage. It does not change schema, extraction,
  indexing, prompt/model configuration, identity or persistent infrastructure.

### Scope And Implementation Approach

#### Batch 1 — Pure Retrieval And Citation Domain Contracts

1. Extend `backend/app/domain/chat_citations.py` with a typed, pure
   used-source compactor. It parses already-validated numeric markers, records
   original ordinals in first-occurrence order, rewrites only those marker
   tokens to consecutive display ordinals and returns response copies of the
   selected citations. It must be idempotent for an already compact view and
   must never mutate the input answer or citation objects.
2. Add pure helpers for complete reciprocal-rank fusion and deterministic
   tie-breaking. Contributions are calculated only for channels where a hit is
   present; the candidate identity is the stable OpenSearch hit/Chunk identity.
3. Add a deterministic structural classifier for Markdown-heading-only and
   short colon-ended lead-in Chunks using Unicode grapheme length and body-shape
   checks. Keep this separate from retrieval I/O so the boundary and false
   positives are directly testable.

#### Batch 2 — Authorized Structure-Aware Retrieval

1. Refactor `_opensearch_hybrid_search` to fuse the vector/keyword union, retain
   a bounded candidate pool and expose enough ordered candidates for structural
   promotion before the final `top_k` slice.
2. In `_search_hybrid_chunks`, build an ordered per-document/version active
   Chunk index from the collection already loaded after authorization. For a
   structural-only candidate, examine at most two contiguous successors; stop
   at version/document/section or same/higher-heading boundaries and promote
   only the first content-bearing successor.
3. The promoted citation uses the successor's own canonical ID, index, excerpt,
   source mapping and content type. Dedupe a successor already in the fused set,
   preserve deterministic relation priority, evict structural-only/lowest-value
   candidates first and keep the prompt list at or below requested `top_k`.
4. Reuse the same retrieval path for Document staging, Project published and CSV
   validation. Do not add a second embedding or Chat Provider call, database
   query, OpenSearch write or index rebuild.

#### Batch 3 — Shared Compact Response Views

1. Keep provider marker validation, ChatRecord parent-first persistence, raw
   `answer` and full prompt-candidate `reference_docs` unchanged. After the raw
   record/evidence is established, create the compact view for the immediate
   response.
2. Apply the same helper after authorized legacy `chunk_index` hydration in
   conversation history, feedback response, CSV completed results/download,
   submit-review and Approval evidence builders. Internal Judge and usage/audit
   logic continue to consume raw evidence.
3. Apply equivalent compact final output to Public API JSON and SSE without
   changing its stored request/response audit identity. SSE `delta`, citation
   and done events must agree on the same compact mapping; invalid raw markers
   still fail closed before any success response.
4. Keep `ChatResponseEvidence` and safe Markdown marker behavior aligned with
   the Backend contract. Add a defensive idempotent presentation path only where
   raw legacy nested evidence can reach the component directly; do not maintain
   a second divergent numbering algorithm.

#### Batch 4 — Verification, Delivery Planning And Acceptance

1. Run pure/focused tests first, then real PostgreSQL authorization/no-write
   checks and a read-only OpenSearch characterization using existing indexed
   vectors rather than a new embedding Provider call.
2. Run full relevant Backend/Frontend, coverage, governance and deployment
   checks without reducing thresholds. Broad suites that require destructive
   live fixtures must remain blocked/unavailable unless separately authorized.
3. After repository Gate 5 passes, prepare a versioned Backend/shared Worker and
   Frontend image plan only if runtime delivery is requested. Any image build,
   Helm revision/Jobs or live billable re-query requires a separate exact
   rendered action approval.
4. A future exact live acceptance may ask the reported question once. It must
   prove one embedding invocation, one Chat invocation, promoted Chunk #5,
   a substantive three-principle answer, compact citations starting at `[1]`,
   history reload and no unapproved application-data mutation or replay.

### Expected Files

- `backend/app/domain/chat_citations.py`
- `backend/app/api/routes/serving.py`
- `backend/app/domain/validation_runner.py`
- Public API response/stream presentation helpers under `backend/app/`
- `frontend/src/components/ChatResponseEvidence.tsx`
- `frontend/src/components/SafeMarkdown.tsx` only if defensive legacy handling
  cannot stay inside the shared evidence component
- Focused Backend and Frontend tests
- `SPECIFICATION.md`, `SPEC_CHANGELOG.md`, `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md`,
  `TEST_PLAN.md`, `TRACEABILITY.md`

No SQL migration, OpenSearch re-index, extraction change, Prompt/model update,
new secret or deployment-template change is planned.

### Test Strategy

- `CHAT-RETR-RRF01..RRF04`: vector-only/keyword-only/shared union, channel-local
  contribution, dedupe, deterministic tie and scope-filter retention.
- `CHAT-RETR-STRUCT01..STRUCT06`: Unicode structural classifier, heading and
  colon lead-in, content-bearing negative, contiguous successor, two-Chunk
  lookahead, section/version boundary, dedupe and top_k cap.
- `CHAT-COMPACT-B01..B06`: `[3][5][3] -> [1][2][1]`, first-use ordering, raw
  immutability, idempotence, no-marker zero list, invalid-marker fail-closed and
  canonical Chunk identity preservation.
- `CHAT-COMPACT-S01..S06`: immediate/history/feedback, validation/export,
  submit-review/Approval, Public API JSON/SSE and Frontend marker/card parity.
- `CHAT-COMPACT-L01..L05`: content-minimized current-record characterization,
  real authorized PostgreSQL no-write proof, read-only OpenSearch union evidence,
  protected delivery preflight and separately approved one-query acceptance.
- Regression coverage retains CHG-274 parent/usage ordering and CHG-275 title,
  marker safety, turn count, loading feedback and authorization boundaries.

### Deployment And Configuration Impact

- Repository implementation changes application code only. The current
  `top_k` API bounds, model rows, system prompts, embedding profile and index
  mappings remain unchanged.
- Runtime delivery would require a new Backend image used by Backend, Worker,
  Beat and init/bootstrap containers. A Frontend image is required only if the
  defensive/shared presenter changes. Migration stays at the current image and
  schema remains `045` unless an action-time render proves otherwise and Peter
  separately approves it.
- No committed or live secret, ConfigMap value, PVC/PV, Ingress, Keycloak, LDAP,
  identity, model, Chunk or OpenSearch application index may be changed by the
  repository implementation approval.

### Risks And Rollback

- Over-broad adjacency can cite an unrelated next section. Exact structural
  classification, same-section boundary, two-Chunk lookahead and canonical
  successor identity are mandatory.
- Replacing structural hits can lower recall when the heading itself is useful.
  Raw fused candidates remain auditable; only structural-only hits are eligible,
  and deterministic regression cases cover ordinary content Chunks.
- Compacting only the UI would diverge exports/Public API; compacting persisted
  rows would destroy audit fidelity. The shared response helper and raw/view
  separation prevent both failures.
- Marker replacement must not touch ordinary bracketed numbers outside the
  already validated citation-token grammar or change answer Markdown.
- Code rollback restores the current retrieval and presentation behavior. No
  schema/data/index rollback is needed. A later image rollout rolls images back
  to revision 20 and does not alter persistent resources.

## CHG-277 Safe Markdown Ordered List Structure Preservation Development Plan

### Status And Approval Boundary

- Gate 1 read-only diagnosis completed on 2026-08-27. The latest persisted
  answer stores ordered markers `1..6`; the shared Frontend parser discards them
  and emits separated `<ol>` blocks that each default to 1.
- Gate 2 confirmation: complete — Peter confirmed with
  `同意 CHG-277 Gate 2，採用上述建議`.
- Gate 4 approval: approved — Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-08-27 with
  `Peter approves CHG-277 Safe Markdown Ordered List Structure Preservation`.
  Peter later authorized the Frontend image build and deployment preparation
  with `好，建置新版 Frontend 映像並部署`. The image build is complete;
  the actual Kubernetes write remains bound to a separate exact action approval.
  Provider use remains outside both approvals.

### Scope And Design

1. Replace the lossy ordered-list shape in
   `frontend/src/components/SafeMarkdown.tsx` with typed ordered blocks/items
   that preserve the source start and each explicit ordinal.
2. Parse line-start `N.` and `N)` markers without confusing citation `[N]`,
   decimals, versions, dates or sentence-internal numbers. Retain run-on list
   normalization only where a conservative executable regression proves it is
   unambiguous.
3. Preserve consecutive ordered items in one block. Support the bounded safe
   subset of indented continuation paragraphs and nested unordered/ordered
   lists as item children; keep genuinely unindented independent blocks in
   source order without swallowing them into a list item.
4. Render semantic `<ol start>` and `<li value>` only where the explicit source
   ordinal differs from natural HTML progression. Keep the existing inline
   bold/citation renderer, tables, headings, paragraphs and unordered lists.
5. Keep `ChatResponseEvidence` and every existing caller on the shared
   component. Do not add page-specific ordinal correction, CSS counters,
   string-prefix numbering, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` or a second Markdown
   implementation.
6. No i18n string is expected. If implementation reveals a new user-facing
   state, update both locale files before use rather than hard-coding text.

### Non-Goals And Compatibility

- Do not rewrite persisted ChatRecord/Validation/Approval answers, document
  Markdown artifacts or Chunk content.
- Do not modify Backend routes, APIs, database schema/data, Provider prompts,
  retrieval, citations, usage ledger, extraction or indexes.
- Do not attempt full CommonMark compliance or introduce a new rendering
  framework. This is a bounded extension of the repository's existing safe
  subset and local pattern.
- Do not build an image or write Helm/Kubernetes state under Gate 4 alone.
  After repository verification, any delivery will require a separate exact
  Frontend image/render/protected-resource approval.

### Implementation Tasks

1. Add typed ordered-item/child-block structures and pure parsing helpers that
   expose deterministic output for direct tests.
2. Change normalization/parser state so explicit ordinals survive block flushes,
   while current table/list/heading behavior and source order remain stable.
3. Render `start`/`value`, continuation content and nested lists with stable keys
   and semantic DOM.
4. Add executable component tests using the current six-section answer shape,
   split blocks, jumps/restarts, nested content and interactive citations.
5. Add negative regressions for `[1]`, `v1.2`, `2026.08.27`, decimal/sentence
   numbers and raw HTML/script; retain existing SafeMarkdown table/bold/bullet
   tests and shared-surface source contracts.
6. Run focused tests first, then full Frontend lint/build/test and unchanged
   coverage checks. Record any unrelated baseline failure without weakening it.

### Test And Verification Strategy

- Lowest useful level: pure parser output and DOM/component semantics for
  `ol[start]`, `li[value]`, ordered item children and citation callbacks.
- Shared regressions: Document/Project Chat, Approval/submit-review and Knowledge
  Detail/Chunk callers continue using the same component and existing citation
  mapping.
- Accessibility/security: semantic list roles/order, keyboard-operable citation
  buttons, no raw HTML execution and no CSS-only ordinals.
- Responsive/i18n: zh-Hant/en content structure and narrow layout remain stable;
  no new translated string is expected.
- Deployment/configuration: Frontend-only source change; Helm lint and config
  policy prove no chart/config drift. Cluster write remains separately gated.

### Risks And Mitigations

- Shared renderer regression: focus tests on all existing block kinds and shared
  callers before the full Frontend suite/build.
- Ambiguous run-on numbering: parse only bounded marker positions and test common
  numeric non-list text; prefer preserving text over inventing a list.
- Incorrect nesting: use explicit indentation/continuation rules and preserve
  independent unindented blocks rather than heuristic cross-block swallowing.
- React key/DOM instability: use structural indices plus explicit ordinals only
  within the immutable parsed output and assert deterministic rerender behavior.
- Repository-wide Frontend coverage is already below 80%; do not lower the gate
  or claim focused coverage as a release waiver.

## CHG-278 Model Usage Numeric And Cost Presentation Correction Plan

### Gate Status And Objective

- Gate 4 implementation approval: APPROVED by Peter on 2026-08-27.
- Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-08-27 with
  `Peter approves CHG-278 Model Usage Numeric And Cost Presentation Correction`.
- Gate 1 read-only diagnosis and Gate 2 confirmation completed on 2026-08-27.
  Peter confirmed the recommended scope with
  `同意 CHG-278 Gate 2，採用上述建議`.
- Gate 3 synchronized specification 10.35, the changelog, this plan, test design
  and traceability. Peter approved Gate 4 repository implementation and
  non-billable feature tests on 2026-08-27; Provider/billing, model-data, image
  and Kubernetes actions remain separately gated.
- Objective: correct the model-usage table's identity, number, cost and error-rate
  contracts without inventing official billing data, exposing API-key material,
  rewriting ledger history or changing unrelated report behavior.

### Scope And Design

1. Frontend model-usage columns:
   - reorder the existing fields to model type, model name, Provider, project and
     purpose;
   - use a new explicit `ai_model_name` projection of the first AI Model form
     field `AIModel.name`; do not display the Provider identifier from
     `config.model_name`; make model type/name the two sticky left columns;
   - remove Integration Client/API-key fields and selectors from table, filter
     state/options and requests.
2. Shared report numeric presentation:
   - replace value-range inference with a key-aware formatter receiving locale;
   - maintain explicit integer, decimal/latency, ratio, money, text and null
     field sets for the model-usage table;
   - use `Intl.NumberFormat`/equivalent locale formatting, up to two latency and
     eight monetary fraction digits; use percent only for error rate;
   - render missing official cost with localized Not provided while preserving
     numeric zero.
3. CSV policy:
   - include `ai_model_name`, remove provider `model_name`,
     `integration_client_id` and `api_key_prefix` from the model-usage export
     field list and localized header map;
   - retain raw machine-readable numeric cells without UI grouping, percent or
     unit suffixes;
   - keep authorization, scope, filter and bounded streaming behavior unchanged.
4. Backend aggregation:
   - add `AIModel.name` as a stable response/group identity and stop filtering or
     grouping model usage by Integration Client/API key; remove those filter
     options and query parameters from this report contract;
   - apply `attempted=true` consistently to call, success and failure counts;
   - compute error rate only from attempted failures/calls and retain the zero-call
     zero ratio contract;
   - prevent zero-count OCR components from creating estimated zero and require
     complete matching prices for every positive usage component;
   - for OCR choose one matching pricing basis: token components when positive
     token usage and complete OCR-model token pricing exist, otherwise positive
     page/image components with complete unit pricing. Never add both bases.
5. Configuration boundary:
   - do not hard-code or fetch prices and do not borrow another AI Model's config;
   - repository work only validates the typed behavior. Correcting the current
     Docker Desktop OCR model from page pricing to its own Token pricing is an
     application-data mutation and remains separately action-approved.
6. i18n/CSS:
   - update aligned zh-Hant/en labels and missing-cost copy;
   - implement sticky offsets, backgrounds, z-index and responsive overflow using
     existing report-table styles and accessible focus behavior.

### Files Expected To Change

- `frontend/src/app/reports/page.tsx`
- `frontend/src/app/globals.css`
- `frontend/src/i18n/locales/zh.json`
- `frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json`
- `frontend/src/lib/reportExport.ts` only if export metadata is client-owned
- `frontend/src/lib/api.ts`
- focused report component/contract tests under `frontend/tests/`
- `backend/app/api/routes/reports.py`
- `backend/app/domain/model_usage.py`
- focused model-usage tests under `backend/tests/`
- governance files only as required to record Gate 4 and verification evidence

No SQL migration, Helm template, Secret, credential, provider adapter, Chat,
Chunk, index, identity or LDAP source change is planned.

### Implementation Tasks

1. Add failing executable tests for the exact screenshot values, sticky identity
   fields, CSV columns, null/zero official costs and zh-Hant/en labels.
2. Extract or expose a deterministic field-aware report cell formatter and apply
   it from `ReportTable` with the field key and active locale.
3. Reorder/label/stick model identity columns and remove API-key prefix from the
   visible table, filter state, selector and report requests.
4. Add the explicit `AIModel.name` projection; remove Integration Client joins,
   grouping/filter/options from model usage; update Backend/Frontend CSV field
   policies and assert raw numeric export plus local model name and no provider
   identifier/client/prefix.
5. Change aggregation predicates so calls/successes/failures share the attempted
   universe; add bounded error-rate invariants.
6. Change cost component selection to ignore zero usage, require complete
   matching prices and select exactly one OCR pricing basis.
7. Run focused Frontend and Backend tests, then full applicable suites, builds,
   coverage and governance/deployment-static checks. Record all unchanged
   baseline gaps without weakening gates.

### Test And Verification Strategy

- Frontend unit/component: exact numeric formats for counts, latency, ratios,
  costs, null and zero; column order/sticky classes; no API-key field; aligned
  zh-Hant/en; narrow horizontal-scroll behavior.
- CSV: exact header/field set, `AIModel.name` present, Provider model name,
  Integration Client identity and API-key prefix absent, with raw `17058`,
  `0.0042168` and ratio values without UI decorations.
- Backend pure/route: attempted and non-attempted status matrix; error rate never
  above one; official null versus zero; OCR token/page positive/zero/missing-price
  cases and no double charge.
- Backend contract: two Integration Clients with otherwise equal dimensions
  aggregate into one row; filter options and summary/export request contracts do
  not expose or accept the removed model-usage filter.
- Real services: use the configured local PostgreSQL in a rollback transaction to
  prove aggregation and ledger non-mutation. No Provider or organization billing
  call is necessary or authorized.
- Regression: report scope/authorization/filter/paging/export tests plus existing
  model-usage ledger tests, Frontend lint/build and unchanged 80% coverage gates.

### Deployment And Data Impact

- Repository implementation requires Backend and Frontend source changes but no
  schema migration or historical row rewrite.
- Image builds and Helm/Kubernetes writes are outside this Gate 4 plan approval
  and require later immutable image IDs, exact render digest, target revision,
  Jobs and protected-resource baselines.
- Updating current Docker Desktop OCR pricing is a distinct application-data
  action. A later proposal must state exact model ID, before/after non-secret
  pricing keys and data fingerprint; credentials remain untouched.

### Risks And Mitigations

- Cross-client aggregation regression: remove Integration Client from select,
  group/order/filter together and prove summed totals using two distinct clients;
  retain the identity only in immutable ledger/audit evidence.
- Money rounding: format Decimal-derived values to at most eight places and test
  sub-cent values plus large grouped amounts and legitimate zero.
- Cost over/under-counting: require complete positive-usage pricing and exactly
  one OCR basis; fail to unavailable instead of partial or invented estimates.
- Sticky overlap on narrow screens: assign deterministic widths/offsets and test
  table overflow, focus and z-index in both locales.
- Existing repository coverage may remain below 80%; report it as a release gap,
  never lower or waive the threshold.
