## CHG-281 Markdown Structure-Aware Retrieval Pipeline Plan

### Gate Status And Authorization Boundary

- Gate 1 read-only architecture diagnosis completed on 2026-08-29.
- Gate 2 confirmation: Confirmed by Peter on 2026-08-29 with
  `同意 CHG-281 Gate 2，採用上述建議`.
- Gate 4 implementation approval: Approved by Peter on 2026-08-29 with
  `Peter approves CHG-281 Markdown Structure-Aware Retrieval Pipeline`.
- Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-08-29.
- This section is the approved Gate 3 development plan. Peter approved Gate 4
  with `Peter approves CHG-281 Markdown Structure-Aware Retrieval Pipeline`.
- Repository implementation, additive V046 and non-billable verification are
  complete. Image/deployment, Provider use, existing-data reprocess/reindex,
  published-manifest switch and application-data mutation remain unapproved.
- A later Gate 4 authorizes repository implementation, additive migration and
  non-billable tests only. Image builds, Helm/Kubernetes writes, OCR/Embedding/
  LLM Provider calls, existing-data reprocessing/reindex and manifest switches
  remain separately action-bound.

### Current Architecture And Identified Problems

1. `backend/app/domain/extraction_pipeline.py` creates canonical Markdown, then
   `_split_paragraphs()` uses blank-line Regex and `_create_chunks()` creates one
   random-UUID Chunk per paragraph. Effective boundaries ignore the version's
   configured chunk size and overlap.
2. `_document_layout_artifact()` uses limited Regex heuristics rather than an AST;
   it cannot reliably preserve nested headings, lists, tables, inherited section
   context, source node identity or page relationships.
3. `backend/app/domain/embeddings.py::_chunk_text()` prefers synthetic
   `markdown_content`; formatting tokens and generated `### title #index` enter
   embedding input, while token estimation is character-length based.
4. Staging/published OpenSearch rows mix `content` and `markdown_content` and lack
   retrieval text, heading/page metadata, processing versions and canonical
   embedding-content hashes.
5. `serving.py` performs real vector+BM25 fusion, but searches legacy fields.
   CHG-276 successor promotion compensates after ingestion instead of preserving
   document structure at ingestion.
6. `ai_provider.py` uses citation excerpts as bounded context; raw, display and
   retrieval representations are not explicit generation inputs.
7. Full canonical Markdown already exists in the version-scoped artifact and must
   remain CHG-273's sole source. Existing source validation assumes display
   `content` equals the raw range and needs a version-aware compatibility path.

### Target Architecture And Module Boundaries

```text
OCR / parser canonical Markdown
  -> MarkdownStructureParser
  -> DocumentStructure
  -> StructureAwareChunker + TokenCounter
  -> Chunk(display_text, raw fragment, metadata)
  -> RetrievalTextNormalizer
  -> retrieval_text + embedding_content_hash
  -> EmbeddingService
  -> versioned staging/published hybrid index
  -> authorized retrieval rehydrate
  -> display_text (raw fragment only when needed) to LLM
```

Planned new modules:

- `backend/app/domain/markdown_structure.py`: CommonMark/GFM AST adapter, typed
  nodes, exact source spans, warnings and safe paragraph fallback.
- `backend/app/domain/structure_chunking.py`: heading inheritance, structure
  boundaries, list/table batching, controlled overlap and deterministic identity.
- `backend/app/domain/retrieval_text.py`: semantic renderer, bounded context
  prefix, noise removal and explicit normalization version.
- `backend/app/domain/tokenization.py`: model-aware TokenCounter interface and a
  recorded deterministic fallback.
- `backend/app/domain/retrieval_evaluation.py`: expected-hit dataset and
  Recall@K/MRR/Top-K reporting without document-content logging.

Existing integration points after Gate 4:

- `extraction_pipeline.py`: use structure after the canonical artifact is saved;
  retain compatible pipeline step/API state names.
- `embeddings.py`: embed only `retrieval_text`, use real token counts and the
  canonical hash, with controlled legacy fallback.
- `markdown_artifacts.py` / `chunk_artifacts.py`: preserve the full artifact and
  map Chunk exact raw fragments/node ranges.
- `review_publish.py` / `serving.py`: mapping v2, weighted BM25 fields, authorized
  hydration and generation-context selection.
- `ai_provider.py`: receive bounded display text, not citation preview or a
  retrieval-only prefix as the sole context.
- `models.py`, `schemas.py`, documents route and SQL migration: additive fields,
  debug response contract and legacy-null behavior.
- typed Settings, environment examples and Docker/Helm ConfigMap values:
  externalize all approved chunking/normalization settings.

### Data Model And Migration Plan

- Preserve full raw Markdown only in the `DocumentVersion` artifact.
- Reuse `Chunk.content` as backward-compatible display text. For new rows,
  `Chunk.markdown_content` is the exact raw fragment. Add `retrieval_text`,
  `embedding_content_hash`, heading/page/sequence/stable-key data as queryable
  columns where needed; keep table/link/node/source/processing snapshots in typed
  metadata where relational indexing is unnecessary.
- Record parser/chunker/normalizer/tokenizer versions and effective config;
  include embedding model/version/dimension in the canonical hash.
- Prepare additive V046 after Gate 4. New fields remain nullable so schema-045
  rows and APIs stay readable. No row update, backfill or destructive constraint
  is permitted in the migration.
- New source mappings validate raw fragments/ranges/node IDs. Legacy mappings
  continue under their recorded processing version.

### Structure, Normalization And Configuration

- Select and pin a maintained CommonMark/GFM AST library with table support and
  source positions after Gate 4; do not build a new Regex parser.
- Boundary priority is heading/section, paragraph, list, table, sentence, token.
  Defaults: target 500, max 700, min 80, overlap 60 tokens; heading depth 4;
  context prefix 96 tokens; table batches 10 rows; document-title context on.
- Short sections do not merge across unrelated headings. Table batches repeat
  headers. Overlap applies only to split siblings, not whole tables/lists/headings.
- Repeated header/footer removal requires at least three reliable pages and
  recurrence evidence. Otherwise preserve content and record warning.
- Normalization removes formatting noise, not business words, ordering, headings,
  notes, captions, lists, table labels or code. It introduces no LLM rewrite.

### Index, Rebuild And Rollback Strategy

- Introduce mapping/profile v2 without altering current active indexes. BM25
  weighting is retrieval text `^3`, document title `^2`, heading path `^2` and
  display text; vector input is retrieval text; legacy fields remain fallback.
- A staging pilot creates a disposable/new-version index and validates document
  count, authorization, dimension, hashes and retrieval metrics before publish.
- Published content uses a new extraction revision and existing review/publish
  flow. Build the index first and switch Active Version Manifest only after
  validation. Rollback restores the previous manifest/index.
- Deploying code/V046 must not mutate the existing 26 Chunks or vectors. If the
  raw artifact is valid, later approved reprocessing skips OCR but still requires
  reparse/rechunk/reembed/reindex. Provider-billable work needs exact approval.

### Implementation Sequence After Gate 4

1. Add fail-first pure tests for the approved examples, spans, identity, hashes
   and legacy fallback.
2. Pin dependencies and implement isolated parse/chunk/normalize/token modules.
3. Add V046 model/schema/API/config contracts and source-mapping compatibility;
   validate migration without changing application rows.
4. Integrate the new extraction/embedding/staging/publish/retrieval paths behind
   explicit processing/mapping versions.
5. Add protected debug API, metadata-only logs and failure fallback.
6. Run pure and real-service suites, then produce the isolated Before/After
   evaluation harness.
7. Stop before any billable pilot/reindex/deployment and present exact document,
   model, index and protected-baseline actions for separate approval.

### Test And Verification Strategy

- Unit: AST nodes/spans; heading inheritance; formatting; lists; small/large
  tables; links; notes; code; captions; short sections; sentence split; page/
  header/footer policy; deterministic identity; hash invalidation; fallback.
- Compatibility: CHG-273 canonical Markdown/source mapping, CHG-276 retrieval/
  citations, legacy-null fields, API responses, review/publish authorization and
  manifest rollback.
- TEST-002 integration: real configured PostgreSQL/OpenSearch and, only after
  separate approval, live embedding provider; disposable version/index cleanup.
- Evaluation: dataset with expected document/section/chunk and Before/After
  Recall@K, MRR and Top-K Hit Rate, including table and heading-section queries.

### Risks

- Complex GFM/HTML and OCR page boundaries may be incomplete: preserve raw
  Markdown, emit warnings and fall back per block rather than guess.
- Table semantic text can expand: enforce row/token caps and repeat only headers.
- Provider tokenizers can differ: record tokenizer/version and fail closed on
  profile or vector-dimension mismatch.
- Structural correctness can still regress ranking: do not switch an active
  manifest until approved evaluation and existing-query regressions pass.
- Additive columns can remain on code rollback; old data/indexes are never
  overwritten, so legacy read/index and prior manifest remain the rollback path.

## CHG-282 Lossless Paginated Safe Markdown Rendering Plan

Status: Gate 3 plan recorded on 2026-08-30. Gate 2 was confirmed with
`同意 CHG-282 Gate 2，採用上述建議`. Peter approved Gate 4 with
`Peter approves CHG-282 Lossless Paginated Safe Markdown Rendering`.
Repository implementation, dependency installation and non-Provider feature tests
are authorized. Image build, cluster write, layout regeneration, authenticated
Browser mutation and Provider/data/index actions remain separately gated.

### Objective And Evidence

- Eliminate every content-loss path at document page boundaries while retaining
  the A4-like multi-page reading model, page numbers, source anchors, selection
  and Knowledge Detail/Approval Evidence parity.
- Replace the shared hand-written Markdown grammar with one safe CommonMark/GFM
  AST rendering boundary so inline/fenced code, blockquotes, links, emphasis,
  strikethrough, task/nested lists, tables and existing citations behave
  consistently without executing raw HTML.
- Gate 1 evidence is concrete: `_document_layout_artifact()` splits only generic
  paragraphs longer than 900 characters; `_paginate_layout_blocks()` trusts a
  fixed 910px estimate and accepts an oversized block on an empty page; the CSS
  then applies `overflow: hidden` to both page and content. `SafeMarkdown` has
  only five block variants and its inline Regex recognizes only `**bold**` and
  `[n]`, so the screenshot's backticks are expected current behavior.

### Scope

In scope:

1. Add a typed, deterministic `document_layout` v2 paginator built from the
   existing CHG-281 CommonMark/GFM structure rather than raw paragraph Regex.
2. Add lossless continuation handling for paragraph, list, table and code, with
   stable source identity/ranges and table-header/list-ordinal preservation.
3. Make the document paper a minimum-height surface that grows when runtime
   layout exceeds the estimate; keep horizontal overflow local to table/code.
4. Replace `SafeMarkdown` parsing/rendering with a pinned CommonMark/GFM AST
   dependency and shared block/inline/security component policy.
5. Share or parity-lock the layout block/page renderer used by Knowledge Detail
   and Approval Evidence; preserve Chunk and Chat shared rendering behavior.
6. Add safe URL/image handling, inert raw HTML, semantic DOM, keyboard/focus,
   responsive and citation regressions.
7. Add a non-mutating layout-only regeneration preview contract for legacy
   artifacts; any live apply remains a later exact data action.

Out of scope:

- OCR, canonical Markdown generation, CHG-281 chunk/retrieval/embedding logic,
  model/provider calls, Chunk or ChatRecord rewriting, re-embedding/reindexing,
  active-manifest switching, PostgreSQL schema changes and application-data
  mutation.
- Rendering the canonical Markdown source tab as HTML. That tab remains exact
  raw source; this plan changes rendered reading surfaces only.
- Image/Helm build or Docker Desktop deployment. Those require later immutable
  image/render/resource-bound approvals after repository acceptance.

### Target Design

#### Backend layout model and paginator

- Add `backend/app/domain/document_layout.py` containing an isolated paginator,
  budget estimator and continuation splitters. It consumes CHG-281
  `DocumentStructure` nodes or a narrow typed layout input; extraction pipeline
  orchestration calls it but does not own parsing/pagination details.
- Additive API metadata in `backend/app/api/schemas.py`:
  `layout_version`, pagination policy/version, original/continuation identity,
  continuation ordinal/count, source offsets, code language, table header and a
  typed ordered/list-item representation. Preserve legacy `items`/`rows` fields
  for old artifacts and clients. Add `blockquote` and `horizontal_rule` only as
  additive block kinds.
- Paragraph continuation uses explicit line boundaries, then sentence
  boundaries, then bounded Unicode-safe text ranges. It must neither drop nor
  duplicate code points and must preserve the shared source anchor.
- List continuation never cuts one item in the middle unless the single item is
  itself oversized; it preserves ordered start/value and nested children.
  Table continuation repeats its exact header and splits by rows. Code
  continuation splits only at line boundaries and retains language/text.
- The paginator rejects no readable document because of one malformed block;
  it falls back to a lossless paragraph and records a non-sensitive warning.
  An oversized unit that cannot be safely split becomes a dedicated page whose
  Frontend is allowed to grow, never a clipped page.
- `backend/app/domain/extraction_pipeline.py` adopts the paginator for newly
  generated artifacts. `documents.py` and `approvals.py` must use the same
  validation/readback path and retain legacy fallback.

#### Shared safe Markdown renderer

- Pin `react-markdown` and `remark-gfm` (or an equivalent reviewed
  CommonMark/GFM AST pair) in `frontend/package.json` and the lockfile after Gate
  4. Do not include or enable `rehype-raw`; set raw HTML to inert behavior.
- Refactor `frontend/src/components/SafeMarkdown.tsx` into one AST/security
  boundary with `block` and `inline` presentation modes. Custom components own
  link/image policy, inline/fenced code, table wrappers, task controls and the
  current interactive citation mapping.
- Citation detection runs only in normal text nodes. Code, link destinations,
  image destinations and raw HTML never become citations. Existing ordinal,
  mismatch, label and click behavior remains unchanged.
- URL policy permits only reviewed schemes/targets, applies safe external-link
  relations and never automatically fetches arbitrary remote images. Rejected
  links/images retain safe visible text or caption.
- Move duplicated `LayoutBlockView`/`LayoutPageView` behavior into a shared
  component or pure renderer used identically by Knowledge Detail and Approval
  Evidence. Raw source selection continues through `CanonicalMarkdownSource`.

#### Lossless paper presentation

- Change `.document-page` from a clipping fixed-aspect container to A4-like
  minimum dimensions with content-sized rows. Page/content vertical overflow is
  visible inside the paper sizing flow, not outside the paper; footer follows
  content. The paper retains its border, shadow, page gap and responsive width.
- `.structured-layout-content` must not clip vertical content. Table/code
  wrappers receive bounded horizontal scrolling. Source-active backgrounds and
  focus rings remain inside the paper and may span continuation blocks.
- Long content is primarily split by Backend layout v2. Frontend auto-growth is
  a mandatory safety invariant for legacy artifacts and font/viewport variance,
  not a substitute for structure-aware pagination.

### Planned File Changes

| File/area | Planned purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `backend/app/domain/document_layout.py` | New typed budget, lossless block split and deterministic pagination module. |
| `backend/app/domain/extraction_pipeline.py` | Replace approximate inline pagination call with layout v2 orchestration; retain legacy helpers only where compatibility needs them. |
| `backend/app/api/schemas.py` | Add optional layout/pagination/continuation/list/table/code metadata and block kinds. |
| `backend/app/api/routes/documents.py` | Validate/read new and legacy artifacts through the shared contract. |
| `backend/app/api/routes/approvals.py` | Use identical artifact readback; remove divergent fallback behavior where safe. |
| `frontend/package.json`, lockfile | Pin reviewed CommonMark/GFM renderer dependencies. |
| `frontend/src/components/SafeMarkdown.tsx` | Shared AST renderer, citation text-node handling and security policy. |
| `frontend/src/components/DocumentLayoutViewer.tsx` | Shared page/block rendering for Knowledge Detail and Approval Evidence. |
| Knowledge Detail and `ApprovalEvidenceViewer.tsx` | Replace duplicated local renderers with the shared component. |
| `frontend/src/app/globals.css` | Lossless paper flow plus semantic Markdown/code/table/blockquote/task styles. |
| Frontend/Backend focused tests | Fail-first parser, paginator, security, parity and responsive evidence. |
| Governance artifacts | Keep spec, changelog, test plan and trace synchronized with results. |

### Task Breakdown

1. Add fail-first Backend tests for oversized block splitting, no-loss joins,
   page budget, stable continuation metadata and legacy artifact validation.
2. Implement the isolated paginator and additive schema; integrate newly
   generated layout artifacts without touching existing rows.
3. Add fail-first Frontend tests for the exact inline-code examples, full GFM
   block set, citations/code isolation, unsafe inputs and raw-source invariance.
4. Replace the Regex renderer with the AST renderer and explicit security
   policy; retain CHG-277 ordered-list behavior and citation accessibility.
5. Add fail-first shared page component/CSS tests, then remove duplicated route
   renderers and enforce non-clipping, paper growth and local horizontal scroll.
6. Run focused suites, relevant CHG-273/277/281 regressions, full Frontend and
   Backend harness checks, coverage, static deployment checks and spec gates.
7. Report repository results and remaining coverage/browser gaps. Stop before
   image build/deploy or layout regeneration until a separate action approval.

### Test Strategy And Planned Commands

Focused Backend IDs:

- `VIEWER-PAGE-B01`: oversized paragraph lossless sentence/Unicode continuation.
- `VIEWER-PAGE-B02`: ordered/nested list ordinal and anchor continuity.
- `VIEWER-PAGE-B03`: large table row batching with repeated header.
- `VIEWER-PAGE-B04`: fenced code line splitting/language preservation.
- `VIEWER-PAGE-B05`: deterministic page/budget/continuation identity.
- `VIEWER-PAGE-B06`: malformed and legacy artifact compatibility.

Focused Frontend IDs:

- `MD-RENDER-F01`: inline code examples render `<code>` without backticks.
- `MD-RENDER-F02`: fenced code preserves literal content and ignores citation
  parsing inside code.
- `MD-RENDER-F03`: headings, emphasis, strikethrough, blockquote, nested/task
  lists, table, link, horizontal rule and captions produce semantic DOM.
- `MD-RENDER-F04`: CHG-277 ordered starts/values and interactive citations
  remain correct.
- `MD-SEC-F01`: raw HTML/script/events and dangerous URLs remain inert.
- `MD-SEC-F02`: remote image policy prevents unauthorized fetch while retaining
  alt/caption.
- `VIEWER-PAGE-F01`: legacy page content has no vertical clipping and footer
  follows content.
- `VIEWER-PAGE-F02`: source highlight, selection and continuation anchors remain
  accessible in both Knowledge Detail and Approval Evidence.
- `VIEWER-PAGE-F03`: 1440/1024/768/375px styles preserve page/panel separation,
  40px controls, zoom readability and local table/code scrolling.
- `MD-COMPAT-F01`: canonical raw source view remains byte-equivalent and shared
  rendered surfaces use the same grammar/security boundary.

Planned verification after Gate 4:

```bash
./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor
./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace
./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor
./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved
./HARNESS/harness.sh backend:syntax
./HARNESS/harness.sh test:backend
./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:lint
./HARNESS/harness.sh test:frontend
./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:build

./HARNESS/harness.sh helm:lint
./HARNESS/harness.sh deploy:config-policy
```

Authenticated Browser acceptance is separately gated and, when authorized,
must use the actual affected document/layout. It will verify that the previously
clipped page text is complete, inline code has no visible backticks, no network
request is made for hostile external images and both Knowledge/Approval surfaces
remain navigable. It must not call an AI Provider or mutate application data.

### Compatibility, Migration And Deployment Impact

- Database schema: none. Index mapping and vectors: none. Runtime secrets and
  Helm configuration: unchanged unless later dependency build evidence requires
  only immutable application image tags.
- API: optional additive layout metadata only; legacy payloads remain accepted.
  Existing stored layout artifacts are not automatically rewritten.
- New extraction runs produce layout v2 after repository/deployment approval.
  Legacy artifacts immediately receive the no-clipping Frontend safety boundary.
- A layout-only regeneration tool/preview may be added but defaults to dry-run.
  Executing it against Docker Desktop is a distinct data write and needs a
  document/version-bound approval. It may update only `document_layout` metadata
  and must prove unchanged canonical Markdown, Chunk/Embedding/index/application
  rows and zero Provider calls.

### Risks And Mitigations

- AST dependency changes ordered-list/citation behavior: retain exact CHG-277
  fixtures and implement citation transformation at text-node level only.
- Page estimate remains font-dependent: Backend typed pagination reduces error;
  Frontend content-sized safety makes any residual error non-destructive.
- Table/list continuation could alter source navigation: share anchor plus exact
  continuation/range metadata and test multi-page selection in both surfaces.
- Raw HTML/link/image content can create XSS or tracking: omit raw HTML support,
  enforce allowlisted URL transformation and prohibit unapproved image fetches.
- New layout fields could break old clients: all additions optional, legacy
  fields retained, and API compatibility tests cover both versions.
- Full repository coverage may remain below the 80% release gate: report exact
  numbers without relaxing thresholds; new logic must independently exceed 80%.

  `desktop-worker2`; the bounded ten-second test times out. This one-way result

  The remaining target is DaemonSet-owned `kube-system/kindnet-dfbkj` UID
  `c5143059-7cd8-491e-957d-bf31cc1efeba` on `desktop-worker2`.

No resource outside the first approved Pod was deleted or restarted. No Helm,
application-data, PVC, Secret, identity, index, layout or Provider change
occurred. Final acceptance remains blocked pending a separately UID-bound R2
repair for the remaining worker2 kindnet member.

## CHG-283 Markdown-Faithful Display And Retrieval-Only Embedding Plan

Status: Gate 4 was approved by Peter on 2026-08-30; Gate 5 repository
implementation completed with the release/integration gaps recorded below.
Gate 2 was confirmed with
`同意 CHG-283 Gate 2，採用上述建議`. Peter approved Gate 4 with
`Peter approves CHG-283 Markdown-Faithful Display And Retrieval-Only Embedding`.
Repository implementation, additive V047 source and non-Provider/disposable
feature tests are authorized. Image build, deployment, Provider call, reprocess,
re-embed, reindex and live application-data/index mutation remain separately
gated.

- Approved by: Peter
- Approval date: 2026-08-30
- Approval evidence: `Peter approves CHG-283 Markdown-Faithful Display And Retrieval-Only Embedding`

### Objective And Evidence

- Make every authorized full-content reading surface render a deterministic
  Markdown representation instead of attempting to reconstruct Markdown
  semantics from `Chunk.content/display_text`.
- Make every future Embedding Build fail closed unless its exact input is a
  validated, versioned `retrieval_text`; raw/display Markdown and display text
  must never be Provider fallback inputs.
- Bring manual create, edit and split paths under the same parse/display/
  normalize/hash contract as automatic CHG-281 ingestion.
- Gate 1 evidence is concrete: Knowledge Detail retains
  `chunk.markdown_content` but `ChunkPreview` renders only `chunk.content`;
  `embeddings._chunk_text()` currently resolves
  `retrieval_text or content or markdown_content`; manual create/edit/split
  assign `retrieval_text=content`; staging and publish writers also project
  `retrieval_text or content`. These compatibility paths can silently erase
  Markdown presentation or allow unprocessed Markdown into a future build.

### Confirmed Scope

In scope for repository Gate 5 after Gate 4:

1. Add nullable `chunks.display_markdown` through additive Flyway V047, ORM and
   API/debug projections; do not backfill existing rows in the migration.
2. Extend the CHG-281 parser/chunker boundary to build deterministic,
   chunk-specific `display_markdown` alongside exact `markdown_content`, plain
   `content/display_text` and normalized `retrieval_text`.
3. Preserve only the selected items/rows/lines in split list/table/code display
   Markdown while repeating necessary ordinal/header/fence context.
4. Add one manual Chunk representation factory shared by create, edit and split
   so all four representations, versions, token count and hashes are derived
   through the existing AST and normalizer.
5. Replace embedding/build/index fallback with one strict retrieval-input
   resolver for all new/rebuilt data. Missing or inconsistent retrieval
   evidence fails before Provider, build-vector, index or manifest mutation.
6. Keep legacy null rows and already-active indexes readable through explicitly
   read-only compatibility paths; prohibit that fallback from new build/index
   readiness.
7. Add one shared Frontend Markdown-content view/source selector and use it for
   Knowledge Detail Chunk, Approval Evidence, Knowledge Graph Chunk inspector
   and authorized Chat citation detail. Rendered original and raw-source tab
   contracts remain intact.
8. Give inline `<code>` and the other shared semantic elements reusable classes
   whose core presentation does not depend on an outer route-specific wrapper.
9. Add authorization-safe additive Chat/Graph response fields only where the
   full display Markdown must be rehydrated; do not persist raw body content in
   ChatRecord citation evidence.

Out of scope for repository Gate 4:

- Reprocessing or backfilling the current 26 active legacy Chunks, generating
  vectors, calling an OCR/Embedding/LLM Provider, creating a new application
  OpenSearch index, switching an active manifest or running a retrieval-quality
  evaluation.
- Image build, Helm render/write, Kubernetes mutation or authenticated live-data
  write. Those actions require separate immutable image/render/resource/data
  approvals after repository verification.
- Changing the default LLM generation context from `display_text`, changing
  prompts/models, rewriting canonical Markdown, modifying existing vectors or
  changing the meaning of existing ChatRecord answers/citations.
- Rendering compact titles, list summaries or score rows as full Markdown.
  Those remain safe display-text projections.

### Target Representation Contract

```text
canonical Markdown artifact
  └─ exact source fragment        -> Chunk.markdown_content
       ├─ chunk display projection -> Chunk.display_markdown -> SafeMarkdown UI
       ├─ visible text projection  -> Chunk.content/display_text -> preview/LLM
       └─ semantic normalization   -> Chunk.retrieval_text -> BM25/Embedding
                                                └─ embedding_vector
```

- `markdown_content` stays exact and traceable even when one source node is
  divided into multiple semantic Chunks.
- `display_markdown` is derived rather than canonical. It may repeat necessary
  table headers, list ordinals or code fences, but it may not rewrite business
  text or include retrieval prefixes.
- `retrieval_text` remains a normalized semantic body with bounded document and
  heading context. It is never rendered as user-facing Markdown.
- `embedding_content_hash` binds retrieval text and its processing/model
  versions. A display-only change must not change the hash.

### Backend Design

#### Additive persistence and API

- Add `sql/migrations/V047__markdown_display_and_retrieval_only_embedding.sql`
  with only nullable `chunks.display_markdown text`, its comment and one safe
  migration-audit row. No data update/backfill is allowed.
- Add the nullable ORM field and additive response/debug fields. Maintain old
  client compatibility when the field is null.
- Full Markdown returned through Graph or Chat citation APIs must be hydrated
  only after the existing Project/version/Chunk authorization checks. It must
  not be written to Neo4j, ChatRecord `reference_docs`, general logs or error
  envelopes.

#### Display projection

- Extend `ChunkDraft` with `display_markdown` and keep `raw_markdown` exact.
  Common blocks use the exact source where it matches the Chunk unit.
- List/table/code splitters construct a safe Markdown projection from AST node
  children: preserve source ordinal/start/value and nesting; repeat table
  headers for each selected row batch; preserve code fence language and only
  selected lines. The visible-text projection must equal the Chunk's intended
  display content modulo structural whitespace.
- Add deterministic display-projection version metadata. Display projection
  version changes alone do not invalidate `retrieval_text` or vectors.

#### Manual representation factory

- Introduce a focused domain helper consumed by manual create, edit and split.
  It accepts the validated canonical fragment/source range, inherited document
  title, heading/page metadata, configuration and requested edit content.
- Parse Markdown through `MarkdownStructureParser`, build display Markdown and
  visible text, normalize retrieval text through `RetrievalTextNormalizer`,
  calculate token/hash/version evidence and return one typed representation.
- Remove every direct `retrieval_text=content` and synthetic
  `markdown_content=content` shortcut from those paths. Reconciliation may be
  queued only after representation validation succeeds.

#### Strict embedding and index readiness

- Replace the multipurpose `_chunk_text()` fallback with explicit resolvers:
  one strict resolver for new/rebuilt embedding and index work, and one clearly
  named legacy read-only projection where compatibility still requires it.
- Strict resolution requires non-empty `retrieval_text`, normalizer/tokenizer/
  parser evidence where applicable and a matching fingerprint/hash contract.
  It raises a stable safe error such as `retrieval_reprocessing_required`
  before opening a Provider request or persisting a build.
- Staging and publish writers may not use `retrieval_text or content` to claim a
  v2-ready field. They verify the completed build fingerprint, vector checksum,
  model/profile/dimension and Chunk retrieval hash before the first index write.
- Existing active legacy indexes remain queryable. A legacy Chunk can enter a
  new build only through a separately approved extraction revision that
  generates all CHG-283 representations.

### Frontend Design

- Add one shared `ChunkMarkdownView` or equivalent source-selection component.
  It accepts distinct `displayMarkdown`, `rawMarkdown` and `displayText` values,
  selects in that order under the approved legacy fallback contract and passes
  only a complete source to `SafeMarkdown`.
- Knowledge Detail must stop sending only `chunk.content` to `SafeMarkdown`.
  Approval must stop overloading its local `content` property with
  `markdown_content`. Graph and authorized Chat citation detail use the same
  component; compact cards continue to use safe text previews.
- Truncated Markdown must never be passed to the full renderer because it can
  break fences, tables or links. Citation cards may remain truncated plain text;
  the expanded detail receives the complete authorized display representation.
- `SafeMarkdownInline` and block mode share stable semantic component classes.
  Inline code presentation is defined on the code component/class itself, not
  only `.safe-markdown code`. Existing raw-HTML, URL/image and citation security
  policy remains unchanged.

### Planned File Changes

| File/area | Planned purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `sql/migrations/V047__markdown_display_and_retrieval_only_embedding.sql` | Add nullable display projection only; no row backfill. |
| `backend/app/db/models.py`, `backend/app/api/schemas.py` | Add nullable `display_markdown` contracts. |
| `backend/app/domain/markdown_structure.py`, `structure_chunking.py` | Preserve AST/raw ranges and generate chunk-specific display Markdown. |
| `backend/app/domain/retrieval_text.py` | Retain semantic normalizer; expose typed use by the manual factory. |
| New/focused manual representation domain helper | Centralize manual create/edit/split raw/display/retrieval derivation. |
| `backend/app/api/routes/documents.py` | Remove direct representation assignments; use the shared factory. |
| `backend/app/domain/embeddings.py` | Add strict retrieval-only input resolver and fail-closed evidence. |
| `backend/app/domain/extraction_pipeline.py`, `review_publish.py` | Enforce retrieval/build/index consistency and serialize display metadata without indexing it. |
| `backend/app/api/routes/serving.py`, Graph response path | Authorized display-Markdown hydration only where full detail is requested. |
| `frontend/src/lib/api.ts` | Add nullable display-Markdown response types. |
| New shared Chunk Markdown component | Central source selection and SafeMarkdown rendering. |
| Knowledge Detail, Approval, Graph, Chat evidence components | Adopt the shared component; retain compact text summaries. |
| `frontend/src/components/SafeMarkdown.tsx`, `globals.css` | Stable semantic classes and identical inline-code presentation. |
| Focused Backend/Frontend tests | Fail-first representation, strict embedding, authorization, parity and invariance evidence. |
| Governance artifacts | Keep spec, changelog, plan, test design and traceability synchronized. |

### Task Breakdown After Gate 4

   raw/display Markdown/display text/retrieval text separation.
2. Add fail-first split list/table/code fixtures, then implement deterministic
   `display_markdown` generation and V047/additive API support.

### Test Strategy And Planned Commands

Focused requirement IDs are detailed in `TEST_PLAN.md`. Repository verification
after Gate 4 will use the narrowest applicable commands, followed by broader
gates:

```bash
./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor
./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace
./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor
./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved
./HARNESS/harness.sh backend:syntax
./HARNESS/harness.sh test:backend
./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:lint
./HARNESS/harness.sh test:frontend
./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:build
./HARNESS/harness.sh coverage:check
./HARNESS/harness.sh helm:lint
./HARNESS/harness.sh deploy:config-policy
```

- Pure parser/normalizer/resolver tests use the real implementation and no
  Provider. Disposable PostgreSQL migration/API tests use the real configured
  database or report unavailable under `TEST-002`.
- A real billable Provider assertion, reprocess/re-embed/reindex quality pilot,
  authenticated Browser acceptance, image build and Helm deployment are not
  represented by repository tests and remain separately gated.
- New Backend/Frontend application logic must meet at least 80% line and branch
  coverage. Existing repository-wide coverage gaps remain release gates and may
  not be relaxed.

### Migration, Rollback And Data Boundaries

- V047 is forward-compatible and nullable. Rolling application code back leaves
  an unused nullable column and does not require destructive down migration.
- Gate 5 must prove zero updates to pre-existing Chunk representations, vectors,
  builds, OpenSearch documents, manifests and Provider usage. Existing 26 active
  Chunks remain legacy/null until an exact data action is approved.
- A later pilot must identify the exact Project/document/version, canonical
  artifact digest, model/profile, expected Chunk/index counts, Provider budget,
  new staging-index name, validation metrics and rollback/manifest boundary.
  It may not overwrite the current active index in place.

### Risks And Mitigations

- Exact raw spans for one large list/table can cover the full parent node while
  a semantic Chunk contains only a subset. Separate `display_markdown` avoids
  corrupting traceability or duplicating the full parent in every card.
- Manual source ranges can be ambiguous after edits. The representation factory
  must fail closed on unresolved mapping rather than inventing raw text.
- Exposing full source Markdown through Chat/Graph can leak authorized document
  content if scope checks drift. Hydration stays Backend-owned, scoped and
  non-persistent, with denial/no-existence parity tests.
- Strict retrieval-only enforcement will intentionally block legacy rebuilds
  that previously appeared to work through fallback. The stable error must
  direct operators to reprocess instead of weakening the contract.
- Display Markdown generation may preserve semantics while changing harmless
  whitespace. Tests compare semantic DOM and visible-text projection in addition
  to exact canonical raw-source invariance.

## CHG-284 Original-Chunk Range And Markdown Presentation Parity Plan

### Gate Status And Approval Boundary

- Gate 1 completed on 2026-08-30 with read-only repository and live
  `docker-desktop` evidence.
- Gate 2 confirmation: complete. Peter confirmed Gate 2 with `OK`, accepting the correct right Chunk as the
  range/content/style baseline and the no-data/no-vector/no-Provider boundary.
- Gate 4 approval: approved by Peter on 2026-08-30.
- This section is the Gate 3 development plan. Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-08-30 with
  `Peter approves CHG-284 Original-Chunk Range And Markdown Presentation Parity`;
  repository implementation and non-Provider feature tests are complete. Image
  build, Helm write and data/index/Provider actions remain separately gated.

### Scope And Root Cause

The live fixture proves the Chunk canonical range `[64,373)` is correct and
contains one paragraph plus one ordered list. Backend persists one mapping whose
`source_anchor` is only the first paragraph while `node_ids` contains the
paragraph, list and list-item children. Frontend reduces this to the single
anchor, so the list cannot be highlighted or reverse-selected. Separately,
`document_layout` persists list-item visible text after inline Markdown has been
stripped, so the Original viewer cannot reproduce the correct right Chunk's
`<strong>` semantics even though both eventually call safe renderers.

In scope:

1. Formalize ordered renderable source anchors and exact validation at the shared
   Backend read/write mapping boundary.
2. Preserve safe canonical inline representation for layout leaf content and
   hydrate legacy artifacts read-only where canonical evidence exists.
3. Make all relevant Frontend selection, reverse lookup, scroll and interaction
   paths consume every resolved renderable anchor.
4. Render Original leaf semantics through the shared SafeMarkdown boundary and
   shared semantic design tokens while preserving paper/pagination chrome.
5. Add focused Backend, Frontend, compatibility, Browser and preservation tests.

Out of scope:

- changing Chunk boundaries, counts, titles, token counts or any raw/display/
  retrieval representation;
- OCR, extraction revision creation, reprocess, re-embedding, reindexing,
  manifest switch or Provider calls;
- PostgreSQL migration, application-row or stored-artifact rewrite;
- image build, Helm render/write, Kubernetes mutation or deployed authenticated
  acceptance without a later exact action approval;
- pixel-identical wrapping between differently sized Original and Chunk panels.

### Planned Implementation

#### A. Backend Mapping Contract

- Extend source-mapping response/types with optional ordered
  `source_anchors` and, where needed, per-anchor exact range evidence.
- Build new mappings from renderable top-level structure units rather than
  `draft.node_ids[0]`; retain the existing exact global fragment/range/hash.
- Add one shared resolver that intersects stored `node_ids`/ranges with the
  actual document layout/structure. It must exclude structural-only children,
  return document-order anchors and fail unresolved when ranges disagree.
- Stop treating a first-node local range spanning the entire multi-block Chunk
  as valid merely because the global canonical fragment hash matches.
- Candidate files: `backend/app/domain/extraction_pipeline.py`,
  `backend/app/domain/markdown_artifacts.py`, source-mapping response schemas and
  their callers.

#### B. Backend Layout Semantic Representation

- Extend layout block/list-item/table-cell payloads with optional
  `inline_markdown` or an equivalent serializable typed inline AST produced from
  canonical Markdown AST nodes.
- Preserve `text` for compatibility, accessibility fallback and measurements.
- For legacy layout artifacts, hydrate inline representation from the authorized
  canonical artifact/structure without persisting a rewrite. Never infer markup
  from plain text.
- Keep pagination, continuation identity, ordered-list start/value and range
  behavior unchanged.
- Candidate files: `backend/app/domain/markdown_structure.py`,
  `backend/app/domain/document_layout.py`, response schemas and read services.

#### C. Frontend Mapping And Navigation

- Extend `ResolvedSourceMapping` to retain the authoritative ordered renderable
  anchors.
- Update selected-anchor construction, reverse lookup, interaction filtering and
  selected-Chunk scrolling to use all resolved anchors and the first visible
  document-order anchor.
- Keep Raw Markdown global-offset segmentation unchanged.
- Candidate files: `frontend/src/lib/markdownSourceMapping.ts`, Knowledge Detail
  and Approval Evidence consumers, and `DocumentLayoutViewer.tsx`.

#### D. Frontend Markdown Presentation

- Render layout leaf `inline_markdown ?? text` through `SafeMarkdownInline` and
  use block-mode `SafeMarkdown` where the layout unit is a complete Markdown
  block.
- Consolidate paragraph/list/list-item/strong/inline-code/table/blockquote core
  semantic classes/design tokens with `ChunkMarkdownView`.
- Preserve paper/page/footer/highlight and chunk-card chrome as surface-specific
  layout. Do not force identical line wrapping.
- Candidate files: `DocumentLayoutViewer.tsx`, `ChunkMarkdownView.tsx`, shared
  SafeMarkdown components and scoped rules in `globals.css`.

### Test Strategy

- Backend unit tests cover paragraph+list multi-anchor construction, exclusion
  of list-item children, exact per-anchor validation, inline strong/code/link
  preservation, continuation behavior, deterministic order and fail-closed
  legacy resolution.
- Frontend component tests cover selecting one Chunk highlights both blocks,
  clicking either block selects the same Chunk, first-anchor scroll, unresolved
  non-interaction, continuation blocks and Raw Markdown range parity.
- Cross-surface tests compare Original and right Chunk semantic DOM/visible text
  for paragraph, ordered list, strong and inline code, plus shared computed core
  style; surface width/chrome is intentionally excluded from equality.
- Compatibility tests use old payloads without `source_anchors` or inline
  representation and prove safe fallback/no invented semantics.
- New/changed logic must meet at least 80% line and branch coverage. Existing
  repository-wide coverage gaps remain visible and cannot be relaxed.
- Tests must not call an OCR/Embedding/LLM Provider or mutate live application
  data/indexes.

### Risks And Mitigations

- **Structural child over-selection:** never expose raw `node_ids` directly;
  intersect with actual renderable layout anchors.
- **False resolved status:** validate anchor-local evidence separately from the
  global canonical fragment and fail closed.
- **Legacy formatting loss:** hydrate only from canonical AST/ranges; otherwise
  show plain text rather than guessing.
- **Continuation duplication:** retain CHG-282 original anchor/continuation
  identity and deduplicate source anchors before selection.
- **CSS regressions:** share semantic tokens, not surface geometry, and compare
  semantic DOM/computed core properties in Chromium.
- **Unintended retrieval impact:** assert unchanged Chunk representations/hashes
  and zero Provider/index/manifest side effects.

### Rollback And Delivery

Repository rollback is limited to CHG-284 code/tests/docs because no migration
or stored-data change is planned. A later image/deployment action must use new
immutable tags, a reproducible hidden-Secret server render and rollback-on-
failure, and must be separately approved with protected-resource baselines. The
repository implementation itself does not authorize that delivery action.

### Exit Criteria

- All `KDETAIL-MAP-*`, `KDETAIL-DISPLAY-*`, `KDETAIL-STYLE-*` and
  `KDETAIL-COMPAT-*` tests pass at their authorized level.
- The live regression shape is represented by an executable fixture: exactly two
  renderable anchors, no child-node over-selection, bidirectional navigation and
  equivalent paragraph/list/strong semantics.
- Raw Markdown exact-range behavior and CHG-273/281/282/283 regressions pass.
- New logic meets 80% focused line/branch coverage; broader gaps are reported.
- Static deployment/governance checks pass, with no Provider, live data/index,
  image or Kubernetes action.

## CHG-285 One Chunk One Visual Selection Group Plan

### Gate State And Approval Boundary

- Gate 1 read-only diagnosis completed on 2026-08-31 using the deployed CHG-284
  regression shape. The right card remains one Chunk and the canonical range is
  `[64,373)`. The database has one mapping with paragraph/list plus structural
  list-item nodes; the authorized read path correctly resolves two renderable
  anchors. Per-anchor Original CSS and multiline inline Markdown outline create
  the misleading multiple-box presentation.
- Gate 2 confirmation: complete on 2026-08-31.
- Peter approved Gate 2 with
  `同意 CHG-285 Gate 2，採用上述建議`, including the recommendation that a
  cross-page Chunk renders at most one group enclosure per physical page with a
  shared Chunk identity rather than one rectangle through the paper gap.
- Gate 4 implementation approval: APPROVED. Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-08-31
  with `Peter approves CHG-285 One Chunk One Visual Selection Group`.
- This section is the Gate 3 development plan. Peter approved Gate 4 with
  `Peter approves CHG-285 One Chunk One Visual Selection Group`; repository
  Frontend implementation and non-deployed verification may proceed. Image
  build, Helm render/write, Kubernetes mutation and data/index/Provider action
  remain outside this approval.
- Approved Gate 4 phrase:
  `Peter approves CHG-285 One Chunk One Visual Selection Group`.
- Gate 4, when granted, authorizes only repository Frontend code, tests and
  governance verification. Image build, Helm delivery and authenticated deployed
  Browser acceptance remain separate exact-action approvals.

### Scope And Design Decisions

1. Preserve CHG-284's Backend-authoritative `source_anchors`, exact canonical
   ranges, per-anchor reverse navigation, Markdown semantics and fail-closed
   behavior. CHG-285 consumes that evidence only at the Frontend view layer.
2. Represent the current selection as deterministic Chunk groups rather than an
   anchor-only `Set`. Each group carries `chunkId`, ordered source anchors and
   exact Markdown ranges. Multiple selected Chunks remain separate groups.
3. In rendered Original, partition each Chunk's anchors by physical page and
   adjacency. Consecutive mapped blocks on the same page render inside one
   selection-group surface whose background includes the existing inter-block
   spacing. Its children retain their current source-anchor DOM identity and
   click/keyboard handlers but do not draw independent active cards.
4. A cross-page Chunk renders one page-local group per page with the same
   `data-chunk-id`/accessible identity. A non-contiguous or inconsistent mapping
   is never expanded across an unrelated block; it produces safe contiguous
   fragments under the same Chunk identity or the existing fail-closed fallback.
5. In Raw Markdown, retain the exact mapped text segments for interaction and
   offset calculation but move the visible border/background to a chunk-level
   geometry layer. One enclosure is measured from the selected canonical range,
   independent of the browser's inline line boxes. Recompute after source/view
   changes, responsive reflow, font/layout resize and zoom without changing the
   preformatted source or copied text.
6. Keep the established NomoSmart Calm Green/Fresh Mint/Slate design tokens; the
   UI design review adds clear focus state, non-color active semantics, stable
   150–300ms transitions and `prefers-reduced-motion` handling rather than
   introducing a new palette or styling framework.
7. Preserve selection scroll-to-first-anchor, reverse selection, manual text
   selection/chunk creation, link behavior, keyboard order and the CHG-282
   pagination safety boundary.

| `frontend/src/app/project/[id]/knowledge/[knowledgeId]/page.tsx` | Pass selected Chunk group identity/ranges to both Original and Markdown viewers while retaining current selection and scroll handlers. | `KDETAIL-GROUP-001`, `KDETAIL-GROUP-COMPAT-001` |
| `frontend/src/components/DocumentLayoutViewer.tsx` | Partition selected anchors into same-page contiguous groups; render one group surface while keeping child anchor interaction and continuation behavior. | `KDETAIL-GROUP-002`, `KDETAIL-GROUP-A11Y-001` |
| `frontend/src/components/CanonicalMarkdownSource.tsx` | Keep exact interactive segments and add one measured/structured visual enclosure per selected Chunk range with resize/reflow lifecycle safety. | `KDETAIL-GROUP-003`, `KDETAIL-GROUP-A11Y-001` |

### Deployment, Migration, Risks And Rollback

- No migration or reprocessing is required. Existing documents gain the corrected
  view after a future approved Frontend image/Helm rollout.
- Primary risks are wrapper-induced pagination geometry changes, measured overlay
  drift after reflow/zoom, pointer interception, overlapping selection ambiguity
  and loss of individual anchor focus. Tests above are release-blocking for those
  risks.
- Repository rollback is limited to CHG-285 Frontend code/tests/docs. There is no
  data, schema, vector, index, manifest or Provider rollback because none is in
  scope.

## CHG-286 Explicit-profile One-click Installer And Positive Installation Guide Plan

### Status and Gate

- Gate 1 read-only characterization: complete on 2026-08-31.
- Gate 2 decision confirmation: complete. Peter confirmed the five recommended
  decisions on 2026-08-31 with `確認 Gate 2，採用上述五項建議`.
- Gate 3: complete in this plan and the synchronized specification, changelog,
  test design and traceability.
- Gate 4 implementation approval: approved.
- Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-08-31 with
  `Peter approves CHG-286 Explicit-profile One-click Installer And Positive Installation Guide`.
- CHG-286 wrapper, template, release-package and README implementation plus the
  approved non-destructive/disposable verification may now begin.

### Specification Understanding

The existing Kubernetes deployment implementation remains
`deploy/installer/nomosmart-install`. The shell wrapper is a safe operator
orchestration layer that already runs plan, requires confirmation, derives
install/resume/verify from status and preserves protected identity checkpoints.
The typed TOML and Helm chart already support two strict named profiles:

- `bundled` deploys the NomoSmart application plus PostgreSQL, Redis, RustFS,
  OpenSearch, Neo4j and Keycloak in one Kubernetes release;
- `external-services` deploys only the NomoSmart application tier and required
  Jobs, while operator-owned external services, runtime Secret and CA inputs
  remain untouched.

CHG-286 makes that profile choice visible at the one-click boundary, adds a
safe way to initialize the matching non-secret TOML, keeps the signed release
package complete for both profiles and makes the root installation journey
accurate and encouraging. It does not add a third topology, per-service mixed
mode, infrastructure provisioning or destructive lifecycle command.

### Discussion And Confirmation Items

Gate 2 resolved every scope decision:

1. Keep one `nomosmart-one-click` entry point and add explicit
   `--profile bundled|external-services` plus safe config initialization.
2. Update both examples, wrapper/release tests and signed-package contents.
3. Make signed release package acquisition and verification the normal
   Kubernetes Production entry; the install host needs no Git or image builder.
4. Rewrite the root installation guide in a positive, detailed and complete
   step-by-step style while retaining fail-closed safety and linked runbooks.
5. Keep Docker Compose as its existing single-host full-stack journey; do not
   merge it into the Kubernetes wrapper.

Remaining blocking questions: none. Gate 4 is approved.

### Development Plan

#### Scope

In scope after Gate 4:

- `deploy/installer/nomosmart-one-click` help, parsing, profile validation,
  config initialization and positive actionable messages;
- `deploy/installer/nomosmart-install.example.toml` and
  `deploy/installer/nomosmart-install.external-services.example.toml` comments
  needed to align the new commands and responsibility boundary;
- focused wrapper tests, installer live acceptance coverage and signed release
  closed-inventory assertions;
- `README.md`, `deploy/installer/README.md` and
  `deploy/release/PACKAGE_README.md`; update another deployment/package guide
  only when a command or responsibility link would otherwise become stale;
- traceability and verification evidence for both profiles.

Out of scope:

- Docker Compose CLI/orchestration changes;
- Helm topology or values-schema changes unless implementation finds a direct
  conformance defect, which must stop and return to specification first;
- VM, OS, Kubernetes/RKE2, DNS, CA, Ingress Controller, StorageClass, registry
  or directory-server provisioning;
- mixed bundled/external service selection for new installs;
- upgrade, restore, rotation, uninstall, reset, permanent deletion or any live
  UAT/Production mutation;
- application API, database schema, migration, Frontend/Backend product code,
  Secret values or external-service credential changes.

#### CLI And Config Design

1. Extend argument parsing with:

   ```text
   --profile bundled|external-services
   --init-config
   ```

   `--profile` is required for `--init-config` and is the documented form for
   plan/apply commands. Existing config-only calls remain compatible for this
   release: the wrapper parses and displays the config profile, then prints the
   equivalent explicit command as a migration hint.

2. Validate the selected profile before invoking `nomosmart-install`. Use
   Python 3 `tomllib` or the existing typed config boundary instead of an ad-hoc
   shell regex. A mismatch, invalid TOML or unsupported profile exits `20`,
   reports that no cluster change was requested and gives a safe correction.

3. Implement `--init-config` as a local-only operation:

   - require `--config PATH` and explicit `--profile`;
   - select the adjacent bundled or external-services example from the same
     verified source/package;
   - verify the selected profile's chart/values in that package and resolve the
     generated config's chart/values to absolute paths in the same immutable
     package, because the config itself lives outside the package;
   - require an existing owner-private parent directory;
   - reject an existing destination, symlink or destination inside the
     extracted release package/repository template area;
   - create one regular file without overwrite and force mode `0600`;
   - verify the resulting typed profile, print the created path/profile/mode and
     show the next edit and `--plan-only` command;
   - never invoke kubectl/Helm/the guided installer and never generate/read a
     Secret value.

4. Keep current plan/digest/install/resume/status/verify behavior unchanged.
   Display the selected profile and concise responsibility summary before the
   read-only plan. Keep `--yes`, matching `--confirm-digest`, identity checkpoint
   and all existing exit-code/security semantics.

5. Refine messages to be positive and actionable without weakening truth:
   lead with the preserved/safe state, state the exact problem, then give one
   next command or linked action. Never call blocked/unavailable/failed output a
   success and never reveal config secrets or raw installer internals.

#### Documentation Design

1. Correct root README anchors and split acquisition by journey:

   - signed package acquisition, independent signer fingerprint and package
     verification for Kubernetes bundled/external-services;
   - source clone/exact checkout only for Docker Compose source/local use and
     Engineering Development.

2. Define every placeholder before first use, including release package path,
   signer fingerprint, private installer directory, config path, public URL and
   service diagnostic name. Use safe copyable quoting and no shell metacharacter
   placeholder that can be interpreted as redirection or substitution.

3. Give bundled and external-services independent numbered journeys. Each step
   retains the existing seven fields: purpose, prerequisite, replacement,
   command/operator action, observable success, safe handling when incomplete
   and next step. The journeys cover tools/capacity, package verification,
   private directory, config init/edit, Secret/CA/identity responsibilities,
   plan, digest approval, install/resume, identity checkpoint, status, verify,
   first login and post-install acceptance.

4. Keep root README complete as a journey but link authoritative release,
   Secret/TLS, recovery, upgrade, rollback and destructive lifecycle details to
   their existing runbooks. Do not duplicate Secret values or dangerous
   procedures.

5. Retain Docker Compose and Development workflows while correcting only links,
   prerequisites and wording needed for consistency. State clearly that
   Compose is single-host/non-HA and not controlled by the Kubernetes wrapper.

#### Implementation Tasks After Gate 4

1. Add fail-first wrapper guardrail tests for parsing, explicit profiles,
   compatibility inference, config initialization and all safe failure cases.
2. Implement profile parsing/validation and `--init-config` in the wrapper,
   preserving the existing installer delegation and confirmation flow.
3. Align both TOML examples and installer/package documentation.
4. Expand release-package tests so both templates, executable wrapper and
   updated docs are required by the signed closed inventory and tamper checks.
5. Rewrite root README's acquisition and both Kubernetes journeys, repair
   anchors/links and retain Compose/Development/post-install sections.
6. Run narrow syntax/unit/document checks, then broader installer/release,
   governance, Helm/config-policy and live disposable profile acceptance as
   prerequisites permit.
7. Record exact passed, failed and blocked evidence in TEST_PLAN.md and
   TRACEABILITY.md; do not claim Production readiness from static checks.

### Test Strategy

Guardrail tests:

- help lists exactly `bundled` and `external-services`, the init behavior,
  compatibility note and non-destructive boundary;
- both profile/template selections create a new `0600` regular file with the
  exact typed profile and no Secret value;
- existing destination, symlink, unsafe parent, unknown profile, malformed TOML
  and profile mismatch stop before any underlying installer invocation;
- explicit and compatible inferred-profile plan/install/resume/status/verify
  sequences preserve current exit codes, digest confirmation and checkpoints;
- output is redacted, positive/actionable and gives the next safe command;
- package assembly/verification includes the executable wrapper, both examples
  and current docs, and rejects tamper/missing inventory;
- root README links, anchors, commands, placeholders, profile terms and journey
  ordering are machine-checked.

Live acceptance required for behavior claims:

- one real disposable Kubernetes bundled install/resume/status/verify journey
  with the real chart, services, TLS, OIDC/directory and readiness;
- one real disposable external-services journey using real PostgreSQL, Redis,
  S3, OpenSearch, Neo4j and Keycloak endpoints plus existing runtime/CA Secrets;
- prove the external journey renders/creates no bundled peripheral workloads
  and does not modify external service data, credential or lifecycle state;
- preserve `TEST-002`: fake wrapper binaries may test command ordering only and
  cannot satisfy runtime acceptance. Missing services are reported blocked or
  unavailable rather than passed.

Coverage and regression:

- new executable wrapper/config-selection logic must achieve at least 80% line
  and branch coverage in the narrow useful harness;
- existing installer/release suites, Helm named-profile renders, deployment
  policy and shell syntax remain green;
- repository-wide Frontend/Backend 80% gates remain release requirements and
  cannot be reduced for this documentation/deployment-wrapper change.

### Deployment And Configuration Impact

- No application runtime configuration, API, database migration or Helm values
  schema is planned.
- The TOML `deployment_profile` remains the deployment source of truth;
  `--profile` is a safety assertion and user-facing selector, not a second
  topology engine.
- Existing config-only wrapper calls remain valid for this release with a
  visible migration hint. New docs and packages always use explicit profile.
- No environment is mutated by repository implementation or static tests.
  Disposable live acceptance needs separately configured safe targets; current
  UAT/Production changes remain separately gated.

### Risks And Mitigations

- **CLI/profile divergence:** parse with the typed TOML boundary and stop before
  plan/status when values differ.
- **Accidental config overwrite or disclosure:** exclusive creation, symlink and
  parent checks, mode `0600`, no Secret generation and redaction assertions.
- **Breaking existing automation:** preserve config-only inference for this
  release and emit the exact explicit-profile replacement command.
- **External profile accidentally deploying peripherals:** retain strict Helm
  profile policy and add render plus real-cluster negative inventory checks.
- **README/package drift:** package closed-inventory checks and executable/link/
  command tests bind docs to the same reviewed source.
- **Positive wording obscuring a failure:** require status truth and exit codes
  first; positive language supplies a safe next step but never converts failure
  into success.

Rollback is limited to wrapper, examples, tests and documentation. Existing
config files remain valid, no data migration exists and no live deployment is
authorized by this Gate 4 request.

### Planned Verification Commands After Gate 4

```bash
sh -n deploy/installer/nomosmart-one-click
./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor
./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace
./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor
./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved
./HARNESS/harness.sh test:installer
./HARNESS/harness.sh test:release
./HARNESS/harness.sh helm:lint
./HARNESS/harness.sh deploy:config-policy
./HARNESS/harness.sh integration:installer-live
./HARNESS/harness.sh integration:release-live
```

The live selectors run only when their real disposable cluster, services,
trusted TLS, directory/OIDC and release prerequisites are present. Exact missing
prerequisites and command outcomes must be reported.

### Plan Approval

Gate 4 is approved. Approval authorizes only the repository files, non-destructive
guardrail tests and disposable live acceptance described above. It does not
authorize current UAT/Production mutation, external credential changes,
uninstall, reset, deletion or any application-data operation.

## CHG-287 Project Detail Owner Authorization Consistency Plan

Status: Gate 1 root-cause analysis completed on 2026-09-02. Peter confirmed the
scope at Gate 2 under the provisional CHG-286 identifier, then approved the
collision-safe renumbering with
`同意將本次修正改編為 CHG-287，Gate 2 範圍不變`. Gate 3 planning is complete;
Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-09-02 with
`Peter approves CHG-287 Project Detail Owner Authorization Consistency`.

### Scope And Root Cause

The deployed database proves `user01@nomosmart.test` is an active MAAS Owner in
both `project_owners` and `project_members`. Its effective role also has the
existing ProjectMembers permissions. The deployed Backend nevertheless serializes
the single-project detail as `is_owner=false` while the same response computes
`capabilities.can_manage_lifecycle=true`.

`list_projects` explicitly attaches `is_owner` and current roles to each ORM
instance, but `get_project` returns the object from `get_scoped_project` after
attaching capabilities only. Because `is_owner` is a response-only field with a
schema default, serialization silently emits `false`. The project workspace
uses that false value as its Owner-only Permission Management gate.

This is a conformance repair for `PROJECT-002` and new consistency requirement
`PROJECT-008`; it is not a new authorization model.

### Approved Design Decisions

1. Add one shared Backend Project response-projection function in the existing
   project access/domain area. It receives the session, Project and current
   `IdentityContext` (or its explicit user/scope values) and deterministically
   attaches `is_owner`, deduplicated/sorted `current_user_project_roles`, and
   existing `project_capabilities`.
2. Use the shared projection for both list and detail and for every route that
   returns `ProjectResponse`, including create/update, archive lifecycle and
   member-removal responses. Do not duplicate Owner queries in each route.
3. Keep `ProjectResponse` fields, endpoint methods and Frontend contract
   unchanged. Do not introduce `can_manage_members` as a second authority or use
   `can_manage_lifecycle` as a Frontend workaround.
4. Preserve mutation-time Backend authorization. Projection controls response
   truth and UI state only; it never grants scope or replaces
   `require_project_owner`.
5. Add fail-first coverage before implementation, then run focused and broader
   governance/test/build checks. Live mutation acceptance must use disposable
   data or an exact later approval; repository Gate 4 does not authorize changing
   current MAAS membership.

### Planned Changes And Traceability

| File / module | Planned change | Requirements |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend/app/domain/project_access.py` | Add the shared current-user Project response projection, reusing existing role/capability policy. | `PROJECT-008` |
| `backend/app/api/routes/projects.py` | Replace route-specific/missing response decoration with the shared projection across list/detail and ProjectResponse mutations. | `PROJECT-002`, `PROJECT-008` |
| `backend/tests/test_chg287_project_owner_projection.py` or the closest existing live Backend suite | Fail-first Owner/detail/list parity, role deduplication, non-Owner and serialization-path regressions without mocked authorization success. | `PROJECT-008-B01..B06` |
| Existing Frontend project-workspace component/contract tests | Prove live-shaped `is_owner=true` shows and opens Permission Management and `false` hides it; production Frontend code changes only if a test exposes another defect. | `PROJECT-008-F01..F03` |
| `SPECIFICATION.md`, `SPEC_CHANGELOG.md`, `TEST_PLAN.md`, `TRACEABILITY.md` | Maintain requirement, decision, test and verification trace. | Governance |

### Implementation Sequence After Gate 4

1. Run governance gates and add fail-first tests that reproduce the deployed
   `is_owner=false` / Owner-capability contradiction.
2. Implement the shared response projection using existing `ProjectOwner`,
   `ProjectMember` and `project_capabilities` policies.
3. Route every `ProjectResponse` path through the projection and remove the
   duplicate list-only enrichment logic.
4. Run focused Backend and Frontend regressions, then syntax/lint/build and the
   broader project test selectors.
5. If an authenticated, non-mutating local read acceptance is separately safe,
   verify the deployed-shaped Owner projection. Do not build images, write Helm,
   mutate members or touch Provider/index/data under this repository approval.

### Compatibility, Security And Operations

- No API shape or status-code change; existing false values for real non-Owners
  remain false. The only corrected value is a false-negative Owner projection.
- No database/schema migration, seed, LDAP/Keycloak mapping, role permission,
  application row, document, vector, OpenSearch, Neo4j or object-store change.
- The Backend remains the only authorization authority. Frontend visibility is
  not accepted as mutation authorization.
- Queries remain bounded to one current user/project relationship. Response
  projection must not log token, LDAP DN or sensitive membership content.
- Image build, Helm render/write and Docker Desktop deployment are a later,
  separately approved delivery stage.

### Risks And Mitigations

- **Endpoint drift remains:** enumerate all `ProjectResponse` routes and assert
  shared projection usage plus response behavior.
- **Owner duplicated in roles:** form a set union and emit stable sorted roles.
- **A UI-only workaround weakens semantics:** keep Frontend on authoritative
  `is_owner`; fix the Backend projection instead.
- **Projection mistaken for authorization:** retain and test mutation-time
  `require_project_owner` denial for non-Owners.
- **Stale lock conflicts masked:** preserve current `lock_version` and 409
  behavior; projection runs only on the successful response object.

Rollback is limited to CHG-287 Backend response-projection code and tests. There
is no migration or data rollback.

### Planned Verification Commands After Gate 4

```bash
./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor
./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace
./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor
./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved
./HARNESS/harness.sh backend:syntax
./HARNESS/harness.sh test:backend
./HARNESS/harness.sh test:frontend
./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:lint
./HARNESS/harness.sh frontend:build
./HARNESS/harness.sh coverage:check
```

Focused pytest/component selectors will be run before the broader harness and
reported with exact pass/fail/blocked evidence. The 80% thresholds remain in
force and will not be relaxed.
