## CHG-288 Eligible Project-Member Search And Protected Owner Controls Plan

### Status And Gate

Gate 1 read-only diagnosis completed on 2026-09-02. Gate 2 confirmation: complete.
Peter confirmed Gate 2 with `同意 CHG-288 Gate 2，採用上述更新建議`.
This Gate 3 plan is complete. Gate 4 implementation approval: approved.
Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-09-02 with
`Peter approves CHG-288 Eligible Project Member Search And Protected Owner Controls`.
CHG-288 repository implementation and tests are authorized; Local Role/user/group/
member current-data mutation, image build and Kubernetes action remain unauthorized.

### Scope And Root Cause

- Frontend currently loads `listUsers(..., "project_members")` once when the
  Permission Management Modal opens, filters the returned subset locally and
  renders no state when the filtered list is empty. The Add button remains
  disabled without explaining why.
- Backend intentionally limits that scope to active users with effective
  `Menu.KnowledgeProjects.can_view`. Read-only Docker Desktop evidence shows
  `user01` is eligible, while active synchronized `user02`/`user05` have no
  Local Role and therefore are not eligible. This authorization gate must remain.
- Existing Backend last-Owner protection is not enough to provide the requested
  proactive UI behavior or prohibit an Owner from changing their own Owner row
  when multiple Owners exist.

### Approved Design Decisions

1. Add an Owner-only Project-scoped candidate query rather than expanding the
   unbounded global user endpoint. Search is server-side and supports display/
   family/given name, Email, employee ID and account aliases including Email
   local part; response items remain eligibility-filtered safe summaries.
2. Return safe aggregate evidence for identity matches that are ineligible, so
   the UI can distinguish no identity match from missing Knowledge Projects
   access without disclosing ineligible identity details.
3. Frontend uses approximately 300ms debounce, cancels/ignores stale requests,
   and provides localized loading, no-match, missing-access, no-more-role and
   error states. Selection remains staged until Add is submitted.
4. Keep mutation-time candidate validation authoritative. Search results never
   grant permission, and adding a Project member never auto-assigns a Local Role.
5. Define `knowledge-project-user` as the recommended minimal non-administrative
   role with only `KnowledgeProjects.can_view`. Repository behavior/config support
   is in scope; creating or assigning it in current Docker Desktop data is a
   separate exact-action approval with named users/groups.
6. Treat a sole Owner row and the signed-in Owner's own row as protected. Every
   role checkbox is read-only, delete is absent and a localized reason is shown.
   Backend rejects protected-row role-set/delete with a stable 409 and no partial
   write; Frontend protection is not the security boundary.
7. With multiple Owners, another Owner remains editable. A sole Owner can add an
   eligible second Owner, after which that second Owner may adjust the original
   Owner subject to the current transaction/lock rules.

### Planned Changes And Traceability

| Requirement | Planned implementation | Compatibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PROJECT-009` | Add typed candidate request/response schemas and a Project route/service query with authorization, escaped deterministic search, bounded pagination and safe eligibility aggregates. Extend Frontend API types and replace one-shot filtering with debounced server search/state handling. | Retain `/users?scope=project_members`; no User or Project schema change expected. |
| `PROJECT-009` minimal access role | Add V048 as an additive/idempotent data seed for an unassigned `knowledge-project-user` with only `Menu.KnowledgeProjects.can_view`; never assign it during member mutation. | No schema column/index change. Applying V048 and changing current role/user/group rows require a separately bound deployment/data action. |
| `PROJECT-010` | Centralize protected-Owner predicate/error codes in Backend member policy; enforce it transactionally for PUT/DELETE. Derive the matching Frontend row state from current user, effective members and Owner count; disable all role controls, omit delete and render localized reasons. | Retain current Owner union, last-owner, stale-lock, Project-state and eligibility behavior. |
| i18n/accessibility | Add Traditional Chinese and English search/protection/error strings, live status semantics, keyboard-safe result selection and accessible disabled/reason associations. | Existing visual system, control sizes and Owner tab model remain. |

### Implementation Sequence After Gate 4

1. Add fail-first Backend tests for candidate search qualification, matching,
   authorization, safe response and protected Owner transactions.
2. Add fail-first Frontend component/contract tests for all search states,
   stale-request ordering, staging and protected rows.
3. Implement shared Backend candidate query and protected Owner policy, preserving
   existing mutation validation and transaction boundaries.
4. Implement Frontend API/query state, localized UI, protection derivation and
   accessible controls using existing project workspace patterns.
5. Add the minimal role definition only through the repository's existing
   role/bootstrap pattern; do not mutate current Docker Desktop data.
6. Run focused suites and coverage, then broader permission/project regressions,
   lint/build and governance harnesses. Inspect the final diff for unrelated or
   generated changes.
7. Prepare a no-write delivery/release plan only if Peter separately requests an
   image build or Docker Desktop deployment. Bind any current role/user/member
   data action to explicit IDs, before/after evidence and rollback boundaries.

### Test Strategy

- Backend real SQLAlchemy/PostgreSQL tests cover Owner authorization; all query
  aliases; active/eligible/ineligible users; escaping, sorting and pagination;
  non-disclosure; mutation-time revalidation; sole/self/other Owner behavior;
  stale lock, race and rollback/no-partial-write.
- Frontend component tests cover debounce/cancellation/latest-response wins,
  query states, keyboard selection, pending candidate/Add behavior, successful
  refresh, error preservation and protected row behavior across role tabs.
- Retain role permission union, disabled user, Project scope, CHG-247 member
  management and CHG-287 Owner projection suites. Focused changed logic must meet
  at least 80% line and branch coverage without weakening repository thresholds.
- Live tests use disposable users/roles/projects or require a later exact local
  data-action approval. Static/mocked evidence cannot substitute for Backend
  authorization or persistent transaction acceptance under `TEST-002`.

### Deployment, Migration And Operations

- V048 is a data-only migration that creates one previously absent Local Role,
  one minimal permission and one migration audit row; it adds no schema column/
  index and assigns zero users/groups. Document reprocess, embedding, reindex,
  manifest and Provider calls are excluded. API additions are backward compatible.
- Image build, Helm render/write and Kubernetes rollout are separate later gates.
  Current revision 32 and its protected Secret/Ingress/PVC/data/index baselines
  are not modified by repository implementation.
- Production logs may record Project ID, normalized query length, result counts,
  eligibility outcome and latency; they must not record full queries, identity
  secrets, tokens, credentials or full LDAP DN.
- Stable Backend error codes and aggregate search states support observability
  without leaking which ineligible identity matched to unauthorized callers.

### Risks And Mitigations

- Username is not a uniformly stored User field: match the configured synchronized
  alias when available and always support normalized Email local part; test the
  user-facing `user02` case explicitly without inventing identity data.
- Search enumeration risk: require Project Owner authorization, bound query/limit,
  return safe summaries only and expose ineligible matches as aggregate evidence.
- Stale responses can reintroduce “no reaction”: use cancellation plus monotonic
  request identity so only the latest query controls visible state.
- UI-only Owner locks are bypassable: perform the protected predicate inside the
  same Backend transaction and use stable 409 responses.
- Owner-count races: recompute current effective Owners in the transaction and
  retain `lock_version`; never trust the count sent by Frontend.
- Assigning the minimal role expands access: do not auto-assign it and require a
  later target-bound approval for current environment data.

## CHG-289 Accessible Project-Member Autocomplete And Permission-Based Eligibility Plan

### Status And Gates

Gate 2 understanding confirmation: complete.

Gate 1 read-only diagnosis completed on 2026-09-03. Peter confirmed Gate 2 with
`同意 CHG-289 Gate 2，採用上述更新建議`. This Gate 3 development plan is
complete. Peter approved Gate 4 with
`Peter approves CHG-289 Accessible Project Member Autocomplete`; scoped
repository implementation and non-deployment verification are authorized.

### Scope And Decisions

- Replace only the Project Permission Management candidate presentation with an
  accessible async Autocomplete. Keep the existing Project-scoped Owner-only
  Backend endpoint, 300ms debounce, stale-response protection, safe summaries,
  aggregate ineligible evidence and mutation-time authorization.
- Render an ARIA combobox/listbox with at most five option rows visible; additional
  bounded results scroll vertically inside the dropdown. Keep Backend limit 20
  and deterministic pagination semantics—the UI height does not reduce the result
  set to five.
- Require explicit click/touch or keyboard selection. Do not infer the first
  result as selected. Clear stale selection when the query/result/modal changes;
  enable Add only for a currently valid selected/pending candidate.
- Preserve the current no-match, missing-access and no-additional-role meanings.
  A true zero-match response never selects, guesses or substitutes an identity.
- Eligibility remains role-name agnostic: any active, undeleted effective Local
  Role with `Menu.KnowledgeProjects.can_view=true` qualifies. The V048
  `knowledge-project-user` role is only a least-privilege option.
- Do not change Backend API/schema, create a migration, assign Local Roles, mutate
  Project members, or touch documents/vectors/indexes. `user02` role assignment
  and any image/Helm action remain separately gated.

### Planned Implementation

1. Add fail-first Frontend component tests for combobox/listbox semantics,
   explicit selection, keyboard/mouse parity, five-row scrolling, state
   classification and stale selection cleanup.
2. Extract or refine the existing Project permission candidate UI into the
   smallest reusable component/state helper consistent with current local
   patterns. Reuse `useDebouncedProjectMemberCandidateSearch`; do not introduce a
   styling or component framework.
3. Update `frontend/src/app/project/[id]/import/page.tsx` so `selectedPermissionUser`
   is explicit state rather than an alias for the first filtered result. Add only
   necessary styles in `frontend/src/app/globals.css` and preserve the current
   Calm Green enterprise visual language.
4. Update both locale files only if a new accessible label/instruction is needed;
   retain existing translated search-state strings otherwise.
5. Add/retain Backend live PostgreSQL regression cases proving permission-union
   eligibility is independent of Role name and that an unassigned Role grants no
   access. Backend production code should remain unchanged unless fail-first
   evidence reveals a contract defect.
6. Run focused coverage, all Frontend contracts/components, retained CHG-288
   Backend permission tests, lint/build, governance checks and diff inspection.
   Use a real configured service/browser path for behavioral acceptance; static
   markup alone is not live evidence under `TEST-002`.

### Test And Acceptance Strategy

- Component/Browser geometry verifies five full option rows, internal vertical
  scroll for row six, stable Modal dimensions, no horizontal overflow at 375px,
  desktop and 400% zoom.
- Accessibility verifies `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, active descendant or
  equivalent option focus, visible focus, Up/Down/Enter/Escape, no keyboard trap,
  and mouse/touch parity.
- Async tests verify debounce, abort/latest-response wins, loading/error, query
  change, modal close and stale selected-candidate cleanup.
- Live PostgreSQL integration creates two disposable differently named Roles with
  the same Knowledge Projects view permission and proves identical eligibility;
  it also proves the Role name alone and an unassigned Role grant nothing.
- Focused changed Frontend logic must meet at least 80% statement/branch coverage.
  Repository-wide thresholds are not reduced; pre-existing gaps are reported.

### Deployment And Risk Boundaries

- No database migration, API response change, configuration or Secret change is
  expected. A later Frontend image/Helm rollout requires a separate immutable
  image/render-bound approval and preservation baseline.
- Exact current-user Local Role assignments are security-sensitive data actions
  outside CHG-289. They require named targets, the chosen existing Role or exact
  new-role contract, before/after permission evidence and explicit approval.
- The main UX risk is implicit selection or stale state adding the wrong person;
  explicit selection identity plus query/result invalidation is the mitigation.
- The design-skill recommendations used here are accessible autocomplete,
  visible focus, loading/empty feedback and compact scrolling. Its unrelated
  vibrant marketing palette/type recommendations are rejected in favor of the
  repository's approved NomoSmart design system.

### Planned Implementation

1. Add fail-first Frontend contract tests proving only `role-users` receives the
   dedicated class and fixed height; prove the generic CRUD Modal retains its
   existing max-height behavior.

   fixed height with dynamic-viewport fallback, remaining-height form layout,
   internal vertical overflow and stable footer placement.
4. Run the existing System Management manual-role-user contracts/components,
   full Frontend tests, focused coverage if changed logic exists, Lint, production
   build, governance gates and diff inspection.

   dialog bounding boxes for empty/filtered/draft-expanded states at desktop,
   short viewport, 375px and 400% zoom. Static CSS assertions do not replace this
   `TEST-002` browser evidence.

### Test And Acceptance Strategy

- Capture one outer-dialog height per content state at the same viewport and
  require exact equality apart from browser sub-pixel normalization.
- Verify header and footer bounding positions remain stable while internal
  content scrolls; tab through the last reachable control to prove no hidden
  focus or keyboard trap.
- Verify short/dynamic viewport containment, vertical internal scrolling and no
  horizontal or background-page overflow.
- Assert other System Management CRUD Modal classes and content-driven sizing are
  unchanged.
- Retain ROLE-UI-001 behavior tests for immediate filtering, draft summaries,
  external/break-glass retention and manual-only save semantics.

### Deployment And Risk Boundaries

- Repository change is Frontend-only. No migration or configuration change is
  expected. Image build, Helm render/write and deployed browser acceptance need
  a separate exact approval and preservation baseline.
- The primary UX risk is making controls unreachable on short screens. Dynamic
  viewport bounding, a min-height-zero flex child, internal scrolling and a
  stable footer mitigate it.
- The `ui-ux-pro-max` guidance applied is stable geometry, viewport containment,
  keyboard reachability and no horizontal overflow. Its unrelated palette and
  marketing recommendations are not adopted; the existing NomoSmart design
  system remains authoritative.

#### Deployment rollback review and next gate

The combined revision-35 render is valid but must not yet be written. V049 is
forward-only: after it adds the unique membership constraint, automatic rollback
to revision 34 would restore the old multi-select Frontend/Backend writer, which
can submit multiple roles and then fail against the new database invariant.
Therefore a single atomic upgrade does not provide a fully compatible rollback.

The recommended deployment is split into two separately bound revisions:

1. Deploy CHG-291 Backend and Frontend first while retaining the CHG-288
   Migration image and `forward-v047`; verify the new single-role writer. Its
   rollback target remains schema-compatible revision 34.
2. After that succeeds, take and verify a pre-V049 database backup, then render
   and deploy the CHG-291 Migration image with `forward-v049`. Its rollback
   target will already run the CHG-291 single-role writer.

Neither write nor the backup is authorized by the Stage A approval. Each next
stage requires its own exact image/render/resource-bound approval.

Peter approved this two-stage deployment strategy on 2026-09-03 with
`核准上述兩階段部署策略`. This approval confirms the sequencing and authorizes
the no-write application-first revision-35 binding render. It does not by itself
authorize either Helm write, a database backup, or the V049 current-environment
migration.

For the application-first binding render, retain
`nomosmart/migrations:0.1.0-chg288` and `forward-v047`, override only Backend and
Frontend to CHG-291, render twice with hidden Secrets, and stop if revision 34,
the immutable image IDs, current application image matrix, protected resources
or data/index baselines differ. The resulting canonical SHA and current baseline
must be named in a later exact revision-35 write approval.

- Post-render state remains revision 34 with zero revision-35 Jobs, Flyway V048,
  no V049 constraint/audit, three membership rows for two distinct Project
  members and one Editor+Viewer overlap. All previously recorded Secret, PVC,
  Ingress, application, identity, vector and OpenSearch bindings match.

#### Application-first revision-35 deployment result

- The immediate fail-closed preflight repeated the approved comparison and
  matched revision 34, both immutable CHG-291 application image IDs, the
  retained CHG-288 Migration image, `forward-v047`, zero revision-35 Jobs,
  Flyway V048 with no V049 constraint/audit, the protected Secret/PVC/Ingress
  bindings, every approved application-row count and both OpenSearch counts.
- `helm upgrade nomosmart-local deploy/helm/nomosmart -n nomosmart
  --reuse-values --set-string image.backend.tag=0.1.0-chg291 --set-string
  image.frontend.tag=0.1.0-chg291 --rollback-on-failure --wait
  --wait-for-jobs --timeout 15m` completed as revision 35 on 2026-09-03.
  Exactly migration-35 and bootstrap-35 completed successfully; migration-35
  retained `nomosmart/migrations:0.1.0-chg288` and bootstrap-35 used the
  CHG-291 Backend image.
- Backend, Worker and Beat main/init containers plus the Frontend readiness
  init resolved to the approved Backend image ID; Frontend main resolved to the
  approved Frontend image ID. All four Deployments and supporting StatefulSets
  were Ready. Internal Backend health/readiness, Frontend loopback and
  Frontend-to-Backend checks returned HTTP 200. Host HTTPS `/`, Backend health,
  Backend readiness and Keycloak discovery also returned HTTP 200 with live-CA
  certificate validation enabled.
- The deployed Backend accepted exactly one role and rejected a two-role
  payload with stable HTTP 422 code `invalid_project_role_cardinality`. The
  deployed Frontend bundle contains the exclusive role-control marker. These
  checks were read-only and did not save membership changes.
- Post-deploy database signature, Secret UID/data digest, seven-PVC digest,
  both Ingress UIDs/allowlists and OpenSearch document counts exactly matched
  preflight. Flyway remains V048, the V049 unique constraint/audit is absent,
  and the existing Editor+Viewer overlap remains for the migration-second
  stage as designed.
- A final Helm snapshot kept every workload Ready, but exposed an unrelated
  pre-existing Redis Sentinel operational issue: one 15-day-old Sentinel Pod
  has 163 accumulated restarts because its one-second TLS liveness/readiness
  command intermittently times out. Its last termination was clean exit 0 and
  the Pod is currently Ready. Revision 35 did not change or roll the Sentinel
  Deployment; remediation is outside this approval and must be handled as a
  separate scoped operations change.
- Browser UI acceptance reached the previously open Project permission dialog,
  but the post-deploy reload expired the OIDC application session and returned
  to Keycloak login. The login tab is preserved for user handoff; no credential
  was read or entered and no membership/permission change was saved. Final
  authenticated UI radio-state verification remains pending a fresh sign-in.

Application-first revision 35 is therefore deployed and platform/API accepted.
The separately gated next stage remains: create and verify a pre-V049 database
backup, produce a fresh migration-second render bound to the then-current
revision-35 baseline, obtain exact approval, and only then select the CHG-291
Migration image with `forward-v049`.
